Furthermore, the *iṭ* is considered non-existent (*asiddha*), whereby my *ṇi* is elided; and this [elision of *ṇi*] is permanent, subverting the cause for the *valādi-iṭ*.

The meaning of this is as follows: regarding the *ciṇvad-bhāva* [treatment], there is *vṛddhi* in forms such as *anubhāviṣīṣṭa*; *yuk* is applied by the rule *ato yuk ciṇ-kṛtoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.33); in *ghāniṣyate*, the substitution of *gh* for *han* occurs by the rule *ho hanter ñṇitsu* (Pāṇini 7.3.54); in *śamiṣyate*, because it ends in *am*, the shortening occurs by the rule *mitāṃ hrasvaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.92), or optionally the long vowel occurs by the rule *ciṇṇamulor dīrgho 'nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 6.4.93). How, then, is there the elision of the *ṇi*-affix here?

Regarding the rule *ṇeraniṭi* (Pāṇini 6.4.51), [the author] says: "And since the augment *iṭ* is *asiddha*, by that [rule], the *ṇi* is elided for me. Because both the *ṇilopa* and the *ciṇvadbhāva* are based on scriptural authority (*ābhācchāstrīyatvāt*), when the *ṇilopa* is to be performed, the *ciṇvat-iṭ* is *asiddha*; therefore, the *ṇi* is elided for me. Now, one might object: "Since it follows a root with the marker *seṭ*, there ought to be an *iṭ* according to the rule concerning roots beginning with a consonant (*valādi-lakṣaṇa*). This is not so; for this [elision of *ṇi*] is *nitya* because it applies whether the *iṭ* has been added or not (*kṛtākṛta-prasaṅgitvena*). It obstructs the *iṭ* which is conditioned by a *val* sound; whereas the *iṭ* conditioned by a *val* sound is *anitya* because the relationship is reversed.

The concise meaning is that these are the purposes [of the rule]: "it will be pacified" (*śamiṣyate*) and "it will be calmed" (*śāmiṣyate*), where there is an option for lengthening according to the rule *ciṇṇamulordīrgho 'nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 6.4.93). Regarding the rule *suṭ tithoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.107): the augment *suṭ* occurs in connection with the *liṅ* [optative] suffix, specifically before its *t* and *th* sounds. In this case, the *t* and *th* are the augments (*āgaminau*), whereas *sīyuṭ* is an augment of the *liṅ* itself. Thus, because their domains are distinct, there is no conflict between these two. The *s* of these two becomes *ṣ*. Example: *anubhāviṣīṣṭa*.

In the absence of the *iṭ* augment in the *ciṇvadiṭ* [formation], the *iṭ* characterized by the rule for roots beginning with *val* [is applied]: *anubhaviṣīṣṭa*, *anubhāviṣīyāstām*, *anubhāviṣīran*, *anubhāviṣīṣṭhāḥ*, *anubhāviṣīyāsthām*. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 8.3.78 (*iṇaḥ ṣīdhvaṃluṅliṭāṃ dho’ṅgāt*), when a root ending in *iṇ* is followed by the suffixes *ṣīdhvam*, *luṅ*, or *liṭ*, the dental *dh* is replaced by a cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) substitute.

*Vibhāṣeṭaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.79): After an *aṅga* ending in the root *iṇ*, the dental *ḍha* of the affixes *ṣīdhvam*, *luṅ*, and *liṭ* is optionally replaced by a cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) substitute. Examples: *anubhāviṣīdhvam* / *anubhāviṣīḍhvam*; *anubhāviṣīya*; *anubhaviṣīvahi*; *anubhaviṣīmahi*. *Parokṣe liṭ* (Pāṇini 3.2.115): The suffix *liṭ* occurs after a verbal root when it denotes an action that took place in the past, not belonging to the current day, and was not witnessed by the speaker.

Pāṇini Sūtra 3.4.82 states: *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatususthalathusaṇalvamāḥ*. Following the rule for the *liṭ* [affix], these nine substitutes—*ṇal*, *atus*, *us*, *thal*, *athus*, *a*, *ṇal*, *va*, and *ma*—occur respectively as the replacements for the nine *parasmaipada* endings of the *liṭ* tense.

Regarding *liṭi dhātoranabhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 6.1.8): when *liṭ* follows, two instances of either the first or the second *ekāc* (single-vowel) syllable of the root—which is not subject to reduplication—are doubled as appropriate. Regarding *indhibhavatibhyāñca* (Pāṇini 1.2.6): the *liṭ* suffix following the roots *indh* and *bhū* becomes marked with the *k* indicator (*kit*).

*bhuvo vuk luṅliṭoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.88): the augment *vuk* is added to the base *bhū* when followed by the *luṅ* or *liṭ* suffixes beginning with a vowel. *bhavateraḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.73): when the *liṭ* follows, the substitute *a* is applied to the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) of the root *bhū*. *abhyāse car ca* (Pāṇini 8.4.53): in the context of reduplication, the *jhal* sounds are replaced by *car* sounds; thus, for the letter *b*, there is the substitution of the *jaś* sound *b* [which becomes *ba*]. In this regard, the sequence is as follows when *tip* is applicable in place of *liṭ*:

Then, because of the *kit* designation, there is an absence of *guṇa* and *vṛddhi*; then the insertion of *vuk*, then reduplication, and the operations of the reduplicated syllable. For the sake of transition, the *kit* status of the root *bhū* need not be prescribed if *vuk* were to be permanent; however, this is not the case, because the rule for inserting *vuk* after a stem ending in the vowel *u* applies to a different word-form (*śabdāntara*), and consequently, *vṛddhi* and *guṇa* would subsequently apply. Therefore, the *kit* status of the *liṭ* suffix is established as having been made by a *pit* [suffix]. How can *vṛddhi*, which has a specifically designated locus, be prevented by the *kit* status? By the force of the governing rule (*adhikāra*) of *kit*, it is prohibited just like *guṇa*.

*babhūva*, *babhūvatuḥ*, *babhūvuḥ*. Regarding the *sip* and *thal* suffixes: observe here that [the root] is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) when it ends in a vowel; however, those who know the science declare these [roots] to be *seṭ* (possessing the *iṭ* augment).
*ad*, *dānt*, *śīṅ*, and *śiṅ* as well;

those ending in *ū* and *u* found in the [Dhātu] lists, as well as *ru*, *snū*, and *kṣu*; likewise *ūrṇu*, and then *yu*, *nu*, and *kṣṇu*—thus have the roots ending in vowels been skillfully compiled. Now, learn also those ending in consonants.

In this context, because of the rule *gaṇastha-mūdantam* [the root ending in /u/ or /ū/ belonging to the *gaṇa* group], the augment *iṭ* is applied according to *ārdhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.35), which states that the augment *iṭ* occurs before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant (*val*). Due to the *kit* status [of the suffix], there is no *guṇa* substitution; thus we have *babhūvitha* and *babhūtha*. This is established by the Vedic rule *babhūthātatanthajagṛbhma* (Pāṇini 7.2.64). The remainder should be understood as follows: by *bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.13) and *liṭastajhayoreśirec* (Pāṇini 3.4.81), which prescribes that for the substitutes *ta* and *jhi* of *liṭ*, the replacements *eś* and *irec* respectively occur. Thus, in the impersonal sense (*bhāve*), we have *babhūve*; in the passive sense (*karmaṇi*), *anubabhūve*, *anubabhūvāte*, and so on.

Regarding the forms *anubabhūvire* and so forth, under the governing rule *bhūte* (Pāṇini 3.2.84), which states that the suffix *luṅ* occurs after a verbal root when expressing a past (*bhūta*) sense, the following applies: by *itaśca* (Pāṇini 3.4.100), there is elision [of the final *i*]; the augment *aṭ* is added; and by *cli luṅi* (Pāṇini 3.1.43), the suffix *cli* is applied when *luṅ* follows. By *cleḥ sic* (Pāṇini 3.1.44), *sic* is the substitute for *cli*. When the sequence *a-bhū-s-t* is established, [the rule] *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 2.4.77) [applies].

(2/4/77) When there is the mention of *gā*, there is the inclusion of both *iṇ* and *piba*; when there is the mention of *iṇ* and *piba*, there is the inclusion of *ghu*. [The roots included under *ghu* are: *ḍudāñ* in the sense of giving; *do* in the sense of cutting; *deṅ* in the sense of protecting; *dāñ* in the sense of giving; *ḍudhāñ* in the senses of giving, supporting, and nourishing; and *dheṭ* in the sense of drinking. There is the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *sic* following these [roots] as well as *gā*, *sthā*, and so on. Then, when the *guṇa* substitution for the *sārvadhātuka* suffix would have applied, [Pāṇini’s rule] *bhūsuvostiṅi* (Pāṇini 7.3.88) states that for the two roots *bhū* and *su*, there is no *guṇa* substitution before a *tiṅ* *sārvadhātuka* suffix. Thus: *abhūt*.

For *tas* and other suffixes, *tām* and others are substituted. Regarding the root *bhū*, the augment *vuk* is applied by the rule *abhūtāṃ bhuvo vug luṅ-liṭoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.88), resulting in *abhūvan*. Due to the restriction "after [a stem] ending in *at*," the *jus* substitution does not occur. By the rule *ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.66), the substitute *ciṇ* is applied to the *cli* that follows a verbal root when expressing the sense of the impersonal (*bhāva*) or passive (*karman*). When the suffix *ta* follows a word expressing the impersonal or passive, there is the elision of *ciṇ*. There is elision of the suffix following *ciṇ*, and by the rule *aco ñṇiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.115), there is *vṛddhi* [substitution], resulting in *abhāvi devadattena* ("it was become by Devadatta").

The wealth was experienced [by them]; *lakṣmīḥ* is the subject. First, there is the substitution of *sij* for the suffix, and then the augment *iṭ* as if it were *ciṇ*. Thus we have *anvabhāviṣātām*, and so forth. Regarding the *jha* suffixes in the *ātmanepada*, by the rule *anataḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.5), we have *anvabhāviṣata*. For *thās*, we have *anvabhāviṣṭhāḥ*; for *āthām*, *anvabhāviṣāthām*. In the case of *dhvam*, by the rule *dhi ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.25), there is the elision of the *s* sound. Then, by the rule *vibhāṣeṭaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.79), there is optionally the substitution of the retroflex *ḍha*. Thus we have *anvabhāviḍhvam* or *anvabhāvidhvam*, and so forth. When the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied to the root *bhū*, forming *bhāv-i*, and then the *caṅ* suffix is applied, [the resulting form is derived] from that which ends in *san* etc., according to the rule *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.32).

In the case of the *luṅ* [aorist] suffix with the sense of "becoming" (*dhātusaṃjñā*), by the rule *ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ* (Pāṇini 3.1.48), the *cli* suffix is replaced by *caṅ*. When the form *bhāvi-at* is established, the rule *ṇau caṅy upadhāyā hrasvaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.1)—which states that when a *ṇi*-affix followed by *caṅ* is present, the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) of the verbal base (*aṅga*) becomes short—applies, and thus the vowel is shortened. The doubling [of the root] occurs because of the rule regarding *caṅ*; however, this is due to the status of *sthānivadbhāva* (the substitute acting like the original) for the root *bhū*. But is it not the case that the cause for doubling is the immediate proximity of a non-*ṇi* [vowel], as indicated by the evidence?

What indicates this? The rule *oḥ puyaṇjyapara* (Pāṇini 7.4.80)—which prescribes the substitution of *c* for the final *i* of an abhyāsa (reduplicated syllable) ending in *i*, when followed by a consonant of the *pa*-group (*pu*), *yaṇ*, or *ja*, provided an *a*-vowel follows—indicates that even though reduplication is performed merely to achieve the status of having an *u*-vowel at the end of the abhyāsa, the substitute [of the reduplication] possesses the status of the original (*sthānivadbhāva*). Therefore...

Regarding the root *bhū*, there is reduplication; the treatment of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsakārya*) is as follows: by Pāṇini 7.4.93 (*sanvallaghuni*), the reduplication undergoes the *san*-treatment; by 7.4.80 (*oḥ puyaṇjyapara*), the vowel of the reduplication is changed to *i*; and by 7.4.94 (*dīrgho laghoḥ*), because the condition "when a light [vowel] follows" (*laghuni*) is specified, a long vowel is substituted for the reduplicated syllable when a light radical vowel follows. Thus, *abībhavat*. When the fruit of the action is intended for the agent, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used by Pāṇini 1.3.74 (*ṇicaśca*); thus, *abībhavata*.

*lṛṭ śeṣe ca* (Pāṇini 3.3.13): [The suffix] *lṛṭ* occurs in the sense of the future (*bhaviṣyati*). What is the "remainder" (*śeṣa*)? The remainder is that which is other than when another action is the motive (*kriyārthopapada*). In the case of the pure future (*śuddhe bhaviṣyati kāle*) and, by virtue of the word *ca*, when another action is the motive (*kriyārthāyāṃ copapade*), the suffix *lṛṭ* occurs after a verbal root. For example, in the case of a motive for action: *bhaviṣyāmīti manyate* ("He thinks, 'I shall be'"). But in the case of the pure future, forms such as *bhaviṣyati*, *bhaviṣyataḥ*, *bhaviṣyanti*, and so forth, are easily understood.

Regarding the rule *bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.13): *bhāviṣyate*, *bhaviṣyate*, *anubhāviṣyate*, *anubhaviṣyate*. Here, by the rule *syatāsī lṛluṭoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.33), the suffix *sya* is applied. Due to its higher status (*paratva*) and its being more internal (*antaraṅgatva*), it supersedes the suffix *yak*.

Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.3.139 states: *liṅ-nimitte lṛṅ kriyātipattau* ("The conditional suffix *lṛṅ* occurs when there is a cause for the conditional *liṅ*, provided that there is a failure of the action"). That is to say, when there is a future time (*bhaviṣyati*) characterized by a cause for the conditional *liṅ*—such as the relationship between cause and effect (*hetu-hetumad-bhāva*)—and provided that there is a "failure of the action" (*kriyātipatti*), the conditional suffix *lṛṅ* is employed. "Failure of the action" refers to the non-actualization of an action due to some deficiency in its causes, such as the occurrence of an adverse condition (*vidhura-pratyaya-upanipāta*).

Or perhaps there was a deficiency or defect in the causal factors; for if [the ox] had been facing south, the cart would not have overturned. This statement concerns the future and is intended as a reason for avoiding future humiliation; but what is the point of understanding that the calling of Kamalaka was the cause of that [humiliation]?

Having repeatedly observed that the cart overturned when Kamalaka was summoned in the past, and having understood through a mark (*liṅga*) that even a future summons of Kamalaka will be the cause of the cart's overturning, the speaker—having again [perceived] the mark and again [the mark's relation to] the general properties (*sāmānyadharma*), and having understood the non-occurrence of the summons of Kamalaka through the mark of Kamalaka’s departure to another place, and having also understood the non-occurrence of the cart’s overturning through the loading of a heavier burden upon the cart—uttered the sentence.

He employs [the term]. The entire rule beginning with "liṅ is used when there is a cause in the past" (bhūte ca liṅ nimitta) follows. In the past tense, and in the scope of the previous sūtra, the conditional suffix (lṛṅ) occurs; this is the prescription for the conditional suffix as a cause [of action] by the rule "utāpyoḥ" (Pāṇini 3.3.152). Prior to that, he will state the option.

The example is as follows: "It was seen that your sons were walking about for the sake of food. If he had been seen by the other [person] seeking a Brahmin, then he would have eaten; but since he did not eat, he went by another path. Regarding the rule *syatāsī lṛluṭoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.33): the term *lṛ* is a general designation for both *lṛṅ* and *lṛṭ*. For these two (*lṛṅ* and *lṛṭ*), *syat* and *tāsī* are substituted respectively when the agent (*kartṛ*) is expressed, as in *abhaviṣyata*, *abhaviṣyatām*, *abhaviṣyan*, and so forth. In the case of the passive and impersonal voices (*bhāvakarmaṇoḥ*), [the suffixes are added accordingly].

By the rule *ciṇvadiṭ* (Pāṇini 3.1.44), the augment *iṭ* is applied as if it were *ciṇ*; then by the rule *aco ñṇiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.115), there is *vṛddhi*. Thus, [the forms] *abhāviṣyata* (you were caused to become) and *anvabhāviṣyata* (you were caused to experience) are formed. The remainder, beginning with *śrīḥ*, should be understood accordingly. For the future tense not referring to today, the suffix *luṭ* is used (Pāṇini 3.3.15), meaning "it will be."

The *luṭ* suffix occurs after a verbal root when the sense is that of the future not pertaining to the current day; it is an exception to *lṛṭ*. Regarding *luṭ*: "In place of the first person of *luṭ*, whether in the *parasmaipada* or the *ātmanepada*, the substitutes *ḍā*, *rauḥ*, and *ras* are applied respectively" (Pāṇini 2.4.85). Thus, these substitutes—*ḍā*, *rauḥ*, and *ras*—are applied in their respective order to the first person endings of both the *parasmaipada* and the *ātmanepada*.

Because the singular substitute is marked with the *ḍi*-sign, when the *ṭi*-elision (*ṭilopa*) is applied to the stem ending in *tās*, the form *bhavit-ā* remains. At this stage, although the *guṇa* substitution for a light penultimate vowel would apply, it is prohibited by the rule *dīdhīvevīṭām* (Pāṇini 1.1.6). Then, by the rule *ri ca* (Pāṇini 7.4.51), the *s* of *tās* is elided, resulting in *bhavitā*. In the second person singular, when the form *bhavitās* remains, the *s* is elided by the rule *tāsastyorlopaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.50); specifically, the *s* of both *tās* and *as* is elided when followed by an affix beginning with *s*.

*bhavati* | *bhavitāsi* | *bhavitāsthaḥ* | *bhavitāstha* | *bhavitāsmi* | *bhavitāsvaḥ* | *bhavitāsmaḥ*. With the augment *iṭ* as in the *ciṇ* case, [the forms are] *bhāvitā*, *bhāvitā tvayā*. In the pure passive (*śuddhakarmaṇi*), [the forms are] *anubhāvitā*, *anubhavitā śrīḥ*; *anubhāvitārau*, *anubhavitārau*; *anubhāvitāraḥ*, *anubhavitāraḥ*. As before, there is the elision of the indicatory letter (*anubandhalopa*); by *thās* becoming *se* (Pāṇini 3.4.80), [we have] *anubhāvitāse*.

By the rule *anubhāvitāśāstetvaṃ dhi ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.25), there is the elision of the *sakāra*. Optionally, by *jaśtva*, one has *anubhāvitād-dhve* or *anubhavitād-dhve*. Regarding the first person singular (*uttamaikavacana*), while the rule *tāsastyorlopaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.50) is still in effect, the rule *ha eti* (Pāṇini 7.4.52) prescribes that the substitute *ha* occurs for the *sakāra* of both *tāsi* and *asti* when followed by *e*. Thus, one obtains forms such as *anubhāvitāhe* and *anubhavitāhe*.

From the rule *dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkādicchāyāṃ vā* (Pāṇini 3.1.7), the word *san* is understood as a governing term (*anuvartate*). A verbal root whose object is the object of the desire (*iṣi-karma*) and which has the same agent as that desire (*iṣiṇā samānakartṛkaḥ*) takes the suffix *san* when expressing a desire. According to *iko jhal* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), a suffix *san* beginning with a *jhal* consonant following a root ending in an *ik* vowel becomes *kit*. Due to its *kit* status, there is no *guṇa* substitution. Furthermore, by the rule *sani grahaguhośca* (Pāṇini 7.2.12), the augment *iṭ* is not added to the roots *grah* and *guh*, nor to roots ending in long *u*, when *san* follows. This applies to both *san* and *yaṅ*.

(Pāṇini Sūtra 6.1.9) For a root ending in *san* or *yaṅ*, the first or second *ekāc* (single-consonant) syllable undergoes reduplication as appropriate. Regarding *bhū-sa* (the root *bhū* with the suffix *san*), there is reduplication; then by "halādiśeṣaḥ" (Pāṇini Sūtra 7.4.60), the initial consonant of the reduplicated syllable remains and the non-initial consonants are elided. There is shortening of the reduplicated syllable, and by "iṇkoḥ" (Pāṇini Sūtra 8.3.57), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs. When *bubhūṣa-* is established, [the rule] "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.32) applies: those suffixes which have *san* as their beginning are called *sanādi*; what, then, are they?

Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.8: *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* (roots include those ending in *san*, etc., and those ending in *sup*). Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.9: *kāmyacca* (the suffix *kāmyac* is added after a word denoting the self). Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.10: *upamānādācāre* (the suffixes *kyac* and *kāmyac* are added after a word used as a standard of comparison when expressing behavior). Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.11: *kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaśca* (the suffix *kyaṅ* is added after a word denoting the agent of an action, with the elision of the final *s*). It should be stated that *kvip* is optionally added after *vagalbha*, *klība*, and *hoḍha* when expressing behavior; some say it is added after all nominal stems (*prātipadika*). Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.13: *lohitādi-ḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣ* (the suffix *kyaṣ* is added after words beginning with *lohita* and after those ending in *ḍāc*). Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.19: *namovarivaścitraṅ kyaṅ* (the suffix *kyaṅ* is added after *namaḥ*, *varivaḥ*, and *citraṅ*). Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.20: *pucchabhāṇḍacīvarāṇ ṇiṅ* (the suffix *ṇiṅ* is added after *puccha*, *bhāṇḍa*, and *cīvara*).

The suffix *ṇic* follows the roots *muṇḍa*, *miśra*, *ślakṣṇa*, *lavaṇa*, *vrata*, *vastra*, *hala*, *kala*, *kṛta*, and *tūsta* (Pāṇini 3.1.21). The suffix *yaṅ* follows a root that has a single vowel (*ekāc*), begins with a consonant (*halādi*), and expresses the repetition of an action (*kriyāsamabhivyāhāre*) (Pāṇini 3.1.22). The suffix *ṇic* follows the words *satyāpa*, *pāśa*, *rūpa*, *vīṇā*, *tūla*, *śloka*, *senā*, *loman*, *tvaca*, *varman*, *varṇa*, *cūrṇa*, and the roots beginning with *cur* (Pāṇini 3.1.25). The suffix *yaṅ* follows the group of roots beginning with *kaṇḍū* (Pāṇini 3.1.27). The suffix *āya* follows the roots *gup*, *dhūp*, *vicch*, *paṇ*, and *pani* (Pāṇini 3.1.28). The suffix *īyaṅ* follows the root *ṛti* (Pāṇini 3.1.29). The suffix *ṇiṅ* follows the root *kam* (Pāṇini 3.1.30).

By this rule (Pāṇini 3.1.30), these [roots] or those ending in them are designated as verbal roots (*dhātu*). Consequently, the *laṭ* and other suffixes are applied, as in *bubhūṣati* and so forth. The purpose of the vowel *u* in the suffix *san* is for the sake of perception (*pratīti*). In *pipaṭhiṣati*, there is reduplication of the second monosyllabic (*ekāc*) element according to the rule "of a monosyllabic root beginning with a consonant" (Pāṇini 6.1.2). The suffix *yaṅ* is applied by the rule "in the case of the frequent repetition of an action" (Pāṇini 3.1.22); "frequent repetition" (*paunaḥpunya*) or "intensity" (*bhṛśārtha*) constitutes the "frequent repetition of an action" (*kriyā-samabhivyāhāra*).

The suffix *yaṅ* occurs after a root that has a single consonant (*ekāc*), begins with a consonant (*halādi*), and denotes an action characterized by repetition (*samabhivyāhāraviśiṣṭakriyā*). As before, there is reduplication (*dvirvacana*), and the rule *halādi śeṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.60) applies. Regarding the operation on the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsakārya*), the rule *guṇo yaṅlukoh* (Pāṇini 7.4.82) states that when *yaṅ* or its elision (*yaṅluk*) follows, the reduplicated syllable undergoes *guṇa*. When *bobhūya-* is established, it receives the designation of a verbal root (*dhātu*) according to *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.32). Consequently, the verbal suffixes (*lakāra*) apply; because they are marked with *ṅ*, the *ātmanepada* endings are used: *bobhūyate*, *abobhūyata*, *bobhūyatām*.

*bobhūyeta*, *bobhūyiṣīṣṭa*, *bobhūyāñcakre*, *bobhūyitā*, *bobhūyiṣate*, *bobhūyāmbabhūve*, *bobhūyāmāsa*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], *abobhūyiṣṭa*. *Bobhūyiṣyate*, *abobhūyiṣyata*, *bobhūyiṣyatām*. In the passive (*karmaṇi*) *luṅ*, one should apply forms such as *abobhūyi*, and so forth. Regarding the verbal roots ending in *san* and others, that which has been introduced here as common to all *tiṅanta* (conjugated) words should be followed accordingly hereafter as far as possible; however, we shall state the specific details as they arise.

The root *edh* means "to grow. Although the word *vṛddhi* (growth) is derived as a feminine noun by the rule *ktin* (Pāṇini 3.3.94), it should nevertheless be understood that the meaning of the verbal root (*dhātvartha*) is clarified precisely as something to be accomplished (*sādhya*). The same applies to subsequent cases. In the present tense (*laṭ*), the substitution of *e* for *ṭi* occurs: *edhate*. For roots beginning with a vowel, the augment *āṭ* is added to the stem (Pāṇini 6.4.72), and by the rule *āṭaśca* (Pāṇini 6.1.90), *vṛddhi* is substituted [for the preceding vowel and the following *a*]: *aidhata*. In the imperative (*loṭ*): *edhatām*. In the optative (*liṅ*): *edheta*. In the benedictive (*āśis*): *edhiṣīṣṭa*.

Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.36: *liṭi ijādeśca gurumato'nṛcchaḥ*—after a root beginning with *ij*, which is heavy (having a long vowel or a conjunct consonant), and excluding the root *ṛcch*, the suffix *ām* occurs in the *liṭ* tense. Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.40: *kṛñcānuprayujyate liṭi*—the roots *kṛ*, *bhū*, and *as* are to be employed as subsequent applications (*anuprayoga*) after the *liṭ*. Pāṇini Sūtra 1.3.63: *ām-pratyayavat-kṛño'nuprayogasya*—the *ātmanepada* endings are applied to the root *kṛ* used as an application (*anuprayoga*) after *ām*, just as they would be to the original root. Examples: *edhāñcakre*, *edhāmbabhūva*, *edhāmāsa*; in the *laṅ* tense: *aidhiṣṭa*.

*aidhiṣātām*, *aidhiṣata*. When the form *edhi* followed by the suffix *at* in the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist) is established, both reduplication (*dvirvacana*) and the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasva*) are applicable. Since reduplication is "obligatory" (*nitya*)—because it applies regardless of whether the other rule has already taken effect or not—it would apply first. Consequently, there would be no shortening because the penultimate vowel would no longer be short; thus, the form *mā bhavānididhat* would not be established. Therefore, even though reduplication is obligatory, it is superseded by the shortening of the penultimate vowel due to an interpretive indicator (*jñāpaka*). What is that indicator? It is the marking of the root *oṇ* with the letter *ṛ* as its *it*.

Indeed, the rule *nāglopiśāsvṛditām* (Pāṇini 7.4.2)—which prohibits the shortening of the penultimate vowel—is formulated so that this prohibition may apply. If the second doubling were to occur first, then since the penultimate vowel of the root *oṇ* would no longer be subject to shortening, the designation *ṛdit* (having an indicatory *ṛ*) would be rendered useless. Therefore, by virtue of this *jñāpaka*, the shortening of the penultimate vowel occurs first in the case of roots beginning with vowels (such as *ajīgaṇat*). However, in the case of roots beginning with consonants—such as *abībhavat* and *apīpavat*—since both operations are equally obligatory (*nitya*), the shortening of the penultimate vowel takes precedence due to its subsequent position in the rules. Thus is the established order.

The shortening of the penultimate vowel occurs before the suffix *ṇic* and before *caṅ*, provided that [the root] begins with a consonant; however, by means of an indicator (*jñāpaka*), this applies even when [the reduplicated syllable] begins with a vowel. In the cases of *lṛṭ* and *luṅ*: *edhiṣyate* (future), *aidhiṣyata* (conditional), and *edhitā* (periphrastic future). When the augment *ṇiṭ* is added, there is a second doubling [of the root]. From the causative form ending in *san*, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) applies as before by the rule *sanaḥ*. Thus: *edidhiṣate*. There is no *yaṅ* [intensive] because the root does not begin with a consonant.

*Spardh* means rivalry or competition. *spardhate* (he competes), *aspardhata* (he competed), *aspardhetām* (they two competed), *spardheta* (he may compete). In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), *spardhiṣīṣṭa* (may he compete). According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.61, *śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ*, in the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) only the *khayaḥ* (consonants other than nasals and semivowels) remain, while the other consonants (*hal*) are elided. Thus: *paspardhe* (he competed), *aspardhata* (he competed). *Pasparde* (he competed).

Regarding the rule *aspardhiṣṭa*: "In the case of a *ṇi* followed by *caṅ*, when there is a light syllable, the operation is like that of a *san*-affix, provided there is no elision of *a*" (Pāṇini 7.4.93). When a *ṇi* followed by *caṅ* contains a light syllable, the operation is as if it were a *san*-affix; however, because the light syllable of the verbal root is not followed [by the *san*-affix], the *sanvadbhāva* does not apply, and thus the substitution of *i* for the vowel of the reduplicated syllable according to *sanyataḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.79) does not occur. Regarding the rule *dīrgho laghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.94): "There is lengthening of the light reduplicated syllable."

By the rule *sanvallaghuni caṅpare'naglope* (Pāṇini 7.4.93), because the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*) is not followed by a light syllable, the lengthening does not occur. Thus: *apaspardhata*; in the *lṛṭ* and *luṭ* tenses: *spardhiṣyate*, *aspardhiṣyata*; in the *luṭ*: *spardhitā*; with the suffix *san*: *pispardhiṣati*. By the rule *yaṅi dīrgho'kitaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.83), there is lengthening of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) when it is not marked with *k*.

Furthermore, where *nuk* is enjoined by the rule *nugato 'nunāsikāntasya* (Pāṇini 7.4.85) through the inclusion of the term *akit*, as in *yaṃyamya-te* and so forth, [the substitution] does not occur there. Now, one might object: "The inclusion of *ak* is useless, for *nuk* will simply be an exception (*apavāda*) to the long vowel. If this is the case, then this very point informs us that "in the case of modifications of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), an exception does not supersede the general rule (*utsarga*)," as in *pāspardhyate*.

The root *gādh* is used in the senses of "to stand firm," "to desire support," and "to tie. The letter *ṛ* is for the purpose of the specific rule *nāglopiśāsvṛditām* (Pāṇini 7.4.2). Forms such as *gādhate* and *agādhata* are derived accordingly. In the case of the causative with *caṅ* (the reduplicated aorist), as before, there is an absence of the *sanvadbhāva*, *it*-treatment, and lengthening. When the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasvatva*) would apply in the causative with *caṅ*, the rule *nāglopiśāsvṛditām* (Pāṇini 7.4.2) applies: for bases ending in a lost *a* (*aglopī*), for the root *śās*, and for those marked with an indicatory *ṛ* (*ṛdita*), the shortening of the penultimate vowel does not occur. Thus, we have *ajagādhata*. Similarly, *gādhiṣyate*, etc. The root *bādh* is used in the sense of "shaking" or "disturbing"; its treatment is the same as the preceding one.

The roots *nāthṛ* and *nādhṛ* are used in the senses of begging, distressing, exercising lordship, and blessing; they are both transitive and intransitive. Regarding the sense of blessing (*āśis*), by the rule of the supplementary statement (*aupasaṃkhyānika*) "nātha" [is used], the Ātmanepada occurs only in the sense of blessing; in other cases, because they fall under the "remainder" (*śeṣa*), the Parasmaipada occurs. In the case of the Ātmanepada, it is as previously described. In other cases: *nāthati*, *anāthat*, *nāthatu*, *nāthet*. In the sense of blessing: *nāthyāt*. [In the Perfect: *nanātha*. In the Aorist (*luṅ*), *sic* replaces *cli*, and there is the augment *iṭ*.

According to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 7.3.96 (*asti-sico'pṛkte*), the augment *iṭ* is added to a *sārvadhātuka* affix consisting of a single phoneme (*apṛkta*) following the root *as-* and the suffix *sic*. By Pāṇini’s Sūtra 8.2.28 (*iṭa īṭi*), there is elision of the final *s* of the suffix *sic* when followed by the augment *iṭ*. Regarding the elision of *sic*, it should be stated that it is established in the context of a single-substitute (*ekādeśa*) operation; thus, a long vowel by class (*savarṇadīrgha*) occurs. The increase (*vṛddhi*) that would otherwise apply to the *parasmaipada* endings according to Pāṇini’s Sūtra 7.2.1 (*sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu*) is prohibited by the rule "not when *iṭ* follows" (*neṭi*).

Therefore, by the rule *ato halāder laghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.7), [the substitution of *iṭ*] is optionally prescribed; thus we have *anāthīt*. The result of being taught with an initial *ṇ* is the substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*] by the rule *upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya* (Pāṇini 8.4.14). In the *lṛṭ* [future], we have *nāthiṣyati*, and so forth. The root *dadh* means "to hold" or "to support. [Present: *dadhate*; [Imperfect: *adadhata*; [Imperative: *dadhātām*; [Optative: *dadhet*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), *dadhiṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* [perfect], due to the substitution of *etva* and elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsalopa*), we have *dedhe*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], *adadhiṣṭa*. In the *caṅ* [reduplicated aorist] after the causative suffix (*ṇau*), we have *adīdadhat*, and so forth.

The root *dada* means "giving," as before. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, by the rule *na śasadadavādiguṇānām* (Pāṇini 6.4.126), there is a prohibition against the *etva* (change to *e*) and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsalopa*). Thus: *dadade*. The root *vadi* means "salutation" and "praise. By the rule *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.58), the augment *num* is added. Thus: *vandate*. [Conjugations follow: *avandanta* (imperfect); *vandatām* (imperative); *vandeta* (optative); *vandiṣīṣṭa* (precative). *avandiṣṭa* (aorist). In the causative with *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist): *avavandat*. *vandiṣyate* (future); *avandiṣyata* (conditional). *vanditā* (periphrastic future). *vivandiṣate* (desiderative); *vāvandyate* (intensive). The root *bhadi* means "prosperity" and "happiness."

The root *mad* is used in the senses of praise, joy, intoxication, sleep, and gait; it is both transitive and intransitive. *Spadi* means slight movement; it is intransitive. These [roots] are like *vand*.

*SVAD* (in the forms *svada* and *svarda*) means to taste. Present: *svadate* Aorist: *asvadata* Imperative: *svadatām* Optative: *svadeta* Precative: *svadiṣīṣṭa* Perfect: *sasvade* Aorist: *asvadiṣṭa* Causative Aorist (*caṅ*): *asisvadat*; others say *asiṣvadat*. Future: *svadiṣyate* Conditional: *asvadiṣyata* Periphrastic Future: *svaditā* Desiderative: *sisvadiṣate* Intensive: *sāsvadyate* *SVARD* (meaning to taste): Present: *svardate* Causative Aorist (*caṅ*): *asasvardat* The remainder is as before.

The root *mud* means "to rejoice. By the rule for the strengthening of a light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇaḥ*), we have: *modate* (he rejoices), *amodata* (he rejoiced), *modatām* (let him rejoice), *modeta* (he may rejoice). In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), *modiṣīṣṭa* (may he rejoice). By the rule *asaṃyogālliṭ kit* (Pāṇini 1.2.5), the suffix *liṭ* is treated as *kit*, resulting in the absence of *guṇa*: *mumude* (he rejoiced). In the benedictive, *amodiṣīṣṭa* (may he not rejoice); in the imperfect, *amodiṣṭa* (he did not rejoice); in the periphrastic perfect, *amūmudat* (he caused [someone] to rejoice). In the future, *modiṣyate* (he will rejoice); in the conditional, *amodiṣyata* (he would have rejoiced).

And so forth. According to Pāṇini’s sūtras 1.2.26 (*saniralo vyupadhāddhalādeḥ saṃśca*) and 1.2.18 (*na ktvā seṭ*), the suffixes *san* and *ktvā* are optionally *kit* after a root that begins with a consonant, has *i* or *u* as its penultimate vowel (*vyupadhāt*), and ends in a consonant (*ralantāt*). Thus, from the roots *mud* (with *i* as the penultimate vowel) and *mud* (with *u* as the penultimate vowel), both *san* and *ktvā* followed by *iṭ* are optionally *kit*. Consequently, one forms *mumudiṣate* and *mumodiṣate*. Furthermore, according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.82 (*yaṅi guṇo yaṅlukoḥ*), there is *guṇa* substitution for the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) in the *yaṅ* formation and its elision (*yaṅluk*); thus, one forms *momudyate*.

The root *ṣūd* is used in the senses of flowing and harming. By the rule *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.64), the *ṣ* at the beginning of the root becomes *s*, resulting in *sūdate*. From this, forms such as *asūdata* and so forth are derived. In the *liṭ* (perfect tense), by the rule *iṇkoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.57), the *ṣ* is restored, yielding *suṣūde*. In the *āśīrliṅ* (precative), one has *asūdiṣṭa*. In the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist) of the causative (*ṇic*), there is shortening of the penultimate vowel; then, by the rule *dīrgho laghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.94), the reduplication is lengthened, resulting in *asūṣudat*.

The root *hrādī* means "to sound indistinctly" (*avyakte śabde*) and "to rejoice" (*sukhe*). The long vowel *ī* is for the purpose of prohibiting the augment *iṭ* by the rule *śvīdito niṣṭhāyām* (Pāṇini 7.2.14). [Forms: *hlādate*, *ahlādata*, *hlādatām*, *hlādeta*, *hlādiṣīṣṭa*, *jahlāde*, *ahlādiṣṭa*, *ajihlādat*.
The root *svāda* means "to taste" (*āsvādane*). Forms such as *āsvādata*, *asvādata*, etc., are like the previous ones.
The root *parḍa* means "to utter a contemptible sound. In the *caṅ* (reduplication) formation, [the form is] *apapardat*; elsewhere, it is like *hrādī*.

The root *yat* (yatī) means "to strive. Present: *yatate* Imperfect: *ayayata* Imperative: *yatatām* Optative: *yateta* Benedictive: *yatiṣīṣṭa* Perfect (*liṭ*): *yete* Aorist (*luṅ*): *ayatiṣṭa*, and so forth. The roots *vithṛ* and *vedhṛ* mean "to entreat. There is a difference in form between *vidhati* and *vedhati* when followed by a *kit* suffix. Present: *vethate* Imperfect: *avethata*, and so forth. Benedictive: *vethiṣīṣṭa*. The root *ślatha* means "to loosen" or "slackness. Present: *ślathate* Imperfect: *aślathata* Imperative: *ślathatām*, and so forth.

*Grath* (grantha) in the sense of twisting or stringing: *grathate*, *agrathata*, *grathatām*, *grathet*. In the benedictive: *grathiṣīṣṭa*. Perfect: *jagrathe*. Aorist: *agrathiṣṭa*. With the causative suffix *ṇic* and the *caṅ* reduplication: *ajagrathata*; but for *graṃth*, it is *ajagranthat*. The remainder is like *grath*.

*Kattha* in the sense of boasting: *katthate*, *akatthata*. With the causative suffix *ṇic* and the *caṅ* reduplication: *acakatthata*. The roots beginning with *bhū* are *seṭ* (having an indicatory *i*). Those beginning with *edh* are *ātmanebhāṣā* (middle-voiced) and *anudāttet* (having an anudātta accent on their initial vowel).

From the root *at* in the sense of continuous motion: *atati*, *ātata*, *atatu*, *atet*, *atyāt*. In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, by the rule *ata ādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.70), there is lengthening of the reduplication: *āta*, *ātatuḥ*. In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, by the rule *āḍajādīnām* (Pāṇini 6.4.72), the augment *āṭ* is added; then by *āṭaśca* (Pāṇini 6.1.90), there is *vṛddhi* [vowel strengthening], and the augment *iṭ* is applied. For the *sic* suffix, the augment *iṭ* is added and the *sic* of the single-consonant (*apṛkta*) suffix is elided: *ātīt*, *ātiṣṭām*. By the rule *sijabhyastavidibhyaśca* (Pāṇini 3.4.109), [the *jherjus* substitution occurs]: *ātiṣuḥ*.

The root *cit* is used in the sense of "perceiving. The *guṇa* substitution applies because the penultimate vowel is light. [Present tense: *cetati*, *cetataḥ*, *cetanti*. [Benedictive (āśīrliṅ): *cityāt*. [Perfect (liṭ): *ciceta*. Because of the rule *asaṃyogālliṭ kit* (Pāṇini 1.2.5), which states that the *liṭ* affixes following a root ending in a non-conjunct consonant are *kit*, there is an absence of *guṇa*. Thus: *cicitatuḥ*, *cicituḥ*. [Aorist (luṅ): By the rules *vadavraja-halantasyācaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.3) and *sicivṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.1), a *vṛddhi* substitution occurs in place of the vowel (*ac*) of the stems *vad*, *vraj*, and those ending in a consonant (*halanta*), when followed by the *sic* augment and a *parasmaipada* personal ending. Thus, [the forms are derived accordingly].

Thus, when the occasion for *vṛddhi* has arisen, there is a prohibition by the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4), which states that when a *parasmaipada* suffix beginning with *iṭ* follows *sic*, no *vṛddhi* occurs for the vowel of a stem ending in a consonant. As before, the operations beginning with *iṭ* apply: *acetīt*, *acetiṣṭām*, and so forth. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), there is an option for the *kit* designation by the rule *sani ralo vyupadhāt* (Pāṇini 1.2.26): *cicitiṣati* or *cicetiṣati*.

The root *cyu* means "to flow. The designation *irit* is for the purpose of [triggering] the augment *iṭ* according to Pāṇini 3.1.57 (*irito vā*). In the present tense (*laṭ*), the suffix *śap* is applied, and the *guṇa* substitution occurs because the penultimate vowel is light: *cyotati*. The aorist (*luṅ*): *acyotat*. The imperative (*loṭ*): *cyotatu*, *cyotatāt*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *cyotyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *cucyota*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ* by Pāṇini 3.1.57: *aścyutat*, *aścotīt*, and so forth. In the desiderative (*san*), there is likewise an option as before: *cucyutiṣati*, *cucyotiṣati*. Some maintain that the form of the root *ścyut* meaning "to flow" is exactly the same.

The roots *kuthi*, *puthi*, *nuthi*, and *luthi* belong to the class meaning "injury" and "affliction. Because they are marked with the *it*-augment (*idit*), the nasal augment *num* is added [before the *śnā* suffix]. Thus: *manthati*, *amanthat*, and so forth. In this manner, examples for the remaining roots should be inferred. The root *ṣidhu* means "going. The letter *u* is for the purpose of specification, according to the rule *udito vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.56).

The root *ṣidhū* is used in the sense of "instruction" (*śāstra*) and "auspiciousness" (*māṅgalya*). The vowel *ū* is for the purpose of making the augment *iṭ* optional, according to Pāṇini’s rule *svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā* (Pāṇ. 7.2.44). Similarly, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs hereafter as well. Except when following a prefix (*upasarga*) or in the sense of motion (*gati*), the substitution of *ṣ* is prescribed by the rule *upasargātsunotyādīnām* (Pāṇ. 8.3.65); however, in the sense of motion, the rule *sedhatergatāv* (Pāṇ. 8.3.113) prohibits it. In the *laṅ* tense, the substitution of *ṣ* occurs even when there is an intervention by the augment *aṭ* placed before the suffix, according to the rule *prāksitādaḍvyavāye’pi* (Pāṇ. 8.3.63); the roots [intended] by the term "prior to *sit*" are those beginning with *ṣu*.

According to Pāṇini’s sūtras 8.3.65–70—namely, *upasargāt sunoti-suvati-syati-stauti-stobhati-sthā-senaya-se-dha-sica-sañja-svañjām*, 8.3.66 *sadir aprateḥ*, 8.3.67 *stanbheḥ*, 8.3.68 *avāc cālambanāvidūryayoḥ*, and 8.3.69 *veś ca śvano bhojane*—the forms ending with the root *sita* (from 8.3.70 *parinivibhyaḥ sevasita...*) are included. Thus: *nyaṣedhat*, *niṣedhatu*, *niṣedhet*, *niṣidhyāt*, *niṣedhitha*.

In the *liṅ* (optative) mood, there is an optional *iṭ* augment because the root is marked with *ū*. In the case where *iṭ* is present, as before, there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi*, and the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel occurs: *nyaṣedhīt*. Otherwise, there is *vṛddhi* of the *sic* suffix conditioned by a consonant ending [the root], and the change of *dh* to *t* (*cartva*) by Pāṇini 8.4.55, resulting in *nyaṣaitsīt*. By Pāṇini 8.2.26 (*jhalo jhali*), there is the elision of the *sic* suffix. For the third person plural, *tas* becomes *tām*: *nyaṣaiddhām*. By Pāṇini 3.4.109 (*sijabhyastavidibhyaśca*), *jhi* becomes *jus*: *nyaṣaisuḥ*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with *caṅ* (reduplication), it is *nyaṣīṣidhat*.

Because the roots *lṛ* and *luṭ* are marked with *ū*, there is an optional application of *iṭ*, which will be prohibited [by the following rules]: *niṣedhiṣyati* / *niṣetsyati*; *nyaṣedhiṣyata* / *nyaṣetsyat*; *niṣeddhā* / *niṣedhitā*. Regarding the suffix *san*: by the rule *ralovyupadhāt* (Pāṇini 1.2.26), there is an option for *kit* status; thus, in the case where *iṭ* is applied, there is both the presence and absence of *guṇa*. By the rule *stautiṇyoreva ṣaṇyabhyāsāt* (Pāṇini 8.3.61), when *san* follows a root ending in *stauti* or a causative (*ṇyanta*) root, and when the *ṣatva* (the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*) has occurred, the *ṣatva* of the *s* belonging to the substitute that follows the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) takes place. Since this is already established [by general rules], the formulation of this specific rule is for the purpose of restriction (*niyamārtha*).

The rule *ṇyoreva ṣaṇyabhyāsāt* (Pāṇini 8.3.61) is stated so that [the substitution] occurs only after the two roots *ṣi* and *dhā* when followed by the suffix *san*, and not after any other; for example: *sisidhiṣati* and *sisedhiṣati*. Regarding the rule *upasargāduttarasya sthādiṣvabhyāse ca* (Pāṇini 8.3.64), the phrase *prāksitāt* (Pāṇini 8.3.63) is understood to carry over. In the case of roots beginning with *sthā* and others, prior to the mention of *sit*, the cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) substitution occurs even when there is an intervention by the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), provided it follows a prefix (*upasarga*).

Furthermore, there is a substitution of the cerebral *ṣ* for the initial of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). According to the rule stating that the mention of "separation by the reduplicated syllable" (*vyavāya*) is for the sake of [the application of] *ṣopadeśa*, for the sake of [the application of] the reduplicated syllable ending in an *a*-vowel, or for the sake of prohibiting [the substitution] when *ṣaṅ* follows, the substitution of *ṣ* is prohibited: *niṣiṣedhiṣati*, *niṣiṣitsati*. In the absence of the augment *iṭ*, it is *niṣiṣitsati*; here, due to the *kit* designation according to Pāṇini 1.2.10 (*halantācca*), there is an absence of *guṇa*.

The root *mṛ* is used in the sense of "dying. In forms such as *marati* (he dies) and *amarat* (he died), when followed by the suffixes of the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), the *liṭ*, and the *luṅ* with *sic*, the substitution of *riṅ* occurs according to Pāṇini 7.4.28 (*riṅ śayagliṅkṣu*). Thus, [in the benedictive] we have *mriyāt*. In the *liṭ*, [the perfect tense], we have *mamāra*. In the *luṅ*, [the aorist], we have *amārṣīt*. In the *caṅ* (the reduplicated aorist), we have *amamarat*, and so forth. The root *khādṛ* is used in the sense of "eating. In forms such as *khādati* (he eats) and *akhādat* (he ate), when the *caṅ* follows the causative (*ṇic*), because the root is marked with the *ṛt* indicatory letter (*ṛdit*), the prohibition against shortening the penultimate vowel applies according to Pāṇini 7.4.2 (*nāglopiśāsvṛditām*). Due to the absence of the cause, the effect also does not occur; thus, [in the causative aorist] we have *acakhādat*. The roots *vad* and *khad* are used in the sense of "firmness" or "stability. [Examples include] *vadati* (he speaks) and *khadati* (he strikes/firmly holds), and so forth. They also function in the sense of "injury" or "harming."
The root *gad* is used in the sense of distinct speech;

*nad* is used in the sense of indistinct sound. Regarding forms such as *praṇigadati*, the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* occurs by the rule *upasargātparasya ner-gadanada-* (Pāṇini 8.4.17). In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, for roots beginning with *vad* and others, the rule *neṭ* prohibits the augment *iṭ* after *sic*. Consequently, when the vowel-lengthening (*vṛddhi*) conditioned by a root ending in a consonant is barred, the optional lengthening prescribed by *ato halāder-laghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.7) applies, resulting in forms such as *anadīt* or *anādīt*.
The root *rad* means "to scratch" or "to carve," and is treated in the same manner as the preceding ones.

The roots *nard* and *gard* mean "to injure. Examples include *nardati* (he roars/injures), *anardat* (he roared/injured), and so forth. The root *ardh* means "to go" and "to beg. In forms such as *ardhati*, the vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) is lengthened by Pāṇini 6.4.70 (*ata ādeḥ*), and the augment *nuṭ* is added by Pāṇini 7.4.71 (*tasmānnuḍ dvihalaḥ*). Thus, *ānardha* is the form [of the perfect tense]. Elsewhere, [the forms] are easily understood. The root *ardh* [also] means "to injure."
* tarda* means to injure.
* parda* means a contemptible sound.
* khardha* and * kardha* mean a contemptible sound; one *khardhati*. [The roots] *dantaśūka* and *dantasukha* are also included; the examples for these are to be inferred.

The root *ṇidi* is used in the sense of censure (*kutsā*). By *ṇo naḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.65), *ṇ* becomes *n*. Regarding the forms *praṇindati* and *pranindati*, there is an optional substitution of *ṇ* for *n* by the rule *upasargātparasya vā niṃsanikṣanindām* (Pāṇini 8.4.33). Because it is marked with the *it* indicatory letter, the augment *num* is added [in the present tense]. Thus: *praṇindati*, *pranindati*. [Imperfect: *anindata* [Imperative: *nindatu* [Optative: *nindet* [Benedictive: *nindyāt* [Perfect: *nininda* [Aorist: *anindata* [Periphrastic Perfect: *caṅi* (in the reduplicated aorist) *aninindat*, and so forth. The root *ati* (or *adi*) is used in the sense of binding (*bandhana*). The root *idi* is used in the sense of supreme sovereignty (*paramaiśvarya*).
*ṭunadi* means to prosper;
*cadi* means to rejoice and to shine.
The root *trad* is used in the sense of movement;
*krad*, *klad*, and *klad* are used in the senses of calling out and weeping; *klid* is used in the sense of lamentation. For these roots, the [grammatical operations] are as previously described.

The root *śundh* means "to purify. It forms *śundhati*, *aśundhat*, and so forth. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), there is elision of the nasal according to Pāṇini 6.4.24, resulting in *śudhyāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), it is *śuśundha*; in the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *aśundhīt*; and with the causative suffix *ṇic* followed by the reduplicated aorist (*caṅ*), it is *aśuśundhat*. The future form is *śundhiṣyati*, and so on. Among the roots beginning with *āt*, *mṛ* ("to die") is one that lacks the augment *iṭ* (*aniṭ*). There is an option regarding the *iṭ* augment for the root *sedh*; the others are *seṭ* (with *iṭ*) and are conjugated in the Parasmaipada.

The root *sīkṛ* means "to sprinkle. [Present tense: *sekate*; [imperfect: *asekata*, and so forth. In the *caṅ* (reduplication) of the causative (*ṇau*), [the form is] *asisekat*. Due to the presence of the marker *ṛt*, there is no shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasva*). This should be understood similarly in subsequent cases as well. The root *lokṛ* means "to see. [Present tense: *vilokate*; [imperfect: *vyalokata*; [imperative: *vilokatām*; [optative: *viloketa*. In the benedictive (*āśiṣi*), [the form is] *vilokiṣīṣṭa*. [Perfect: *viluloke*; [aorist: *vyalokiṣṭa*. In the *caṅ* [of the causative], [the forms are] *vyalulokata*, *vilokiṣyata*, and so forth. The root *ślokṛ* means "to collect" or "to assemble."
*drekṛ* and *dhrekṛ* mean "to utter a sound with enthusiasm"; *rekṛ* means "to fear";
*śrekṛ* and *srekṛ* mean "to go," as before.

The root *śaki* is used in the sense of "doubt. Because it is marked with the *it*-augment, the nasal augment *num* is applied: *śaṅkate*, *aśaṅkata*, *śaṅkitā*, *śaṅketa*. In the benedictive: *śaṅkiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect: *śaśaṅke*. In the aorist with the causative suffix *ṇic* followed by *caṅ*: *aśaśaṅkat*. [In the future: *śaṅkiṣyate*, and so forth. The roots *aki* and *vaki* mean "marking"; *vaki* means "crookedness."
*maṅk* in the sense of adorning; *kak* in the sense of longing; as before;
*kuk* and *vṛk* in the sense of seizing.
The roots *caka* and *sraka* mean satisfaction and striking back, respectively; their examples are to be inferred.

The roots *ḍhaukṛ*, *traukṛ*, *kaki*, *śvaki*, *traki*, *ṣvaṣka*, *maska*, *ṭikṛ*, *ṭīkṛ*, *raṅghi*, and *laṅghi* have the sense of motion. One should apply them as follows: *ḍhaukate*, *traukate*, *ṭīkate*, *ṣvakkate*, *vaskate*, *ṭīkate*, *raṅghate*, and *laṅghate*. In the case of the causative with *caṅ* (the reduplicated aorist), one forms *aḍuḍhaukat*, *atutraukat*, and so on. Regarding *ṣvakkate*, because of the rule "a prohibition must be stated for the sibilant of roots beginning with *asub*, *ṣṭhivu*, and *ṣvak*," there is no change of the initial *ṣ* to *s*. [Examples: *raṅghate*, *araṅghata*.

*laghi* is used in the sense of eating little and abstaining from food; *ślāghṛ* is used in the sense of praising or boasting. [Conjugations: *ślāghate* (present indicative) *aślāghata* (imperfect) *ślāghatām* (imperative) *ślāgheta* (optative) *ślāghiṣīṣṭa* (precative) *śaślāghe* (periphrastic perfect) *aślāghiṣṭa* (aorist), and so forth. The roots beginning with *sikṛ* are *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*) and are *ātmanebhāṣā* (middle-voice).
*Phakk* means "to go downwards"; *tak* means "to laugh";
*taki* means "to live with difficulty."
*Śuk* means "to go";
*bukka* means "to speak";
*kakkha* means "to laugh."
*rikha* means "to go. Examples such as *phakkati* should be cited accordingly. *tvagi* means "to tremble": *tvaṅgati*, *atvaṅgat*, *tvaṅgatu*, *tvegeta*, *tvaṅgyāt*, and so forth.
*yugi*, *jugi*, and *bugi* mean "to avoid" or "to exclude."
*dagh* in the sense of protecting; *lagh* in the sense of drying up;
*kakha* in the sense of laughing.
These [roots] ending in -seṭ are spoken of as parasmaipada.

The root *varc* means "to shine" (*dīptau*). It is conjugated as follows: *varcate*, *avarcata*, *varcatām*, *varceta*, and so forth. The root *locṛ* means "to see"; it is treated like *lokṛ* in the sense of seeing. The root *kaca* means "to bind."
*kañci* in the sense of binding and illuminating;
*maci* in the sense of holding, raising, and filling;
*paci* in the sense of making manifest. Because it is marked with *idit*, the augment *num* is added.

The root *ej* means "to tremble. Present: *ejate* Imperfect: *aijata* Imperative: *ejatām* Optative: *ejeta* Benedictive: *ejiṣīṣṭa* In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, by the rule *ijādeśca gurumato'nṛcchaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.36), we have *ejāñcakre*, and so forth. Aorist: *aijiṣṭa*. There is no shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasva*). There is reduplication (*dvirukti*), and then *āṭ*-vṛddhi, resulting in *aijijat*.

The roots *ejṛ*, *rejṛ*, and *bhājṛ* signify shining (*dīptau*). *Rejate*: present; *arejata*: imperfect; *rejatām*: imperative; *rejeta*: optative; *rejiṣīṣṭa*: precative; *ririje*: perfect; *arejiṣṭa*: aorist. In the causative (*ṇau*) with the suffix *caṅ* (reduplication), the form is *arirejat*, and so forth. Regarding the root *bhrāj* in the causative with *caṅ*, there is an optional shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasva-vikalpa*) according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.3: *bhrājabhāsabhāṣadīpajīvamīlapīḍāmanyatarasyām*. Thus, we have *abibhrajat* or *ababhrājat*. For this very reason, some say that the marking of *bhrāj* and *bhās* as having an *ṛt* augment (*ṛdit*) is un-Pāṇinian; for we see no purpose for the *ṛt*-marking other than the prohibition of the penultimate vowel-shortening prescribed by the grammar (*śāstra*). These roots are *seṭ* (taking the *iṭ* augment) and are *ātmanebhāṣā* (middle-voiced).

The root *śuc* is used in the senses of "grief" and "purification. *śocati* (he grieves), *aśocat* (he grieved), *śocatu* (let him grieve), *śocet* (he might grieve). *Śucyāt* (may he purify): here, by the rule *śuśoca neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4), the prohibition of *vṛddhi* applies. *aśocīt* (he grieved), *aśūśucat* (he grieved repeatedly). *Śociṣyati* (he will grieve), *aśociṣyat* (he would have grieved), *śocitā* (he will have grieved). Regarding the desiderative (*san*), by the rule *sani ralo vyupadhāt* (Pāṇini 1.2.26), there is an option for the suffix to be *kit*. Thus: *śuśuciṣati* (he wishes to grieve) or *śuśociṣati* (he wishes to grieve). In the intensive (*yaṅ*), it becomes *śośucyate*. The root *kuc* is used in the sense of "loud sound," following the same pattern as before.

The root *kuñc* is used in the senses of "crookedness of movement" (*gatikauṭilya*) and "becoming small" (*alpa-bhāva*). According to Pāṇini 7.2.56, *ukāra udito vā*, the suffix *iṭ* is optional; this applies similarly in subsequent forms as well. In the *āśis* (benedictive) mood, by Pāṇini 6.4.24 (*aniditām...*), there is elision of the nasal (*n*): *kucyāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), it is *cukuñca*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *akuñcīt*. In the causative (*ṇau*) with the reduplication suffix (*caṅ*), it is *acukuñcata*. The root *luñc* means "to remove" (*apanayana*). The forms beginning with *luñcati* follow accordingly.

The root *añc* is used in the senses of "going" and "honoring. From *prāñcati* and *prāñcat*, and so forth: in the sense of "going," there is elision of the nasal (*n*) according to *aniditām...* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), resulting in *prācyāt*; however, in the sense of "honoring," there is a prohibition according to *nāñceḥ pūjāyām* (Pāṇini 6.4.30), resulting in *gurumañcyāt*.

In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, there is lengthening of the initial vowel of the reduplicated syllable according to Pāṇini 7.4.70 (*abhyāsasya ata ādeḥ*). Then, according to Pāṇini 7.4.71 (*tasmānnuḍdvihalaḥ*), the augment *nuṭ* is added after that reduplicated syllable—provided it has been lengthened by 7.4.70—if the stem following it consists of two consonants (*dvihala*). Thus, *nuṭ* is applied. Furthermore, the suffix *ānaC* is used in the *luṅ* [aorist] tense; for example, *prāñcīt*. Due to the rules for *anusvāra* and *parasavarṇa*, we have *prāñciṣṭām* and *prāñciṣuḥ*.

In the case of the *ṇau* (causal suffix) with *caṅ* (the reduplication marker), there is reduplication of the second syllable, but the *na* of the second word does not undergo doubling because of the prohibition "not *n*, *d*, or *r* when they are the first members of a conjunct" (*na ndrāḥ saṃyogādayaḥ*, Pāṇini 6.1.3). Thus, one forms *prāñcicat*; *prāñciṣyatīti* and so forth should be applied accordingly.
The roots *vaṃcu*, *caṃcu*, *taṃcu*, *tvaṃcu*, *graṃcu*, *glaṃcu*, *sraṃcu*, *ślaṃcu*, *mrucu*, and *mlucu* have the sense of "going.
The root *glucu* has the sense of "stealing."

The root *gluñcu* means "to go. Present: *nimrecati*, *nyamrocat*, *nimrocatu*, *nimrocet*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *nirmucyāt*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *animrucat* or *amrocīt*. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.1.58, *jṝ stambhu mrucu mlucu grucu glucu gluñcu śvi*—the substitute *aṅ* optionally occurs after these roots, including *jṝ* and the others; because *aṅ* is marked with *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa* strengthening. In the causative with *caṅ*: *amumrucat*. Future: *mrociṣyati*, etc. In the desiderative (*san*), as before, there is an option regarding *kit* status: *nimumruciṣati* or *nimumrociṣati*.

For *mlucu* and *glucu*, everything is as before. For *gluñc*, however: [present] *gluñcati*; [imperfect] *agluñcat*; [imperative] *gluñcatu*; [optative] *gluñcet*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), there is elision of *n*: *glucyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *jugluñca*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), with *cl* replaced by *aṅ* and elision of *n*: *aglucat*; [with *sic*] *agluñcīt*. In the causative with *caṅ* (reduplication), *ajugluñcat*. [Future] *gluñciṣyati*, etc. In the desiderative (*san*), *jugluñciṣati*, etc.

In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, there is the augment *nīg* by the rule *vañcu-sraṃsu-dhvaṃsu-bhraṃsu-ka-sapa-tapa-pada-skandām* (Pāṇini 7.4.84), and the elision of the nasal by the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24). Thus: *vanīvacyate*. In the present tense (*laṭ*): *vañcati*; in the imperfect (*laṅ*): *avañcat*; in the imperative (*loṭ*): *vañcatu*; in the optative (*liṅ*): *vañcet*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is the elision of the nasal: *vacyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *vavañca*; in the aorist (*luṅ*): *avañcīt*; in the imperfect: *avañcat*; in the future (*lṛṭ*): *vañciṣyati*, and so forth. In the same manner, examples for the other [roots] should be cited. The roots *kuji* and *guji* mean "inarticulate sound": *kujjati*, *gujjati*, and so forth.

The root *arca* is used in the sense of worship. It forms *arcati* (he worships), *ārcat* (he worshipped). In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, there is lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; by the rule *tasmānnuḍ dvihalaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.71), the augment *nuṭ* is added: *ānarca*, *ānarcatuḥ*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, it forms *ārcīt*. When the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied and the *caṅ* (reduplication) follows, there is reduplication of the second syllable containing the vowel *ci*, not of the letter *r*; this is because of the prohibition stated in *nandrāḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.3): *ārcicat*. The root *mleccha* is used in the sense of indistinct speech; it forms *mlecchati*, and so forth. The roots *lacchi* and *lāchi* mean "marking" (*lakṣaṇe*); with the augment *num*, they form *lāñchati*, and so forth.
*Vāñch* is used in the sense of desire; *vāñchati*.
*Hrīcch* is used in the sense of shame; *hrīcchati*, and so forth.
*Hūrch* is used in the sense of crookedness; *hūrcchati*.

The root *mūrch* is used in the senses of fainting (*moha*) and increasing (*samucchrāya*). By the rule *ākāra āditaśca* (Pāṇini 7.2.16), the augment *iṭ* is prohibited in the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*); thus, [the form] is *mūrchita*. The root *kūj* is used in the sense of an indistinct sound; [it forms] *kūjati*.
The roots *arj* and *sarj* are used in the sense of acquisition (*arjana*); [they form] *arjati*. [In the imperfect: *ārjat*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *ānarja*, *ānarjatuḥ*, *ānarjuḥ*.

*garj* means "to roar"; *garjati*, *agarjat*. *tarj* means "to threaten"; *atatarjat*. *aja* means "to go" and "to throw"; *ajati*, *ājat*, *ajatu*, *ajet*. Regarding the benedictive (*liṅ*), because it is treated as an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix by the rule *āśiṣi liṅāśiṣi* (Pāṇini 3.4.116), the substitution of *vi* for the root *aja*—which means "to go" and "to throw"—occurs before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, except when *ghañ* or *ap* follows, according to the rule *ajervyaghañapoḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.56). Furthermore, by the rule *akṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.25), there is lengthening of a stem ending in *a* before an *akṛt* suffix containing *ya* or an *asārvadhātuka* suffix containing *ya*. Thus: *vīyāt*, *vīyāstām*.

*vīyāsuḥ*. In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, because it is an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix, there is the substitution of *vī* [for the root *vyā*]. In *vivāya*, there is the *yaṇ* replacement according to Pāṇini 6.4.82 (*eranekāco’saṃyogapūrvasya*). [In the dual and plural: *vivyatuḥ*, *vivyuḥ*. Regarding the form with the *sip* suffix and the *thal* suffix: by the rule *kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.13), when the *liṭ* follows, an *iṭ* augment does not occur for the roots beginning with *kṛ*. Why is this stated, since [these roots are already listed as] *ḍukṛñ* in the sense of making, *sṛ* in the sense of moving, *ḍubhṛñ* in the sense of supporting, *vṛñ* in the sense of choosing, *ṣṭuñ* in the sense of praising, *dru* in the sense of moving? [The answer is: It is for the sake of excluding the *iṭ* augment in other tenses where the *liṭ* does not follow. Otherwise, the *iṭ* would apply even in the *luṅ* (aorist) and *lṛṅ* (conditional) due to the rule *krādibhyaḥ sārvadhātuke* (Pāṇini 7.2.13). To prevent this, the restriction "only when *liṭ* follows" is necessary. Thus, forms such as *akārṣīt* (aorist) and *kariṣyati* (future) do not take the *iṭ* augment. Furthermore, the mention of *vṛ* here is for the purpose of including the root *vṛ* (to choose) which belongs to the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *vṛ* mentioned in the rule *vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38) refers to the root *vṛ* (to cover) belonging to the *adādi* class. The mention of *stu* is for the purpose of including the root *stu* (to praise) from the *tudādi* class, whereas the *stu* mentioned in the rule *stusudhūñbhyaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.72) refers to the root *stu* (to praise) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *dru* is for the purpose of including the root *dru* (to run) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *dru* mentioned in the rule *dravamūrtisparśayoḥ śyaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29) refers to the root *dru* (to run) from the *divādi* class. The mention of *sru* is for the purpose of including the root *sru* (to flow) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *sru* mentioned in the rule *sruvaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.36) refers to the root *sru* (to flow) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *śru* is for the purpose of including the root *śru* (to hear) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *śru* mentioned in the rule *śruvaḥ śṛ ca* (Pāṇini 3.1.74) refers to the root *śru* (to hear) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *kṛ* is for the purpose of including the root *kṛ* (to make) from the *tanādi* class, whereas the *kṛ* mentioned in the rule *kṛño dvitīyatṛtīyaśambabījāt kṛṣau* (Pāṇini 5.4.58) refers to the root *kṛ* (to make) from the *tanādi* class. The mention of *bhṛ* is for the purpose of including the root *bhṛ* (to support) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *bhṛ* mentioned in the rule *bhṛño’saṃjñāyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.112) refers to the root *bhṛ* (to support) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *vṛ* is for the purpose of including the root *vṛ* (to choose) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *vṛ* mentioned in the rule *vṛṅśca* (Pāṇini 3.1.90) refers to the root *vṛ* (to choose) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *stu* is for the purpose of including the root *stu* (to praise) from the *tudādi* class, whereas the *stu* mentioned in the rule *stusudhūñbhyaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.72) refers to the root *stu* (to praise) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *sru* is for the purpose of including the root *sru* (to flow) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *sru* mentioned in the rule *sruvaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.36) refers to the root *sru* (to flow) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *śru* is for the purpose of including the root *śru* (to hear) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *śru* mentioned in the rule *śruvaḥ śṛ ca* (Pāṇini 3.1.74) refers to the root *śru* (to hear) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *kṛ* is for the purpose of including the root *kṛ* (to make) from the *tanādi* class, whereas the *kṛ* mentioned in the rule *kṛño dvitīyatṛtīyaśambabījāt kṛṣau* (Pāṇini 5.4.58) refers to the root *kṛ* (to make) from the *tanādi* class. The mention of *bhṛ* is for the purpose of including the root *bhṛ* (to support) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *bhṛ* mentioned in the rule *bhṛño’saṃjñāyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.112) refers to the root *bhṛ* (to support) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *vṛ* is for the purpose of including the root *vṛ* (to choose) from the *juhoty-ādi* class, whereas the *vṛ* mentioned in the rule *vṛṅśca* (Pāṇini 3.1.90) refers to the root *vṛ* (to choose) from the *adādi* class. The mention of *stu* is for the purpose of including the root *stu* (to praise) from the *tudādi* class, whereas the *stu* mentioned in the rule *stusudhūñbhyaḥ parasmaip

Regarding the roots *śru* (in the sense of hearing) and *sru* (in the sense of moving), there exists a prohibition based on the root itself by virtue of Pāṇini’s rule 7.2.10 (*ekāca upadeśe'nudāttāt*), which applies generally to the augment *iṭ* characterized as beginning with *vāl*.
[The root] *vṛṅ* (in the sense of choosing).

The root *vṛñ* means "to choose. For these two roots (*vṛ* and *vṛñ*) as well, there is a prohibition based on the suffix [beginning with *k*] by the rule *śryukaḥ kiti*. Since these two are *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment), this [prohibition] is already established; therefore, the present formulation is for the sake of a restrictive rule (*niyamārtha*). The restriction is: "Only the roots beginning with *kṛ* are *aniṭ* (without *iṭ*) in the *liṭ* [perfect]; others are *seṭ* in the *liṭ*. Thus, when *iṭ* would have been required, the following applies: *acastāsvatthalyaniṭo nityam* (Pāṇini 7.2.61). This means: for a root ending in a vowel (*ajanta*) which is invariably *aniṭ* in the *tās* [future], the *iṭ* augment does not occur in the *thal* [perfect suffix] just as it does not in the *tās*. Since a permanent prohibition of *iṭ* would thus apply in the case of *thal*, the next rule follows: *ṛto bhāradvājasya*.

(Pāṇini Sūtra 7.2.63) Regarding the suffix *thal*: according to the opinion of the teacher Bhāradvāja, the augment *iṭ* does not occur after a root ending in ṛ, whereas for other roots ending in vowels (*ajanta*), the augment *iṭ* does occur. According to the opinion of Bhāradvāja, for those other teachers, the augment *iṭ* after roots ending in vowels that are invariably non-*iṭ* (except for those ending in ṛ) is declared to be optional. However, for roots beginning with *kṛ* (the *krādi* group), there is always an absolute prohibition of *iṭ* in the *liṭ* (perfect tense). A summary verse states: "In establishing the rule for the *krādi* group, the quality of having *iṭ* (*seṭ*) is not [applied] to those [roots] ending in *u*."
Furthermore, for roots ending in *ṛ* that are invariably aniṭ, the affix *tās* is brought forward by those who know the rules of word-formation and grammatical augmentations.

In that case, [the augment] is optional. By the rule *atvatām* (Pāṇini 7.2.61), the scope of *upadeśe 'tvataḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.62) is indicated. Therefore, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*: *vivetha*, *vivayitha*. This principle should be remembered everywhere in the domain of the *thal* suffix where *iṭ* is optional. In the *luṅ* [aorist], with the *sic* suffix, there is *vṛddhi*: *avaiṣīt*, *avaiṣṭām*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the *caṅ* [reduplication], *avīvayat*. In the *lṛṭ* [future] and *luṭ* [periphrastic future], *veṣyati*, *aveṣyat*. The periphrastic future (*tācchīlye ṇini*) is *vetā*. The desiderative is *vivīṣati*. The intensive is *vevīyate*. Likewise, in the sense of the impersonal (*bhāva*) and passive (*karman*), by Pāṇini 1.3.13: *vīyate*, *avīyata*.

Let it be performed; let it be performed. In the benedictive (āśīrliṅ), there is an optional insertion of the *iṭ* augment as in the *ciṇvadiṭ* case: *veṣīṣṭa* or *vāyiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the form is] *vivye*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *avāyi* or *aveṣātām*. In the future (*lṛt*) and periphrastic future (*luṭ*), *veṣyate* or *aveṣyata*, *vāyiṣyate*. [In the conditional,] *aveṣyata* or *avāyiṣyata*. [The futures are] *vetā* or *vāyitā*. In this same manner, for roots ending in *i*, the formation of forms follows the same pattern when the *ciṇvadiṭ* applies hereafter. The root *khaj* means "to limp" or "to have impaired movement. [Forms such as] *khañjati* and so forth. The root *ejṛ* means "to tremble. [Present: *ejati*. [Imperfect: *aejat*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the form is] *ejāñcakāra*.

*ṭuosphūrjā* (DhP 9.13) means "the thundering of a vajra. The sound *ṭu-* is for the purpose of [forming] the suffix *-athuc* according to *ṭvito'thuc* (Pāṇini 3.3.89). The vowel *o-* is for the purpose of nasalization (*niṣṭhānatva*) by the rule *oditaśca* (Pāṇini 8.2.45). [The root] *sphūrj* [is conjugated as]: *sphūrjati*, *asphūrjat*. *Kṣi* (DhP 9.14) means "to perish. [Present: *kṣayati*; [Aorist: *akṣayat*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is lengthening by the rule *akṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.25): *kṣīyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *cikṣāya*; *cikṣayitha* or *cikṣetha*. [Aorist: *akṣaiṣīt*.
In the desiderative (*san*), *cikṣīṣati*; here there is lengthening by the rule *ajjhanagamāṃ sani* (Pāṇini 6.4.16). *Yuṣa* (DhP 9.15) means "to love. [Present: *yoṣati*; [Aorist: *ayoṣat*.

*Jaja* and *jaji* mean "to fight. From *jajati*, etc., we derive *jañjati*, etc. *Tuja* and *tuji* mean "to injure": *tojati*, *tuñjati*. *Vaja* and *vraja* mean "to go": *vajati*, *avajad*, etc.; *vrajati*, *avrajat*. [Imperative: *vrajatu*; [Optative: *vrajet*; [Precative: *vrajyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), *vavrāja*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), when the *vṛddhi* substitution is indicated by the rule for roots ending in consonants (*halanta-lakṣaṇā*), there arises the possibility of the optional prohibition [of *vṛddhi*] by the rule *ato halāder laghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.7), which would result in a constant prohibition. However, because of the application of the rule *vadavraja-* (Pāṇini 7.2.3), the *vṛddhi* occurs [only optionally], resulting in *avrājīt*. [Future: *vrajiṣyati*, etc.
The roots beginning with *aṭṭ* are *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment) and are spoken of as *parasmaipada*.

*aṭṭ* (in the sense of transgression and injury): Present: *aṭṭate* Imperfect: *āṭṭata* Imperative: *aṭṭatām* Optative: *aṭṭeta* Precative: *aṭṭiṣīṣṭa* Periphrastic Perfect (*liṭ*): *ānaṭṭe* Aorist (*luṅ*): *āṭṭiṣṭa* *veṣṭ* (in the sense of encircling): Present: *veṣṭate* Imperfect: *aveṣṭata* Imperative: *veṣṭatām* Optative: *veṣṭeta* Precative: *veṣṭiṣīṣṭa* Periphrastic Perfect (*liṭ*): *viveṣṭe* Aorist (*luṅ*): *aveṣṭiṣṭa* Regarding the Aorist with the causative suffix (*ṇic*) and the *caṅ* reduplication, by the rule *vibhāṣā veṣṭiceṣṭyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.96), there is optionally the substitution of *a* for the reduplicated syllable; thus: *avaveṣṭat*.

*Ceṣṭ* is used in the sense of "moving" (*ceṣṭāyām*). *Ceṣṭate*, etc., are formed as before. *Ghaṭṭ* means "to move. *Ghaṭṭate*, *aghaṭṭata*, *ghaṭṭatām*, *ghaṭeta*. [These] are *seṭ* roots and belong to the *ātmanepada*.

The root *aṭ* (meaning "to go") is conjugated as follows: present—*aṭati*; imperfect—*āṭat*; imperative—*aṭatu*; potential—*aṭeta*; benedictive—*aṭyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *āṭa*, *āṭatuḥ*; in the aorist (*luṅ*), *āṭīt*. In the causative with *caṅ*, *āṭiṭat*. In the future, *aṭiṣyati*, and so forth; in the desiderative (*san*), *aṭiṭiṣati*. Regarding the intensive (*yaṅ*), according to the supplementary rule (*upasaṃkhyāna*) stating that *sūci*, *sūtri*, *mūtri*, *agha*, *arti*, and *śūrṇoti* are included, there is reduplication of the syllable *ya* (the *yaṅ* suffix), and after performing the operations on the reduplicated stem, we have *aṭāṭyate*. Similarly for *paṭ*: present—*paṭate*, *paṭati*; imperfect—*apaṭat*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *ato halāderlaghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.7), the vowel substitution is optionally long, resulting in *apāṭīt* or *apaṭīt*.
The rest is easily understood. The roots *vaṭ* (in the sense of "encircling"), *jaṭa*, and *juṭa* (in the sense of "heaping together") follow the same pattern.
*bhaṭa* means "to hire";
*taṭa* means "height" or "elevation";
*naṭa* means "to dance."
*Saṭa* means "to break" or "to divide.
*Iṭa*, *kiṭa*, and *kaṭī* mean "to go"; examples of these should be inferred.
*Ruṭi* and *luṭi* mean "the act of stealing"; [examples include] *ruṇṭati*, *luṇṭati*, and so forth.

The root *paṭh* is used in the sense of distinct speech; *paṭhati*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, there is an optional prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule *ato halāder laghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.7), resulting in *apaṭhīt* or *apāṭhīt*.
The roots *vaṭh* and *maṭh* mean dwelling; they follow the same pattern as the preceding.
The root *raṭh* means speaking around; it follows the same pattern as the preceding.
*ruṭh* and *luṭh* mean "to cause pain": *uparoṭhati*, *loṭhati*. *śaṭh* means "deceit";
*śuṭhi* means "drying. The application of the augment *num* and other such operations should be inferred accordingly.

In what manner does one play? One plays (*krīḍati*). With the prefix *anu*, *pari*, or *ā*—but not with *kūj*—and with *sam* preceded by *anu*, *sam*, or *pari* (Pāṇini 1.3.21), the *ātmanepada* is used: *anukrīḍate*, *parikrīḍate*, *ākrīḍate*, *saṃkrīḍate* [the boy]. In the *laṅ* tense: *samakrīḍata*. [Optative: *saṃkrīḍetām*, *saṃkrīḍeta*. [Precative: *saṃkrīḍiṣīṣṭa*. [Perfect: *sañcakrīḍe*, *samakrīḍiṣṭa*, and so forth.
The root *gaḍi* means "to swell" or "to become prominent in a part of the face. [Present: *gaṇḍati*. These roots ending in *iṭ* are *parasmaipadī*.

The root *ṭuvepṛ* means "to tremble. *vepate*, *avepata*, *vepatām*, *vepeta*, *vepiṣīṣṭa*, *vivepe*, *avepiṣṭa*. In the *caṅ* (reduplication) formation, *avivepat*; there is no shortening because of the *ṛdit* designation. *vepiṣyate*, etc.
*ṣevṛ*, *kevṛ*, and *gevṛ* mean "to serve," and so forth.

The root *trap* is used in the sense of shame (*lajjā*). The letter *ṣ* is for the purpose of [triggering] the suffix *aṅ* by the rule *ṣidbhidādibhyo’ṅ* (Pāṇini 3.3.104). Present: *trapate*; Aorist: *atrapata*; Imperative: *trapatām*; Optative: *trapeta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ* due to the marker *ū* [in *ūdit*]; thus, *trapiṣīṣṭa* or *trapsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *tṛphalabhajatrapaśca* (Pāṇini 6.4.122), there is *etva* (substitution of *e*) and elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsalopa*); thus, *trepe*, *trepāte*, etc. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *atrapta* or *atrapiṣṭa*. In the causative with the suffix *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist), *atitrapat*. In the first and second futures (*lṛluṭ*), *trapsyate* or *trapiṣyate*, and so forth. In the desiderative (*san*), *titrapsyate* or *titrapiṣate*.

The root *kapi* means "to tremble. Present: *kampate* Imperfect: *akampata* Optative: *kampetām* Precative: *kampiṣīṣṭa* Periphrastic Perfect: *cakampe* Aorist: *akampiṣṭa* Conditional: *acakampat* Future: *kampiṣyata*, and so forth. The roots *ravi* and *labi* mean "to hang down" (*avasraṃsana*). [The augment] *num* is added. Present: *raṃvate*, *lambate* Imperfect: *alambata*, and so forth. The root *klībṛ* means "lack of courage" (*adhārṣṭya*). Present: *klībate* Imperfect: *aklībata* Optative: *klībeta* Precative: *klībatām* Precative (passive): *klībiṣīṣṭa* Periphrastic Perfect: *ciklībe* Aorist: *aklībiṣṭa* In the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist), it is *aciklibata*.
The root *kṣībṛ* means "to become intoxicated"; *kṣībate*, etc., as before.
*Cībhṛ* and *śībhṛ* mean "to prattle.
*Rebhṛ* means "to sound"; *rebhate*, *arebhata*.

The roots *ṣṭabhi* and *stabhi* mean "to obstruct. The addition of *num* and so forth is as before, and the root takes the augment *satva*. Thus: *stambhate*, *astambhata*. The roots *jabha* and *jṛbhi* mean "to yawn" (*gātravināma*). By the rule *radhijabhor aci* (Pāṇini 7.1.61), the augment *num* is added: *jambhate*, *ajambhata*. *Jṛmbhate*, *ajṛmbhata*; *jṛmbhatām*, *jṛmbheta*; *jṛmbhiṣīṣṭa*; *jajṛmbhe*; *ajṛmbhiṣṭa*; in the *caṅ* (reduplication) form: *ajajṛmbhat*; *jṛmbhiṣyate*, and so forth. In the *yaṅ* (intensive) formation, by the statement that under the rule *rīgṛdupadhasya ca* (Pāṇini 7.4.90) one must say "*ṛt-vanta*" (ending in *ṛ*), the augment *rīk* is applied to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*). Thus: *jarījṛmbhyate*.

Regarding the root *jambh* (to chew), the suffix *yaṅ* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.24 (*jarījṛbhyate jambhestu lupasadacarajapajabhadahadaśagṛbhyo bhāvagarhāyām*), and the augment *nuk* is added to the reduplication according to Pāṇini 7.4.86 (*japajabhadahadaśabhañjapaśāṃ ca*). Thus, *jañjabhyate*.
The root *valbh* (to eat): *valbhate*, *avalbhata*.
The root *galbh* (to be bold): *pragalbhate*, *prāgalbhata*.

The roots *sraṃsu* and *pramāde* take the suffix *sraṃsate*; they belong to the *ātmanepada*. The roots *stanbhu*, *stunbhu*, *skanbhu*, *skunbhu*, *skuñ*, and *saṃbhedas* are Vedic (*sautrā*) roots. The root *stuca* is used in the sense of "possessing" or "entering"; it forms *stocate* and *astocata*.
*Stubh* is used in the sense of agitation: *stobhati*, *astobhat*.
*Sac* means to assemble or join: *sacate*, *asacata*, *sacati*, *asacat*; the remainder is to be understood in this manner.
[These roots] are spoken of as having both [voices].

The root *gup* is used in the sense of "protection. In the domain of *sārvadhātuka* suffixes, the suffix *āya* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.28 (*gupū-dhūpa-vichi-paṇi-panibhya āyaḥ*). Because that [derivative] ends in *san* and so forth, it receives the designation of a verbal root (*dhātu*). Thus: *gopāyati* (he protects); *agopāyat* (he protected). Regarding the benedictive (*āśis*), the suffix *āya* is optional according to Pāṇini 3.1.31 (*āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā*). Thus: *gupyāt* or *gopāyyāt*.
