In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), because it is a root ending in a suffix, the suffix *ām* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.35 (*kāspratyayādām amantre*), resulting in *gopāyāñcakāra*. The form *jugopa* [occurs when the *āya* suffix is not applied].

In the *laṅ* [aorist], because it is marked with *ū*, there is an option regarding the augment (*iṭ*); and because the suffix *sic* is an *ārdhadhātuka*, there is an option regarding the substitution of *ay*. Thus, there are three forms: *agopāyīt*. When the augment is not present, there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4), resulting in *agopīt*. When the *vṛddhi* characterized by a final consonant applies, it is *agaupsīt*. In the *caṅ* [reduplicated aorist] of the causative (*ṇau*), we have *ajūgupat* and *ajugopāyat*. Due to the status of the elision of *a* as *sthānivadbhāva*, there is no shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhāhrasva*).

The root *dhūp* is used in the sense of "to fumigate" (*santāpe*). Due to the presence of the augment *alaghūpadhatvāt*, there is an absence of the *guṇa* strengthening. In the periphrastic forms ending in *liṭ*, it follows the pattern of *gup*. In *luṅ*: *adhūpāyīt* or *adhūpīt*. In the causative with *caṅ*: *adūdhupat* or *adūdhupāyat*. [Future]: *dhūpiṣyati* or *dhūpāyiṣyati*, and so forth. The roots *jap* and *jalp* mean "in distinct speech. *japati*. Imperfect: *ajapat*. In *luṅ*: *ajāpīt*. [Future]: *japiṣyati*, and so forth. By the rule *lupasada0* (Pāṇini 3.1.24) and others, and by the rule *japajabha0* (Pāṇini 7.4.86), the augment *nuk* is added to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), resulting in *jañjapyate*. *jalpati*. Imperfect: *ajalpat*. In *luṅ*: *ajalpīt*. [Future]: *jalpiṣyati*, and so forth; these should be applied accordingly.

The roots *apa* and *mānasa* are used in the sense of consolation; *rapa* and *lapa* are used in the sense of distinct speech. One says *lapati*, *alapat*; in the *luṅ* (aorist), *alāpīt* or *alapīt*.

*Cupa* is used in the sense of slow movement; one says *copati*. In the *luṅ*, because of the prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule "neṭ" (*na iṭ*), there is the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel: *acopīt*, *acopiṣṭām*. There is an option regarding the *kit* status in the *san* (desiderative): *cucupiṣati* or *cucopiṣati*.
*cu* in the sense of kissing: *cumbati*, *acumbat*, *cumbyāt* (in the benedictive), *cucumba* (in the periphrastic perfect), *acumbīt*.
*ku* in the sense of covering: [conjugated] as before.
*kṛ* in the sense of doing: *karati*; [the roots] beginning with *gup* undergo the *yoṣiṣad* [substitution].
With the exception of roots ending in *kṛ*, those marked with *seṭ* are spoken in the *parasmaipada*.

The root *ghuṇ* (in the sense of whirling or revolving) forms *ghūrṇate*, *aghūrṇata*, and so forth. In the benedictive mood, it is *ghūrṇiṣīṣṭa*. The perfect form is *jughūrṇe*. The aorist is *aghūrṇiṣṭa*. In the causative with *caṅ* (the reduplicated aorist), it is *ajughūrṇata*; the remainder is to be understood accordingly.

The root *paṇ* is used in the senses of "transaction" (*vyavahāra*) and "praise" (*stuti*). According to the rule for roots beginning with *gup*, when *paṇ* has the sense of praise and takes the suffix *āya*, it belongs to the *śeṣa* category; therefore, it takes the *parasmaipada* (active voice). Examples: *paṇāyati* (he praises), *apaṇāyat* (he praised). In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), because it is an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, there is an option regarding the *āya*: *paṇiṣīṣṭa* or *paṇāyyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [with the suffix *āya*]: *paṇāyāñcakāra*; [without it]: *peṇe*, *peṇāte*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *apaṇiṣṭa* or *apaṇāyīt*. The rest should be understood accordingly. But in the sense of "transaction," it is *paṇate*, *apaṇata*, and so on. The root *pana* also has only the sense of praise, as before. The root *bhām* is used in the sense of "anger": *bhāmate*.

The root *kṣam* is used in the sense of enduring (*sahane*). It takes the form *kṣamate*. In the benedictive (*āśiṣi*), because it is marked with *ū*, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*: *kṣaṃsīṣṭa* or *kṣamiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *cakṣame*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *akṣaṃsta* or *akṣamiṣṭa*. The root *kam* is used in the sense of longing (*kāntau*). By the rule *kamerṇiṅ* (Pāṇini 3.1.30), the suffix *ṇiṅ* is applied. Since it ends in *sanādi*, it is a verbal root (*dhātuḥ*). Because it ends in *am*, the rule *janījṝṣaknasurañjomantāśca* would have assigned it the technical designation *it*; however, this is prohibited by the rule *krampati ca mām*. Consequently, by the rule *ata upadhāyāḥ*, there is *vṛddhi* [of the penultimate vowel]. Because the suffix is marked with *ṅ*, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used: *kāmayate*. In the benedictive, there is an option regarding *ṇiṅ*: *kamiṣīṣṭa* or *kāmayiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *kāmayāmāsa* or *cakame*.

By the rule *luṅi ṇiśri0* (Pāṇini 3.1.48), the suffix *caṅ* is applied in the sense of the agent (*kartari*), resulting in *acīkamata*. In the absence of the *ṇiṅ* suffix, there is an extension (*upasaṃkhyāna*) for the root *kam*, resulting in *acakamata*. The forms *kamiṣyate* and *kāmayiṣyate*, etc., [are derived from the desiderative and causative]. In the desiderative (*san*), we have *cikamiṣate* and *cikāmayiṣate*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), we have *caṅkamyate*. In the case of the *ṇiṅ* suffix, the *yaṅ* is not applicable because the root has more than two syllables (*anekāctvāt*). The roots *śubh* and *śumbh* mean "to beautify" (*śobhārtha*); their forms include *śobhate*, *aśobhata*, and so on. The root *ṛt* means "speaking the truth" (*tathyabhāṣaṇa*) and "compassion" (*ghṛṇā*). The root *ṛt* with the suffix *rīyaṅ* is a Vedic (*sautra*) root; its forms include *ṛtīyate*, and so on.
With the exception of *kṣam*, those [roots] which always take the Ātmanepada are termed *ātmanebhāṣā*.

*Aṇ*, *raṇ*, *maṇ*, *kvaṇ*, *jaṇ*, and *bhaṇ* have the meaning "sound. One should infer [their forms] from such as *aṇati*, *raṇati*, and *maṇati*. *Oṇṛ* means "to remove" (*apanayane*). From *oṇati* and so on, because it begins with *ijādi*, there is *ām* in the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*): *oṇāñcakāra*. Furthermore, the inclusion of *odit* [in the rule for the elision of *ṇi*] is an indicator (*jñāpaka*) that even though reduplication (*dvirvacana*) is obligatory, it is superseded by the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasvatva*); thus one says *mā bhavān uṇiṇat*. *Vaṇ* and *bhaṇ* mean "sound. [Examples: *bhaṇati*, *abhaṇat*; in the intensive (*yaṅ*), *baṃbhaṇyate*.
The root *kan* is used in the senses of shining, beauty, and motion; it forms *kanati* and *akanat*.

The roots *stan*, *van*, and *man* are used in the sense of sound; they form *stanati*, and so forth. *Kaṇ* and *paṇ* are also included; because of the rule stating "for *kaṇ* and others, the substitution of a short vowel for the penultimate [vowel] is optional when followed by the causal suffix (*ṇic*) and the *caṅ* [aorist marker]," there is an optionality regarding the shortening of the penultimate vowel. Thus, one forms *acakaṇat* or *acīkaṇat*, and so on.

The roots *vana* and *sañ* mean "to share" (*sambhaktau*). [Examples: *vanati*, *avanat*; *sanati*, *asanat*. The roots *svan* and *dhvan* mean "sound" (*śabde*). [Example: *svanati*. Regarding the root *svan*, there is the substitution of *ṣ* by Pāṇini’s rule *verupasargātparasya veśca svano bhojane* (8.3.69), and the substitution of *ṇ* by *raṣābhyāṃ noṇaḥ samānapade* (8.4.1). Thus, *viṣvaṇati* means "he eats. When used in a sense other than eating, it is *visvanati*. By the rule *aḍabhyāsavyavāye’pi* (6.1.136), we have the form *vyaṣvaṇat*.

The roots *vam*, *cham*, *jam*, and *jham* are used in the sense of "eating. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.3.75 (*āṅpūrvasya vameḥ ṣṭhivuklamucamām*), there is lengthening [of the vowel] when preceded by *ā*; thus one says *āvāmati*, whereas otherwise one says *vamati*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.2.5 (*hrm-y-anta-kṣaṇa-śvasa-jāgṛ-ṇi-śvi-ed-itām*), there is a prohibition against *vṛddhi*; thus, *avamīt*.

The root *kram* is used in the sense of "stepping" (*pādavikṣepa*). By the rule *kramaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.3.76), there is lengthening [of the vowel] to form *krāmati*; or, by the rule *bhrāśabhlāśabhramukramuklamutrasitruṭilaṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.70), the suffix *śyan* is applied, and as before, there is lengthening to form *krāmyati*, and so forth. In the benedictive mood, [the form is] *kramyāt*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *hmyanta* (Pāṇini 7.2.5), there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi*, resulting in *akramīt*. The future forms are *kramiṣyati* and *kramitā*. The desiderative is *cikramiṣati*.

The suffix *yaṅ* is prescribed by the rule *nityaṃ kauṭilye gatau* (Pāṇini 3.1.23), as in *caṅkramyate*. Regarding the roots *vṛt* and others, the *ātmanepada* is ordained for the root *kram* by the rules *vṛttisargatāyaneṣu kramaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.38), *upaparābhyām* (Pāṇini 1.3.39), *āṅ udvamane* (Pāṇini 1.3.40), *veḥ pādaviharaṇe* (Pāṇini 1.3.41), *propābhyāṃ samarthābhyām* (Pāṇini 1.3.42), and *anusargādvā* (Pāṇini 1.3.43); this applies here in the context of an *ārdhadhātuka* affix beginning with *val*.

There is also a prohibition of the *iṭ* augment by the rule *snukramoranātmanepadanimitte* (Pāṇini 7.2.36). In that context, *vṛtti* means lack of obstruction; *sarga* means exertion; *tāyana* means expansion; and *upapūrvaḥ kramiḥ* (the root *kram* preceded by *upa*) occurs in the sense of undertaking, while *parāpūrvaḥ* (preceded by *parā*) occurs in the sense of valorous effort (*parākrama*). Nevertheless, even here, this [rule] is for the sake of restriction regarding *vṛtti* and the others, specifically when preceded by the prefixes *upa* and *parā*. The root *kram* preceded by *āṅ* occurs in the sense of the rising of celestial bodies (*jyotirudgamana*), and preceded by *vi* in the sense of stepping with the feet (*pādaviharaṇa*). Preceded by *pra* and *upa*, it occurs in the sense of undertaking (*ārambha*).

Except for these [roots], after the root *kram* (to step) when not preceded by a prefix, the Ātmanepada is optionally used; as stated in the *vṛtti*: *kramate*, *akramata*; in the benedictive (*āśis*), *kraṃsīṣṭa*; in the perfect (*liṭ*), *cakrame*; in the aorist (*luṅ*), *akraṃsta*; in the future, *kraṃsyate*; in the conditional, *akraṃsyata*; in the periphrastic future, *krantā*; in the desiderative, *cikraṃsyate*. It is the same elsewhere as well. These roots ending in a *seṭ* suffix are *parasmaibhāṣā* (spoken in the Parasmaipada).
The roots *aya*, *vaya*, *ṣaya*, *maya*, *caya*, *daya*, *taya*, and *naya* mean "to go.
*Taya* means "to protect.
*Daya* means "to give," "to go," and "to protect."

The root *ray* means "to go. Regarding the substitution of *l* for the initial of the prefix *pra-* when preceded by *pra-* or *parā-* before the verb *ā-yat* (Pāṇini 8.2.19), we have *palāyate*, *apalāyata*; in the benedictive (*āśis*), *palāyiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by Pāṇini 3.1.37 (*dayāyāsaśca*), there is the suffix *ām*: *palāyāñcakre*. The suffix *ām* occurs after these roots—*aya*, *āsa*, and so on—as well as *day*, thus: *palāyāñcakre*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *palāyiṣṭa*; in the conditional (*lṛṅ*), *palāyiṣyat*. [From the root *day*: *dayate*, *adayata*; in the benedictive, *dayiṣīṣṭa*; in the perfect, *dayāñcakre*. For the remaining forms, examples should be inferred accordingly.

*Ūyī* means "to weave" (*tantu-santāna*). It is conjugated as *ūyate*, *auyata*; in the benedictive (*āśis*), *ūyiṣīṣṭa*; and in the perfect (*liṭ*), because it begins with *ij*, the augment *ām* is applied: *ūyāñcakre*, and so forth should be applied accordingly. *Pūyī* means "to putrefy" (*viśaraṇa*) and "to have a foul odor" (*durgandha*). It is conjugated as *pūyate*. *Knūyī* means "to sound" (*śabda*). It is conjugated as *knūyate*. In the causative (*ṇau*) with the *caṅ* suffix, by the rule *arti-hrī-...* (Pāṇini 7.3.36), the *puk* augment is added; there is elision of the semivowel (*vali-lopaḥ*), *guṇa* substitution, shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasvaḥ*), and the reduplication operations (*abhyāsa-kāryam*), resulting in *acuknupat*.

The root *kṣmāyī* is used in the sense of shaking, as before. The roots *sphāyī* and *opyāyī* are used in the sense of increasing (*vṛddhi*). Examples include *sphāyyate* and *āpyāyate*, etc. In the *liṭ* [perfect], *liṅ* [optative], and *yaṅ* [intensive] suffixes, there is the substitution of *pī* according to Pāṇini 6.1.29. Then, by the rule *eranekācaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.82), there is the substitution of *yaṇ*. Thus, in the *liṭ*, we have *pipye*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], according to Pāṇini 3.1.61—*dīpajanabudhapūritāyipyāyibhyaḥ anyatarasyām*—there is optionally the substitution of *ciṇ* for *cl* when the agent is expressed. Thus, *āpyāyi* or *āpyāyiṣṭa*. In the *yaṅ*, there is the substitution of *psā* and reduplication: *āpepīyate*. The examples for *sphāyati* should be inferred accordingly.

The root *tāyṛ* is used in the senses of continuity, protection, worship, and investigation, like the root *pyāy*. Except for the substitution of *pyā*, all [rules] apply; and because of its *ṛdit* designation, there is shortening when the suffix *ṇic* is followed by *caṅ*:

*atatāyat*. *Val* and *vall* mean "to cover" and "to move about. *valate*, *avalata*. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), there is a prohibition against the elision of the reduplication [of the root], according to Pāṇini 6.4.126 (*na śasa...*).
*Mala* and *malla* mean "to hold."
*bal* in the sense of attaining strength;
*bhala* and *bhall* in the senses of addressing, injuring, and giving;
*kala* in the senses of sound and counting.
*Kala* is used in the sense of indistinct sound; examples for these [roots] are to be inferred.
*Tevṛ* and *devṛ* are used in the sense of playing (*devana*). They are marked with the *seṭ* [augment] and are conjugated in the Ātmanepada.

The root *mavy* means "to bind. It forms *mavyati*. The roots *sūrkṣya*, *īrkṣya*, *īrṣya*, and *īrṣya* have the meaning of "envy. From *īrṣya*: present *īrṣyati*; aorist *airṣyat*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it forms *īrṣyāñcakāra*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), it should be stated that "the third [consonant] becomes doubled": as for which is the "third," some say it is the consonant; according to that view, it becomes *īrṣyāyiyiṣati*. Others, however, state that it refers to a monosyllabic root (*ekāc*); according to that view, it becomes *īrṣyiṣiṣati*. The other two cases are to be inferred accordingly. The root *haya* means "to go."

The root *ala* is used in the senses of adorning, sufficiency, and warding off. *Ñi-phal* means "to burst open" or "to expand. The marker *ñi* is for the purpose of specific grammatical designation according to Pāṇini’s rule *ñitaḥ ktaḥ* (3.2.187); its practical application, however, is the prescription of the suffix *kta* in the present tense. Examples: *phalati* (present), *aphalat* (imperfect). In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), the form is *paphāla*. In the case of a *kit* suffix in the perfect, by the rule *tṛphalabhajatrapaśca* (6.4.122), there is *etva* (change of *a* to *e*) and the elision of the reduplicative syllable; thus: *phelatuḥ*, *pheluḥ*. In the *thal* suffix when followed by a *seṭ* augment, the form is *phelitha*.
The root *phal* in the sense of "production" or "ripening" follows the same pattern as the previous one.

The roots *mīla* and *smīla* mean "to close the eyes. In the present tense (*laṭ*), one says *nimīlati*; in the perfect (*liṭ*), *nimimīla*; and in the aorist (*luṅ*), *nyamīlīt*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the reduplication (*caṅ*), by the rule *bhrājabhrāsa...* (Pāṇini 7.4.3), there is shortening of the penultimate vowel, resulting in *nyamimīlat* or *nyamīmilat*. For the other [root, *smīla*], however, it is *asismilat*; the rest is the same. The root *śīla* means "to practice" or "habituation. The root *kīla* means "to bind."
*śūla* means pain;
*tūla* means to extract or pull out;
*pūla* means a cluster or heap.
In the *Mūlapratiṣṭhā*: examples of these are to be inferred.
*Skhal* in the sense of "stumbling": *skhalati*, *askhalat*. *Khala* in the sense of "moving about."
*Gala* means to swallow; *ala* means to perish.

[In the root *ala*: *alati*. In the *luṅ* tense, by the rule *ato lrāntasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.2), there is invariably *vṛddhi*, resulting in *ālīt*. *Tsara* means to move stealthily. *tsarati*. In the *liṭ* tense, it becomes *tatsāra*; in the *luṅ* tense, as before, there is *vṛddhi*, resulting in *atsārīt*.

The root *kvar* is used in the sense of moving; in the *luṅ* tense, it becomes *akvārīt*. The root *car* means "to move" and "to eat. It takes *vṛddhi* as before, resulting in *acārīt*. However, regarding the root *car* preceded by *ud*, the two rules *udaścaraḥ sakarmakāt* (Pāṇini 1.3.53) and *samastṛtīyāyuktāt* (Pāṇini 1.3.53) prescribe the *ātmanepada* voice: *uccarate* and *sañcarate*. By the rule *lupasada...* (Pāṇini 3.1.24) and others, the *yaṅ* suffix is applied. By the rule *caraphaloraca* (Pāṇini 7.4.87), the augment *nuk* is added to the reduplication (*abhyāsa*). Then, by the rule *abhyāsātparasya utparasyātaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.79), the vowel following the reduplication is changed to *u*, and by *hali ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.2)... [the rest of the sūtra application follows].

By [Pāṇini 8.2.77], there is lengthening. *cañcūryate* is formed in this manner; likewise, for *phalati*, it should be inferred with the exception of lengthening: *pampalyate*. For *ṣṭhivu* in the sense of spitting, there is a prohibition of *ṣatva* as before. By [Pāṇini 7.3.75], "there is lengthening for *ṣṭhivu*, *klam*, and *cam* before a suffix marked with *ś*," there is lengthening: *niṣṭhīvati*. *niraṣṭhīvat*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*) and before a consonant (*hal*), by [Pāṇini 8.2.77], there is lengthening: *niṣṭhīvyāt*.

In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, when a suffix beginning with *th* follows, the *khayaḥ* (consonants other than *ha*) of the reduplicated syllable remain, as do the *guṇa* substitution for a light penultimate vowel. Thus, from the root *ṣṭhīv*, we have *ṭiṣṭheva*, *ṭiṣṭhīvatuḥ*, *ṭiṣṭhivuḥ*, and *ṭiṣṭhevitha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], regarding the rule *sanīvantardhabhrasjadambhuśrivṛyūrṇubharajñapisanām* (Pāṇini 7.2.49): the augment *iṭ* optionally occurs after roots ending in *i*, as well as after *ṛdhi*, *sup*, and others, and after the verbal base *bhṛ* (where *bhṛ* refers to the *śap*-class conjugation). Consequently, we have *tiṣṭheviṣati*. In the absence of *iṭ*, the rule *halāntācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10) applies.

By the rule *pā0sū0 1/2/10*, because the suffix *san* begins with a *jhal* sound, it is *kit*. Furthermore, by the rule *pā0sū0 6/4/19*, *śū* replaces *ch* and *ūṭh* replaces *v* when followed by an *anunāsika*. Since the substitution of *yaṇ* is *antaraṅga*—as it depends on individual letters (*varṇāśrayatvāt*)—it is considered *asiddha* (non-existent) relative to the *bahiraṅga* operations. Thus, because *ūṭh* is *asiddha*, how can there be a *yaṇ* substitution? This is not so; for there is an indicator (*jñāpaka*) that "when there is immediate proximity of vowels (*nājānantarye*), the status of being *bahiraṅga* is not applied. Where, then, is this indicator found? It is in the rule *adhig nityā* (Pāṇini 8.1.37). However, in that case...

In order to provide a counter-exception (*pratiprasava*) for the *bahiranga-paribhāṣā* regarding what is to be performed, by the statement "the [substitution of] *ṣaṭ* is as if non-existent" (*asiddha*), reduplication then occurs, as in *tuṣṭyūṣati*. From the root *ji* (to conquer): *jayati*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), by the rule "lengthening of vowels before non-*kṛt* and non-*sārvadhātuka* suffixes," we have *jīyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect tense), by the rule "in *san* and *liṭ*, there is *kutva* [change] for *ji*" (*san-liṭorjer*), there is *kutva* of the letter following the reduplication, resulting in the letter *g*: *jigāya*. By the rule "after a non-conjunct consonant, *liṭ* is *kit*" (*asaṃyogālliṭ kit*, Pāṇini 1.2.5), there is *kutva*. Then, by the rule "for *eṅ* followed by a non-monosyllabic word... (*eranekācaḥ*, Pāṇini 6.4.82), there is the *yaṇ* substitute: *jigyatuḥ*, *jigyuḥ*.

In *thali*, the augment *iṭ* is obtained by the rule *krādiniyamaprāptasyeṭaḥ*. However, this is prohibited by the rule *acastāsvatthalyaniṭo nityam* (Pāṇini 7.2.61). Consequently, by the rule *ṛto bhāradvājasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.63), [the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied]. Thus, we have *jigetha* and *jigayitha*. In the *luṅ* tense with *sic*, there is *vṛddhi*: *ajaiṣīt*. In the *caṅ* of the *ṇic* suffix, there is *vṛddhi*; then, by the rule *krīṅjīnām* (Pāṇini 6.1.48), there is *ātva*, then *puk*, then shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhāhrasva*), and finally reduplication—this is the sequence of the grammatical operations.

If the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasvatva*) were performed after reduplication has occurred, then the *sanvadbhāva* prescribed by Pāṇini 7.4.93 (*sanvallaghuni caṅpare*) would not take effect because of the status of the substitute as being like the original (*sthānivadbhāva*) of that short vowel. However, when the shortening of the penultimate vowel is carried out first, as before, there is no rule applying to what precedes an unstated vowel; thus, the substitution of the short penultimate vowel does not possess the status of being like the original (*sthānivat*). Consequently, since the syllable with the light penultimate vowel follows, the condition for Pāṇini 7.4.93 (*sanvallaghuni caṅpare*) is met.

The operations such as the treatment as *saN* (*sanvadbhāva*) are established; [he] caused to whisper (*ajījapat*). Because of the *kit* designation by the rule *sani iko jhal* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), there is an absence of *guṇa*; by the rule *aj-jhan-gamāṃ sani* (Pāṇini 6.4.16), there is lengthening; as before, there is the change to *k* (*kutva*), [resulting in] *jigīṣati*. From the prefix *vi-* or from a prefix beginning with *vi-*, the *ātmanepada* occurs by the rule *viparābhyāṃ jeḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.19): [he] conquers (*vijayate*). [He] conquered (*vyajayata*). In the benedictive, [he] may conquer (*vijeṣīṣṭa*). In the perfect (*liṭ*), as before there is the change to *k*: [he] has conquered (*vijigye*). In the aorist (*luṅ*), [he] conquered (*vyajeṣṭa*).

The root *jīv* (meaning "to live") is used in the sense of maintaining life. It forms *jīvati*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, it becomes *ajīvīt*. When the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is applied and followed by the *caṅ* (reduplication), there is an optional shortening of the penultimate vowel according to Pāṇini 6.1.15 (*bhrājabhāsabhāṣadīpajīvamīla-hṛkṣaṇaḥ*), resulting in either *ajijīvat* or *ajījivat*. The roots *pīv* and *mīv* mean "to become stout. Everything is as before; when the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is applied and followed by the *caṅ*, it becomes *apīpivat*. The root *kṣiv* means "to eject" (as saliva). There is the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel, resulting in *kṣevati*. Because the root ends in *ivant* (the letter *i*), there is an optionality regarding the augment *iṭ* in the desiderative, resulting in *cikṣeviṣati* or *cikṣiviṣati*.
The roots *turvī*, *thurvī*, *durvī*, and *dhurvī* have the sense of "injuring.
*Gurvī* means "to lift up.
*Turvī* means "to bind. The examples for these should be inferred accordingly.

The root *carv* is used in the senses of eating and injuring; it forms *carvati* (he eats) and *acarvat* (he ate). The roots *karva*, *kharva*, and *garva* mean pride; they signify pervasion (*vyāpti*). There is the addition of the augment *num*; thus, *invati* means "he bestows riches.
The roots *pivi*, *nivi*, and *mivi* mean sprinkling (*secana*); thus, *pinvanti āpo marutaḥ* means "the waters and the Maruts cause to swell."

The roots *dhivi* and *jivi* are used in the sense of pleasing. Because they are marked with the indicatory letter *it*, they take the augment *num*. By the rule *dhinvikṛṇvoraca* (Pāṇini 3.1.80), the suffix *u* is added as an exception to the suffix *śap*; the vowel *a* is for the purpose of indicating the final substitution. By the rule *ato lopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.48), that [augment] is elided. The *guṇa* substitution occurs for the *sārvadhātuka* suffixes. Thus, from these roots, *śap* is applied: *dhinoti* and *jinoti*. It quickens (*jinvati*) the minds of those who have fallen away. The root *kṛvi* is used in the senses of harming and doing; everything regarding it is like *dhinoti*. The root *mava* means to bind; it forms *mavati*.

The root *ava* is used in the senses of protecting, moving, beauty, affection, satisfaction, understanding, entering, ownership, requesting, action, desire, flaming, carrying away, embracing, harming, existence, and increase. Examples include *avatī* and so forth. These roots ending in *iṭ* (seṭ) are conjugated in the Parasmaipada.
The root *dhāv* is used in the senses of "running" and "purifying. It is conjugated as *dhāvati* (Parasmaipada) and *dhāvate* (Ātmanepada).
It is *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*) and is spoken in both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣa*).
*dhukṣ* and *dhikṣ* are used in the senses of kindling, afflicting, and living; it forms *sandhukṣate*.
*vṛkṣ* is used in the sense of covering;
*śikṣ* is used in the sense of acquiring knowledge; it forms *śikṣate* and *aśikṣata*.

The root *bhikṣ* is used in the sense of begging; whether there is no gain or there is gain, one begs: *bhikṣate*, *abhikṣata*. The root *dīkṣ* is used in the sense of tonsure, initiation (*upanayana*), observance of rules, and instruction in vows: *dīkṣate*, *adīkṣata*. The root *īkṣ* is used in the sense of seeing: *īkṣate*, *aikṣata*, *īkṣatām*, *īkṣeta*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), [the form is] *īkṣiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the form is] *īkṣāmāsa*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), [the form is] *aikṣiṣṭa*. In the future, etc., [the form is] *īkṣiṣyata*, and so forth.

The root *bhāṣ* is used in the sense of distinct speech. It forms *bhāṣate* (he speaks) and *abhāṣata* (he spoke). According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.3 (*ṇau caṅi bhrājabhāsa...*), there is an option for the penultimate vowel to become short in the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist) following the causative suffix (*ṇic*); thus, one forms either *ababhāṣat* or *abībhaṣat*. The roots *heṣṛ* and *hreṣṛ* are used in the sense of indistinct sound. They form *heṣate* and *hreṣate*, as in "the horse neighs. The root *kāsṛ* is used in the sense of contemptuous sound. It forms *kāsate*. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), by Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.1.35 (*kāspratyayādāmamantre liṭi*), the suffix *ām* is added; thus, one forms *kāsāñcakre*.
The root *bhāsṛ* means "to shine. In the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist) following the causative suffix (*ṇic*), there is an optionality regarding the short vowel: *ababhāsat* or *abībhasat*.
The roots *bhāsṛ*, *nāsṛ*, and *rāsṛ* mean "to sound" and "to shine," respectively; examples for these should be inferred accordingly.

The root *kuṭ* is used in the sense of crookedness; it takes the form *kuṭati*. The root *mṛṣ* is used in the sense of forgetting; it takes the form *mṛṣyate*. The root *bhī* is used in the sense of fear; it takes the form *bibheti*.
The roots *grasu* and *glasu* are used in the sense of devouring; they take the forms *grasate* and *agrasata*.

*Īh* means "effort" or "striving. *Īhate*, *aihta*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), because it is marked with the *idit* designation, the suffix *ām* is applied: *īhāñcakre*. *Garh* and *gart* mean "censure. *Garhate*, *agarhata*.
*Varh* and *valh* mean "preeminence."
*plu* means "to go. *vehr̥*, *jehr̥*, and *vāhr̥* mean "exertion"; examples for these should be inferred.
*kāśr̥* means "to shine"; it is used in *prakāśate*.

The root *vāśṛ* is used in the sense of sound; *vāśate*. The root *ūh* is used in the sense of deliberation; *ūhate*. When it is accompanied by a prefix (*sopasarga*), the *parasmaipada* occurs optionally according to the rule "after a prefix, [the roots] *as* and *ūh* take the *parasmaipada*" (*upasargād asy-ūhyor vāvacanam*); thus, *samūhate* or *samūhati*. In the *liṭ* [perfect], it is *samūhāñcakre* or *samūhāñcakāra*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], it is *samauhiṣṭa* or *samauhīt*. The root *gāhū* is used in the sense of plunging or churning; *gāhate*. [Imperfect: *agāhata*. [Imperative: *gāhatām*. [Optative: *gāheta*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), because it is marked with *ū*, there is an option regarding *iṭ*: *gāhiṣīṣṭa*. In the absence of *iṭ*, the substitutions for *bhaṣ*, *k*, and *ṣ* apply: *ghākṣiṣṭa*. In the *liṭ*, it is *jagāhe*. In the *luṅ*, in the absence of *iṭ*, there is elision of the *s* by the rule "after a *jhāl* [consonant], before a *jhāl* [consonant]" (*jhalo jhali*); thus, *aghātta* or *agāhiṣṭa*.
The roots ending in *ghu* are always *ātmanepada*, with the exception of *gāh*.

The root *ghuṣ* has the meaning "to sound. Present: *ghoṣati*; *aghoṣat*; *ghoṣatu*; *ghoṣet*; *ghuṣyāt*. Perfect: *jughoṣa*. Aorist (*luṅ*): By the rule *irito vā* (Pāṇini 3.1.57), there is optionally *aṅ*: *aghoṣīt*; otherwise, *ajaghuṣat*. In the reduplicated aorist (*caṅ*), *ajūghuṣat*. Future: *ghoṣiṣyati*; *aghoṣiṣyat*. Periphrastic Future: *ghoṣitā*. Desiderative: *jughoṣiṣati*; *jughuṣiṣati*. Passive: *jughuṣyate*.

The root *akṣ* is used in the senses of pervading (*vyāpti*) and collecting (*saṅghāta*). By the rule *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.73), the affix *śnu* is applied; then, by the option provided in *akṣonyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.75), *śnu* is optionally applied. Thus, [in the present tense] one says *akṣati* or *akṣṇoti*. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, it is *ānakṣa*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, because the root is marked with *ū*, there is an optional application of the augment *iṭ*: *mā bhavānakṣīt*. In the alternative where *iṭ* is absent, there is the elision of the consonant following the *saṃyoga* (conjunction) by the rule *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* (Pāṇini 8.2.41); furthermore, by the same rule, the *ṣ* is changed to *k*, resulting in *ākṣīt*. When a *jhal* (palatal, retroflex, or dental stop) follows, there is elision of the consonant following the *saṃyoga*; then, by the rule for *ṣṭutva*, the *t* is changed to *ṣ*, resulting in *āṣṭām*. [In the plural,] *ākṣuḥ*.

The roots *takṣ* and *tvakṣ* mean "to make thin. By the rule *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.73), and specifically by *tanūkaraṇe takṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.76), the suffix *śnu* is applied; thus, *takṣṇoti* means "he makes wood thin. Because verbal roots have multiple meanings, when used in senses other than "making thin," one says *takṣati* and *atakṣat*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), because the root is marked with *ū*, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*; in the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4), the prohibition of *vṛddhi* applies, resulting in *atakṣīt*. In the absence of *iṭ*, after the elision of the initial *saṃyoga*, the substitution of *ṣ* and *vṛddhi* occur, resulting in *atākṣīt*. In the *caṅ* (periphrastic aorist), it is *atatakṣat*. In the *lṛt* (future) and *luṭ* (periphrastic future), it is *takṣiṣyati*.

In the absence of *iḍ*, the operations such as the elision of the *saṃyoga* [consonant cluster] will apply: *atakṣyat*, *atakṣyat*, *atakṣiṣyat*. The future forms are *takṣitā* and *taṣṭā*. With the desiderative suffix (*san*), it is *titakṣiṣati*. The same should be inferred for *tvakṣ* as well. *Ukṣ* (meaning "to sprinkle"): *prokṣati*. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), because it begins with *ijādi*, there is *ām*: *ukṣāñcakāra*, *prokṣāmbabhūva*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *aukṣīt*. In the causative (*ṇau*) with the reduplicated aorist (*caṅ*), it is *aucikṣat*. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *ucikṣiṣati*. *Rakṣ* (meaning "to protect"): *rakṣati*.

The root *nikṣ* means "to kiss. Regarding the form *praṇikṣati* or *pranikṣati*, etc., there is an optionality of the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 8.4.33: *ṇo naḥ rephavadupasargāt parasya vā niṃsanikṣanindām*. The root *mṛkṣ* means "to collect" (*saṃghāta*); it forms *mṛkṣati*.
The root *pakṣ* means "to embrace" or "to take sides" (*parigraha*); it forms *pakṣati*.

*Kākṣi*, *vākṣi*, and *mākṣi* are used in the sense of desiring (*kāṅkṣā*). [Examples: *kāṅkṣati*, *akāṅkṣata*; in the *liṭ* [perfect], *cakāṅkṣa*; in the *luṅ* [aorist], *akāṅkṣīt*; and with the causative suffix *ṇic* followed by the *caṅ* [reduplication], *acakāṅkṣata*. *Drākṣi*, *dhrākṣi*, and *dhvākṣi* are used in the sense of a terrible howling (*ghoravāśita*). [Example: *dhvāṅkṣati*. *Cūṣa* means "to drink" (*pāna*). [Examples: *cūṣati*; in the *liṭ*, *cucūṣa*.

The root *tuṣ* means "to be pleased. [Present: *toṣati*. [Perfect: In the *liṭ* [perfect], *tutoṣa*. [Aorist: In the *luṅ* [aorist], *atoṣīt*. [Future: *toṣiṣyati*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), there is an option for *kit* status: *tutuṣiṣati* or *tutoṣiṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), *totuṣyate*. The root *muṣ* means "to steal. Regarding the desiderative, it is as before. By the rule *rudavidamuṣagrahisvapipracchaḥ saṃśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.8), there is obligatory *kit* status: *mumuṣiṣati*. The roots *vaṣ* and *puṣ* mean "to grow."

The roots *kaṣ*, *śiṣ*, *jiṣ*, *jhaṣ*, *vaṣ*, *ruṣ*, and *ṛṣ* have the meaning "to injure. Regarding *kaṣ*, *ruṣ*, and *riṣ*, there is an option for the augment *iṭ* after the beginning of an affix marked with *t* (by Pāṇini 7.2.48: *tīṣasahalubharuṣariṣaḥ*). Thus, [the forms] are *roṣṭā* or *roṣitā*; *reṣṭā* or *reṣitā*. The root *bhaṣ* means "to revile"; it has sound as its object.

The root *uṣ* means "to burn. In the forms *oṣati* and *auṣat*, [the rules apply]. Regarding the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), the suffix *ām* is optionally applied by Pāṇini 3.1.38: *uṣavidajāgṛbhyonyatarasyām*. Thus, one form is *oṣāmāsa*. In other cases, such as the *ṇal* suffix, because it is subsequent [in the order of rules], the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel occurs first; subsequently, reduplication takes place. When the form *o oṣa* is established, the substitution of *uvaṅ* for the reduplicated syllable—by Pāṇini 6.4.78: *abhyāsasyāsavarṇe*—does not take effect, because the *guṇa* substitute is treated as the original element (*sthānivadbhāva*) due to its being a substitute for a vowel (*ajādeśa*).

Because the substitution of *uvaṅ* is a rule (*vidhi*) applying to what precedes an unspecified vowel (*anādiṣṭādacaḥ pūrvasya*), there is the status of being a *sthānivadbhāva* with respect to the rule concerning what precedes that unspecified vowel. Thus: *uvoṣa* (in the perfect, *liṭ*, with a *kit* suffix, there is *savarṇadīrgha*); *ūṣatuḥ*, *ūṣuḥ*; in the *thali* suffix, *uvoṣitha*; in the aorist (*luṅ*), *auṣīt*. In the benedictive (*āśiṣi*), *uṣyāt*. In the aorist, because it is *aniṭ* and has a short *u* as its penultimate (*upadhā*), [the suffix] becomes *s* and [the result is] *auviṣṭām*. In the causative (*ṇau*) with the *caṅ* reduplication, *mā bhavānuṣiṣat*;
*uṣiṣyati*, etc. The root *puṣ* (meaning "to nourish") is entirely like *tuṣ*. *Śliṣ* and *pluṣ* (meaning "to give").

The roots *pruṣ* and *pluṣ* mean "to burn. *Ploṣati* (he burns), *aploṣat* (he burned), *ploṣatu* (let him burn), *ploṣet* (he might burn). In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), *pluṣyāt*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, because the root is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment), Pāṇini’s rule *śala igupadhādaniṭaḥ ksaḥ* (3.1.45) applies: "After a root ending in *śal*, having a penultimate *ik* vowel, which is *aniṭ*, the substitute *ksa* takes the place of *cli*. Since the term *aniṭ* qualifies *cli*, the *ksa* substitute is established even for roots that have optional *iṭ*. The *k* of *ksa* is for the purpose of triggering *kit*-operations. Due to its *kit* status, there is no *guṇa* substitution; thus, by the rules for *katva* and *ṣatva*, we get *aplukṣata* (he burned).
Śiṣi, piṣi, śuṣyati, puṣyati, itviṣi, tuṣyati, duṣyati, idviṣi—these ten they teach as ending in ṣ, belonging to the class beginning with ani; likewise, kṛṣa and karṣati [are taught].

By this statement, [the root] is *aniṭ* [before *liṭ*]; however, in *liṭ*, it is always *seṭ* due to the rule beginning with "krādi. In *lṛṭ* and *luṭ*, there is the substitution of *k* for *ṣ*, and by *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ*, [it becomes] *ploṣyati* and *ploṣṭā*. By the rule *halantācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10), there is *kitva* [in the *sa* of the desiderative], resulting in *puplukṣati* and *popluṣyate*.

The roots *pṛṣu*, *vṛṣu*, and *mṛṣu* mean "to sprinkle. With the suffix *śap*, there is *guṇa*: *varṣati* (he rains), *avarṣat* (he rained). In the optative, *varṣatu* (may he rain); in the benedictive, *varṣet*; and in the benedictive with a blessing, *vṛṣyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *vavarṣa*, *vavṛṣatuḥ*, *vavṛṣuḥ*, *vavarṣitha*. Here, by the rule for roots beginning with *krī*, the addition of *iṭ* need not be requested because the root is *seṭ* (possessing *iṭ*). [Other forms: *vavṛṣathuḥ*, *vavṛṣa*, *vavarṣa*, *vavṛṣiva*, *vavṛṣima*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *avarṣīt*. By the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4), the *vṛddhi* substitution conditioned by a final consonant is prohibited.

When the form *ṇau caṅi vṛṣi at* is established, and the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) is about to apply, the rule *urṛt* (Pāṇini 7.4.7)—which states "optionally" (*vā*)—prescribes that when a *ṇic* suffix followed by *caṅ* is present, the substitute *ṛ* takes the place of the vowel *ṛ* in the penultimate syllable. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the other [rules]. Thus, when the substitution of *ṛ* occurs, the operations such as *sanvadbhāva* apply, resulting in *avīvṛṣat*. In the other case, because the condition of having a light penultimate vowel (*laghupadhātva*) and being followed by a single consonant (*ekācparatva*) is absent, there is no *sanvadbhāva*, resulting in *avavarṣat*. The same should be understood for subsequent forms such as *varṣiṣyati*, etc. The roots *pṛṣu* and *mṛṣu* mean "to injure" (*hiṃsā*) and "to afflict" (*saṃkleśana*). The root *mṛṣu* also means "to endure" (*sahana*). Examples for these should be inferred accordingly.
*dhṛṣu* in the sense of rivalry;
*mṛṣu* in the sense of falsehood. The remainder is to be understood as being like *vṛṣ*.
*tusa*, *hrasa*, *hvasa*, and *rasa* in the sense of sound: *rasati*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), [the forms are] *arasīt* and *arāsīt*.

The root *ghaslṛ* means "to eat. It forms *ghasati* (present), *aghast* (imperfect), and in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), *jaghāsa*. In the perfect tense, when a *kit* affix follows, there is elision [of the penultimate vowel] according to Pāṇini 6.4.98: "There is elision of the penultimate vowel of *gam*, *han*, *jan*, *khan*, and *ghas* before a *kit* or *ṅit* affix, except before *anaṅ*. This elision does not behave as if it were a substitute for the original (sthānivat) when the rule Pāṇini 8.4.55 (*khari ca*)—which requires the substitution of a *car*-sound—is to be applied, because the prohibition of sthānivadbhāva is established by the rule beginning with Pāṇini 1.1.58 (*na padānta...*). Furthermore, by the rule Pāṇini 8.3.60 (*śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca*), the cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) sound is substituted [for the dental *s*], resulting in *jakṣatuḥ* and *jakṣuḥ*.

Regarding the rule *ṛto bhāradvājasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.63), there is an option for the augment *iṭ* in the suffix *thal*; thus we have *jaghasitha* when *iṭ* is present, and *jaghattha* when *iṭ* is absent. But how can there be an absence of *iṭ*, given that by the restriction of the *krādi* group, *iṭ* ought to be mandatory?

This is not so; for in the instruction on that [suffix], under the governing rule *atvataḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.61), the rule *ṛto bharadvājasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.63) provides an option regarding the suffix *thali*. If that were the case, then in the rule *acastāsvatthali* (Pāṇini 7.2.61), the mention of *tāsvat* would be intended to prohibit [the substitution] in the case of *thali* when it follows *tās*. Consequently, the statement of the author of the Vṛtti—that "for that which is *asan* in *tās*, being *atvataḥ* and invariably *aniṭ*, there is no prohibition in *thali*, as in *jaghasitha*"—would be contradicted. This is not a fault, because that [prohibition] is stated there with reference to the substitute *ad*.
The suffix *śak* is desired after words ending in *kānta*, while *aniyaṭ* alone is desired after words ending in *dhasi*; *dhi* is extended after words ending in *śānta*,
and *rabhi* after those ending in *bhānta*, as well as in the sense of sexual intercourse.
Because of that, [the breaths] are indeed three, and not others.

In the course of this explanation, it is stated that *ghas* exists as a distinct verbal root (*prakṛti*), because it has been cited [by Pāṇini] as such. In the *luṅ* (aorist), because it belongs to the *puṣādi* group and is marked with *ḷ*, the rule *puṣādidyutādyalṛditaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 3.1.55) applies, resulting in *cleraṅ*. Thus: *aghast* (aorist). By the rule *saḥ syārdhadhātuke* (Pāṇini 7.4.49), there is the substitution of *t* for *s*. Future: *ghatsyati*. Conditional: *aghatsyat*. With the desiderative suffix (*san*): *jighatsati*. With the intensive suffix (*yaṅ*): *jāghatsyate*. The root *las* means "to cling" and "to play. Present: *lasati*. In the *luṅ*: *alast* or *alāsīt*.

In the case of *hase* (to laugh): in the present tense (*laṭ*), it is *hasati*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), because of the *eṭ* augment, the optional *vṛddhi* prescribed by Pāṇini 7.2.7 (*ato halāder laghoḥ*) is prohibited by Pāṇini 7.2.5 (*hrmyantakṣaṇaśvasajāgṛṇiśvīditām*). Consequently, the prohibition [of *vṛddhi*] by Pāṇini 7.2.4 (*neṭi*) applies. Thus, the forms are *ahāsīt* and *hasiṣyati*.
The root *śab* means "to go. The root *śaś* means "to leap/go quickly."

The root *śasu* is used in the sense of "to injure. It forms *viśasati*. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, it becomes *viśaśāsa*. By the rule *na śasadadavādiguṇānām* (Pāṇini 6.4.126), there is a prohibition against the substitution of *e* and the elision of the reduplication; thus, *viśaśasatuḥ*, *viśaśasuḥ*, and *viśaśasitha*. The root *śaṃsu* is used in the sense of "to praise. It forms *praśaṃsati*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), it becomes *prāśaṃsat*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is the elision of the nasal: *praśasyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), it becomes *praśaśaṃsa* and *praśaśaṃsitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), it becomes *aśaṃsīt*. The future form is *śaṃsiṣyati*, and so forth. The root *maha* is used in the sense of "to honor. It forms *mahati*.
*raha* means to abandon; *rahati*. *rahi* means to go; *raṃhati*. *dṛha*, *dṛhi*, *bṛha*, and *bṛhi* mean growth; [from *bṛhi*] *bṛṃhati*.
The root *bṛh* is used in the sense of sound; an elephant roars (*bṛṃhati*).
The roots *tuhi* and *uhi* mean to injure; [one] injures (*tohati*) or strikes away (*apohati*).

The root *arh* is used in the sense of "to worship" or "to deserve. Present tense (*laṭ*): - *arhati* - *ārhat* - *arhatu* - *arhet* - *arhyāt* Periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*): By the rules *ata ādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.70) and *tasmān nuḍ dvihalahaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.71), the augment *nuṭ* is added after the reduplication: - *ānarha* - *ānarhitha* Aorist (*luṅ*): With the augment *āṭ*, there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4): - *ārhīt* Causative (*ṇic*) with *caṅ* (reduplication): There is reduplication of the syllable *hi*: - *ārjihat* Future (*lṛṭ*): - *arhiṣyati*, etc.
These roots, excluding those marked with the indicatory letter *ū*, are invariably characterized by the augment *iṭ* and belong to the Parasmaipada (active voice).

From here onwards are *dyut* and the others. Among them, although they are invariably *ātmanepada* in other [tenses], by the rules *dyudbhyo luṅi* (Pāṇini 1.3.91), *vṛdbhyaḥ syasanoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.92), and *luṭi ca klṛpaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.93), the *ātmanepada* is optionally prescribed when followed by the suffixes *syat* (the future marker) and *san* (the desiderative marker). In that regard, in the case of the *parasmaipada*, the substitution of *aṅ* for *cl* occurs according to the rule for the *puṣādi* group; in the other case (*ātmanepada*), however, there is the *sic* suffix—such is the distinction. The root *vṛt* means "to turn."

In the case of these four roots beginning with *sy*, *san*, and *klṛp*—specifically when they take the *parasmaipada* endings—the augment *iṭ* is prohibited by the rules *na vṛdbhyaś caturbhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.59) and *tāsi ca klṛpaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.60), which fall under the governing heading *gameriṭ parasmaipadeṣu*. We shall provide examples accordingly.

The root *dyut* means "to shine. The penultimate short vowel undergoes *guṇa*. [Present tense: *dyotate*; [Imperfect: *adyotata*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), [the form is] *dyotiṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), under the heading of reduplication (*abhyāsa*), by the rule *dyutisvāpyoḥ saṃprasāraṇam* (Pāṇini 7.4.67)—which is an exception to the rule regarding the retention of the first consonant (*halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*)—there is *saṃprasāraṇa* of the letter *y*, resulting in the vowel *i*. Because of the rule *asaṃyogālliṭ kit* (Pāṇini 1.2.5), which makes the *liṭ* suffix *kit*, there is an absence of *guṇa*. [Perfect forms: *didyute*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *adyutat* or *adyotiṣṭa*. In the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist) after the causative suffix (*ṇau*): *adidyutat*. [Future: *dyotiṣyate*.
Regarding the desiderative (*san*), by the rule *ralovyupadhāt...* (Pāṇini 1.2.26), there is an option for the suffix to be *kit*. [Desiderative forms: *didyutiṣate* or *didyotiṣate*.

*Ñimidā* (to become moist): present *medate*; aorist *amidat*, *amediṣṭa*; future *mediṣyate*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), there is an option for *kit*-treatment by Pāṇini 1.2.26 (*ralovyupadhāt*), resulting in *mimidiṣate* or *mimediṣate*.

*Śvitā* (in the sense of color): present *śvetate*; benedictive *śvetiṣīṣṭa*; perfect *śiśvite*; aorist *aśvitat*, *aśvetiṣṭa*; intensive (*caṅ*) *aśiśvitat*. *Ñiṣvidā* (in the senses of becoming moist, delusion, and release).

The two [roots] *kṣar* and *sru* mean "flowing" (*gātrakṣaraṇe*), as before. *Ruc* means "to shine" (*dīptau*) and "to please" (*prītyām*). Present: *rocate*. Imperfect: *arocata*. Imperative: *rocatām*. Optative: *roceta*. Benedictive: *rociṣīṣṭa*. Perfect: *ruruce*. Aorist: *arucat*; *arociṣṭa*. Periphrastic aorist: *arūrucat*. Future: *rociṣyate*. Desiderative: *ruruciṣate*, *rurociṣate*.
*Ghuṭ* and *puṭ* mean "turning around" (*parivartane*). Present: *ghoṭate*. Imperfect: *aghoṭata*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *aghuṭat*; *aghoṭiṣṭa*.

*ruṭ* and *luṭ* mean "to shine. *Ruṭh* and *luṭh* mean "to strike against" or "to resist. In the present tense (*laṭ*), it is *loṭhate*; in the imperfect (*laṅ*), *aloṭhata*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *aluṭhat* or *aloṭhiṣṭa*. The remainder should be understood in this manner. *Śubh* means "to shine. [Present: *śobhate*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *aśubhat* or *aśobhiṣṭa*. In the desiderative (*san*), *śuśubhiṣate* or *śuśobhiṣate*.
*kṣubha* means "to move. *Kṣobhate*, etc., is as before.
*Nabha* and *tubha* mean "to injure. In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, [the forms are] *anabhat* and *anabhiṣṭa*.
*Sransu*, *dhvansu*, and *bhransu* mean "to fall down" or "to collapse."

The root *dhvansu* means "to go" and *sransu* means "to trust. According to Pāṇini’s rule *naścāpadāntasya jhali* (8.3.24), there is an *anusvāra*; thus, [the forms] are *sraṃsate*, *asraṃsata*, *sraṃsatām*, *sraṃseta*, and *sraṃsiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), *sasraṃse*. In the aorist (*luṅ*) with the suffix *aṅ*, by the rule *aniditām* (6.4.24), there is elision of the *n*: *asrasat*. In the periphrastic aorist (*luṅ* with *sic*), *asraṃsiṣṭa*.

In the causative (*ṇic*) with the suffix *caṅ* (reduplication), because the elision of the *ṇi* is treated as *sthānivadbhāva* (as if it were still present) by the rule *acaḥ parasmin* (1.1.57), and because it is considered *asiddha* (non-existent) by the rule *asiddhavadatrābhāt* (6.4.22), the elision of the *n* according to *aniditām* (6.4.24) does not occur; thus, *asasraṃsata*. In the future, *sraṃsiṣyate*.

By the rule *yaṅi nīg vañcu-sraṃsu-* (Pāṇini 7.4.84), the augment *nīg* is added to the reduplication; by the rule *aniditām-* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), there is the elision of the nasal (*n*). Thus: *sanīsras-yate*, *danīdhvas-yate*, *banībhra-syate*. The same should be applied to the others as well. However, for the root *sraṃs*, in the *yaṅ* [intensive], it becomes *sāsraṃsyate*.

The root *vṛt* means "to turn" (*vartane*). Present: *vartate*. Imperfect: *avartata*. Imperative: *vartatām*. Optative: *varteta*. Benedictive: *vartiṣīṣṭa*. Periphrastic perfect: *vavṛte*. Aorist: *avṛtat*. Conditional: *avartiṣṭa*. Regarding the forms *avīvṛtat* and *avavartat*, the grammatical operations such as those prescribed by Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.4.51 (*ṇau caṅi ṇer aniṭi*) apply. Future active: *vartsyati*. Future middle: *vartiṣyate*. Conditional active: *avartsyat*. Conditional middle: *avartiṣyata*. Periphrastic future: *vartitā*. In the desiderative (*san*), the suffix is marked with the *kit* designation according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 1.2.10 (*sani halantācca*), resulting in *vivṛtsati* (active) and *vivartiṣate* (middle). In the intensive (*yaṅ*), the augment *rīg* is added to the reduplicated syllable, yielding *varīvṛtyate*. This root is both transitive and intransitive. The root *vṛdh* means "to grow. The root *śṛdh* means "contemptuous sound"; it is treated like the previous one.

The root *syand* (meaning "to flow") is used with the suffix *āśis* (the benedictive). Because it is marked with *ū*, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*; there is also the substitution of *s* for *t*. Thus: *syantsīṣṭa* or *syandiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *sasryande*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *asyandat* or *asyandiṣṭa*; or [with the *ātmanepada* marker], *asyaṃsta*. In the causative with *caṅ* (reduplication), it is *asasyandat*. Regarding the roots *syas* and *san*, this prohibition—which applies even though the optional *iṭ* prescribed by the rule for *syand* is an internal (*antaraṅga*) factor—overrides it due to the inclusion of the word "four" (*catur*). Thus: *syansyati*; in the conditional (*luṅ*), *asyansyat*. In the periphrastic future (*luṭ*), it is *syantā*. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *sisyansati* or *sisyaniṣati*.

The root *kṛp* is used in the sense of capability (*sāmarthya*). By the rule of *guṇa* substitution and the replacement with *r* (*raparatva*), it becomes *kalp*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), we have *kalpiṣīṣṭa*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rules *iko jhal* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), *halantācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10), and *liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), there is an absence of *guṇa* due to the *kit* designation; thus, through partial modification (*ekadeśavikāra*), the *ṛ* becomes *l*, resulting in *klṛpsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *caklṛpe*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *aklṛpat* or *akalpiṣṭa*.

In the absence of the *iḍ* augment, as before, there is *kit*-tva and *latva*. By *jhalo jhali* (Pāṇini 8.2.26), there is the elision of the *sic* suffix: *aklṛpta*, *aklṛpsātām*. In the case of the causative (*ṇau*) with the *caṅ* suffix, because *latva* is considered non-existent (*asiddha*), the shortening [of the penultimate vowel] supersedes the rule for *guṇa*: *aciklapat*, *acakalpata*. [Future: *kalpsyati*, *kalpiṣyate*. [Conditional: *akalpsyat*, *akalpiṣyata*.

In the *luṭ* [future] tense, according to the view that it takes the *parasmaipada* endings, there is a prohibition by Pāṇini 7.2.60 (*tāsi ca klṛpaḥ*), resulting in *kalptāsi*; otherwise, it is *kalpitāse*. In the *san* [desiderative] suffix, by Pāṇini 1.2.10 (*sani halantācca*), the suffix is *kit*, resulting in *ciklṛpsati*. In the *liṭ* [perfect], it is *cikalpiṣyate*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, it is *carīklṛpyate*. [The roots] from *dyut* onwards and from *vṛt* onwards [are completed]. From this point forward are the *ghaṭādi* [roots].

The root *ghaṭ* is used in the sense of "exertion" (*ceṣṭā*); it forms *ghaṭate*. The root *vyath* is used in the senses of "fear" and "trembling" (*bhaya-calanayoḥ*); it forms *vyathate*. Regarding the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *vyatho liṭi* (Pāṇini 7.4.68), there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) of the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *vivyathe*. The root *prath* is used in the sense of "becoming well-known" (*prakhyāne*); it forms *prathate*. In the imperfect (*laṅ*), it forms *aprathata*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it forms *aprathiṣṭa*. When the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied and the reduplicated aorist (*caṅ*) follows—resulting in the sequence *pratha-i-a-t*—the rule *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.116) prescribes *vṛddhi* (vowel strengthening). However, because the root belongs to the *ghaṭādi* group, it receives the designation *mit*, which would normally result in shortening (*mitāṃ hrasvatvam*). Nevertheless, the rule for shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasva*) in the *caṅ* of the aorist with a causative suffix takes precedence and overrides the *vṛddhi*. Thus, [the form becomes] *apīprathat*.

Then there is a repetition [of the root]. Since the following light vowel and consonant constitute a *san*-like condition, the substitution of *i* (by Pāṇini 7.4.79, *sanyataḥ*) would apply; however, this is superseded by its exception (Pāṇini 7.2.95, *atsmṛdṛtvaraprathamradastṝspaśām*). For the roots *smṛ*, *dṛ*, *tvar*, *pratha*, *mrada*, *stṝ*, and *spaś*, when followed by a *caṅ*-ending *ṇic*, the *abhyāsa* (reduplicated syllable) undergoes the substitution of the vowel *a*. [Examples: *apaprathat* (from *pratha* "to expand").
*Mrada* means "to soften. Everything else is as before. *Pṛthu* means "to expand."
Śas means "to cut"; skhad means "to strike" or "to injure"; svad means "to taste" or "to relish."
*khaj* means "to move" and "to give"; *dakṣa* means "to move" and "to injure"; *kṛpa* means "to pity. The examples for these should be inferred.

*Ñitvarā* is used in the sense of agitation. In the *caṅ* (reduplication) of the causative (*ṇau*), it becomes *atatvarat*. With the exception of those marked with *ūdi*, those that necessarily take the suffix *iṭ* before *tāsi* are designated as *ātmanepada*.

In the case of the disease *jvara*: with the suffix *luṅ*, by the rule *ato lrāntasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.2), there is invariably *vṛddhi*; thus, *ajvārīt*. *Gala* means "to drip": *galati*. *Hela* means "to embrace": *helati*.
Naṭ (nṛttau) means to dance; vaṭa and taṭa mean to speak or address;
caka means to be satisfied.

*ṣṭaka* in the sense of striking back; their examples are to be inferred. *kakha* in the sense of laughing: in the *luṅ* tense, due to its being an *edit* vowel, there is no *vṛddhi* [substitution], resulting in *akakhīt*. *rage* in the sense of apprehension.
*lage* means to adhere; *age*, *hrage*, and *hlage* mean to cling;
*sthage* means to conceal.
*kaga* is not mentioned [in this context]. *Aka* (√ak) means to move crookedly;
*vaṇa* and *śraṇa* mean to give.

The roots *katha*, *matha*, *knatha*, and *klatha* have the meaning "to injure. The root *caṇa* is not mentioned; *vana* is also not mentioned. The root *jvala* means "to blaze"; in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, it becomes *ajvālīt*.
*jval* (to blaze), *hval* (to move), *hmala* (to move).

*Smṛ* (to remember): *smarati*, *asmarat*, *smaratu*, *smaret*. In the optative (*liṅ*) expressing a blessing, by the rules *rīṅ ṛtaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.27), *riṅ śayagliṅkṣu* (Pāṇini 7.4.28), and *guṇo’rtisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29), there is *guṇa* substitution, resulting in *smaryāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *sasmāra*.

By the rule *ṛtaśca saṃyogāder guṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.10), there is guṇa substitution: *sasmaratuḥ*, *sasmaruḥ*, *sasmartha*. By the restriction *ṛto bhāradvājasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.63), the augment *iṭ* does not occur. In the *luṅ* tense with *sic*, there is vṛddhi: *asmārṣīt*. In the causative (*ṇau*) with *caṅ*, as before, there is *ātva* for the reduplicated syllable: *asasmarat*. By the rule *ṛddhanoḥ sya* (Pāṇini 7.3.70), there is *iṭ*: *smariṣyati*. [In the conditional: *asmariṣyata*. [In the periphrastic future: *smartā*.

In the case of the suffix *san*, [the following rules apply]: by Pāṇini 6.4.16 (*sani ajjhanagamām sani*), there is lengthening; by 1.2.9 (*iko jhal*), there is *kit*-status; by 7.1.100 (*ṛt iddhātoḥ*) and 7.1.102 (*udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*), there is the substitution of *u*; and by 8.2.77 (*hali ca*), there is lengthening. However, doubling (*dvirvacana*) by 8.4.46 (*aco rahābhyāṃ dve*) does not occur for the *sakāra*, because of the prohibition in 8.4.49 (*śaro'ci*). From the root ending in *san*—namely *jñā*, *śru*, *smṛ*, and *dṛś*—[the suffix *liṭ* is applied] by Pāṇini 3.1.55 (*jñāśrusmṛdṛśāṃ sanaḥ*).

In the case of *susmūrṣate*, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is applied according to [Pāṇini 1.3.57]. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, there is a *guṇa* substitution for the root *smṛ* because it begins with a consonant and ends in a vowel, by [Pāṇini 7.4.29] and [7.3.94]; then follows reduplication and the lengthening of the vowel in the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *sāsmaryate*.

The root *dṛ* is used in the sense of fear (*bhaya*). In the sense of blessing (*āśis*), by Pāṇini 7.1.100, the vowel *ṛ* of the root becomes *i*, and by 8.2.77, there is lengthening before a consonant (*hal*), resulting in *dīryāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), it is *dadāra*. By Pāṇini 7.4.12, "for *śṝ*, *dṝ*, and *prā*, there is optionally shortening," the vowel is shortened, resulting in *dadratuḥ* and *dadruḥ*. In the alternative case, by that same rule, there is *guṇa* substitution, resulting in *dadaratuḥ* and *dadaruḥ*. The form *dadaritha* [occurs]. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *adārīt*. In the causative with *caṅ* (reduplication), as before, there is *ātvam* for the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *adadarat*. The forms *dariṣyati* etc., follow. The root *nṛ* is used in the senses of leading and so forth; *narati* etc., [follow]. In the causative with *caṅ*, it is *anīranat*.

The root *śrā* is used in the sense of cooking; we shall provide examples for it under the section on roots beginning with *ad*. Its inclusion here is for the purpose of assigning it the technical designation *mit*.

For the roots *jñā*—in the senses of killing, pleasing, and perceiving—the designation *mit* applies when these meanings such as killing and so forth are intended. The root *cali* is designated *mit* in the sense of trembling.
*chadiḥ* is used in the sense of covering;
*laḍiḥ* is used in the sense of binding the tongue. *Chadi* and *laḍi* belong to the curādigaṇa.
*Madī*, meaning joy and languor, belongs to the divādigaṇa.
The roots *jan*, *jṛṣ*, *kna*, *suran*, and *añj* are also included as those ending in *am*.
*Jan* and *jṛṣ* belong to the Divādi class;

*ṇasi* (the root *ṇas*) is used in the sense of crookedness (*kauṭilye*). Here, the roots *rañj* and those ending in *am* are the ones intended. These—*jval*, *hval*, *hmal*, *svan*, *dhvan*, *ram*, *nam*, and *man*—are optionally [treated as such] when preceded by a prefix (*anusargāt*). Furthermore, for the roots *ślāgh*, *nu*, and *vam*, and for the roots *kam*, *yam*, and *cam*, the designation *it* which would otherwise apply because they end in *am* is prohibited.
The root *śam* is used in the sense of seeing;
*yam* in the sense of serving food;

and *skhad* after the prefixes *ra* and *pari*. The roots beginning with *ghaṭ* are marked as *mit*. Among the subsequent roots beginning with *phaṇ*, for seven of them, there is optionally the substitution of *e* for the radical vowel and the elision of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa-lopa*) in the *liṭ* (perfect) tense when the suffix *thal* follows and is accompanied by the augment *iṭ*, according to the rule "phaṇaśca saptānām."

The root *phaṇ* means "to go. It forms *phaṇati*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *paphāṇa*, *pheṇatuḥ*, *pheṇuḥ*; in the perfect, *pheṇitha* or *paphaṇitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *aphāṇīt* or *aphaṇīt*.
[Roots] ending in *ṛ*, excluding those with a penultimate vowel, are *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*) and take the *parasmaipada* endings.

The root *rājṛ* means "to shine. It forms *rājati* and *rājate*. Aorist: *arājat*, *arājata*. Imperative: *rājatu*, *rājatām*. Optative: *rājet*, *rājeta*. Precative: *rājyāt*, *rājiṣīṣṭa*. Perfect tense: *rarāja*, *reje*; *reraje*, *rejatuḥ*; *rarājatuḥ*, *rarājāte*; *rejāñcakre*, *rejuḥ*; *rarājuḥ*, *rejire*, *rarājire*. Forms such as *rarājitha* and so forth should be applied accordingly.
The languages on both sides of the boundary.

The roots *ṭubhrājṛ*, *ṭubhrāśṛ*, and *ṭubhlāśṛ* mean "to shine. [In the present tense: *bhrājate*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *bhreje* and *babhrāje*. By the rule *vā bhrāśa-bhlāśa-bhramu-trasa-truṭi-laṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.70), the suffix *śyan* optionally applies; thus, *bhrāśate* and *bhrāśyate*. In the perfect, [the forms are] *bhreśe* and *babhrāśe*; [and with the other root,] *bhleśe* and *babhlāśe*. In the causative with the *caṅ* suffix, [the forms are] *ababhrāśat* and *ababhlāśat*. Because it is marked with an indicatory *ṛ* (*ṛdit*), the shortening of the vowel is prohibited; however, for *bhrāj*, there is an option: *ababhrājat* or *abibhrāśat*. These are *seṭ* roots and belong to the *ātmanepada*.

The root *syam* is used in the sense of sound (*dhvani*, *śabda*). In the present tense (*laṭ*), it is *syāmati*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *sasyāma*, *sasyamatuḥ*, *sasyamuḥ*; [and] *syemitha*, *sasyamitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *hmyanta* (Pāṇini 7.2.5), there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi*, resulting in *asyamīt*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the rule *svapisyamivyeñāṃ yaṅi* (Pāṇini 6.1.19), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*); thus, *sesimyate*. It also means "it sounds" (*svanati*) or "it resounds" (*dhvanati*). In the perfect tense, it is as before. The root *jval* is used in the sense of flaming; it is cited among the *ghaṭādi* roots. The root *cal* is used in the sense of trembling.
*Jala* means water; *dhānya* means grain;
*tala* and *ṭvala* mean deficiency;
and *sthala* means place.
*Hala* means to plough;
*nala* means fragrance;
*pala* means to go.
*bala* in the sense of breathing;
*śala* and *hvala* in the sense of moving; as before;
*pula* in the sense of greatness.
Regarding the formation of the *kula* stem and the *bandhu* stems, the examples for these should be inferred accordingly.

The root *pat* means "to go. In the present tense (*laṭ*), it is *patati*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *papāta*, *petatuḥ*, *petuḥ*, *papattha* (or *pepitha*). In the aorist (*luṅ*), because it is marked with the *ḷ*-diacritic, the augment *puṅ* is applied by Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.19, *pataḥ pum* [in the aorist], resulting in *apaptat*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), by the rule Pāṇini 7.2.49, *sanīvantardha...* and specifically by the rule *tanipatidaridrāṇām*, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*; thus, one may have *pipatiṣati*.

In the absence of *iḍ*, by the rule *sani mīmāghurabhalabhaśakapatapadāmaca iṭ* (Pāṇini 7.4.59), there is the elision of the first letter of the conjunct (*saṃyogādilopa*). Thus, in the *san* [desiderative] suffix, we have *pipatsati*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, by the rule *nīgvañcusraṃsu...* (Pāṇini 7.4.84), the augment *nīg* is added to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*), resulting in *panīpatyate*.

The root *kvath* means "to boil" or "to cook. In the *luṅ* [aorist], because it has the marker *eṭ*, there is no shortening of the vowel; thus, *akvathīt*. The forms *kvathiṣyati* etc. follow accordingly. The root *math* means "to churn" or "to agitate."

In the sense of "gone" (*pathe gatau*), it is as before. The root *ṭuvam* is used in the sense of "vomiting" (*udgiraṇe*). It forms *vamati*. In the *liṭ* (perfect tense), it becomes *vavāma*. Because it belongs to the *vad* group, by the rule *na śasadadavādiguṇānām* (Pāṇini 6.4.126), the substitution of *et* and the elision of the reduplication do not occur; thus, *vavamatuḥ*, *vavamuḥ*, and *vavamitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *hmyanta* (Pāṇini 7.2.5), there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi*; hence, *avamīt*. In the future, it is *vamiṣyati*.

The root *bhram* means "to wander. It takes the *śyan* affix according to the rule *bhrāśa-bhlāśa-bhrama...* (*Pāṇini* 3.1.70). In the present tense, one forms *bhramati* or *bhrāmyati*; the lengthening of the vowel occurs according to the rule *śamādīnām* (*Pāṇini* 7.3.74). In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), by the rule *vṛ-bhramu-trasām* (*Pāṇini* 6.4.124), there is an option for the substitution of *e* and the elision of the reduplication, resulting in *bebhrāma*, *babhrāma*, *vabhrāma*, *vabhrama*, *vabhrāma*, *babhrama*, *vavre*, *vavre*, *vavruḥ*, *vavruḥ*. In the case of *bhram*, the options are *bhrematuḥ* or *babhramatuḥ*, and *bhremuḥ* or *babhramuḥ*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *abhramīt*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the addition of *nuṭ* to the reduplication, it becomes *baṃbhrāmyate*.

The root *kṣar* means "to flow"; it is both transitive and intransitive. Examples: *kṣarati kṣīram* ("the milk flows") and *kṣarati gauḥ* ("the cow flows [milk]"). In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *ato lrāntasya* (*Pāṇini* 7.2.2), it is *akṣārīt*. These roots ending in *tāsi* are *seṭ* and belong to the *parasmaipada* voice.

The root *ṣaha* is used in the sense of endurance (*marṣaṇe*). It takes the form *satvam* [with the substitution of *sa* for *ṣa*] in the sense that it "endures" (*sahate*). Regarding the rule *parinivibhyaḥ parasya sevasitasayasivusahasuṭstusvañjām* (Pāṇini 8.3.70), which prescribes the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*, this is prescribed even though the prohibition by the rule *sātpadādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.111)—which would have barred the application of *iṇkoḥ ādeśapratyayoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.59)—would otherwise apply. Thus, one forms *viṣahate*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, the substitution of *ṣ* optionally applies according to the rule *sivādīnāṃ vāḍvyavāye’pi*, resulting in either *vyaṣahiṣṭa* or *vyasahiṣṭa*. The same applies subsequently when the suffix *ṇic* is added and *caṅ* (the reduplication of the aorist) follows.

By the rule *stambhu-sivu-sahāṃ caṅi* (Pāṇini 6.1.15), there is a prohibition against the substitution of *ṣ*. Thus: *vyasīṣahat*, *sahiṣyate*, *asahiṣyata*. In the *luṭ* (future) tense, by the rule *tīṣasaha-lubha-rudha-ma-daḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.48), there is an optional *iṭ*. Hence: *sahitā*. In the absence of *iṭ*, after the application of *ḍhatva*, *ṣṭutva*, and *ḍhalopa*, the rule *ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho’ṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.3.111) is superseded by its exception, *sahivahor odavarṇasya* (Pāṇini 6.3.112), which effects *utva*. Since the root begins with *sa*, the rule for *ṣatva* would have applied as before due to a prefix; however, this is prohibited by the rule *soḍhaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.115). Thus: *visoḍhā*.

The root *ram* is used in the sense of "to play" (*krīḍā*). Present: *ramate* (he plays). Imperfect: *aramata*. Imperative: *ramatām*. Optative: *rameta*. Benedictive: *raṃsīṣṭa*. Perfect: *reme*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *araṃsta*. Future: *raṃsyate*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), it becomes *raṃramyate*. When the rule *vyāṅparibhyo ramaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.83) applies, the Parasmaipada (active voice) is used; thus, in that case: *viramati*. In the Aorist (*luṅ*) under the heading of Parasmaipada, by the rule *yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.73), there is the addition of *sak* to the stem as well as the augment *iṭ*; thus: *vyaraṃsīt*, *vyaraṃsiṣṭām*.

They ceased [to be aniṭ] after the root *sah* and others, except when followed by a suffix beginning with a consonant (*val*) that has an indicatory *ṅ* (*seṭ*) in the *ārdhadhātuka* state, or when the *niṣṭhā* suffixes are used; however, the *tās* suffix is optionally [aniṭ]. Among those ending in *yam*, *nam*, and *ram*, only one is accepted as being aniṭ. Both *rami* and *yam* are recited in the *śyan* class (the tenth class); *maṇi* is the fourth, *han* is the fifth, and *gam* is the sixth among those expressing prohibitions.
Thus ends the section on roots that are invariably aniṭ in the ātmanepada.

The root *ṣad* is used in the senses of falling apart, going, and sinking. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.3.78—*pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartisartiśadasadāṃ pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchadhauśīyasīdāḥ*—the eleven substitutes beginning with *piba* are applied respectively to the eleven roots beginning with *pā* when followed by a suffix marked with *ś*. Regarding the application of *śit*, for the roots beginning with *pā*, the substitutes *piba* and so forth occur; thus, for the eleven [roots], the substitutes *piba* and so forth occur in their respective order. In this context, concerning the domain of *śit*, the rule *aprater upasargāt iṇaḥ parasya sadir aprateḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.66) prescribes the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* in the verb *sad*, as in the form *niṣīdati*.

Regarding the rule *aḍvyavāye’pi* ("even when there is an intervention by *aṭ*"): he sat down (*nyaṣīdat*). In the case of the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, the prohibition of *ṣatva* for the letter following the reduplication of the roots *sad* and *svañj* applies by the rule *liṭi sadisvañjyoḥ parasya liṭi*. Thus: *niṣasāda*, *niṣedatuḥ*, *niṣeduḥ*. By the rule *vali upadeśetvataḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.62), there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ* which would otherwise be required by the restriction of the *kry-ādi* group. Regarding the rule *ṛto bhāradvājasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.63), it is made optional; thus, the prohibition of *ṣatva* in the reduplication is also optional. [In the second person singular *thāl*: *niṣasattha*]. When [the *th*] is elided, it does not exist [and thus no *ṣatva* occurs]: *niṣeditha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], because the root is marked with *ḷt*, the suffix is *aṅ*: *nyaṣadat*.

The root *śad* is used in the sense of "falling" (*śātana*). In the domain of the *śit* affixes, the Ātmanepada is applied by the rule *śadeḥ śitaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.60), and in that very context, there is the substitution of *śī* [for *śad*]. Thus: *śīyate*. In the past tense: *aśīyata*. In the imperative: *śīyatām*. In the optative: *śīyeta*. In the benedictive: *śayyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the form is] *śaśāda*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), [the form is] *aśadat*. When the causative suffix *ṇic* is added and the reduplication (*caṅ*) follows, except in the sense of "going," the rule *śaderagatau taḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.42) applies the substitution of *t* [for the final *d*], resulting in *aśīśatat*.

The root *kruś* is used in the senses of calling out and weeping. In the present tense (*laṭ*), it is *krośati*. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), it is *cukrośa*; by the rule regarding roots beginning with *krādi*, the augment *iṭ* is added, resulting in *cukrośitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), the suffix *ksa* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.45 (*śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ*). Due to the *kit* nature of the suffix, there is no *guṇa* strengthening; the rules for *ṣatva*, *katva*, and *ṣatva* apply, resulting in *ākrukṣat*. The future form is *krokṣyati*, and so forth. The root *kruc* is used in the senses of rubbing together, crookedness, obstruction, and scratching. Forms such as *ākuñcati* ("he contracts") and others follow from this root.

The root *budh* (to understand): *bodhati*. In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense: *bubodha*, *bubodhitha*, *abodhīt*, *bodhiṣyati*, and so forth. The root *ruh* (to grow, from the production of a seed): *rohati*. [In the imperfect: *arohat*. In the *liṭ* tense: *ruroha*, *rurohitha*. By the rule regarding roots beginning with *krā* etc., the augment *iṭ* is applied. In the *luṅ* [aorist], the *cleḥ* is replaced by *ksa*; then the substitution of *ḍha*, *ka*, and *ṣa* take place: *aruksat*, *aruksatām*, *aruksan*. By the rule *ṇau caṅi ruhaḥ po’nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 7.3.43), the letter *ha* is optionally changed to *pa* when the suffix *caṅ* follows a causative (*ṇic*): *arūruhat* or *arūrupat*. [In the future: *rokṣyati*, and so forth. In the desiderative (*san*), because of the rule *halantācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10), there is *kit*-status, and thus an absence of *guṇa*: *ārurukṣati*.
The root *kas* means "to go. From *kas* with the suffix *yaṅ*, the reduplicated form becomes *cakasate*.
[The following roots are also included: *adi*, *hadi*, *skandi*, *bhid*, *chid*, *kṣud*, *rād*, *svidyati*, *padyati*, *khidi*, *tudi*, *nudi*, *vidyati*, and *vindi*.
"Pass over the ten and five that are aniṭ," [it is said].
*śad* and *sad* are aniṭ.

The ancient grammarians recite these eight roots as ending in *i* and being aniṭ (not taking the augment *iṭ*)— namely *dṛśi*, *diśi*, *daṃśi*, *mathi*, *mṛśi*, *spṛśi*, *nuśi*, *riśi*, *krośati*, and eighthly *viśi* and *liśi*;
among those readings, only these ten are accepted and no others.
Thus he cries out: "The roots *aniṭ* (those without an indicatory *i*) are *kuci*,
*budhi*, *siṭau* (the two with an indicatory *s*), *kasi*, *dihi*, *duhi*, *mahi*, *rohati*,
*vahih*, *nāh*, *tuṣaṣṭaḥ*, *dahati*, and likewise *lihi*."
These eight roots ending in *h* have been proclaimed as being without the augment *iṭ*, free from doubt, and divided among the classes [of roots].
Thus ends the section on roots ending in *h* that lack *iṭ* in the rule for the suffix *ṇa*; these roots beginning with *jval* and ending with *kas* take the *parasmaipada* (active voice).
*Hikka* is used in the sense of an indistinct sound; one *hikkati* or *hikkate*. *Arca* means "to go" and "to beg"; some say it means "to go. One *arcati* or *ārcat*.

The root *ṭuyācṛ* is used in the sense of begging (*yāñcā*). It forms *yācati* and *yācate*; it takes two objects (*dvikarmakaḥ*). The roots *cate* and *cade* are also used in the sense of begging. They form *catati* and *catate*. Because of the vowel *e*, there is no *vṛddhi* substitution in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense: *acatīt* and *acatiṣṭa*. The same applies to *cade*. The root *prothṛ* is used in the sense of sufficiency (*paryāpti*). It forms *prothati* and *prothate*. In the *caṅ* (periphrastic perfect) tense, it becomes *apuprothat*.
*midṛ* and *medṛ* mean "to injure" (*ahiṃsā*).
*Midhṛ* and *medhṛ* mean "to meet" (*saṃgama*).
*Sidṛ* and *sedṛ* mean "censure" (*kutsā*) and "proximity" (*sannikarṣa*).

The roots *śṛ*, *dhṛ*, and *mṛ* mean "to wet. Examples for these should be inferred. The root *ubundir* means "to perceive clearly. The verbal root (*dhātu*) lies between the two indicatory letters (*anubandha*). [In the present tense: *bundati*, *bundate*. The root *khanu* means "to dig. [Present: *khanati*, *khanate*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *gamahana...* (Pāṇini 6.4.98), there is elision of the penultimate vowel: *cakhāna*, *cakhne*; *cakhnatuḥ*, *cakhnuḥ*; *cakhanitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *akhanīt*, *akhānīt*, *akhaniṣṭa*. In the periphrastic reduplicated aorist (*caṅ*): *acīkhanat*. [Future: *khaniṣyati*. In the desiderative (*san*): *cikhaniṣati*, *cikhaniṣate*.

Under the governing rule *yaṅi janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.42), there is an optional substitution of *āt* by the rule *ye vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini 6.4.43): *cākhāyate*, *caṅkhyate*. From the root *cāyṛ* in the sense of "worship" or "perception," one has *cāyati* and *cāyate*. In the *yaṅ* formation, there is the substitution of *kī* by the rule *cāyaḥ kī* (Pāṇini 6.1.41), and by the rule *guṇo yaṅ-lukoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.82), there is *guṇa* substitution, resulting in *cekīyate*.

The roots *vyaya* in the sense of "to go" and "to spend": *vyayati*, *vyayate*. In the *liṭ* (perfect tense), [the forms are] *vavyāya* and *vavyaye*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *hmyanta* (Pāṇini 7.2.5), there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi* in the *parasmaipada*: *avyayīt*. In the *ātmanepada*, since there is no occasion for *vṛddhi*, [the form is] *avyayiṣṭa*. The root *dāśṛ* in the sense of "to give": *dāśati*, *dāśate*.
The root *lasa* in the sense of "shining": *lasati*, *lasate*.

The root *spaś* is used in the senses of "hindering" and "touching. It is conjugated as *spaśati* (Parasmaipada) and *spaśate* (Ātmanepada). In the *luṅ* (aorist), the forms are *aspaśīt*, *aspāśīt*, and *aspaśiṣṭa*. In the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist) of the *ṇic* (causative), by the rule *smṛdṝtvara-prathimradisraji-sādhyaścaṅi* (Pāṇini 7.4.95), the vowel of the reduplication is changed to *a*, resulting in *apaspāśat*.

The root *laṣ* is used in the sense of "desire. By the rule *vā bhrāśa-bhlāśa-bhramu-kas-pata-manāvam* (Pāṇini 3.1.70), the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied. Thus, one forms *abhilaṣati*, *abhilaṣyati*, *abhilaṣate*, and *abhilaṣyate*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), the forms are *abhilalāṣa* and *abhileṣe*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), one should apply the forms *abhyalaṣat*, *abhyalāṣīt*, *abhyalaṣiṣṭa*, and so forth. The root *caṣ* is used in the sense of "eating. It is conjugated as *caṣati* and *caṣate*.

The root *māsṛ* is used in the sense of measuring: *māsati*, *māsate*. The root *guhū* is used in the sense of concealing. Regarding the domain of *guṇa*, by the rule *ūdupadhāyā gohaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.89), there is the substitution of *ū* for the penultimate vowel in *guh*: *nigūhati*, *nigūhate*. In the aorist: *nyagūhat*, *nyagūhata*. In the optative: *nigūhet*, *nigūheta*. In the benedictive: *nigūhyāt*. Due to the presence of the marker *ū*, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*: *nigūhiṣṭa*, *nigūhiṣīṣṭa*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), the suffix is marked with *k* (*kit*), which causes the absence of *guṇa*; consequently, there is no substitution of *ū*. Thus: *nighukṣiṣṭa*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*): *nijugūha*, *nijugūhatuḥ*.

*nijugūhuḥ* | *nijugūhitha*. In the absence of *iṭ*, optionally, after the application of *ḍhatva*, *dhatva*, and *ṣṭutva*, [the forms are] *nijugūḍha*, *nijugūhe*, *nijugūhāte*. In the *luṅ* tense, with the presence of *iṭ*: *nyagūhīt*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.45), and with *ḍhatva* etc. as before, [the form is] *nyaghukṣat*.

Under the governing rule *ksasyāci* (Pāṇini 7.3.72), which states that there is an optional elision (*lugvā*) of the suffix *kṣa* when followed by an affix beginning with a dental consonant in the *ātmanepada*, the following occurs: when an *ātmanepada* affix beginning with a dental follows, there is optionally an elision of *kṣa*. In the case of elision, the operations such as *ḍhatva* apply, resulting in *nyagūḍha*. In the absence of elision, *nyaghukṣata* is formed. When an affix beginning with a vowel follows, by the rule *ksasyāci* (Pāṇini 7.3.72), there is the elision of the element ending in the suffix *kṣa*, resulting in *nyaghukṣātām*, *nyaghukṣata*, and *nyaghukṣathāḥ*.

In the *luk* (zero) alternative, there is the substitution of *ḍha* for *dha*, the substitution of *ṣṭu* for *ṣṭu*, the elision of *ḍh* and *ra*, and lengthening; these [operations] are hidden (*nyagūḍhāḥ*). As before, there is the elision of the suffix ending in *kas*: *nyaghukṣāthām*, *nyaghūḍhvam*, *nyaghukṣadhvam*. With the elision of the suffix ending in *kas*: *nyaghukṣi*; furthermore, the *v* is dental: *nyaghukṣvahi*, *nyaghukṣāvahi*, *nyaghukṣmahi*. In the *iṭ* alternative: *nyagūhiṣṭa*, *nyagūhiṣātām*.
