In the *caṅ* (reduplication) after *ṇi*: *nyajūguhat*. [Future: *nigūhiṣyati*, *nighukṣyati*; [middle voice: *nigūhiṣyate*, *nighukṣyate*. The remainder is to be inferred.

By the rule *sani sani grahaguhośca* (Pāṇini 7.2.12), there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ*. By the rule *halantācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10), the suffix is *kit*. Thus: *nijughukṣati*, *nijughukṣate*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix: *nijoguhyate*. The root *śriñ* is used in the sense of "service" (*sevā*). It takes the forms *śrayati* and *śrayate*. In the *liṅ* for benediction (*āśis*), when not followed by a *yakāra* suffix, there is lengthening: *śrīyāt*, *śrayiṣīṣṭa*. One should observe that it is a non-*iṭ* root ending in a vowel.
Those who know the truth declare that the following roots take the suffix *sruṣ* [the *kṛt* affix *kvip*]:
roots ending in *ad*, roots ending in *ū*, the roots *ṛ*, *vṛṅ*, *vṛṅ*, *śvi*, *iṅ*, and those ending in *i*, as well as *śīṅ* and *śriñ*.

Thus, the root *śri* takes the augment *iṭ* in the *liṭ* (perfect tense): *śiśrāya*, *śiśriye*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *ṇiśrītyādinā cleścaṅ* (*Pāṇini* 6.1.11), there is reduplication; with *iyaṅ*, [the forms] are *aśiśriyat* and *aśiśrayata*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with *caṅ*, it is *aśiśriyat*. [The future forms are] *śrayiṣyati*, and so forth. In the desiderative (*san*), by the rule *sanīvantarddha* (*Pāṇini* 7.2.49), there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*: *śiśrayiṣati* or *śiśrīṣati*.

The root *hṛ* is used in the sense of "taking away. In the Ārdhadhātuka affix *liṅ*, by the rule *riṅ śayagliṅkṣu* (Pāṇini 7.4.28), *riṅ* is substituted [for the radical vowel]; thus, *hriyāt*. By the rule *uś ca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), because the affix is *kit*, there is an absence of *guṇa*; thus, *hṛṣīṣṭa*. In *liṭ*: *jahāra*, *jahvartha*, *jahre*. In *luṅ* with *sic*, there is *vṛddhi*; thus, *ahārṣīt*. By the rule *uś ca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), there is *kit*-ness, and by *hrasvādaṅgāt* (Pāṇini 8.2.27), there is the elision of *sic*; thus, *ahṛta*, *ahṛṣātām*. By the rule *ṛddhanoḥ sye* (Pāṇini 7.2.70), there is *iṭ*; thus, *hariṣyati*. [In the conditional: *ahariṣyat*.

He will take (*hariṣyate*); he would have taken (*ahariṣyata*); he is one who takes (*hartā*). Regarding the desiderative suffix (*san*), by the rule *iko jhal* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), there is *kit*-tva, which results in lengthening and so forth: *jihīrṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the rule *rīṅ ṛtaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.27), there is the substitution of *rīṅ*: *jehrīyate*. When the fruit of the action does not benefit the agent, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used by the rule *harater gatitācchīlye* ("after *hṛ*, when meaning 'to imitate' or 'habitual movement'): *aśvāḥ paitṛkam anuharante* ("the horses imitate their father").

The root *bhṛ* is used in the sense of "supporting" (*bharaṇe*). Forms such as *bharati* and *bharate* are to be understood as before. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), there is an option for the augment *iṭ* by the rule *sanīvantarddhabhrasja0* (Pāṇini 7.2.49), etc.; thus we have *bibhariṣati*. In the absence of *iṭ*, after the lengthening and the *kit*-status [of the suffix] have been applied, the substitution of *u* occurs by the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya* (Pāṇini 7.1.102), and then the lengthening occurs by the rule *hali ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.77); thus we have *bubhūrṣati*. The root *dhṛ* is used in the sense of "holding" (*dhāraṇe*); everything regarding its forms is like that of *bhṛ*.

The root *ṇī* (ṇīñ) is used in the sense of "leading to" (*prāpaṇe*). According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.1.65, *ṇo naḥ*, the *ṇ* of *nayati* is replaced by *n*. The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is prescribed for *nayate* when it signifies respect and so forth, provided the result accrues to the agent (*kartrabhiprāye*). However, according to the rule *svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye kriyāphale* (Pāṇini 1.3.72), the active voice (*parasmaipada*) is used otherwise, as per the general rule of the remainder (*śeṣāt*). Thus: *nayati* (active) and *nayate* (middle). In the optative (*liṅ*) expressing a benediction (*āśiṣi*), we have *nīyāt* and *neṣīṣṭa*; [in the middle voice] *neṣīyāstam*.

Regarding the middle plural [ending], Pāṇini’s rule *iṇaḥ ṣīdhvaṃluṅliṭāṃ dho’ṅgāt* (8.3.78) states that the dental *dha* of the suffixes *ṣīdhvam*, *luṅ*, and *liṭ* following an *aṅga* ending in the vowel *i* is replaced by a cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) substitute. Thus, *neṣīḍhvam*. In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], *nināya*. By the rule *eranekācaḥ* (6.4.82), the *yaṇ* replacement occurs: *ninyatuḥ*, *ninyuḥ*. Regarding the *thal* [suffix], there is an optional *iṭ* augment due to the restriction *ṛto bhāradvājasya* (7.2.63): *ninetha* or *ninayitha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], with the *sic* suffix, there is *vṛddhi* [increment]: *aneṣīt*, *aneṣṭa*, *aneṣātām*.

*dhvam*: as before, the cerebral [substitute] occurs; thus *aneḍḍhvam*. However, regarding the *liṭ* [perfect], by Pāṇini 8.3.79 (*vibhāṣeṭaḥ*), when an *iṭ* augment follows an *aṅga* ending in *iṇ*, the *dh* of the following *ṣīdhvam*, *luṅ*, or *liṭ* optionally becomes a cerebral. Here, by the rule governing the *kryādigaṇa*, the *iṭ* is applied: *ninyiḍhve* or *ninyidhve*. Thus, upon considering these two sūtras, a cerebral substitute must be prescribed everywhere for the *dh* of *ṣīdhvam* and so on, when it follows an *aṅga* ending in *iṇ*. [Roots] ending in *ṛ*, with the exception of *nayati*, which take the *iṭ* augment, are of both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣā*).

The root *dheṭ* means "to drink. The letter *ṭ* is for the purpose of specification, as in the rule *nāsikāstanayordhmādheṭoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.2.29). He drinks: *dhayati*. In the imperfect (*laṅ*) of the *ārdhadhātuka*: *adhat*—here, by the rule *ādeca upadeśe 'śiti* (Pāṇini 6.1.45), there is substitution of *ā*; then by *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali* (Pāṇini 6.4.66), there is substitution of *i*; and finally by *erliṅi* (Pāṇini 6.4.67), there is substitution of *e*, resulting in *dheyāt*.

In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, by the rule *tipo ṇal āta au ṇal* (Pāṇini 7.1.34), there is the substitution of *au* for *ti*, and *vṛddhi* [increment]. Thus, *dadhau*. By the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.64), there is the elision of the vowel *ā*. Thus, *dadhatuḥ*. [The forms are] *dadhau*, *dadhatuḥ*, *dadhathuḥ*, *dada*, *dadhātha* or *dadhitha*.

By the rule *vibhāṣā dhrā-dheṭ-śā-saḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.78), there is the elision (*luk*) of *sic*. By the rule *vibhāṣā dheṭ-syoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.49), there is optionally the substitution of *caṅ* for *cli*. Consequently, there is a threefold form. In that case where *caṅ* occurs, there is reduplication by the rule *caṅi* (Pāṇini 6.1.11), and the elision of the vowel *ā* by the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.64), resulting in *adadhāt*. When *sic* is elided, it is *adhāt*. In the absence of both [the elision of *sic* and the substitution of *caṅ*], there is the augment *īṭ* by the rule *yamarama...* (Pāṇini 7.2.73) et al., which adds the augment *niṭ*, resulting in *adhāsīt* and *adhāsiṣṭām*.

By the rule *sijabhyastavidibhyaśca* (Pāṇini 3.4.109), *jhi* is replaced by *jus*: *adhāsiṣuḥ*. In the case of the causative suffix *ṇic* followed by *caṅ*, we have *adīdhavat*. Regarding forms such as *dhāsyati*: in the desiderative (*san*), by the rule *sani mīmā...* (Pāṇini 7.4.54) and others, there is the replacement of *e* and the elision of the reduplication; then, by the rule *saḥ syārdhadhātuke* (Pāṇini 7.4.49), the *s* is changed to *t*, resulting in *dhitsati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the rule *ghumāsthā...* (Pāṇini 6.4.66) and others, there is the replacement of *i* because of the designation *ghu*; thereafter, reduplication occurs, yielding *dedhīyate*.

The root *glai* is used in the sense of "fading away" (*harṣakṣaye*). It forms *glāyati* (present), *aglāyat* (imperfect). With reference to the rule *āśiṣi liṅi* (Pāṇini 6.4.67), under the heading of *vānyasya saṃyogādeḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.68), there is the substitution of *e* for the *ā* of [the root] ending in *ā*, provided it is other than those beginning with *ghu*, *mā*, *sthā*, etc. Thus, for a root ending in *ā*, beginning with a consonant cluster (*saṃyoga*), and other than those starting with *ghu*, *mā*, *sthā*, etc., the substitution of *e* occurs optionally before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix in the *liṅ* (optative). Hence: *glāyāt* or *gleyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), [it forms] *jaglau*, *jaglātha* or *jaglitha*. Here, by the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.64), because of the mention of *iṭ* [in that sūtra], the elision of the long *ā* occurs. In the *luṅ* (aorist), [it forms] *aglāsīt*.

*aglāsiṣṭām*. Even though there is *mit*-status due to the inclusion [of *glai*] in the *ghaṭādi* group by the rule "ṇau caṅy upadhāyā hrasvaḥ" (*Pāṇini* 7.4.1), the shortening does not occur here; rather, by the rule "mitāṃ hrasvaḥ" (*Pāṇini* 6.4.92), we have *ajiglapat*.
[The roots] *mlai* (to bend the limbs) and *dyai* (to fade) take the *nyat* suffix in the sense of a verbal derivative (*bhāve*).
The root *dru* means "to sleep";
*dhyai* means "in thinking" (*cintāyām*);
and *rai* means "in sound" (*śabde*).
*styai* and *ṣṭyai* mean "to congeal" or "to assemble";
*śrai* and *srai* mean "to cook";
*kṣai* means "to surround."

*kṣai* in the sense of wasting away (*kṣaye*); as before. *dai* in the sense of purifying (*śodhane*). The letter *p* [in the root *dāp*] is for the purpose of general inclusion in the rule *dādhāghvadāp* (Pāṇini 1.1.20). [Present tense: *dāyati*; [imperfect: *adāyat*. In the benedictive (*āśiṣi*): *dāyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *dadau*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *adāsīt*. [Future: *dāsyati*, and so forth.
*dai* in the sense of flowing (*nyakṣaraṇe*).
*Khāi* and *khanane* mean "to eat"; *khāi* also means "in destruction"; *pai*, *ovai*, and *vai* mean "in drying up."

The roots *kai*, *gai*, and *rai* are as before. From *gai*: in the present tense, *gāyate*; in the benedictive (*liṅ*) and the intensive (*yaṅ*), *agīyāt*; in the present indicative, *kāyati* and *gāyati*; in the benedictive, *geyāt*; in the intensive, *jāgīyate*. The form *jegīyate* is thus derived.

The root *pā* means "to drink. In the domain of the *śit* affixes, the substitute *piba* is applied by the rule *pāghrādhmādheṭdṛśaḥ śaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.78), resulting in *pibati*. The forms are: *apibat*, *pibatu*, *pibet*. For the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), the substitution of *ī* prescribed by *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisām liṭi* (Pāṇini 6.4.66) is barred; instead, by *eliṅi* (Pāṇini 6.4.67), the substitution of *e* applies, yielding *peyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), the form is *papau*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), the suffix *sic* is elided by *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 2.4.77), resulting in *apāt*. The dual is *apātām*. By the rule *ātaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.110), the suffix *jhi* is replaced by *jus*; when followed by *usi*, the single-substitute rule (*pararūpatvam*) applies, resulting in *apuḥ*.

When *ṇau caṅi pā i* (Pāṇini 6.1.41) has been established, the rule *śācchāsāhnāvyāvepāṃ yuk* (Pāṇini 7.3.37)—which prescribes the augment *yuk* after the roots *śo*, *chā*, *so*, *hna*, *vyā*, *ve*, and *pā* when followed by *ṇi*—applies. This *yuk* is an exception (*apavāda*) to the *puṅ* augment. Furthermore, the rule *ṇau caṅyupadhāyā hrasvaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.1) is superseded by *lopaḥ pibaterīccābhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 7.4.4), which prescribes the elision of the penultimate vowel and the substitution of *ī* for the reduplicated syllable of *pā*. This is because of the indicator (*jñāpaka*) in the rule *oḥ puyaṇjyapara* (Pāṇini 7.4.80), which teaches that what is effected by *ṇi* is treated as if it were the original element (*sthānivat*).

The reduplication of *pā* is for the purpose of the operations of the reduplicated stem (*abhyāsakārya*); since the status of being like the desiderative suffix (*sanvadbhāva*) and so forth is impossible here, the substitution of *i* for the vowel of the reduplicated syllable is prescribed by this rule: *apipya-t*, *pāsyati*, *apāsyat*, *pātā*. In the desiderative (*san*), there is *pipāsati*. By the rule *ghumāsthāgā...* (Pāṇini 6.4.66), the substitution of *ī* occurs, followed by reduplication: *pepīyate*. In all cases, after the processes of semi-vowel vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*), lengthening, vṛddhi, guṇa, and so forth have been performed, the reduplication is to be applied subsequently.

The root *ghrā* is used in the sense of smelling (*gandhopādāna*). By the rule *pā-ghrā-dhmo dham* (Pāṇini 7.3.78), it undergoes the substitution *jighra*. Thus, *jighrati* ("he smells"). In the benedictive (*āśīḥ*), by the rule *vā’nyasya saṃyogādeḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.68), there is optionally the substitution of *e*: *ghrāyāt* or *ghreyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *jaghrau*; in the *thal* suffix, *jaghrātha* or *jaghritha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *vibhāṣā ghrādheṭśācchāsaḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.78), there is optionally the elision of *as* (*asijluk*): *aghrāt*. In the absence of such elision, by the rule *yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.73), there are the augment *s* and the *iṭ* augment: *aghrāsīt*, *aghrāsiṣṭām*.

By the rules *ṇau caṅi tiṣṭhaterit* (Pāṇini 7.4.5) and *jighratervā* (Pāṇini 7.4.6), the penultimate vowel may optionally become *i*, resulting in *ajighrapat*. The remainder is to be understood accordingly. Furthermore, in the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, by the rule *ī ghrādhmoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.31), the vowel becomes *ī*, resulting in *jeghrīyate*.

The root *dhmā* is used in the senses of blowing and contact with fire or the mouth. By the rule *pā-ghrā-dhā-pā-0* (Pāṇini 7.3.78), it undergoes the substitution *dham*. Thus: *dhamati pāṇī* (he blows on the bellows); *dhamaty agnim* (he blows on the fire). Imperfect: *adhamat*. Imperative: *dhamatu*. Optative: *dhamet*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *vānyasya* (Pāṇini 6.4.68), there is optionally the substitution of *e*: *dhmāyāt* or *dhmeyāt*. Perfect: *dadhmau*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *adhmāsīt*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), as before, there is the substitution of *ī*: *dedhmīyate*.

The root *sthā* means "to stop" or "to stand. By the rule *pāghrādhmādheṭdṛśaḥ śaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.137), the substitute *tiṣṭha* is applied, resulting in *tiṣṭhati*. From this, we derive *atiṣṭhat*, *tiṣṭhatu*, and *tiṣṭhet*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *erliṅi* (Pāṇini 6.4.67), the vowel *e* is substituted, yielding *stheyāt*. When preceded by a prefix, by the rule *upasargāt sunoti-suvati-stauti-stobhati-sthā-s-tiṣṭhati-sthā-s-nāti-syatistobhatyartham* (Pāṇini 8.3.65), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs, resulting in *abhiṣṭhīyāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), by the rule *sthādiṣvabhyāsena cābhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 8.3.64), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs for the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *adhitaṣṭhau*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *sic* by Pāṇini 2.4.77 (*gāti-sthā-...*). There is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* even when preceded by *aṭ* due to the intervention of other sounds, according to Pāṇini 8.3.63 (*prāk-sitād-aḍ-vyavāye 'pi*), as in *adhyaiṣṭhāt*. In the case of the causative (*ṇic*) with the *caṅ* [reduplication], the substitution of *i* for the penultimate vowel of the root *sthā* occurs according to Pāṇini 7.4.5 (*tiṣṭhater-it*); thus, one forms *atiṣṭhipat*. Similarly, one has *adhiṣṭhāsyati*, and so forth. Likewise, regarding the root *sthā*, [the *ātmanepada* endings are used] after the prefixes *sam*, *ava*, and *pra* according to Pāṇini 1.3.22 (*sam-ava-pra-vibhyaḥ sthaḥ*), and also in the senses of "manifesting" and "presiding over" according to Pāṇini 1.3.23 (*prakāśana-stheyākhyayoś-ca*). [The *ātmanepada* ending is used] after *ut* in the sense of an upward action according to Pāṇini 1.3.24 (*ud-ūrdhva-karmaṇi*). It should be stated that [the *ātmanepada* ending is used] after *ut* in the sense of "striving" (*īhā*).

It should be stated that *āṅ* [is used] in the sense of a promise (*pratijñā*). Regarding *upānmantrakaraṇe* (Pāṇini 1.3.25), it should be stated that *upa* [is used] in the senses of worshiping a deity (*devapūjā*), forming a connection (*saṅgatikaraṇa*), making friends (*mitrakaraṇa*), and on a path (*pathi*); or it should be stated [that it is used] in the sense of desire to obtain (*lipsā*). And regarding *akarmakācca* (Pāṇini 1.3.26), by this reading which includes the supplementary rule (*sopasaṃkhyānapāṭha*), the Ātmanepada is prescribed according to its respective rules within these five sūtras; therein [the following forms] are established: *santiṣṭhate*, *samatiṣṭhata*, *santiṣṭhatām*, *santiṣṭheta*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), [the forms are] *saṃsthāsiṣṭha* and *santastha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, by the rule *sthādhvoricca* (Pāṇini 1.2.17), the vowel *ā* is replaced by *i*; because the suffix *sic* is treated as *kit*, there is no *guṇa* substitution. By the rule *hrasvādaṅgāt* (Pāṇini 8.2.27), the *sic* is elided, resulting in *samasthita*. Similarly, *samasthiṣātām* [is formed]. In the same way, examples with other prefixes may be cited. The root *mnā* means "to study" (*abhyāsa*). There is a substitute *manā* [for the root], as in: *āmanati*, *āmanataḥ*, *āmananti*. In the benedictive (*āśīr*), [the form is] *āmnāyāt*. In the *liṭ* [perfect], [it is] *āmamau*. In the *luṅ*, [it is] *āmnāsīt*, and so forth.

The root *dāṇ* means "to give. It takes the substitute *yaccha*. The letter *ṇ* is for the purpose of specification in rules such as *dāṇaśca sā ced...* (Pāṇini 1.3.55). [Examples: *prayacchati*, *prāyacchat*. Regarding the rule *dāṇaśca sā cec caturthyām* (Pāṇini 1.3.55), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used when the giving is contemptible, as in *saṃprayacchate*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), because it is designated as *ghu*, there is an exception to the *it*-substitution by the rule *er liṅi* (Pāṇini 6.4.67); thus, [the form is] *deyāt*. In the case of contempt, [the form is] *dāsīṣṭa*. [Perfect tense: *dadau*, *dade*. By the rule *gātisthā...* (Pāṇini 2.4.77), there is elision of the *sic* suffix; thus, *adāt*.

Elsewhere, by *anyatra sthāghvoricca* (Pāṇini 1.2.17), [the forms] *adita*, *adiṣātām*, *dāsyati*, and so forth, are derived. In the *san* [intensive] suffix, by *sanimīmā* (Pāṇini 7.4.54), there is the substitution of *i* and the elision of the reduplication, resulting in *ditsati* and *ditsate*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, by *ghumāsthā* (Pāṇini 6.4.66), there is the substitution of *i*, resulting in *dedīyate*.

The root *hvṛ* is used in the sense of "crookedness" (*kauṭilye*). Present: *hvarati* Aorist: *ahvarat* Imperative: *hvaratu* Optative: *hvaret* In the case of the substitution of *riṅ* by the rule *riṅ śayagliṅkṣu* (Pāṇini 7.4.28), the rule *guṇortisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29) applies the *guṇa* [substitution], resulting in *hvaryāt*. When the Ātmanepada is used according to the rule *bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.13), then, under the heading *iḍdhrakaraṇe liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), the optional *iṭ* augment is applied by the rule *ṛtaścasaṃyogādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.43), resulting in *hvariṣīṣṭa*.

In the absence of *iṭ*, by Pāṇini 1.2.11 (*liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu*) and 1.2.12 (*uśca*), there is *kit* status [of the suffixes], resulting in *hṛṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, *jahvāra*. By Pāṇini 7.4.10 (*ṛtaśca saṃyogāderguṇaḥ*), there is *guṇa* substitution, resulting in *jahvaratuḥ*, *jahvaruḥ*, and *jahvartha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist] with *sic*, there is *vṛddhi*: *ahvārṣīt*. When the *ātmanepada* is used, there is an option for *iṭ*: *ahvṛta*, *ahvṛṣātām*; or with *iṭ*, *ahvariṣṭa*, *ahvariṣātām*. By Pāṇini 7.2.70 (*ṛddhanoḥ sye*), there is *iṭ*, as in *hvariṣyati*, etc. [The roots] *dhvṛ* [meaning] "to bend" and *spṛ* [meaning] "sound" and "affliction."

The root *dṛp* means "to delight"; *smṛ* means "to remember. It is conjugated as follows: *smarati*. When preceded by other prefixes or used alone, its forms are as previously described. With the prefix *sam-*, the Atmanepada is applied according to the rule *samogamṛcchi* (Pāṇini 1.3.29), resulting in *saṃsmarate*, *samasmṛta*, *saṃsmaratām*, and *saṃsmareta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is an optional *iṭ* augment according to the rule *svarati* (Pāṇini 7.2.44), yielding *saṃsmṛṣīṣṭa* or *saṃsmariṣīṣṭa*. In the potential (*liṅ*), by the rule *ṛtaśca saṃyogāderguṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.10), the guṇa substitution applies, resulting in *saṃsasmarē*.
In the aorist (*luṅ*), the forms are *samasmṛta* or *samasmariṣṭa*.

The root *sṛ* means "to go. In the sense of rapid motion, it takes the substitute *dhāv* before the *śit* affixes; thus, *dhāvati*. In other senses, it is *sarati*. The imperfect is *asarat*. For the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), it is *sriyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *sasāra*; in the *thal* suffix, *sasārtha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by Pāṇini 3.1.56 (*sarti-śāsty-artibhyaś-ca*), there is *aṅ* in place of *cl*; and by Pāṇini 7.4.16 (*ṛdṛśo'ṅguṇaḥ*), there is guṇa substitution.

The root *ṛ* is used in the senses of "motion" (*gati*) and "attaining" (*prāpaṇa*). It undergoes the substitution of *ṛccha*. **Present Tense:** - Indicative: *ṛcchati*, *ārchat* - Imperative: *ṛcchatu* - Optative: *ṛcchet* - Benedictive: By *āśiṣi guṇortisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29), there is guṇa substitution: *aryāt* **Perfekt (Liṭ):** - First person singular: *āra* (by *ṛcchatyṝtām* [Pāṇini 7.4.11], there is guṇa). - Third person dual: *āratuḥ* - Third person plural: *āruḥ* - Second person singular (*thali*): Although the prohibition of *iṭ* by *ṛto bhāradvājasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.63) would apply, *iṭ* is added by *iḍattyartivyayatīnām* (Pāṇini 7.2.66). Then the guṇa of the *ārddhadhātuka* suffix applies: *āritha*. **Aorist (Luṅ):** By *sartā* etc. (Pāṇini 3.1.56), *cler aṅ* is substituted for *cli*. (Note: The text provided contains the grammatical analysis and derivation of the verb *ṛ* according to Pāṇinian rules.)

"Guṇa is substituted for the root ṛ before the suffix aṅ" (Pāṇini 7.4.16). [The forms are] ārat, āratām, and āran. By the rule "In the case of the causative (ṇau) with the suffix caṅ, after roots beginning with ati and hrī... (Pāṇini 7.3.36), the augment *puK* is added. Then, by the rule "Guṇa is substituted for the penultimate light vowel of a stem ending in *puK*" (Pāṇini 7.3.86), the second syllable is reduplicated, resulting in *ārpipat*. By the rule "The augment *iṬ* is added after roots ending in ṛ or having *haN* as their penultimate" (Pāṇini 7.2.70), the form *ariṣyati* is derived.

By the rule *sani smipūṅrañjaśāṃ sani* (Pāṇini 7.2.74), the augment *iṭ* is added; then follows the doubling of the second syllable, resulting in *aririṣati*. For the root *ghṛ*, by the supplementary rule *śūrṇotīnām upasaṃkhyānam*, there is *yaṅ*; then, by the rules *guṇortisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29) and *yaṅi ca* (Pāṇini 7.4.30), *guṇa* substitution occurs. Regarding the prohibition *nandrāḥ saṃyogādayaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.3), since it is stated that the prohibition applies to the *repha* (the letter *r*) followed by the letter *ya*, the syllable *ya* is doubled. Finally, by the rule *dīrghokitaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.83), the vowel is lengthened.

Thus, the long vowel of the root *ṛ* is lengthened [in the reduplication]. From the root *ṛ* preceded by *sam*, the Ātmanepada is applied by the rule *samo gamṛcchi* (Pāṇini 1.3.29), etc.; thus one forms *saṃṛṣīṣṭa*. Because of the suffix *uccha*, there is *kit*-ness; in the case of *dhvam*, the cerebral (*ūrdhanya*) is obligatory: *saṃṛṣīḍhvam*. In the *liṭ* [perfect], by the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), there is *guṇa*: *samāre*, *samārāte*, *samārire*. In the *laṅ* [imperfect]: *samārata*, *samāretām*, *samāranta*. For the roots *gṛ* and *ghṛ* meaning "to sprinkle," forms such as *abhigharati* and so on are to be inferred accordingly.

The root *sru* means "to flow. Present: *sravati* Imperfect: *asravat* Imperative: *sravatu* Optative: *sravet* Aorist (Precative): *srūyāt* Perfect: *susrāva*; [by the substitution of] *uvaṅ*, *susruvatuḥ*; *susruvuḥ*. Regarding the suffix *thali*, since Bhāradvājīya does not accept the optional *iṭ* augment, there is a permanent prohibition by the rule concerning roots beginning with *kryādi*; thus: *susrotha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *ṇi-śri-0* (Pāṇini 3.1.48) etc., the *caṅ* suffix is applied; [with the substitution of] *uvaṅ*, *asusruvat*.

Under the governing rule *ṇau caṅi* (Pāṇini 6.1.31), by the rule *sravati-śṛṇoti-dravati-pravati-plavati-cyavatīnāṃ vā* (Pāṇini 7.4.81), the vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) may optionally become *i*. Thus: *asisravat* or *asusruvat*. The same applies to the others, such as *sroṣyati*, and so forth. An example for the root *sru* (to flow) should be inferred accordingly. The roots *du* and *dru* mean "to go. *Dravati*. The form for *dru* should be inferred as before. The root *dhru* means "to be firm" or "to stand fast. *Dhruvati*. [The noun] *dhruviḥ*.
The remaining [roots] ending in *seṭ* are *aniṭ* and are *parasmaipada*.

The root *smiṅ* is used in the sense of "slight laughter. Present: *smayate*, *asmayata*, *smayatām*, *smayeta*. Benedictive: *smeṣīṣṭa*, *smeṣīḍhvam*. The root *smayi-* is taught with the marker *ṣ* (*ṣopadeśa*). Because it is preceded by a conjunct consonant (*saṃyogapūrvatvāt*), the rule *eranekācaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.82) does not apply, and thus there is no *yaṇ* substitution; instead, *iyaṅ* is applied. Periphrastic Perfect: *siṣmiye*, *siṣmiyāte*, *siṣmiyire*. By the rule governing roots beginning with *krī-* (*krādiniyamāt*), *iṭ* is added: *siṣmiyiṣe*, *siṣmiyāthe*. According to the rule *vibhāṣeṭaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.79), the cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) may optionally replace the dental *d* in the second person plural: *siṣmiyiḍhve* or *siṣmiyidhve*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *asmeṣṭa*, *asmeṣātām*.

In the *caṅ* [aorist] following a causative (*ṇic*), as in *avyasiṣmayat*: the ātmanepada is obligatory after a root ending in *ṇic* when used in the sense of "fear" or "cause of fear" according to Pāṇini 1.3.68 (*bhīsmyorhetubhaye*); furthermore, there is the substitution of *ā* for the root vowel and the augment *puk* for the root *smi*, resulting in *vyasiṣmayata*. In the future, *smeṣyate*. In the desiderative (*san*), by Pāṇini 7.2.74 (*smipūṅrañjvaśāṃ sani*), the augment *iṭ* is applied, resulting in *siṣmayiṣate*. This [root *smi*] is also used in the sense of "disrespect. The root *gurda* means "an indistinct sound. The root *gāṅ* means "motion."

The root *cyu* (with variants *pru*, *plu*) means "to go," "to move. Present tense (*laṭ*): *cyavate* (he moves) Optative (*liṅ*): *acyavata* (he moved) *cyavatām* (let him move) *cyaveta* (he might move) Precative (*āśīrliṅ*): *cyoṣīṣṭa* (may he move) In the second person plural: *cyoṣīḍhvam* (may you move) Perfect tense (*liṭ*): *cucyuve* (he has moved) In the second person plural: *cucyuviḍhve* or *cucyuvidhve* (you have moved) Aorist (*luṅ*): *acyoṣṭa* (he moved) *acyoṣātām* (they two moved) In the second person plural: *acyoḍhvam* (you moved) Causative with *caṅ* (reduplication): *acucyavat* (he caused to move) *acucyuvat* (they two caused to move) Future tense (*lṛṭ*): *cyoṣyate* (he will move) The same applies to the other two [tenses, the conditional and the periphrastic future], up to the *āyatāna* (the future).

The root *meṅ* is used in the sense of "vowing" (*praṇidāna*). In the benedictive (*āśis*) with the suffix *liṅ*, by the rule *ādeca upadeśe’śiti* (Pāṇini 6.1.45), the substitution of *ā* occurs: *māsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *mame*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *amāsta*, *amāsātām*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the suffix *caṅ*, *amīmavat*. In the passive (*karmakartari*), *māsyate*. In the desiderative (*san*), by the rule *sani mīmāghurabhalabhaśakapatapadāmaca is* (Pāṇini 7.4.54) and other rules, the substitution of *is* occurs; the *s* of the suffix becomes *t*: *mitsate*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the rule *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisām hali* (Pāṇini 6.4.66), the substitution of *ī* occurs:

*memīyate*. The root *deṅ* is used in the sense of "protecting" (*rakṣaṇa*). By the rule *dayaterdigiliṭi* (Pāṇini 7.4.9), the substitute *dig* is applied for *dayati*; consequently, reduplication (*dvirvacana*) takes place. Thus: *avadigye*, *avadigyāte*. The remainder is to be understood accordingly.
*Śyaiṅ* means "to go": *śyāyate*, *śyāsīṣṭa*, *śasye*, *aśyāsta*.
*Pyaiṅ* means "to grow": [conjugated] as before.
*Traiṅ* means "to protect": *trāyate*, *atrāyata*.

The root *pūṅ* means "to purify. Present tense: *pavate* (he purifies); *apavata* (he purified). In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *paviṣīṣṭa*; *paviṣīḍhvam*, *paviṣīdhvam*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *pupuve*; *pupuvāte*; *pupuvidhve*, *pupuviḍhve*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *apaviṣṭa*; *apaviḍhvam*, *apavidhvam*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the *caṅ* suffix, due to the application of the *saṃvadbhāva* rule, the penultimate vowel of the reduplicated syllable undergoes *itva* by the rule *oḥ puyaṇjpare* (Pāṇini 7.4.80), and the subsequent lengthening by *dīrgho laghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.94) results in *apīpavat*. Future: *paviṣyate*. In the desiderative (*san*), by the rule *smipūṅrañja...* (Pāṇini 7.2.74), the augment *iṭ* is added; as before, the *iṭ* causes the *saṃvadbhāva*, resulting in *papaviṣate*.

The root *ḍīṅ* (meaning "to move through the air") is conjugated as follows: *ḍayate*, *ḍayiṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, because the original form undergoes *jaś*-substitution, the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) also becomes a *jaś*-sound, resulting in *ḍiḍye*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, it is *aḍayiṣṭa*. The future is *ḍayiṣyate*.
The root *mūṅ* (meaning "to bind") is treated like *pavati*. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *mumūṣati*. [Note:
All roots ending in *ḍayati* except for this one are *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) and are *ātmanebhāṣā* (middle-voiced).

The root *tṛ* is used in the senses of "floating" and "crossing. It forms *tarati*. In the benedictive mood (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *ṛta iddhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.100), the vowel *ṛ* is changed to *i*, and by *hali ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.77), this *i* is lengthened; furthermore, there is reduplication of the *y* sound, resulting in *tīryāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), it becomes *tatāra*. Regarding the kit-form of the perfect, although the prohibition *na śasadadavādiguṇānām* (Pāṇini 6.4.126) would have applied to prevent the guna of the vowel *a*, the rule *tṛphalabhajatrapaśca* (Pāṇini 6.4.122) prescribes the change of the vowel to *e* and the elision of the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *teratuḥ* and *teruḥ*.

In this context, by the rule *ṛcchajyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), there is *guṇa*; and by *thali ca seṭi* (Pāṇini 6.4.121), we have *teritha*. Here, there is *guṇa* for the *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, and because it is *seṭ*, there is the addition of *iṭ*. In the *luṅ* tense, with *sic*, there is *vṛddhi*: *atārīt*. Those who know these matters declare that these [roots] are *seṭ*. Because of the statement "ending in *ad* or *ṝ*," they possess the quality of being *seṭ*. By the rule *vṝto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), after the roots *vṛṅ* and *vṛñ*, as well as after those ending in *ṛ*, the *iṭ* that follows may optionally be long: *tariṣyati* or *tarīṣyati*, and so forth.

By the rule *sani iṭ sani vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.41), the augment *iṭ* is added; by the rule *vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), there is optionally a long vowel. Thus, there are three forms: *titariṣati*, *titarīṣati*, and *titīrṣati*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, it becomes *tetīryate*.
These [roots] ending in *iṭ* are *parasmaipada* (active voice).
*gup* in the sense of protecting and censuring;
*tij* in the sense of sharpening and enduring;
*mān* in the sense of honoring.

The root *badh* means "to bind. Roots beginning with *gup*, which have anudātta indicatory vowels (*it*) and take ātmanepada endings, when they function in the senses of censure, endurance, desire to know, or deformity, as well as those ending in *san* and other affixes, are considered verbal roots (*dhātu*). (Pāṇini 3.1.32). From the roots *gup*, *tij*, and *kit*, the affix *san* is applied. (Pāṇini 3.1.5). *jugupsate* (he censures), *ajugupsata* (he censured), *jugupsatām* (let him censure), *jugupseta* (he might censure), *jugupsīṣṭa* (may he censure). In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, because it ends in an affix, it is treated as a root and takes *ām*: *jugupsāñcakre*. *ajugupsiṣṭa* (he censured). In the *caṅ* (periphrastic aorist) after the causative (*ṇic*), there is no reduplication because the section concerning non-reduplication applies; thus, *ajugupsata*. The rest is to be understood accordingly. *titikṣate* (he endures).

He investigates (*mīmāṃsate*). He feels disgust (*bībhatsate*); the forms are to be understood as before. There is an absence of *iṭ* for these [roots] because the suffix *san* lacks the status of an *ārdhadhātuka*, and because that [augment] is absent since it is prescribed under the governing rule of "not being a verbal root" (*adhātva-*).

The root *rabh* is used in the sense of "beginning" (*rābhasye*). Present tense: *ārabhate*, *ārabhata*, *ārabhatām*, *ārabheta*. In the benedictive (*āśiṣi*), by the rule *khari ca* (Pāṇini 8.4.55), there is the substitution of the hard consonant (*carva*): *ārapsīṣṭa*. However, the absence of the augment *iṭ* is due to the statement: "In the case of roots ending in *rabh*, *grabh*, and *labh*, the augment *iṭ* is added only after the first vowel, and not after the third. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), by the rule *ata ekahalmadhyenādeśāder liṭi* (Pāṇini 6.4.120), there is the substitution of *e* for *a* and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsa-lopa*): *ārebhe*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), when a *jhal*-ending suffix follows, there is the elision of *s*: *ārabdha* (by the rule *jhaṣastathordho'dhaḥ* [Pāṇini 8.2.40]).

By the rule *khari ca* (Pāṇini 8.4.55), there is the substitution of *c* for *r*. Regarding the root *rabh*, before the suffix *ṇic* and when followed by *caṅ* (the reduplicated aorist marker), the augment *num* is applied by the rule *ṇau caṅi rabheraśabliṭoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.63); thus, [the form] is *ārarambhat*. [In the future tense: *ārapsyate*. Regarding the desiderative suffix *san*, the operations beginning with *sani mīmā0* (Pāṇini 7.4.54) apply; here, due to the elision of the reduplication (*lopobhyāsasya*), the elision of the initial consonant of the conjunct (*saṃyogādilopa*), and the substitution of *c* for *r*, [the form] is *āripsate*. The root *ḍulabhaṣ* means "to obtain. As before, when followed by *ṇic* and *caṅ*, the *num* is applied to *labh* by the rule *ṇau caṅi labheśca*; thus, [the form] is *alalambhat*.

The root *svañj* is used in the sense of embracing. Regarding the form *pariṣvajate*: the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs by the rule *upasargāt sunoti...* (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and the elision of the nasal vowel occurs by the rule *daṃśasañjasvañjāṃ śapi* (Pāṇini 6.4.25). Regarding the forms *paryaṣvajata*, *paryasvajata*, *pariṣvajatām*, and *pariṣvajeta*: the optional substitution of *ṣ* for *s* after the prefixes *pari*, *ni*, and *vi* before roots beginning with *s* occurs even when there is an intervening vowel (*vāḍvyavāye’pi*), according to the rule *parinivibhyaḥ sevasitasayasivusahasuṭstusvañjām aṭyavyavāye vā* (Pāṇini 8.3.70). Regarding the form *paryaṣvakṣīṣṭa*: the substitution of *k* for *s* occurs in the benedictive mood by the rule *āśiṣi ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.80).

Regarding the statement "it should be stated that [the rule] applies to the roots *śranth*, *granth*, *danbh*, and *svañj*," when there is *kit* status in the *liṭ* [perfect], there is elision of the nasal by Pāṇini 6.4.24 (*aniditāṃ...*). Regarding the prohibition of *ṣatva* for what follows the reduplication of the roots *sad* and *svañj* in the *liṭ*: *parisvaje*. In the *luṅ*: *paryaṣvaṅkta*. In the *caṅ* of the causative (*ṇau caṅi*): *paryaṣvajata*. Future: *pariṣvaṅkṣyate*. Conditional: *paryaṣvaṅkṣyata*. Periphrastic future: *pariṣvaṅktā*.

By the restrictive rule *sani stautiṇyoreva* (Pāṇini 8.3.61), there is an absence of the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* after the reduplication; thus, *sisvaṅkṣate*. By the rule *sthādiṣvabhyāsena cābhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 8.3.64), when preceded by an upasarga, there is the substitution of *ṣ*; thus, *pariṣiṣvaṅkṣate*. The root *had*, meaning "to void excrement," forms *hadate*. For the benedictive mood, one should apply *hatsīṣṭa*, and so forth.
These are the roots ending in vowels that are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *i*) and belong to the *ātmanepada* voice.

The root *ñikṣvidā* is used in the sense of an indistinct sound: *kṣvedati*. The root *skandir* means "to go" and "to dry up. Regarding the forms *viṣkandati*, *viskandati*, and *pariṣkandati* (or *pariskandati*), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs optionally by Pāṇini 7.3.73 (*veḥ skander aniṣṭhāyām*) and by 7.3.74 (*pareś ca*). When there is no intervention by the augment *aṭ*, the substitution does not take place, as in *vyaskandata*. In the benedictive mood, the nasal is elided according to Pāṇini 6.4.24 (*aniditām...*), resulting in *skandyāt*. The aorist forms are *caskanda* and *skanditha*; the perfect form is *caskantha*. In the aorist, the suffix *aṅ* is optionally applied by Pāṇini 3.1.57 (*irito vā*), yielding *askandata*.

In the absence of the augment *aṭ*, there is *vṛddhi* by virtue of the rule for roots ending in consonants before *sic*: *askāntīt*. With the causative suffix *ṇi* and the reduplication (*caṅ*), it becomes *acaskandat*. [The forms] *skantsyati* and so forth follow. In the case of *yam*, there is the augment *nīg*: *canīskandyate*. For *yabh* in the sense of sexual intercourse: *yabhati* and so forth.

The root *ṇam* is used in the senses of bowing (*prahvatva*) and sound (*śabda*). Regarding it, there is a prohibition of the affixes *yaṅ* and *ciṇ* by the rule *na duhasnunamāṃ yakciṇau* (Pāṇini 3.1.89). Thus: *namati śākhā* (the branch bows), *namati guruṃ* (he bows to the teacher). In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), we have *nanāma*, *nematuḥ*, *nemuḥ*; *nemitha*, *nanantha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.73), the augment *sak* is added to the base, resulting in *anaṃsīt*, *anaṃsiṣṭām*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), we have *naṃnamyate*.

The root *gam* means "to go. By the rule *śiti iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.77), the augment *tuk* is added, resulting in *gacchati*. Forms such as *agacchat* follow accordingly. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), we have *gamyāt*. Here, although the *yāsuṭ* suffix is *kit*, the elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*) does not occur by the rule *gamahana...* (Pāṇini 6.4.98) and so forth, because [the conditions for that rule] do not apply due to the presence of *anaṅ* and other factors. Furthermore, the elision of the nasal (*anunāsikalopa*) by the rule *anudāttopadeśa...* (Pāṇini 6.4.37) and so forth does not take place either, because [the root] begins with a vowel (*aj-*) and is followed by a consonant (*hal-*). In the perfect (*liṭ*), we have *jagāma*; here, the elision of the penultimate vowel by *gamahana...* (Pāṇini 6.4.98) occurs even when there is reduplication (*dvirvacana*) before a vowel (*aci*).

By virtue of the *sthānivadbhāva* (the status of being like the original element) according to Pāṇini Sūtra 1.1.59, there is reduplication: *jagmuḥ*, *jagamitha*, *jagantha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), because the root is marked with the *ḷ* indicatory letter (*ḷdit*), the suffix *aṅ* is applied by the rule *gamahana-* (Pāṇini 6.4.98), and due to the prohibition of the *ṅī* augment, there is no elision of the penultimate vowel: *agamat*, *agamatām*. When a suffix beginning with *s* follows that is not *sic* and pertains to the *parasmaipada*, the augment *iṭ* is added by the rule *gamer iṭ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.58): *gamiṣyati*. [In the conditional: *agamiṣyat*. [In the periphrastic future: *gantā*. [In the simple future: *gamiṣyati*.

By the rule *nityaṃ kauṭilye gatau* (Pāṇini 3.1.23), the suffix *yaṅ* is applied; with the augment *nuk* added to the reduplicated syllable, the form *jaṅgamyate* is derived. It does not take the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) after the prefix *sam*, because of the rule *samo gamṛcchi0* (Pāṇini 1.3.29) and others.

In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), by the rule *āśiṣi vā gamaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.2.13), there is optionally the *kit* designation; in the case of this *kit* designation, the nasal is elided by the rule *anudāttopadeśa...* (Pāṇini 6.4.37), resulting in *saṅgaṃsīṣṭa*. In the absence of the *kit* designation, the form is *saṃgasīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, the penultimate vowel is elided by the rule *gamahana...* (Pāṇini 6.4.98), resulting in *saṃjagmāte*. In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, as before, in the case of the *kit* designation, the nasal is elided and the *sic* suffix is dropped because the stem ends in a short vowel (*hrasvādaṅgāt*), resulting in *samagata*, *samagasātām*, and *samagasata*. In the absence of the *kit* designation, the *sic* remains, resulting in *samagaṃsta* and *samagaṃsātām*.

*Samagaṃsata*, *saṃgaṃsyate*, *samagaṃsyata*, *saṃgantā*. In the case of the desiderative (*san*), [the form] *sañjagaṃsate* does not undergo lengthening by Pāṇini 6.4.16 (*ajjhanagamāṃ sani*), because that rule specifically includes the substitute *iṅ*. Likewise from the root *sṛp*: *sarpati*, *asarpat*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), *sṛpyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *sasarpa*, *sasṛpuḥ*. By the rule governing the *kryādigaṇa*, the augment *iṭ* is added: *sasarpitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *asṛpat*. With the causative suffix *ṇic* followed by *caṅ*, [the forms are] *asisṛpat* and *asasarpat*.

Regarding *lṛ* and *luṭ*: "And for a root with an *ṛ* in the penultimate position that has an unaccented [initial] vowel, *num* is optionally inserted before a suffix beginning with *jhal* and not having *k* or *it*" (Pāṇini 6.1.59). Thus, for a root having *ṛ* in its penultimate syllable, *num* is optionally added when followed by a suffix beginning with *jhal* that lacks *k* or *it*. For example: *sṛpyati*, *asarpyat*, *sraptā*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*): "The suffixes [of the desiderative] have the *kit* designation after a root ending in a consonant" (Pāṇini 1.2.10); hence, *sisarpati*. Regarding the intensive (*yaṅ*): "The augment *rīk* is applied to the reduplicated syllable of a root with *ṛ* in its penultimate position" (Pāṇini 7.4.90); thus, *sarīsṛpyate*.

The root *yam* means "to cease" or "to restrain. As previously mentioned, there is the substitution of *śa* for the root vowel; thus, *yacchati*. In the forms *ayacchat* and so forth, in the *liṭ* (perfect tense), we have *yayāma*, *yematuḥ*, *yemuḥ*, and *yemitha*. In the absence of the augment *iṭ*, we have *yayattha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.73), the suffix *sak* is added after the root, and by the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4), there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi*; thus, *yaṃsīt*, *ayaṃsiṣṭām*. For the future, *yaṃsyati*; for the conditional, *ayaṃsyat*. The agentive form is *yantā*. In the *yaṅ* (intensive), *yiyaṃsati*. Regarding the rule *nugato'nunāsikāntasya* (Pāṇini 7.4.85), the mention of *nu* therein is intended as an indicator (*upalakṣaṇa*) for the *anusvāra*; by this, forms such as *yaṃyamyate* are established.

The *ātmanepada* ending is applied to the root *yam-* preceded by *upa-* in the sense of marriage (*vivāha*), according to Pāṇini Sūtra 1.3.56: *upādyamaḥ svakaraṇe*. To the root *yam-* preceded by *āṅ-* when it is intransitive (*akarmaka*) and refers to one’s own limb, the same ending applies according to Pāṇini Sūtras 1.3.26 and 1.3.28: *āṅgakarmakācca* and *āṅo yamahanaḥ*. Likewise, when it is transitive (*sakarmaka*), it applies according to Pāṇini Sūtra 1.3.75: *samudāṅbhyo yamo’granthe*. Examples include: *upayacchate*, *āyacchate*, *pāṇiṃ saṃyacchate*, and *udyacchate*. For the benedictive mood (*āśis*), examples include: *udyaṃsīṣṭa*, and so forth.

In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], as in *upayeme* and so forth; in the *luṅ* [aorist], by the rule *vibhāṣopayamane* (Pāṇini 7.2.16), there is optionally *kit*-ness for the suffix *sic*. In the case of *kit*-ness, there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika-lopa*) and the elision of *sic* by the rule *hrasvādaṅgāt* (Pāṇini 6.4.103): *upāyata kanyām* ("he married the girl"). In the other case, *upāyaṃsta kanyām*. However, in the sense of "enticing" (*gandhana*), by the rule *yamo gandhane* (Pāṇini 1.2.15), there is obligatory *kit*-ness for *sic*: *udāyata*, *udāyasātām*. In other cases: *samayaṃsta*; *sārathir udayaṃstadyumaṇim* ("the charioteer guided the sun"), and so forth.

The root *tap* means "to heat" or "to torment. In the present tense (*laṭ*), it is *tapati*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), it is *tatāpa*, *tepatuḥ*, *tepuḥ*; and in the second person singular, *tepatha* or *tataptha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is the vṛddhi substitution characterized by the ending beginning with a consonant: *atāpsīt*. [The following roots are listed: *tip*, *tapi*, *math*, *vapi*, *svapi*, *lupi*, *lipi*, *tṛp* (as in *tṛpyati*), and *dṛp* (as in *dṛpyati*).
With a low-pitched voice, recite the *sṛp* [verses], the *nīcana*, the *śapi*, the *cupiñjapī*, the *prīhi*, and the *pāntāḥ*; these are the thirteen fallen [sections].

*Tapi* is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment). However, when it has a limb of one's own (*svāṅga*) as its object, the *ātmanepada* is used after *tapa* preceded by *ud* or *vi*, according to the rule *udvibhyāṃ tapaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.27). Thus, from *uttapate*: *vitapate pāṇim*, *vyatapat*, *vitapatām*, *vitapeta*, *vitapsīṣṭa*, *vitepe*, *vyatapta*, *vyatapsātām*, and so forth. *Tyaj* means "in the sense of abandonment" (*hānau*). It is also *aniṭ*. [The roots] *pac*, *vac*, *vic*, *ric*, *rañj*, and *pracch* are likewise [to be understood as *aniṭ*].
The roots *ṇij*, *sic*, *muc*, *bhaj*, *bhañj*, *bhṛjj*, *tyaj*,
*yaj*, *yuj*, *ruj*, *sañj*,
*majj*, *bhuj*, *dhvaj*, *sṛj*, and *mṛj*— these [roots] ending in vowels are aniṭ (lacking the augment *iṭ*) before the suffix *niṣṭhā*.

Thus, regarding "he abandons" (*tyajati*) and so forth: the root *sañj* means "to adhere. It is taught with a *ṣ* as its initial marker (*ṣopadeśa*). By the rule *daṃśasañjasvañjāṃ śapi* (Pāṇini 6.4.25), the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika-lopa*) applies. Regarding the change to *ṣ*, by the rule *upasargādiṇaḥ parasya upasargāt sunoti* etc. (Pāṇini 8.3.65), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs; thus, one forms *viṣajati*. Even when there is an intervening vowel (*aḍ-vyavāye*), one forms *vyaṣajat*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), there is the elision of the *n*; thus, *viṣajyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *sasañja*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is the augment of lengthening (*vṛddhi*) characterized by the root ending in a consonant; thus, *asāṅkṣīt*. The remainder is to be understood accordingly.

The root *daṃś* means "to bite. With the suffix *śap*, there is elision of the nasal (*n*) as before; thus, *daśati*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), *daśyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *dadaṃśa*, *dadaṃśatuḥ*, *dadaṃśuḥ*, *dadaṃśitha*. In the absence of the augment *iṭ*, there is the substitution of *ṣ* by the rule for *vraśc* etc., followed by *ṣṭutva*; thus, *dadaṃṣṭa*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is the substitution of *ṣ*, *katva*, *parasavarṇatva*, and *vṛddhi*; thus, *adāṃkṣīt*. When a *jhal* follows, there is elision of *s*, and *ṣatva* and *ṣṭutva* apply, but not *parasavarṇa* here; thus, *adāṃṣṭām*, *adāṃkṣuḥ*.
For *daṃkṣyati* and so forth, the intensive (*yaṅ*) is applied by the rule *lupasada-* and the elision (*nuk*) by *japajabha-* (Pāṇini 7.4.86); thus, *daṃdaśyate*.

The root *kṛṣ* means "to scratch" or "to plow. Present: *karṣati*. Benedictive: *kṛṣyāt*. Perfect: *cakarṣa*, *cakṛṣatuḥ*, *cakṛṣuḥ*. In the *thāl* suffix (*thas*), by the rule *kryādiniyamāt* [Pāṇini 1.2.15], there is optionally the augment *iṭ*: *cakarṣitha*. Aorist: By the rule *śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.45), the substitution of *ksa* for *cli* would be mandatory; however, by the rule *spṛśamṛśakṛṣatṛpadṛpīnāṃ sijvā* (Vārttika on Pāṇini 3.1.44), there is optionally the *sic* suffix. When *sic* is applied, the vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) characterized by the ending in *hal* occurs. In that same context, by the rule *anudāttasya cardupadhasya* (Pāṇini 6.1.59), there is optionally the augment *am*. Thus, in one case: *akrākṣīt*; in the other case: *akārṣīt*. (Note: *akārṣīt* is derived from the *sic* form with *am*). *akārṣīt* (in the alternative case).

*kṣaḥ* [is the root]. In the *ṇic* [causal] with *caṅ* [the reduplication], by the rule *urad* etc., we have *acīkṛṣat* and *acakarṣat*. In the *lṛṭ* and *luṭ* [future and periphrastic future], the augment *am* is added as before: *krakṣyati*, *karkṣyati*, and so on. The root *dṛśir* means "to see. In the *śit* [present] tense, by the rule *pāghrādhmā...* there is the substitution of *paśya*: *paśyati*. [Imperfect: *apaśyat*. [Imperative: *paśyatu*. [Optative: *paśyet*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), *dṛśyāt*. In the *liṭ* [perfect]: *dadarśa*; *dadṛśatuḥ*; *dadṛśuḥ*. Since the addition of *iṭ* is obligatory by the rule *krādiniyamāt*, the *iṭ* is optionally applied by the rule *vibhāṣāsṛjidṛśoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.65): thus we have *dadarśitha* or *dadraṣṭha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], because it is marked with *irit*, the suffix *aṅ* is used; by the rule *ṛdṛśo'ṅi guṇaḥ*, there is *guṇa* substitution: *adarśat*.

In the absence of an *aṅ* suffix, the augment *am* is applied by Pāṇini 6.1.58 (*sic-sṛji-dṛśor-jhaly-am-a-kiti*), followed by the *yaṇ* substitution [of *ṛ* for *ri*], resulting in *adrākṣīt*. Due to the prohibition in Pāṇini 3.1.47 (*na dṛśaḥ*), there is no substitution of *ks* for *s*. From the rules for *ṣatva* and *ṣṭutva*, we have *drākṣām* and *adrākṣuḥ*. Through the rules for *ṣatva*, *katva*, and *ṣatva*, we derive *drakṣyati*, and so forth. With *ṣatva* and *ṣṭutva*, the form is *draṣṭā*. The augment *am* is obligatory; it is an exception to *guṇa*. By Pāṇini 1.3.57 (*san-jñā-śru-smṛ-dṛśāṃ sanaḥ*), the *ātmanepada* ending is used in the desiderative (*sana*), as in *didṛkṣate*.

Regarding the rule *sampūrvāt samo gamyṛcchi* (Pāṇini 1.3.29), it should be stated that "and [the root] *dṛś*" also applies; thus, the Ātmanepada ending is used: *saṃpaśyate*, *samapaśyata*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), by the rules *iko jhal* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), *halantācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10), and *liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), there is *kit* status, and consequently no augment (*āgama*). Thus: *sandṛkṣīṣṭa*, *sandadṛśe*.

In the *luṅ* (aorist), there is elision of the *san* suffix; *ṣatva* and *ṣṭutva* [apply], and the *kit* status is as before. Similarly, in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāva*) and the object (*karman*), the *ātmanepada* is used by the rule *bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.13). Because the *yak* suffix has *kit* status, there is no *guṇa* strengthening, and thus *adṛśyata* is seen. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), by the rule *syasicsīyuṭtāsiṣu* (Pāṇini 6.4.62) and others, there is optionally the *ciṇvat* augment *iṭ*, resulting in *darśiṣīṣṭa*; otherwise, *dṛkṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), *dadṛśe*. In the *luṅ* with the *ta* suffix, by the rule *ciṇbhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.66), *ciṇ* replaces *cl*, and by *ciṇo luk*, the result is *adarśi*.

In the *ciṇ* alternative, [the forms] were *adarśiṣātām*. In the absence of that (*ciṇ*), [they were] *adṛkṣātām*. In the *lṛ* and *luṭ* tenses, [the forms are] *drakṣyate* and *darśiṣyate*. [The conditional forms are] *adrakṣyata* and *adarśiṣyata*. [The periphrastic future forms are] *draṣṭā* and *darśitā*. The root *dah* (meaning "to burn to ashes"): *dahati*. In the *liṭ* tense: *dadāha*, *dehatuḥ*, *dehuḥ*, *dehitha*, *dadagdha*. In the *luṅ* tense, after the application of *ghas*, *bhaṣ*-substitution, *cartva*, and *ṣatva*, [the form is] *adhākṣīt*. In the *yaṅ* tense: *dandahyate*. The root *miha* (meaning "to sprinkle"): *mehati*. In the benedictive: *mihyāt*. [In the *liṭ* tense: *mimeha*, *mimihatuḥ*, *mimihuḥ*. By the rule governing the *kryādigaṇa*, *iṭ* is added: *mimehitha*. In the *luṅ* tense, *ksa* replaces *cli*: *amikṣat*. [The future form is] *mekṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *kita* is listed among the roots conjugated in the *parasmaipada*. However, upon careful consideration of the commentary by the author of the *Vṛtti-nivāsa*, we shall provide an example of its usage in the *ātmanepada*.

Regarding the rule *guptijkidbhyaḥ san* (Pāṇini 3.1.5), the author of the *Vṛtti* states that the inclusion of the indicatory letters (*anubandha*) in the roots beginning with *gup* is for the sake of the middle voice (*ātmanepada*). An objection is raised there: "Even if the indicatory letter is attached, the middle voice must still not occur after those roots, because [the suffix] *san* intervenes. This objection is resolved by the author of the *Nyāsa*, who argues that the middle voice does indeed occur due to the force of the inclusion of the indicatory letter. Some maintain that the reading of these roots as *parasmaipada* in the Dhātupāṭha is for the sake of the general list (*gaṇa*), and that the mention of *gup* and the others in the rule refers to those distinct from that specific context, such as in the case of *ketayati*.

Because we see the usage of both forms—*na cikitsata* (he did not treat) and *cikitsati* (he treats)—the verbal root *kit* with the suffix *san* (desiderative) is *cikits*. Thus, in the sense of a benediction: *cikitsiṣīṣṭa*; in the periphrastic perfect: *cikitsāñcakre*, and so forth. These are the roots ending in *san* that are invariably *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) and are *parasmaipada* (active voice).

The roots *dā* (in the sense of cutting) and *śā* (in the sense of sharpening) take the suffix *san* by the rule *mān-badh-dān-śān-vyadha-vas-ti-jñapi-praṇibhyaḥ saḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.6), becoming *dīdāṃsate* and *śīśāṃsate*.

The root *ḍupacaṣ* (in the sense of cooking): *pacati*, *pacate*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *papāca*, *pecatuḥ*, *pecuḥ*; *pecitha* or *papaktha*; *pece*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), [the forms are] *apākṣīt*, *apākta*; the rest is to be inferred accordingly.

The root *bhaj* is used in the sense of "to serve. Present tense: *bhajati*, *bhajate*. Benedictive: *bhajyāt*, *bhakṣīṣṭa*. Perfect tense (*liṭ*): *babhāja*. Because the substitute begins with a vowel (*ādi*), it falls under the scope of Pāṇini 6.4.120 (*ata ekahalmadhye*), and thus by Pāṇini 6.4.122 (*tṛphalabhajatrapaśca*), there is *etva* (change of *a* to *e*) and elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsalopa*): *bhejatuḥ*, *bhejuḥ*. *bhejitha*, *bhabhattha*; *bheje*, *bhejāte*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *abhākṣīt*. When a *jhal* consonant follows, there is elision of the *s*: *abhakta*. Future tense: *bhakṣyati*, *bhakṣyate*.

The root *rañj* means "to color" or "to be attached. According to Pāṇini 6.4.26 (*śapi rañjeśca*), there is the elision of the nasal [before the suffix *śap*]: *rajati* (he colors), *rajate* (he is colored). In the benedictive (*āśis*), by Pāṇini 6.4.24 (*aniditām...*), there is the elision of the nasal: *rajyāt*. Because the suffix is *ārdhadhātuka*, there is no *kit*-status; thus, the nasal is not elided, and after applying *kutva*, *anusvāra*, and *parasavarṇa*, we have *raṅkṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *rarañja*, *rarañjatuḥ*, *rarañjuḥ*; *rarañjitha* or *raraṅktha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is vṛddhi for the consonant-final [root]: *araṅkṣīt*. There is elision of the *sic* suffix: *araṅkta*, *araṅkṣātām*.

In the case of the *ṇic* suffix following the root *rañj* with *caṅ*, as in *ararañjat*: in the sense of "delighting deer" (*mṛgaramaṇa*), there is the addition of *ṇic* by the rule "the addition of *ṇic* to *rañj* in the sense of 'delighting deer'. Consequently, there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika-lopa*) by the rule "elision of the nasal before a *ṇi*-affix," and the substitution of *vṛddhi* for the penultimate vowel by the rule "vṛddhi of the penultimate *a*. Then, by the rule "shortening of the penultimate vowel when *caṅ* follows a *ṇi*-affix" (*pā0sū0* 7.4.1), the vowel is shortened; furthermore, by the rule "shortening of the penultimate vowel when a *mit* affix follows a *ṇi*," we have *arīrajat*. [The futures are: *raṅkṣyati* and *raṅkṣyate*.

The root *śap* is used in the sense of "cursing" (*ākrośe*). Parasmaipada forms: *śapati* (he curses) *aśapat* (he cursed) *śapatu* (let him curse) *śapet* (he may curse) *śapyāt* (may he be cursed) *śaśāpa* (he cursed) *śepatuḥ* (they two cursed) *śepuḥ* (they cursed) *śepitha* / *śaśaptha* (you cursed) In the *luṅ* (aorist): *aśāpīt* (he cursed) Future: *śapsyati*, etc. Regarding the sense of "reproaching" (*upalambhanārthe*), the *ātmanepada* occurs due to the supplementary rule (*upasaṃkhyāna*) stating that *śap* takes the *ātmanepada* when meaning "to reproach": *śapate*. *aśapata* (he reproached) *yaḥ karasthaṃ śapatām* (may he curse what is in his hand) *śapeta* (he may reproach) *śapsīṣṭa* (may he be reproached) *śepe* (he reproached) *aśapta* (he was reproached)

The root *tviṣ* means "to shine. Present: *tveṣati*, *tveṣate*. Benedictive: *tviṣyāt* (Parasmaipada); *tvikṣīṣṭa* (Ātmanepada). In the latter case, there is *kitva* by the rule *liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11). Perfect: *titveṣa*; in the *thali* suffix, *titveṣitha*. Aorist: *cleḥ ksaḥ* [applies]; *ativikṣat*, *ativikṣata*. The root *yaj* is used in the senses of worshiping the gods, forming a connection, and giving. Present: *yajati*, *yajate*. In the benedictive, there is *samprasāraṇa* by the rule *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti* (Pāṇini 6.1.15): *yajo vapo vahaścaiva vyeñ veñoścyatistathā* || 1 || [That is, *yaj*, *vap*, *vah*, *vyeñ*, *veñ*, and *cyu* undergo *samprasāraṇa* before a *kit* suffix.]
The root *vad*, as well as *hvayati* and others such as *navayaj*, are likewise recorded [as having the same meaning].

From this point forward, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* (vowel substitution) by this very rule until the end of the section, unless a specific rule is stated otherwise—[as in the case of] *ijyāt*. [In the optative], the rules for *ṣatva*, *katva*, and *ṣatva* apply: *yakṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), because of the rule *liṭyabhyāsasyobhayeṣām* (Pāṇini 6.1.17), which depends on the reduplication (*abhyāsa*), the doubling occurs first; thus, *iyāja*. Then, the *saṃprasāraṇa* and the single-substitute (*ekādeśa*) result in *ījatuḥ*. *Ījuḥ*. *Iyajitha*. After applying *ṣatva* and *ṣṭutva*, [the form] is *iyaṣṭha*. *Īje*. *Ījāte*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *ayākṣīt*. In the sense of *vīti* (desire) regarding the *agnihotra*: *ayaṣṭa*. Future: *yakṣyati*, *yakṣyate*.

The root *ṭuvap* means "to sow" in the sense of the continuity of seeds and threads. Present: *vapati*, *vapate*. Benedictive: *upyāt*, *vapsīṣṭa*. In the reduplicated form (*abhyāsa*), there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*): *uvāpa*. Vocalization: *ūpatuḥ*, *ūpuḥ*. Perfect: *uvapitha*, *uvaptha*; *ūpe*, *ūpāte*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *avāpsīt*, *avapta*. Future: *vapsyati*, *vapsyate*. Desiderative (*san*): *vivapsyati*. Intensive (*yaṅ*): *vāvapyate*.

The root *vah* is used in the sense of "carrying. Present tense: *vahati*, *vahate*. Benedictive mood: *uhyāt*, *vakṣīṣṭa*. Perfect tense (*liṭ*): *uvāha*, *ūhatuḥ*, *ūhuḥ*; *uvahitha*. In the absence of the augment *iṭ*, after the application of the rules for *ḍhatva*, *dhatva*, *ṣṭutva*, and *ḍhalopa*, the substitution of *o* for the vowel of *sah* and *vah* occurs by Pāṇini Sūtra 6.3.112, resulting in *uvoḍha*. *ūhe*, *ūhāte*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *avākṣīt*. Before a consonant (*jhal*), there is elision of *s*, and the rules for *ḍhatva* etc. apply as before, resulting in *avoḍha*. After the application of *ḍhatva*, *katva*, and *ṣatva*, [the forms are] *avakṣātām*, *avakṣata*. Future tense: *vakṣyati*, *vakṣyate*. By the rule *prād vahaḥ* (Pāṇini Sūtra 1.3.81), when preceded by *pra*, the root *vah* always takes the parasmaipada endings; thus, *pravahati*.
Those roots that do not take the augment *iṭ*—with the exception of those ending in *san*—are termed *ubhayatobhāṣā*.

The root *vas* means "to dwell. In the present tense (*laṭ*), it is *vasati*. For the benedictive (*āśiṣi*), there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) and the substitution of *ṣ* by Pāṇini’s sūtra 8.3.60, *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca*; thus, the form is *uṣyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *uvāsa*. The substitution of *ṣ* is as before; thus, *ūṣatuḥ*, *ūṣuḥ*, *uvasitha*, and *uvasta*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.1.44, *cleḥ sic*, and 7.4.49, *saḥ syārdhadhātuke*, there is the substitution of *s* for *t* and the application of *vṛddhi*; thus, *avātsīt*. [In the future and conditional: *vatsyati*, *avatsyat*. These roots are *aniṭ* (without the *iṭ* augment) and belong to the *parasmaipada* (active voice).

The root *veñ* is used in the sense of weaving (*tantu-santāna*). It takes the forms *vayati* and *vayate*. Regarding the benedictive (*āśiṣi*), there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) and lengthening for [the vowel] before non-ṅit kṛt and sārvadhātuka suffixes (Pāṇini 7.4.25), resulting in *ūyāt*. With reference to the rule "In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), optionally" (Pāṇini 2.4.40), the substitution of *vayi* for *veñ* occurs by the rule "In the periphrastic perfect, *vayi* is substituted for *veñ*" (Pāṇini 2.4.41). The letter *i* is for the sake of pronunciation (*uccāraṇārtha*).

The *samprasāraṇa* of the root *abhi* is prohibited by the rule "not *samprasāraṇa*" (*na saṃprasāraṇam*), which serves as an indicator (*jñāpaka*) that the substitution of *v* for *y* would otherwise have applied; thus, the *v* remains. [Objection: Since the rule "remainder" (*halādi-śeṣaḥ*) applies only when a *samprasāraṇa* has already occurred, and since no letter beginning with a consonant (*hal*) exists here once the *samprasāraṇa* is performed, of what is the remainder being prescribed? [Reply: We do not maintain here that after performing the *samprasāraṇa*, the status of the remaining initial consonant is then prescribed; nor does the rule *halādi-śeṣaḥ* prescribe the persistence of the initial consonant.

What, then, is being prescribed? It is not the elision of the initial consonant (*hal*) that is being enjoined by this rule; rather, the persistence of the initial [consonant] is prescribed for the sake of restriction (*niyamārtham*), meaning that only the initial *hal* persists and not a non-initial one. Thus, the exclusion of the non-initial is the result of the restriction. [Objection: If that were so, then the elision of the non-initial would apply only to an abhyāsa (reduplicated syllable) that begins with a *hal*, and not to one beginning with a vowel (*aj*). [Reply: This is not a fault.

Because of the recourse to the category of those produced by practice (*abhyāsajāti*), under the governing rule *vayo yaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.38), which prescribes that before a *kit* suffix in the *liṭ* [perfect], the semivowel *y* of the root *vī* (to weave) is optionally subject to *samprasāraṇa*—as was previously established for the five roots—the *y* of this *vī* is optionally replaced by *v* before a *kit* suffix in the *liṭ*. Following that, there is reduplication and then the single-substitute (*ekādeśa*) [of the *samprasāraṇa* vowel]. Thus: *ūvatuḥ*, *ūyatuḥ*; *ūvuḥ*, *ūyuḥ*; and *uvayitha*.

According to the followers of Bhāradvāja, however, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ* after the suffix *thal*, based on the statement "tāsvid" [Pāṇini 7.2.45]. Since this root belongs to the sixth class (*tudādi*), the augment does not apply by default; yet, because of the rule for the *krādiniyama* [Pāṇini 7.2.13], it occurs obligatorily. In the alternative where the substitution of *ya* [for *ve*] takes place, the *samprasāraṇa* of the reduplicated syllable is prohibited by the rule beginning with "veñ" [Pāṇini 6.1.41]. By the rule "āta au ṇalaḥ" [Pāṇini 7.1.34], we have *vavau*. By the rule "āto lopa iṭi ca" [Pāṇini 6.4.64], we have *vavatuḥ* and *vavuḥ*. There is an option for the augment *iṭ* after *thal*: *vavātha* or *vavitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), the operations prescribed by the rule "yamaramanamātāṃ sakca" [Pāṇini 7.2.73] apply, resulting in *avāsīt*.

They two remained. Regarding the rule *ṇau caṅi śācchāsāhvāvyāvevāṃ yuk* (Pāṇini 7.3.37), which is an exception to *puk*, we have *avīvayat*, *vāsyati*, and so forth. Likewise, for the root *vay* in the Ātmanepada, in the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*) we have *vāsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are]: *ūye*, *ūyāte*, *ūyire*; *ūve*, *ūvāte*, *ūvire*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *avāsta*. The remainder is to be inferred accordingly.

The root *vyen* is used in the sense of "concealment" (*saṃvaraṇe*). It forms *vyayati*. In the benedictive mood, by Pāṇini 6.1.65 (*ādeca upadeśe’śiti*), there is the substitution of *ā*, and by Pāṇini 6.4.2 (*samprasāraṇācca*), there is lengthening; thus, *vīyāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), by Pāṇini 6.1.46 (*na vyo liṭi*), the substitution of *ā* is prohibited, and there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) of the reduplication; thus, *vivyāya*. Because of the *kit* designation, there is vocalization, and by Pāṇini 6.4.82 (*eranekāco ’saṃyogapūrvasya*), there is the *yaṇ* substitute; thus, *vivyatuḥ* and *vivyuḥ*. In the *thal* suffix, by Pāṇini 7.2.66 (*iḍatyartivyayatīnām*), the augment *iṭ* is obligatory; thus, *vivyayitha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, with the *vṛddhi* augment (*prāgvat*), the forms are *avyāsīt* and *avyāsiṣṭām*. With the causative suffix (*ṇau*) and the *caṅ* [reduplication], as before, there is the *puk* augment, resulting in *avivyapat*. In the future, *vyāsyati*. Regarding the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, by the rule *svapisyamivyeñāṃ yaṅi* (Pāṇini 6.1.19), there is *saṃprasāraṇa*, followed by reduplication, yielding *vevīyate*. Likewise, in the benedictive (*āśiṣi*), *vyāsīṣṭa*; in the perfect, *vivye*; in the conditional, *avyāsta*; and in the passive, *vyāsyate*, and so forth.

The root *hveñ* is used in the sense of "calling" (*spardhā*) and "sound" (*śabda*). It forms *hvayati* (present), *ahvayat* (imperfect). For the benedictive (*āśiṣ*), there is the substitution of *ā*, along with vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) and lengthening, etc., resulting in *hūyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by the rules *hvaḥ samprasāraṇam* (Pāṇini 6.1.32) and *abhyastasya ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.33), there is vocalization, resulting in *juhāva*. In the case of a *kit* suffix, there is vocalization followed by the *uvaṅ* substitute: *juhuvatuḥ*, *juhuvuḥ*, *juhuvitha*, and *juhotha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *lipisici hvaśca* (Pāṇini 3.1.53), *cl* is replaced by *aṅ*; with the elision of the final *ā*, it becomes *āhvat*, *ahvatām*, etc.

By the rule *ṇau caṅi ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.31), there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) of the root *hve*. Thus: *ajūhuvat*. In the future tense: *hvāsyati*. With the desiderative suffix (*san*), there is vocalization as before: *juhūṣati*. With the intensive suffix (*yaṅ*): *johūyate*. Likewise, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, it is *hvayate*. In the imperfect: *ahvayata*. In the benedictive: *hvāsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *juhuve*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *lipisicihvaśca* (Pāṇini 3.1.53) and *ātmanepadeṣvanyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 2.4.44), there is optionally the substitution of *aṅ* for *cl*, and the elision of the vowel *ā*: *ahvata*.

*Āto ṅitaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.81): *ahvetām*. In the absence of the augment *aṅ*, *ahvāsta*, *ahvāsātām*. *hvāsyate*. When the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, the Ātmanepada is used after the root *hve* preceded by *ni*, *sam*, *upa*, or *vi*; likewise, the Ātmanepada is used after *hve* with *āṅ* when meaning "to challenge" (*spardhā*). These are the examples for these rules. [Now follow] the roots that are non-*iṭ* (*aniṭ*) and are spoken of as being of both types (*ubhayatobhāṣā*).

The root *vad* is used in the sense of "speaking clearly. Present tense: *vadati*. In the sense of "blessing," the suffix *āśīrliṅ* is applied: *udyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense: *uvāda*. Before a *kit* suffix, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*): *ūdatuḥ*, *ūduḥ*. In the *thali* (second person singular perfect suffix), it is *uvaditha*. By the rule *vada-vraja-* (Pāṇini 7.2.3), the form *avādīt* is derived [in the imperfect].

Likewise, regarding the rule *tathā bhāsanopasambhāṣājñānayatnavimatyupamantraṇeṣu vadaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.47): the Ātmanepada is prescribed for the root *vad* when it has the senses of "shining" (*bhāsana*) and so forth. Among these, "shining" (*bhāsana*) means radiance; as in *cārvilokāya vadate*, he speaks radiantly. "Consoling" (*upasambhāṣā*) means conciliation; as in *karmakarān upavadate*, he consoles the laborers. "Knowledge" (*jñāna*) means perfect understanding; as in *cārvilokāya vadate*, he speaks with perfect understanding. "Effort" (*yatna*) refers to exertion; as in *kṣetre vadate*, he exerts himself in the field. "Dissent" (*vimati*) means differing opinions; as in *kṣetre vivadate*, they disagree over the field.

*Upamantraṇam* means whispering; it refers to speaking to one's wife in secret. Regarding *vyaktavācāṃ samuccāraṇe* (Pāṇini 1.3.48), *samuccāraṇam* means uttering together; thus, *sampravadante brāhmaṇāḥ* ("the Brahmins speak together"). This does not apply in cases other than uttering together. Regarding *anor akarmakāt* (Pāṇini 1.3.49), *anu* denotes similarity; thus, *anuvadate kaṭhaḥ kālāpīyam* means "Kaṭha speaks like a Kālāpīya."

The option [to use the Ātmanepada] does not apply after a transitive verb in the sense of *vipralāpa* (Pāṇini 1.3.50). In the case of contradictory speech or the utterance of distinct voices, both forms occur: *vipravadante* and *vipravadanti*. Likewise, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent (*kartṛbhiprāya*), [the root] *vad* takes the prefix *apa* (Pāṇini 1.3.73): *apavadate*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), [the form is] *vadiṣīṣṭa*; in the *liṭ* [perfect], *ūde*; and in the *luṅ* [aorist], *avadiṣṭa*, and so forth.

The root *ṭuośvi* is used in the senses of "motion" and "increase. *śvayati* (he swells). *aśvayat* (he swelled). *śvayatu* (let him swell). *śvayet* (may he swell). In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), *śvīyāt*. With reference to the rule *liṭi liṅyaṅośca* (Pāṇini 6.1.29), there is an optional substitution of *samprasāraṇa* (vowel contraction) for *śvayati* by the rule *vibhāṣā śvayateḥ*; this applies both when a *kit* or *akit* suffix follows and otherwise. Thus: *śuśāva* (with *samprasāraṇa*) or *śiśvāya* (without it). By the rules for *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* substitutions, we have: *śiśviyatuḥ* or *śuśuvatuḥ*; *śiśviyuḥ* or *śuśuvuḥ*. In the perfect tense second person singular: *śiśvayitha* or *śuśavitha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, by the rule *vibhāṣā dheṭcchoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.49), there is *caṅ* for the suffix *cli*; and by the rule *caṅi* (Pāṇini 6.1.11), reduplication occurs, resulting in *aśiśviyat*. Having introduced the optionality by the rule *irito vā* (Pāṇini 3.1.57), the rule *jṛstanbhu0* (Pāṇini 3.1.58) etc. prescribes *aṅ* for *cli*; in this *aṅ*, the substitution of *i* for the root *śvi* occurs, resulting in *aśvat* and *aśvatām*.

In the case of the root *śvi* in the *sic* affix when both [the conditions for *iṭ* and *vṛddhi*] are absent, the addition of *iṭ* occurs; however, the *vṛddhi* prescribed by the rule "for roots ending in *ik*" (*sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu*) is prohibited by the rule "the [vṛddhi] of roots ending in *ha*, *m*, *y*, *anta*, *kṣa*, *ṇa*, *śvas*, *jāgṛ*, *ṇi*, *śvi*, and *edit* is prohibited" (*hmyantakṣaṇaśvasajāgṛṇiśvyeditām* Pāṇini 7.2.5). Now, one might ask: why is it not prohibited by the rule "not before *iṭ*" (*neṭi*)? Because that prohibition applies only to the *vṛddhi* characterized by the fact that the root ends in a consonant (*halanta*), as it is immediately contiguous [to that condition]. It is argued: once the form *śvi + īt* is established, since the substitution of *guṇa* and *āy* is internal (*antaraṅga*), the root becomes one ending in *ya*; therefore, why does the prohibition by the rule "of roots ending in *ha*, *m*, *y*, etc. (*hmyanta*) not apply?

This being true, the inclusion of *śvi* is made for the sake of providing an indicator (*jñāpaka*), showing that there is no internal operation (*antaranga*) in the case of *sic*. Thus: *aśvayīt*, *aśvayiṣṭām*. Under the rule *ṇau caṅi vibhāṣā śvayateḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.31), and with reference to *ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.31), there is optionally a vowel-contraction (*samprasāraṇa*). Thus: *aśūśuvat* or *aśiśvayat*. Future: *śvayiṣyati*. Conditional: *aśvayiṣyat*. Periphrastic future: *śvayitā*. Desiderative: *śiśvayiṣati*. Intensive: *śośūyate*. The root *yaj* is said to be *vāvyayati*; *vay* is like *vah*, *vas*, and *vad*. In the forms *śvayati* and *śvayati* (with the causative suffix *nic*), the roots are among those subject to vowel-contraction (*samprasāraṇa*) before *kit* affixes.
The roots *vad* and *śvi*, which take the augment *iṭ* and are conjugated in the *parasmaipada*, [are thus described].
Thus ends the section on verbal suffixes (*śabvikaraṇa*) beginning with *bhū* in the *Dhātupratyayapañcikā* composed by Hariyogin Prollanācārya.

The section beginning with *ad*: the root *ad* means "to eat. The suffixes *laṭ* and so forth are as before. In the active voice (*kartari*), the *śap* augment is applied; by the rule *adi-prabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.72), there is elision (*luk*) of that *śap*. By the rule *khari ca* (Pāṇini 8.4.55), there is the substitution of *c* for *t*, resulting in *atti*. [In the dual: *attaḥ*; [in the plural: *adanti*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): by the rule *itaśca* (Pāṇini 3.4.100), there is elision [of the *i* of the suffix]. Under the heading governing *apṛkta* suffixes, by the rule *adaḥ sarveṣām* (Pāṇini 7.3.100), the augment *aṭ* is added. By the rule *āḍajādīnām* (Pāṇini 6.4.72), the augment *āṭ* is added. And by the rule *āṭaśca* (Pāṇini 6.1.90), there is *vṛddhi* (vowel strengthening), resulting in *ādat*. [In the dual: *āttam*; [in the plural: *ādan*.

In the *loṭ* [imperative] mood, as in the case of *tiP* and other suffixes previously mentioned, the suffix *tu* is substituted by *ruḥ* according to Pāṇini 3.4.86 (*eruḥ*). In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), *tāt* is optionally substituted for *tu* and *hi* according to Pāṇini 7.1.35 (*tuhyo-stātaṅ-āśiṣy-anyatarasyām*). Thus: *attāt*, *attām*, *adantu*. For the suffix *si*, *hi* is substituted; then, by Pāṇini 6.4.101 (*hu-jhal-bhyo her dhiḥ*), *dhi* is substituted for *hi*. Thus: *addhi*, *attāt*, *attam*, *atta*. By Pāṇini 3.4.89 (*merniḥ*), *ni* is substituted for *mā* (the suffix of the first person singular). By Pāṇini 3.4.92 (*āḍ-uttamasya piñ-ca*), the augment *āṬ* is added, and it is marked with *pi*. Thus: *adāni*.

By the rule *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.99), there is the elision of the *s* [of the suffix *sip*] in *adāt* and *adāma*. In the *liṅ* [optative] for the injunctions and so forth, by the rule *yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 3.4.103), the augment *yāsuṭ* is added; then, by the rule *liṅaḥ salopo ‘nantyasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.79), there is the elision of the *s* [of *yāsuṭ*]. Thus, we have *adyāt* and *adyātām*. For the suffix *jhi*, by the rule *jherjus* (Pāṇini 3.4.108), *jus* is substituted; then, by the rule *usyapadāntāt* (Pāṇini 6.1.96), there is the substitution of the single subsequent form (*pararūpa*), resulting in *adyuḥ*.

By the rule *āśiṣi liṅ-loṭau* (Pāṇini 3.3.173), the suffix *liṅ* is used in the sense of benediction (*āśis*). By the rule *skoḥ saṃyogādyorante ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.29), there is elision of the *s*. The elision of the final *s* of the *liṅ* does not apply here by the rule *liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.79), because that rule pertains specifically to *sārvadhātuka* suffixes. Thus: *adyāt*, *adyāstām*, *adyāsuḥ*. In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], by the rule *liṭyanyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 2.4.40), the root *ad* optionally undergoes the substitution of *ghas*. The designation *ṛdit* is for the purpose of [the application of] *aṅ* [augment]. The reduplication process yields *jaghāsa*.

By the rule *kitvād gamahanajana-khanaghasām acaḥ kiti* (Pāṇini 6.4.98), there is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-lopa*). Then, by the rules *iṇkoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.57) and *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* (Pāṇini 8.3.60), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs, resulting in *jakṣatuḥ* and *jakṣuḥ*. For the second person singular, *jaghasitha*. According to the optional view of Bhāradvāja, the augment *iṭ* does not occur in *thali* because the suffix lacks the *t* marker; thus, by the restriction of the *krādiniyama*, *iṭ* is added, yielding *jaghasitha*. In the alternative case where the substitute *ghasl* does not apply, we have *āda*, *ādatuḥ*, and *āduḥ*.

Since the root *ad* is not included among those ending in *tāsi*, the option of *iṭ* being applied by Pāṇini’s sūtras 7.3.62 (*upadeśe'tvataḥ*) and 7.3.63 (*ṛto bhāradvājasya*) would result in an alternation; however, by the rule 7.2.66 (*iḍatyartivyayatīnām*), *iṭ* is applied obligatorily, yielding *āditha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), because the substitute *ghaslṛ* for *ad* is marked with *ḷ* (by the rule 2.4.37: *luṅsanorghaslṛ*), the suffix *aṅ* is applied, resulting in *aghāsat* and *aghāsatām*. In the future tense (*lṛṭ*), it is *atsyati*. In the periphrastic future (*luṭ*), it is *attā*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), there is the substitution of *ghaslṛ* for *ad*; since this occurs before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, the semivowel *y* is changed to *t* by the rule 6.1.16 (*saḥ syārdhadhātuke*), resulting in *jighatsati*.

The root *han* is used in the senses of killing and moving. As before, the suffixes *laṭ* and others are applied: *han-ti*. Because the root is marked with *ṅ*, there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika-lopa*). In the case of forms beginning with vowels that have *k* or *ṅ* as indicatory letters (*kṅit*), there is the elision of the penultimate vowel according to Pāṇini 6.4.98: *gamahana-janakhana-ghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi*, resulting in *ha-taḥ*. Regarding the form *ghnanti*: although the rule *ho hanteḥ ñṇinneṣu* (Pāṇini 7.3.54) prescribes the substitution of *gh* for *h* when followed by suffixes beginning with *ñ*, *ṇ*, or *n*, the application of the *kutva* rule (the change of *h* to *gh*) here takes precedence; thus, due to the force of that specific prescription, the status of being a "substitute" (*sthānivadbhāva*) does not apply, and we get *ghnanti*. Similarly: *haṃsi*, *hathaḥ*, *hatha*, *hanmi*, *hanvaḥ*, *hanmaḥ*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), there is the elision of the *i* of the suffix according to Pāṇini 3.4.100: *itaś ca lopaḥ*, and the elision of the final consonant and following vowels according to Pāṇini 6.1.68: *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal*. Thus: *ahan*, *ahatām*.

*aghnan* (they killed). Again, *ahan* (he killed), and so forth; [the forms] *ahata*, *ahan*, *ahanam*, *ahanva*, *ahanma*. In the *loṭ* (imperative) mood: *hantu*. When the *tātaṅ* substitute is used, there is elision of the nasal because it is marked with *ṅ* (*ṅit*); thus: *hatāt*, *hatām*, *ghnantu*. Regarding *serhiḥ* and *hanterjaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.36): when the substitution of *j* for *han* is made, the elision of *hi* by *ato heḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.105) would normally apply, but the substitution of *j* is treated as *asiddha* (not having taken effect) by *asiddhavadatrābhāt* (Pāṇini 6.4.22); thus: *jahi*.
