[The other forms are: *hatāt*, *hatam*, *hata*, *hanāni*, *hanāva*, *hanāma*. In the *liṅ* (optative) mood: *hanyāt*.

In the *āśīrliṅ* (precative) and in *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes, the substitute *vadha* is applied to the root *han* by Pāṇini 2.4.42 (*hanyātām āśiṣi ārdhadhātuke hano vadha liṅi*). Then, by Pāṇini 6.4.48 (*ato lopaḥ*), the final vowel is elided: *vadhyāt*, *vadhyāstām*, *vadhyāsuḥ*. Regarding the *liṭ* (perfect): under the governing rule Pāṇini 7.3.54 (*hohanterñṇinneṣu*), and specifically by Pāṇini 7.3.55 (*abhyāsācca*), the *kutva* (substitution of *gh*) applies to the reduplicated syllable: *jaghāna*. There is elision of the penultimate vowel and the *kutva* substitution: *jaghnatuḥ*, *jaghnuḥ*, *jaghanitha*, *jaghantha*.

In both *luṅ* and *luṅ*, there is the substitution of *vadh* [for the root *han*]. Because this [substitute] ends in a long vowel (*ā*), the augment *iṭ* is added to the *sic*. Due to the status of the elision of the *a* as being "as if it were the original" (*sthānivadbhāva*), there is no optional *vṛddhi* for what ends in a consonant (*hal*). The rest is as before: *avadhīt*, *avadhiṣṭām*. In the case of the causative (*ṇic*) with *caṅ*, by the rule *ṇau caṅi hanasto'ciṇṇaloḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.32), there is the substitution of *t* [for the *n* of *han*]: *ajīghatat*. By the rule *ṛddhano sye* (Pāṇini 7.2.70), the augment *iṭ* is added: *haniṣyati*.

In the case of *sani* (the desiderative suffix), by Pāṇini 6.4.16 (*sani ajjhanagamāṃ sani*), there is lengthening of the vowel; as before, there is the substitution of *k* for the *h* following the reduplicated syllable: *jighāṃsati*. In the case of *yaṅ* (the intensive suffix), when meaning "to injure," it should be stated that the root *han* undergoes the substitution of *ghnī*: *jeghnīyate* (in the sense of injury). In other cases, there is the augment *nuK* after the reduplicated syllable, and then the substitution of *k* for the subsequent *h*: *jaṅghanyate*. When the object is one's own limb, the *ātmanepada* suffix is used after roots *yam* and *han* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, according to Pāṇini 1.3.28 (*āṅo yamahanaḥ*). There is elision of the nasal of the penultimate vowel as before: *āhate*. Examples: *aghnāte*, *āghnate*, *āhase*.

[Present Indicative: āghnāthe, āhadhve, āhane, āhanvahe, āhanmahe. [Imperfect (laṅ): āhata, āghnātām, āghnata. [Imperative (loṭ): āhatām, āghnātām, āghnatām. [Optative (liṅ): With the addition of *sīyuṭ*, elision of *s*, elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*), and the substitution of *k* for *h* (*kutvam*): āghnīta, āghnīyātām, āghnīran. [Benedictive (āśis): As before, the substitution of *vadh* and the addition of *iṭ*: āvadhiṣīṣṭa. [Perfect (liṭ): ājaghne.

While the rules for the *laṅ* and *luṅ* [tenses] are in effect, the substitution of *vadh* occurs optionally by the rule *ātmanepadeṣvanyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.54); thus, *āvadhiṣṭa*. In the absence of that [substitution], the *han* root takes *sic* by the rule *hanaḥ sic* (Pāṇini 3.1.56), and because *sic* is *kit*, there is the elision of the nasal by *anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnāmanunāsikalopo aliṭi* (Pāṇini 6.4.37). Then, the elision of *sic* occurs by *hrasvādaṅgāt* (Pāṇini 8.2.27): *āhata*. [The dual is] *āhasātām*. Similarly, in the passive (*karman*), the verbal suffixes are as follows: *hanyate*, *ahanyata*, *hanyatām*, *hanyeta*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), there is an option regarding the *ciṇvadiṭ* augment; with the *vṛddhi* by *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.116) and the *kutva* change, it becomes *ghāniṣīṣṭa*.

In the absence of *iṭ*, [the form] is *haṃsīṣṭa*. In the alternative where *vadh* is substituted, even when *ciṇvadiṭ* is applied, the penultimate vowel does not undergo *vṛddhi* because the elision of *at* (*ato lopaḥ*) is considered as if non-existent (*asiddhatva*); thus, [the form] is *vadhiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the form] is *jaghne*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), when the suffix *ta* follows, by the rule *ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.66), *cl* is replaced by *ciṇ*; by the rule *ciṇo luk*, there is elision of that [augment]; thus, [the forms] are *aghāni*, *avadhi*. [The dual forms] are *aghāniṣātām*, *ahasātām*, *avadhisātām*. [The futures] are *haniṣyate*, *ghāniṣyate*. [The conditionals] are *ahaniṣyata*, *aghāniṣyata*. [The periphrastic futures] are *hantā*, *ghānitā*. These two [roots] are *aniṭ* and belong to the *parasmaipada*.

The root *dviṣ* means "to hate. By the rule of *guṇa*, it becomes *dveṣṭi*. Because the suffix is marked with *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa*; thus, the form is *dviṣṭaḥ*. In the third person plural, it is *dviṣanti*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), by Pāṇini 3.4.100 (*itaśca*), there is elision [of the *i* of the *tip* and *sip* endings]. By the rule *halṅyādi* (Pāṇini 6.1.68), there is elision of the *tip* and *sip* suffixes. Through the application of *jaśtva* and *cartva* to the *ṣ* sound, the forms are *adveṭ* and *adveḍ*. The third person dual is *adviṣṭām*. By Pāṇini 3.4.111 (*laṅaḥ śākaṭāyanasyaiva*) and 3.4.112 (*dviṣaśca*), the *jus* substitution optionally occurs for *jhi* in the *laṅ*; thus, *adviṣuḥ* or *adviṣan*. In the *loṭ* (imperative), the form is *dveṣṭu*. In the *liṅ* (potential), it is *dviṣyāt* and *dviṣyātām*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), it is *dviṣyāstām*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), it is *didveṣa*.

*didviṣatuḥ*, *didveṣitha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], the suffix *ksa* replaces *cli*: *advikṣat*. *dvekṣyati*, and so forth. Similarly, for the *ātmanepada*: *dviṣṭe*, *dviṣāte*, *adviṣṭa*, *adviṣātām*, *dviṣṭām*, *dviṣātām*. In the *liṅ* [optative], with the addition of *sīyuṭ* and the elision of *s*, we have *dviṣīta*, *dviṣīyātām*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), *dvikṣīṣṭa*. By the rule *liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), there is *kitva*; and by the rule *liṭi abhyāse car ca* (Pāṇini 8.4.54), since original *jaś*-sounds become original *jaś*-sounds, the *d* of *dviṣ* remains *d*: *didviṣe*. In the *luṅ*, with *ksa* replacing *cli*, we have *advikṣata*, and so forth.

The root *duh* means "to milk. By the rule *jhaṣastathordho'dhaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.40), the substitution of *gh* for *h* occurs when a *jhāl* sound follows or at the end of a word; thus, by *dāderdhātorghaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.32), the *h* of the root becomes *gh*. Then, by *jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi* (Pāṇini 8.4.53), the *gh* is replaced by *g*, resulting in *dogdhi*. By the rule *anaci ca* (Pāṇini 8.4.47), doubling occurs, and the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel applies, yielding *dogdhi*. Due to the *ṅit* nature of the affix, there is no *guṇa* [in the dual], so it is *dugdhaḥ*. The plural is *duhanti*. In the second person singular (*madhyamaikavacana*), the substitutions of *gh*, *bhaṣ*, and *c* apply, resulting in *dhokṣi*. The dual is *dugdhaḥ*, and the plural is *dugdha*.

*duhmi*, *duhvaḥ*, *duhmaḥ*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), there is elision of the *tip* and *sip* suffixes due to the rule *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal*; then *guṇa* substitution; and optionally, the changes to *ghatva*, *bhaṣ-bhāva*, *jaśtva*, and *cartva*: *adhok*, *adugdhām*, *aduhan*. Again, in the *loṭ* (imperative): *dogdhu*, *dugdhāt*, *dugdhām*, *duhantu*. When *si* is replaced by *hi*, *hi* is replaced by *dhi*; because it is *ṅit*, there is no *guṇa* substitution: *dugdhi*. In the *liṅ* (optative): *duhyāt*, *duhyātām*. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*): *duhyāt*, *duhyāstām*. In the *liṭ* (perfect): *dudoha*, *duduhatuḥ*, *duduhuḥ*. By the rule of the *krādiniyama*, *iṭ* is added: *dudohitha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist], *cleḥ* is replaced by *ksa*: *addukṣat*. In the *ṇic* with *caṅ*, it becomes *adūduhat*. [Futures: *dhokṣyati*. [Present indicative: *dugdhe*, *duhāte*. [Imperfect: *adugdha*, *aduhātām*. [Imperative: *dugdhām*, *duhātām*. [Optative: *duhīta*, *duhīyātām*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), it is *dhukṣīṣṭa*; due to the *kit* suffix, there is no *guṇa* substitution. [Perfect: *duduhe*. [Aorist: *adhukṣata*. The root *diha* (to smear) undergoes *guṇa* substitution of the vowel *i* to *e*: *degdhi*. The remainder is as before: *degdhi*, *digdhaḥ*, *dihati*, *dhekṣi*, *digdhaḥ*, *dihate*, and so forth.

The root *lih* means "to taste. By Pāṇini 8.2.31 (*ho ḍhaḥ*), the *t* is changed to *dh*, and the *ḍh* is elided; because that [elision] is considered non-existent (*asiddha*), the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel applies, resulting in *leḍhi*. Due to the *ṅit* nature [of the suffix], there is no *guṇa*; with the elision of *ḍh*, lengthening occurs: *līḍhaḥ*. [In the plural: *lihanti*. [In the second person singular present: *lekṣi*. In the *laṅ* [past tense], regarding word-final positions, the changes of *ḍhatva*, *jaśtva*, and *cartva* apply: *aleṭ*, *aleḍ*. [Dual: *alīḍhām*. [Plural: *alihan*. In the *loṭ* [imperative]: *leḍhu*, *līḍhāt*, *līḍhām*, *lihantu*. For the suffix *si* [of the second person singular], it is replaced by *hi*; *hi* is replaced by *dhi*; then *ṣṭutva*, elision of *ḍh*, and lengthening occur: *līḍhi*. [Dual: *līḍham*. [Plural: *līḍha*.

In the *liṅ* (optative): *lihyāt*, *lihyātām*, *lihyuḥ*. Due to the *kit* suffix, there is no *guṇa* strengthening: *lihyāt*, *lihyāstām*. In the perfect: *lileha*, *lilihatuḥ*, *lilihuḥ*; *lilehitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), *ksa* replaces *cli*: *alikṣat*. [The future is] *lekṣyati*, etc. In the middle voice: *līḍhe*, *lihāte*, *lihate*; *likṣe*. [Aorist: *alīḍha*, *alihātām*. In the benedictive (*āśis*): *alihata*. [Optative: *līḍhām*, *lihātām*, *lihatām*. [Benedictive: *lihīta*, *lihīyātām*, *lihīran*. In the benedictive: *likṣīṣṭa*. [Perfect: *lilihe*. [Aorist: *alikṣata*, etc.

When the three roots *duh* and the others occur in the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, following a dental (*tavarga*) in an *ātmanepada* ending, the suffix *ksa* is also subject to elision. While this remains the case, by the rule *lugvā duhadiha* (Pāṇini 7.3.73), there is optionally an elision of *ksa*. Thus: *adugdha*, *adugdhāḥ*, *adugdhvam*, and so forth, which should be inferred accordingly. In the *ātmanepada* endings beginning with *ātām*, because of the rule *ksasyācī* (Pāṇini 6.1.105), there is the elision of the suffix ending in *ksa*; thus: *adhukṣātām*. The rule *āto ṅitaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.81) does not apply here; thus: *adhukṣāthām*, *adhukṣi*, and so forth, which should be inferred accordingly.
[These roots] are stated to be both *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) and [subject to these rules] in both voices.

The root *cakṣiṅ* is used in the sense of "speaking clearly. There is the elision (*luk*) of the *śap* suffix; there is the elision of the initial consonant of the *saṃyoga* cluster; and the *takāra* undergoes the change to *ṣṭu* (becoming *kṣ*). Thus: *ācaṣṭe*, *ācakṣāte*, *ācakṣate*. Likewise, for the *thās* ending, by *tathāsaḥ se* (Pāṇini 3.4.80), there is the substitution of *se*; then, by *saṃyogādilopaḥ* and *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* (Pāṇini 8.2.41), there is the substitution of *ka*; and by *iṇkoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.57), there is the substitution of *ṣ*. Thus: *ācakṣe*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *ācaṣṭa*, *ācakṣātām*, *ācakṣata*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *ācaṣṭām*, *ācakṣātām*, *ācakṣva*. In the *liṅ* (optative), by *liṅaḥ sīyuṭ* (Pāṇini 3.4.102), there is the addition of *sīyuṭ* and the elision of *s*. Thus: *ācakṣīta*.

[In the present tense: *ācakṣīyātām*, *ācakṣīran*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule "for *cakṣiṅ*, substitute *khyāñ*," there is the substitution of *khyā*; because this [substitute] is marked with *ṅ*, it is conjugated in both voices (*ubhayapaditva*). Regarding the elision of *i* in the *liṅ*, there is an option for *etva* (the substitution of *e*) by the rules "after [a root ending in] *i*, *u*, or *ṛ*" (Pāṇini 6.4.67) and "of any other [root] beginning with a conjunct consonant" (Pāṇini 6.4.68). Thus: *ākhyāyāt*, *ākhyeyāt*, *ākhyāsīṣṭa*, *ākhyāsīyāstām*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), there is an option for the substitution of *khyāñ* by the rule "optionally in the perfect" (Pāṇini 2.4.55); consequently, there is a threefold form: *ācakhyau*, *ācakhye*, *ācacakṣe*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist], by the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyo’ṅ* (Pāṇini 3.1.52), *cl* is replaced by *aṅ*; then, by *āto lopa iṭi ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.64), the vowel *ā* is elided, resulting in *ākhyāt*. The forms are: *ākhyetām*, *ākhyan*, *ākhyata*, *ākhyātām*, *ākhyan*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with *caṅ* [the reduplicated aorist], it becomes *acikhyapat*. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *cikhyāsati*. The root *īr* means "to go. There is the elision of *śap* [the present suffix]; by *ṭeretvam*, the form is *prerte*, *prerāte*, *prerate*, etc.

The root *īḍ* means "to praise. By the rule for changing *t* to *ṣ* (*ṣṭutvam*) and *ḍ* to *c* (*cartvam*), we have *kaḥ agnim īṭṭe*. [Present Indicative: *īḍāte*, *īḍate* (with *supāṇim*). By *īśaḥ se* (Pāṇini 7.2.77) and *īḍajanordhve ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.78), the augment *iṭ* is added: *īḍiṣe*, *īḍāthe*, *īḍidhve*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), there is *āṭ*-vṛddhi: *agnim aiṭṭa*, *aiḍātām*, *aiḍata*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *īṭṭām*, *īḍātām*, *īḍatām*. In the *liṅ* (potential): *agnim īḍīta*, *īḍīyātām*, *īḍīran*. In the benedictive (*āśis*): *īḍiṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* (perfect): *īḍāñcakre*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *aiḍiṣṭa*. In the *lṛṭ* (future): *īḍiṣyate*, and so forth.

The root *īś* is used in the sense of sovereignty (*aiśvarya*). **Present Indicative:** *īṣṭe*, *īśāte*, *īśate*. By the rule *īśaḥ se* (Pāṇini 7.2.77), the augment *iṭ* is added: *īḍiṣe*, *īśāthe*. After applying the rules for *ṣatva*, *jaśtva*, and *ṣṭutva*: *īḍḍhve*. **Imperfect (laṅ):** *aiṣṭa*, *aiśātām*, *aiśata*. **Imperative (loṭ):** *īṣṭām*, *īśātām*, *īśatām*. **Optative (liṅ):** *īśīta*, *īśīyātām*, *īśīran*; *īśīṣṭa*, *īśiṣīyāstām*, *īśiṣīran*. **Periphrastic Perfect:** *īśāñcakre*. **Aorist (luṅ):** *aiśiṣṭa*, *aiśiṣātām*, *aiśiṣata*. **Future (lṛṭ):** *īśiṣyate*. **Conditional (lṛṅ):** *aiśiṣyata*. **Periphrastic Future (lṛṭ):** *īśitā*. **Desiderative (san):** *īśiṣate*.

The root *ās* is used in the sense of sitting. Present tense: *āste*, *āsāte*, *āsate*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *āsta*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *āstām*. In the *liṅ* (potential): *āsīta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *āsiṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), by the rule *dayāyāsaśca* (Pāṇini 3.1.37), the suffix *ām* is applied: *āsāñcakre*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *āsiṣṭa*. The root *āṅ-śās* is used in the sense of wishing. *āśāste*. *āyurāśāste* (he wishes for long life). *āśāsāte*, *āśāsate*. In the second person plural, by the rule *dhi ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.25), there is the elision of *s*: *āśādhve*. The root *vas* is used in the sense of wearing or clothing oneself. * vaste*, *vasāte*, *vasate*.
The root *kasi* is used in the senses of going and teaching; examples for these should be inferred.
The root *ṇisi* is used in the sense of kissing; by the rule *vā niṃsa-* (Pāṇini 8.4.33), there is optionally a change to *ṇ* when preceded by an upasarga, as in *praṇiṃste*.
The root *niji* is used in the sense of purification; [it forms] *niṅkte*, *niñjāte*, and *niñjate*.
*Śij* (in the sense of an indistinct sound): *śiṅkte*, *śiñjāte*, *śiñjate*.
*Vṛj* (in the sense of avoiding): *vṛṅkte*, *vṛñjāte*, *vṛñjate*; in the *laṅ* [aorist]: *avṛṅkta*, *avṛñjātām*, *avṛñjata*.
*Pṛc* (in the sense of contact): *pṛṅkte*, *pṛñcāte*, *pṛñcate*.
The root *añj* means "to smear. From *añj-ati*, *añj-ā-te*, and *añj-ate*: because these roots end in *it*, the augment *num* is added.

The root *ṣūṅ* means "the delivery of a fetus by a living being" (*prāṇigarbhavimocane*). [Present tense: *sū-te*. In the case of roots beginning with *aj* (such as *su*), *uvaṅ* is substituted: *suv-ā-te*, *suv-ā-te*. [Aorist: *asū-ta*, *asuv-ātām*, *asuv-ata*. [Imperative: *sū-tām*, *suv-ātām*, *suvat-ām*. In the first person singular, by the rule *āḍuttamasya* (Pāṇini 3.4.92), the augment *āṭ* is added; since the suffix is *pit* and thus not *ṅit*, the form *sū-e* results. However, the guna substitution that would normally occur before a *sārvadhātuka* suffix is prohibited by the rule *bhūsuvostiṅi* (Pāṇini 7.3.88). Similarly for the dual and plural: *suv-ai*, *suv-āvahai*, *suv-āmahai*.

The root *śīṅ* is used in the sense of "sleeping. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.4.21 (*śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ*), there is *guṇa* substitution for *śīṅ* before a *sārvadhātuka* affix: *śete*, *śayāte*, *śerate*. Here, in the *ātmanepada* endings, the augment *ruṭ* is applied by Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.1.6 (*śīṅo ruṭ*) because of the rule *anataḥ* [which applies to roots ending in *a*]. In the *laṅ* tense: *aśeta*, *aśayātām*, *aśeran*. In the optative: *śayīta*, *śayiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect: *śiśye*, *aśayiṣṭa*. In the future: *śayiṣyate*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the rule *ayaṅ yi kṅiti*, there is the substitution *ayaṅ*: *śāśayyate*. In the periphrastic past (*caṅ*): *aśīśayat*. The root *cakṣiṅ* [is also included here]. With the exception of *vṛṅ*, these roots are *seṭ* (having an *iṭ* augment) and belong to the *ātmanepadī* class.

In the sense of "shining" (*dyu-abhigamane*), by the rule *śapo luk* [Pāṇini 2.4.72] and *uto vṛddhir luki hali* [Pāṇini 7.3.89], there is a *vṛddhi* substitution where *guṇa* would otherwise apply: *dyauti*. [The forms are: *dyutaḥ*, *dyuvanti* (by *uvaṅ*). In the *laṅ*: *adyaut*, *adyutām*, *adyuvan*. In the *loṭ*: *dyautu*, *dyutāt*, *dyutām*, *dyuvantu*. In the *liṅ*: *dyuyāt*, *dyuyātām*, *dyuyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśīḥ*), there is a long vowel: *dyūyāt*, *dyūyāstām*. In the *liṭ*: *dudyāva*. In the *luṅ* with *sic*, there is *vṛddhi*: *adyauṣīt*, and so forth.

The root *yu* is used in the sense of "mixing. As before, there is *vṛddhi*: *yauti*, *yutaḥ*, *yuvanti*. *Ayaut*. Because of the *sanvadbhāva* [treatment] in the *caṅ* [aorist] of the root *yauti* after the causative suffix (*ṇic*), by Pāṇini 7.4.80 (*oḥ puyaṇjyapare*), there is *itva* [the substitution of *i* for *u*]: *ayīyavat*. The root *ru* is used in the sense of "sound": *rauti*, *rutaḥ*, *ruvanti*. The root *ṇu* is used in the sense of "praise": *praṇauti*, *praṇutaḥ*, *praṇuvanti*.
The root *ṭukṣu* is used in the sense of sound. [Examples: *kṣauti*, *kṣutaḥ*, *kṣuvanti*. The root *kṣṇu* is used in the sense of sharpening.

[Examples: *kṣṇauti*, *kṣṇutaḥ*, *kṣṇuvanti*. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 1.3.65, *sampūrvāt samaḥ kṣṇuvaḥ*, the Ātmanepada endings are used after *kṣṇu* preceded by the prefix *sam*: *saṃkṣṇute*, *saṃkṣṇuvāte*, *saṃkṣṇuvate*.

In *stu* (to praise), [we have] *prastauti*, *prastutaḥ*, *prastuvanti*. Because the augment *iṭ* is prescribed for these roots beginning with *yu* when an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant follows, the forms in the *luṅ* (aorist) are *ayāvīt*, *ayāviṣṭām*, *ayāviṣuḥ*; *arāvīt*, *arāviṣṭām*, and so forth. Likewise, in the *lṛṭ* (future) and *luṭ* (periphrastic future), the forms are *yaviṣyati*, *ayaviṣyat*, *yavitā*; *raviṣyati*, *araviṣyat*, *ravitā*, and so on.

In the case of the root *yu* with the suffix *san*, according to Pāṇini 7.2.49 (*yauteḥ sani sanīvantarddha*), when the augment *iṭ* is optionally present, Pāṇini 7.4.79 (*sanyataḥ*) and 7.4.80 (*oḥ puyaṇjyapare*) apply the substitution of *i* for the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *yiyaviṣati*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by Pāṇini 1.2.9 (*iko jhal*), the suffix is marked as *kit*, which prevents *guṇa* substitution; then, by Pāṇini 6.4.16 (*ajjhanagamāṃ sani*), a long vowel is substituted, resulting in *yuyūṣati*. For roots beginning with *ru*, such as *ru*, and for *grah* and *guh*, by Pāṇini 7.4.11 (*śryukaḥ kiti sani grahaguhośca*), there is a prohibition of *iṭ*, resulting in *rurūṣati*.

The analysis beginning with *nunuṣati* is the same [as before]. Regarding the roots *ru* and *stu*, because they are included among the *pit* roots, there is an option for the augment *īṭ* before a *sārvadhātuka* suffix according to Pāṇini 7.3.95 (*turustuśamyamaḥ sārvadhātuke*), resulting in *ravīti* or *stavīti*, and so forth; the rest should be understood accordingly. The root *ku* means "to sound": *kauti*, *kutaḥ*, *kuvanti*, and so forth. In the *yaṅ* intensive, it becomes *cokūyate*.
The root *su* means "sovereignty" and "splendor"; as before, it is *dyauti*.
With the exception of *kauti* and *sauti*, the roots ending in *śīṭ* are spoken of as *parasmaipada*.

The root *ūrṇu* means "to cover. As before, there is *vṛddhi* [substitution]: *prorṇauti*, *praurṇoti*. According to Pāṇini 7.2.6, *ūrṇoter vibhāṣā*, there is optionally *guṇa*: *prorṇutaḥ*; *prorṇuvanti*. In the *laṅ* [past tense], by Pāṇini 7.3.91, *guṇo'pṛkte*, there is optionally *iṭ*; however, this *guṇa* is an exception to the *vṛddhi*, and thus the *vṛddhi* with *āṭ* occurs: *praurṇot*, *praurṇutām*, *praurṇuvan*. In the *loṭ* [imperative]: *prorṇotu*, *prorṇutāt*, *prorṇutām*, *prorṇuvantu*. In the potential (*liṅ*): *prorṇuyāt*, *prorṇuyātām*, *prorṇuyuḥ*.

In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), there is lengthening for [the *liṅ*] other than *kṛt* and *sārvadhātuka* suffixes (Pāṇini 7.4.25): *prorṇūyāt*, *prorṇūyāstām*, *prorṇūyāsuḥ*. Regarding the *liṭ* [perfect], the state of being like *ūrṇu* (*ūrṇuvad-bhāva*) is prescribed to prevent the substitution of *ām*; for the reduplication of the second monosyllable (*ekāc*) beginning with a vowel (*ajādi*), we have *prorṇunāva*, *prorṇunuvatuḥ*, *prorṇunuvaḥ*, *prorṇunavitha*.

In the view that [the suffix] has the marker *ṅit*, there is the addition of *iṭ* to the *sic* suffix in the *luṅ* tense according to Pāṇini 1.2.2 (*vija iṭ*) and optionally according to 1.2.3 (*vibhāṣorṇoḥ*). Because of this, there is optionally the *ṅit*-characteristic for the root *ūrṇu* according to 7.2.6 (*ūrṇotervibhāṣā*), and consequently, there is optionally *vṛddhi*. Thus, there is a threefold form: *ūrṇāvīt*, *ūrṇāviṣṭām*, *ūrṇāviṣuḥ*; *aurṇavīt*, *aurṇāviṣṭām*, *aurṇāviṣuḥ*; and *aurṇavīt*, *aurṇaviṣṭām*, *aurṇaviṣuḥ*. [The futures are: *ūrṇaviṣyati* and *aurṇaviṣyat*; the periphrastic futures are *ūrṇavitā* and *ūrṇavitā*.

In the alternative where *iṭ* is present, by the rule *sanīvantardhaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.49), we have *prorṇunaviṣati* or *prorṇunuviṣati*. In the absence of *iṭ*, we have *prorṇunūṣati*. Regarding the statement that "the substitution of *ūrṇu* for *ūrṇu* is prescribed for the purpose of establishing the *yaṅ* [intensive] formation," the *yaṅ* is applied according to the Vārttika *ūrṇotīnām upasaṃkhyānam*, resulting in *prorṇūnūyate*. Similarly, in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*), we have *prorṇute*, *prorṇuvāte*, and so forth. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), we have *prorṇuviṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *upasargātsunoti* (Pāṇini 8.3.65), we have *prorṇunuve*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist]: *praurṇaviṣṭa*, *praurṇuviṣṭa*; *praurṇaviṣyate*, *praurṇuviṣyate*, and so forth. The root *ṣṭuñ* means "to praise. Present tense: *stauti*, *stutaḥ*, *stuvanti*. Regarding the change of *s* to *ṣ* after a prefix: by the rule *upasargāt sunoti* (Pāṇini 8.3.65), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* when following a prefix; thus, *abhiṣṭauti*. In the *laṅ* [imperfect], by the rule *aḍvyavāye’pi* (Pāṇini 8.3.64), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* even when there is an intervening *aṭ*; thus, *abhyaṣṭaut*, *abhyaiṣṭutām*, *abhyaṣṭuvan*. In the *loṭ* [imperative]: *stautu*, *stutāt*, *stutām*, *stuvantu*. In the *liṅ* [optative]: *stuyāt*, *stuyātām*, *stuyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), there is lengthening: *stūyāt*, *stūyāstām*.

"Of the consonants following a *ś*, the preceding one remains, while the others are elided when a suffix marked with *ñ* or *ṇ* follows" (Pāṇini 7.2.115). Thus, [the form] *tuṣṭāva* is formed; *tuṣṭuvatuḥ*; *tuṣṭavuḥ*. In the case of the suffix *thal*, there is a prohibition by the rule concerning the *kryādi* group: *tuṣṭotha*. Similarly, for those roots listed in the *kryādi* group, there is no *suṭ* augment in *thal*. However, for the root *kṛ*, [there is *suṭ*]. For other forms, in the *luṅ* tense, the augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule "after *stu*, *su*, and *dhūñ*, in the *parasmaipada*" (Pāṇini 7.2.72), and there is *vṛddhi* in the *sic* suffix. By the rule "when *iṭ* follows *iṭ*" (Pāṇini 8.2.28), [the *s* is elided]: *astāvīt*, *astāviṣṭām*. In the *caṅ* (reduplication) of the causative (*ṇic*), [it is] *atuṣṭuvat*. [The future is] *stoṣyati*, and so forth.

Present: *stu-te*, *stuv-ā-te*, *stuv-ate*; Imperfect: *a-stu-ta*, *a-stuv-āt-ām*, *a-stuv-ata*; Imperative: *stu-t-ām*, *stuv-āt-ām*, *stuv-at-ām*; Optative: *stuv-ī-ta*, *stuv-ī-y-āt-ām*, *stuv-ī-r-an*. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*): *stoṣ-ī-ṣṭa*, *stoṣ-ī-y-ās-tām*; in the *dhvam* ending, there is cerebralization: *stoṣ-ī-ḍh-v-am*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), however: *tuṣṭu-ve*, *tuṣṭuv-ā-te*; in the *dhvam* ending, as before, there is the prohibition of *iṭ* and cerebralization: *tuṣṭu-ḍh-ve*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *asto-ṣ-ṭa*, *asto-ṣ-āt-ām*; in the *dhvam* ending, *asto-ḍh-v-am*; the rest is to be understood accordingly.

The root *brūñ* is used in the sense of "distinct speech. According to Pāṇini 7.3.93 (*piti sārvadhātuke bruva īṭ*), the augment *īṭ* is added before a *pit* sārvadhātuka suffix. Present tense: *bravīti*, *brūtaḥ*, *bruvanti*. Aorist: *abravīt*, *abrūtām*. Imperative: *bravītu*, *brūtāt*, *brūtām*. Optative: *brūyāt*, *brūyātām*, *brūyuḥ*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), *brū* becomes *vac* with vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*). Benedictive: *ucyāt*, *ucyāstām*. Similarly for the middle voice (*ātmanepada*): Present: *brūte*, *bruvāte*. Aorist: *abrūta*, *abrūvātām*. Imperative: *brūtām*, *bruvātām*. Optative: *bravīta*, *bravīyātām*. In the sense of a benediction: Benedictive: *vakṣīṣṭa*, *vakṣīyāstām*.

The *samprasāraṇa* [substitution] is a single substitute (*ekādeśa*): *ūve*, *ūvāte*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], by the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyo’ṅ* (Pāṇini 3.1.52), there is the suffix *aṅ*; then, by *vaca um* (Pāṇini 7.4.20), there is the augment *um*: *avocata*. By *āto ṅitaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.81), [the long vowel is applied]: *avocetām*. [In the future: *vakṣyati*; [in the conditional: *avakṣyata*. In the *laṭ* [present], by *bruvaḥ pañcānāmādita āho bruvaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.84), in the alternative where *āha* is the substitute, the suffixes beginning with *tiP* are replaced by those beginning with *ṇal*: *āha*, *āhatuḥ*, *āhuḥ*. By *sipasthali*, the *hakāra* is replaced by *thakāra*: *āttha*. One [of these forms] has the augment *iṭ*, while the other two are without *iṭ*; it is used in both voices.

The root *iṇ* means "to go. The letter *ṇ* is for the purpose of specification, according to the rule *iṇo yaṇ* (Pāṇini 6.4.81). There is elision of the suffix *śap*, and the *guṇa* substitution [of *i*] occurs in the *sārvadhātuka* [suffixes], resulting in *eti*. Because of the *ṅit*-characteristic [of the suffix], there is no *guṇa* [in the case of the *ārdhadhātuka* suffix], resulting in *itaḥ*. Since the *iyaṅ* substitution would otherwise apply, overriding the *yaṇ* substitution prescribed by *iko yaṇādeśaḥ*, the rule *iṇo yaṇ* (Pāṇini 6.4.81) again prescribes the *yaṇ* substitution, resulting in *yanti*. In the *laṅ* [mood], we have *ait*, *aitām*. Because the *yaṇ* substitution for *iṇ* is considered "as if not established" (*asiddhavat*) by the rule *asiddhavadatrābhāt* (Pāṇini 6.4.22), the augment *āṭ* is applied, resulting in *āyan*. [In the imperative: *etu*, *itāt*, *itām*, *yantu*. [In the optative: *iyāt*, *iyātām*.

In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), the vowel is long: *īyāt*, *īyāstām*. By the rule *upasargāddhrasvaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.23), which prescribes shortening for the root *ūh* after a prefix, there is shortening in the optative (*liṅ*): *udiyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), with the suffix *tip* replaced by *ṇal*, once the vowel has been lengthened, there is reduplication; then, due to the status of being a substitute (*sthānivadbhāva*) as governed by the rule *dvirvacane'ci* (Pāṇini 1.1.59), the reduplication occurs. By the rule *abhyāsasyāsavarṇe* (Pāṇini 6.4.78), the *iyaṅ* substitution takes place: *iyāya*. In the perfect with a *kit* suffix, the long vowel is substituted for the guṇa; by the rule *kiti* (Pāṇini 1.1.5), there is lengthening: *īyatuḥ*, *īyuḥ*.

Regarding the root *iṇ* (to go), the substitute *gāṅ* is applied by the rule *īyitha iṇo gā luṅi* (Pāṇini 2.4.45). By the rule *gātisthā...* (Pāṇini 2.4.77) and others, there is the elision (*luk*) of *sic*. Thus: *agāt*, *agātām*. By the rule *ātaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.110), *jhi* is replaced by *jus*: *aguḥ*. In the case of the causative (*ṇic*), when the suffix *caṅ* follows, the rule *ṇau caṅi ṇau gamirabodhane* (Pāṇini 2.4.46) prescribes the substitute *gam* for *iṇ* when not meaning "to understand": *ajīgamat*. However, when meaning "to understand," [the substitute is *pratyāyi*]: *pratyāyiyat*. In the future tense (*eṣyati*), etc., the substitute *gam* is applied by the rule *sanic* (Pāṇini 2.4.47). The augment *iṭ* is added by the rule *gameriṭ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.58):
*jigamiṣati*. But when meaning "to understand," it is *pratīṣiṣati*. This very purpose [of the rule] is for the *u* of *san*; it has no other.
It is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) and belongs to the *parasmaipada* (active voice).

The root *iṅ* means "to study. The roots *iṅ* and *ik* do not deviate from their prefixes; [therefore,] the substitution of *e* for the final vowel of the prefix occurs: *adhīte*, *adhīyāte*, *adhīyate*. With the augment *āṭ*, there is vṛddhi: *adhyaita*, *adhyaiyātām*, *adhyaiyata*. In the imperative: *adhītām*, *adhīyātām*. In the optative (*liṅ*): *adhīyīta*, *adhīyātām*, *adhīyīran*. In the precative (*āśiṣ*): *adhyeṣīṣṭa*, *adhyeṣīyāstām*, *adhyeṣīran*. In the second person plural with the suffix *dhvam*: *adhyaiṣīḍhvam*.

By the rules *liṭi iṅaśca* (Pāṇini 2.4.48) and *gāṅ liṭi* (Pāṇini 2.4.49), the substitute *gāṅ* is applied. Due to the status of the original element (*sthānivadbhāva*) regarding the elision of the vowel *ā*, there is reduplication: *adhijage*, *adhijagāte*, *adhijagire*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, by the rule *vibhāṣā luṅlṛṅoḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.50), when the substitute *gāṅ* is applied, the suffix *sic* becomes *ṅit* by *gāṅkuṭādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.2.1). Consequently, the substitution of *ī* for the final vowel occurs by *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali* (Pāṇini 6.4.66): *adhyagīṣṭa*, *adhyagīṣātām*, *adhyagīṣata*.

In the alternative where *gāṅ* is not substituted, [the forms are]: *adhyaiṣṭa*, *adhyaiṣātām*, *adhyaiṣata*. In the alternative where *gāṅ* is substituted by the rule *ṇau caṅi ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.31), because it is marked with *ṅ*, the substitution of *ī* does not occur; thus [the form] is *adhyeṣyata*, not *adhyagīṣyata*. [The forms are]: *adhyeṣyata*, *adhyetām*. By the rules *sani ca* (Pāṇini 2.4.47) and *iṅśca* (Pāṇini 2.4.48), there is the substitution of *gam* [for *iṅ*]. By the rule *ajjhanagamāṃ sani* (Pāṇini 6.4.16), there is lengthening [of the vowel]; thus: *adhijigāṃsate*. [Roots] ending in a consonant that are marked as *ātmanepada* are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*).

The root *i* is used in the sense of remembering (*smaraṇe*). The letter *k* [in the root *adhī*] is for the purpose of specifying that it takes the accusative case according to Pāṇini’s rule 2.3.52: *adhīgarthadayeśāṃ karmaṇi*. Thus: *adhyeti*, *adhītaḥ*, *adhīyanti*. According to those who maintain that the augment *iṭ* applies generally as in the case of *iṇ*, the substitution of *yaṇ* according to Pāṇini’s rule 6.4.81 (*iṇo yaṇ*) results in *adhiyanti*. In the *laṅ* [imperfect]: *adhyait*, *adhyaitām*, *adhyaiyan*. In the view where there is the substitution of *iyaṅ*, the form is *adhyāyan*. In the *loṭ* [imperative]: *adhyaitu*, *adhītāt*, *adhītām*, *adhiyantu*. Optionally in the *liṅ* [optative]: *adhīyāt*.

In the present tense: *adhīyātām*, *adhīyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *adhīyāt*, *adhīyāstām*, *adhīyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *adhīyāya*, *adhīyatuḥ*, *adhīyuḥ*; [the lengthening occurs] by *dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti* (Pāṇini 7.4.69); [in the second person singular]: *adhīyayitha* or *adhīyetha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), due to the extension [of rules] by *iṇvadikaḥ*, there is the substitution of *gāṅ*; by *gātisthā...* (Pāṇini 2.4.77), there is the elision of *sic*: *adhyagāt*, *adhyagātām*, *adhyaguḥ*.

In the case of the causal suffix *ṇic* followed by *caṅ*, the substitution of *gam* for [the root *iṅ*] occurs by virtue of the extended application (*atideśa*) of Pāṇini 2.4.46, *ṇau gamir abodhane*. Thus: *adhyajīgamat* (he caused to study), *adhyeṣyati* (he will cause to study), *adhyaiṣyat* (he would have caused to study), and *adhyetā* (he will have caused to study). In the case of the desiderative suffix *san*, the substitution of *gam* for [the root *iṅ*] occurs by virtue of the extended application of Pāṇini 7.3.56, *sani ca*; thus: *adhijigamiṣati* (he desires to study).

The root *vī* is used in the senses of motion, procreation, beauty, eating, and cutting. [In the present tense: the suffix *śap* is elided, and there is the *guṇa* substitution for the *sārvadhātuka* affix; however, because it is marked with *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa*, resulting in *vītaḥ*. Before vowel-initial endings, *viyaṅ* is substituted for *vī*: *avīyat*, *avīyatām*, *avīyan*; *āvetu*, *vetu*, *vītāt*, *vītām*, *viyantu*; *vīyāt*, *viyātām*, *vīyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), [the forms are] *vīyāt*, *vīyāstām*, *vīyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *vivāya* (by *eranekācaḥ* Pāṇini 6.4.82, *yaṇ* is substituted); *vivyatuḥ* (here, due to the status of the substitute as the original, there is reduplication); *vivyuḥ*; *vivayitha*.

In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense with *sic*, there is *vṛddhi*: *avaiṣīt*. In the *caṅ* (reduplicated aorist) following the causative (*ṇi*), when the sense is "procreation" (*prajana*), according to the alternative view that *vī* takes *ātva*, there is *puk*: *prāvīvayat*. Otherwise, it is *prāvīvayat*. [The future forms are] *veṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *vā* is used in the senses of "going" (*gati*) and "blowing" (*gandhana*). **Present:** *vāti*, *vātaḥ*, *vānti*. **Imperfect (*laṅ*):** *avāt*, *avātām*. By the rule *laṅaḥ śākaṭāyanasyaiva* (Pāṇini 3.4.111), the suffix *jhi* becomes *jus* (*avuḥ*), resulting in *avāvuḥ*. Otherwise, it is *avāt*. **Optative (*liṅ*):** *vātu*, *vātāt*, *vātām*, *vāntu*. **Precative (*āśīrliṅ*):** *vāyāt*, *vāyātām*, *vāyuḥ*. **Benedictive (*āśiṣi*):** *vāyāt*, *vāyāstām*, *vāyāsuḥ*. **Perfect (*liṭ*):** By the rule *āta au ṇalaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.34), *vavau*; *vavatuḥ*, *vavuḥ*; *vavātha* or *vavitha*. **Aorist (*luṅ*):** With the augment *s* and *iṭ*, *avāsīt*, *avāsiṣṭām*, *avāsiṣuḥ*.
**Future:** *vāsyati*. **Conditional:** *avāsyat*, etc. The root *yā* is used in the sense of "reaching" (*prāpaṇa*).
Bhā means to shine;
pā means to protect;
rā means to give.

The roots *lā* (in the sense of taking), *dāp* (in the sense of cutting), and *mā* (in the sense of measuring) function as before. However, there is this distinction: regarding the root *pā*, it is stated that when the suffix *ṇic* is applied and followed by *caṅ* (the reduplication of the aorist), there is elision (*luk*) [of the causative marker]. Thus, overriding the augment *puk*, the augment *luk* applies, resulting in *apīpalat*. But for the root *lā*, according to Pāṇini 7.3.39, "there is optionally the augment *luk* for *lā* and *lī* in the sense of causing affection or falling," the augment *luk* applies, resulting in *alīlalat*. For the root *mā*, in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), by Pāṇini 6.4.67, "there is *etva* (substitution of *e* for *ai* in the case of *mā* before the *liṅ* ending)," one has *meyāt*. In the case of the desiderative suffix (*san*), by Pāṇini 7.4.54, "before *san*, the roots *mī*, *mā*, etc., [take the *ṅit* designation]," the operations beginning with that apply, resulting in *mitsati*. In the case of the intensive suffix (*yaṅ*), by Pāṇini 6.4.66, "there is *itva* (substitution of *i* for *ai* in the case of *ghu*, *mā*, *sthā*, etc.)," one has *meyīyate*.

The root √*snā* is used in the sense of purification (*śauce*). Due to the absence of the cause [for the substitution], the change to *ṇa* does not occur: *snāti*. [Imperfect: *asnāt*. [Imperative: *snātu*. [Optative: *snāyāt*. Regarding the benedictive (*āśīḥ*), by the rule *vānyasya saṃyogādeḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.68), there is optionally the substitution of *e*: *snāyāt* or *sneyāt*. [Perfect: In the *liṭ* [tense], *sasnau*, *sasnatuḥ*, *sasnuḥ*; [second person singular: *sasnātha* or *sasnitha*. [Aorist: In the *luṅ* [tense], *asnāsīt*, *asnāsiṣṭām*. [Future: *snāsyati*. [Conditional: *asnāsyat*. [Periphrastic future: *snātā*. [Desiderative: *siṣṇāsati*. [Intensive: *sāsnāyate*. The root √*śrā* is used in the sense of cooking (*pāke*). The root √*drā* is used in the sense of going with contempt (*kutsāyāṃ gatau*).
*psā* in the sense of eating;
*khyā* in the sense of speaking;
*prā* in the sense of filling—as before.

The root *vid* means "to know. Examples include *vetti*, *vittaḥ*, *vidanti*, and so forth. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.4.83 (*vido laṭo vā*), the suffixes *ṇal* and others are optionally applied; thus we have *veda*, *vidatuḥ*, *viduḥ*; *vettha*, *vidathuḥ*, *vida*; *veda*, *vidva*, *vidma*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), we have *avedat*, *avittām*. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.4.109 (*sijabhyastavidibhyaśca*), the *jhi* suffix takes *jus*; thus we have *aviduḥ*. In the imperative: *vettu*, *vittāt*, *vittām*, *vidantu*. In the optative: *vidyāt*, *vidyātām*, *vidyuḥ*; *vidyāt*, *vidyāstām*.

In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, by the rule *uṣavidajāgṛbhyo'nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.38), there is optionally *vidāñcakāra*. Because the root ends in a long vowel (*adanta*), there is no *guṇa* substitution; thus, *viveda*, *vividatuḥ*, *vividuḥ*, and *viveditha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], with the augment *iṭ* added to *sic*, it becomes *avedīt*. The future is *vediṣyati*; the conditional is *avediṣyat*; and the periphrastic future is *veditā*. By the rule *sani rudavida0* (Pāṇini 1.2.8), there is obligatory *kit*-treatment in the desiderative, resulting in *vividiṣati*. With the prefix *sam-*, the *ātmanepada* is used by the rule *samo gamyṛcchi0* (Pāṇini 1.3.29), etc.; thus, *saṃvitte*, *saṃvidāte*. [In the benedictive,] there is the augment *ruṭ* after *śīṅ*.

By the rule *vetteḥ vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini 7.1.7), there is optionally the augment *ruṭ* after the substitute *at* for the root *vid*; thus: *saṃvidate*, *saṃvidrate*. In the *laṅ* [imperfect]: *samavitta*, *samavidātām*, *samavidata*, *samavidrata*. In the *loṭ* [imperative]: *saṃvittām*, *saṃvidātām*, *saṃvidatām*, *saṃvidratām*. [In the *liṅ* (potential/optative): *saṃvidīta*, *saṃvidīyātām*, *saṃvidīran*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *saṃvidiṣīṣṭa*, *saṃvidiṣīyāstām*, *saṃvidiṣīran*. In the *liṭ* [perfect]: *saṃvivide*, *saṃvividāte*. In the *luṅ* [aorist]: *samavediṣṭa*, and so forth.
According to the rule *loṭi vidāṃkurvantvityanyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.41), forms such as *vidāṅkarotu*, *vidāṅkurutāt*, *vidāṅkurutām*, and *vidāṅkurvantu* occur.

In the sense of "existence" (*bhuvi*), [the root *as* is used]: In the presence of a *sarvadhātuka* suffix marked with *ṅ*, there is elision of the *a* of *as* and *śnā* (Pāṇini 6.4.111): *asti*; *staḥ*. When followed by a suffix beginning with *y* preceded by *ac*, the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* occurs after the prefixes *pra-* and *āduḥ* when *ati* follows (Pāṇini 8.3.89): *viṣanti*; *prāduṣṣanti*. By the rule "there is elision of *s* before the *sic* augment and before *tas* and *ti*" (Pāṇini 6.4.111), there is elision of *s*: *asi*; *sthaḥ*; *asmi*; *svaḥ*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), by the rule "there is *iṭ* after *sic* before an unaccented (*apṛkta*) ending" (Pāṇini 7.3.96), the augment *iṭ* is added; then by *āṭ*-vṛddhi: *āsīt*; *āstām*; *āsan*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *astu*; *stāt*; *stām*; *santu*; *edhi*.

In this context, there is the substitution of *ser* [for the suffix *sip*]. By the rule *hujhalbhyo herdhiḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.101), there is the substitution of *dhi* for *hi*. By the rule *ghvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaśca* (Pāṇini 6.4.119), there is the substitution of *e* [for the root vowel], and by the rule *dhi ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.25), there is the elision of the *s*. Thus, we have *edhi*. In the *liṅ* [optative] mood, the substitution of *ṣ* would occur. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), by the rule *asterbhūḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.52), we have *bhūyāt*. The remainder is like the verb *bhavati*; however, in the scope of the subsequent application (*anuprayoga*), there is no occurrence of the root *bhū*.

The root *mṛj* means "to cleanse. Regarding its application with the suffixes denoting the *guṇa* stage, by the rule *mṛjervṛddhiḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.114), there is *vṛddhi*. By the rule *vraścabhrasja...* (Pāṇini 8.2.36), the letter *c* is changed to *ṣ*, and by the rule for *ṣṭu* (Pāṇini 8.4.41), the *t* is changed to *ṣ*; thus, *mārṣṭi*. Because the suffix is marked with *ṅ*, there is no *vṛddhi*; thus, *mṛṣṭaḥ*. *Mṛjanti*. According to the statement, "In the case of *mṛj* followed by a suffix beginning with a non-initial vowel (*ajādau*) that causes *saṃkrama*, *vṛddhi* is optionally desired," there is *vṛddhi* in one alternative; thus, *mārjanti* or *mṛjanti*. Regarding the changes to *ṣ*, *k*, and *ṣ*: *mārṣṭi*, *mṛṣṭaḥ*, *mṛṣṭa*. *Mārjmi*, *mṛjvaḥ*, *mṛjmaḥ*.

In the *laṅ* [aorist] tense, after the elision of *tip*, *sip*, and *hal*, there is no elision of the final consonant cluster (*saṃyogāntalopa*) due to the restrictive rule *rātsasya* (Pāṇini 8.2.24). Thus: *nyamārṣṭa*, *nyamṛṣṭām*, *nyamṛjan*. Again, in the *loṭ* [imperative]: *mārṣṭu*, *mṛṣṭāt*, *mṛṣṭām*, *mṛjantu*. In the *liṅ* [optative]: *mṛjyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *mṛjyāt*, *mṛjyāstām*. In the *liṭ* [perfect]: *mamārja*, *mamṛjatuḥ*, *mamṛjuḥ*; *mamārjatuḥ*, *mamārjuḥ*. Because it is marked with *ūdit*, there is an optional *iṭ*: *mamarjitha*, *mamārṣṭha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist]: *amārjīt*, *amārjiṣṭām*.

In the aorist (luṅ), with the absence of *iṭ*, [the forms are] *amārkṣīt*, *amārkṣṭām*, *amārkṣuḥ*. With the causative suffix (*ṇic*) and the *caṅ* reduplication, [the forms are] *amīmṛjat* or *amamārjat*. In the future (*lṛt*) and periphrastic future (*luṭ*), [the forms are] *mārkiṣyati* or *mārjiṣyati*; in the conditional (*lṛṅ*), *amārkiṣyat* or *amārjiṣyat*. In the periphrastic future (*luṭ*), *mārṣṭā* or *mārjitā*. In the desiderative (*san*), *mimārjiṣati* or *mimṛkṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), the *rīk* substitute for the reduplicated syllable yields *marīmṛjyate*.

The root *vac* is used in the sense of speaking. Present tense: *vakti*, *vaktaḥ*, *vacanti*. Aorist (luṅ): *avak*, *avaṭ*, *avaktām*, *avacan*. Imperative (loṭ): *vaktu*, *vaktāt*, *vaktām*, *vacantu*. Benedictive (āśīrliṅ): *vacyāt*, *vacyāstām*, *vacyāsuḥ*. In the benedictive, due to the rule regarding roots beginning with *vac* (*vacyādi-sūtra*), there is the substitution of semivowels for vowels (*samprasāraṇa*) because of the *kit* suffix; thus: *ucyāt*, *ucyāstām*, *ucyāsuḥ*. Perfect (liṭ): There is *samprasāraṇa* of the reduplication (*abhyāsa*); *uvāca*. When a *kit* suffix follows, there is *samprasāraṇa* and the single-substitute (*ekādeśa*) [of the two vowels]; *ūcatuḥ*, *ūcuḥ*. *Uvacitha* or *uvaktha*. The remainder is to be understood accordingly.

The root *rud* is used in the sense of shedding tears. Regarding the five roots beginning with *rud* and ending with *jakṣ*, which will be mentioned later, the augment *iṭ* is added to a following *sārvadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant (*val*), according to the rule *rudādibhyaḥ sārvadhātuke* (Pāṇini 7.2.76). Furthermore, regarding the addition of the augment *aṭ* after these same roots when followed by a suffix not beginning with a vowel (*apṛkta*), the rules *aster aḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.96), *sic ca* (Pāṇini 7.3.97), *apṛkte* (Pāṇini 7.3.91), and *rudaś ca pañcabhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.98)—under the governing heading *asti-sico 'pṛkte*—as well as *aḍ gārgya-gālavayoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.99), both the augments *iṭ* and *aṭ* occur. Thus: *roditi*, *rudataḥ*, *rudanti*; *arodīt*, *aruditām*, *arudan*.

In the present tense (*laṭ*): *rodati*, *roditaḥ*, *rodanti*; *rodiṣi*, *rodithaḥ*, *roditha*; *rodimi*, *rodivaḥ*, *rodimaḥ*. In the imperative (*loṭ*): *rodatu*, *roditām*, *rodantu*; *rodihi*, *roditam*, *rodita*; *rodāni*, *rodāva*, *rodāma*. In the potential (*liṅ*): *rudyāt*, *rudyātām*, *rudyuḥ*; *rudyāḥ*, *rudyātam*, *rudyāta*; *rudyām*, *rudyāva*, *rudyāma*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *rudyāt*, *rudyāstām*, *rudyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *ruroda*, *rurudatuḥ*, *ruruduḥ*; *ruroditha*, *rurudathuḥ*, *ruruda*; *ruroda*, *rurudiva*, *rurudima*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *arodīt* (by the rule *irito vā* [Pāṇini 3.1.57], there is optionally the suffix *aṅ*, hence *arodat*). In the causative with *caṅ* (reduplication), *arūrudat*. In the future (*lṛṭ*): *rodiṣyati*, etc. By the rule *rudavidamuṣagrahi...* (Pāṇini 1.2.8), the suffix *san* is always *kit*, hence *rurudiṣati*.

*niṣvap*: *śete*, *svapiti*, *svapitaḥ*, *svapanti*. In the *laṅ* [past tense]: *asvapīt*, *asvapat*. [Imperative: *svapitu*, *svapitāt*, *svapitām*, *svapantu*. [Optative: *svapyāt*, *svapyātām*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), because of the *kit* designation, there is *saṃprasāraṇa*: *supyāstām*. [Perfect: *suṣvāpa*; because of the *kit* designation, there is *saṃprasāraṇa*: *suṣupatuḥ*, *suṣupuḥ*, *suṣvapitha* or *suṣvaptha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist]: *asvāpsīt*. In the causative with *caṅ* [reduplication], by the rule *svāpeścaṅi* (Pāṇini 6.1.18), there is *saṃprasāraṇa*: *asūṣupat*. [Future, etc.: *svapsyati*, and so forth.

By the rule *sani rudavidaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.18), there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*) due to the *kit* designation [of the suffix], as in *suṣupsati*. In the case of the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the rule *svapisyamivyenāṃ yaṅi* (Pāṇini 6.1.19), there is vocalization, as in *soṣupyate*.

The root *śvas* means "to breathe. Present: *śvasiti* ("he breathes"). Imperfect: *aśvasīt*, *aśvasat*. Imperative: *śvasitu*. Optative: *śvasyāt*. Perfect: *śaśvāsa*, *śaśvasatuḥ*, *śaśvasuḥ*, *śaśvasitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), when the rule for the augment *vṛddhi* (Pāṇini 7.2.3) applies due to the root ending in a consonant, the prohibition by the rule *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4) would have resulted in a permanent (*nitya*) prohibition. However, the optional prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule *ato halāderlaghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.7) would then have applied; this is, however, barred by the rule *hyantakṣaṇaśvasajāgṛṇiśvyeditām* (Pāṇini 7.2.5). Consequently, the permanent prohibition by *neṭi* (Pāṇini 7.2.4) remains unrestrained. Thus: *aśvasīt*. Future: *śvasiṣyati*, and so forth.

And here: by the rule *rephavad-upasargāt parasya aniteḥ* (Pāṇini 8.4.19), there is the substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*] in *an*. Thus: *prāṇiti*, *prāṇitaḥ*, *prāṇanti*. In the *laṅ* [past tense], with the augment *aṭ*, there are two forms: *prāṇīt*, *prāṇat*; *prāṇitām*, *prāṇan*; *prāṇitu*, *prāṇitāt*; *prāṇitām*, *prāṇantu*. In the optative: *prāṇyāt*, *prāṇyātām*, *prāṇyuḥ*; *prāṇyāstām*, *prāṇyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *prāṇa*, *prāṇatuḥ*, *prāṇuḥ*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *prāṇīt*, *prāṇiṣṭām*, *prāṇiṣuḥ*.

By the rule *ṇau caṅi ubhau sābhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 8.4.20), there is the substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*] in the causative with the *caṅ* suffix; thus: *prāṇiṇat*. The future is *prāṇiṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *jakṣ* (meaning "to eat" and "to laugh") forms *jakṣiti*, *jakṣitaḥ*, and so on. Since the six roots beginning with *jakṣ* and ending with *vevī* are designated as *abhyasta* (repeated) by the rule *jakṣityādayaḥ ṣaṭ* (Pāṇini 6.1.6), when the suffix *la* (present indicative) follows, the substitution of *ad* for *jhi* is applied by the rule *adabhyastāt* (Pāṇini 7.1.4). However, when the suffix *li* (imperfect) follows, the substitution of *jus* for *jhi* is applied by the rule *sijabhyastavidibhyaśca* (Pāṇini 3.4.109). Thus, in subsequent forms as well, it is *jakṣati*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), the forms are *ajakṣīt*, *ajakṣat*, *ajakṣitām*, and *ajakṣuḥ*. In the imperative (*loṭ*), they are *jakṣitu* and *jakṣitāt*.

*Jakṣitām*, *jakṣatu*, *jakṣyāt*. The remainder is to be inferred. For the roots *rud*, *svap*, *śvas*, *prāṇ*, and *jakṣ*, when followed by a *sārvadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant (*val*), there is the augment *iṭ*; however, for those not followed by a single consonant (*apṛkta*), the augment *iṭ* is prescribed.

The root *jāgṛ* is used in the sense of "the cessation of sleep. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra *jāgro 'viciṇṇalṅitsu* (7.3.85), a *guṇa* is prescribed both in the domain of *vṛddhi* and in the domain where *guṇa* would otherwise be prohibited. Here, in the domain of *vṛddhi*, the suffixes *ciṇ* and *ṇal* are excluded; and in the domain where *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* are prohibited, the suffixes marked with *ṅ* are excluded by the phrase *aviciṇṇalṅitsu*. However, the suffix *vip* is *auṇādika* (belonging to the *uṇādi* class). Thus, [from the root] we have *jāgarti*. By the rule *sārvadhātukam apit* (1.2.4), which assigns *ṅit*-status [to the suffix], there is an absence of *guṇa*; hence, *jāgṛtaḥ*. There is a substitution of *yaṇ* [for the vowel]; hence, *jāgrati*.

In the *laṅ* [past tense], by the rule *tiptasjhi...lopaḥ*, there is elision of the suffixes; then *guṇa* substitution occurs, followed by the replacement of the vowel with *ra* (*raparatva*), and the *repha* is replaced by *visarjanīya*. Thus: *ajāgaḥ*. In *ajāgṛtām*, [the same applies]. By the rule *jasi ca* (Pāṇini 7.3.109), *guṇa* is applied: *ajāgaruḥ*. [The forms] *ajāgaratam*, etc., follow similarly. In the *loṭ* [imperative]: *jāgartu*, *jāgṛtāt*, *jāgṛtām*, *jāgratu*. For the suffix *si*, it is replaced by *hi*; because this is not *apit*, it is treated as *ṅit*, and therefore there is no *guṇa*: *jāgṛhi*. In the *liṅ* [optative]: *jāgṛyāt*, *jāgṛyātām*, *jāgṛyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), by the rule *kidāśiṣi* (Pāṇini 3.4.104), the *yāsuṭ* augment is *kit*; due to its *kit* status, there is no *guṇa*: *jāgṛyāt*.

One should apply the *liṭ* suffix. By the rule *uṣavidajāgṛbhyo 'nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.38), the suffix *ām* is applied, resulting in *jāgarāñcakāra*. In the absence of *ām*, [the form] is *jajāgara*; with the *ṇal* suffix, there is *vṛddhi*, and because of the *kit* status, there is no *guṇa*: *jajāgaratuḥ*, *jajāgaruḥ*, *jajāgaritha*. In the *luṅ* tense, the augment *iṭ* is added; by the rule *hmyantakṣaṇaśvasajāgṛṇiśvyeditām* (Pāṇini 7.2.5), there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi*: *ajāgarīt*, *ajāgariṣṭām*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the *caṅ* suffix, it is *ajajāgarat*. [The forms] *jāgariṣyati*, etc., follow. There is no *yaṅ* suffix because the root has more than two syllables (*anekāctvāt*), and there is also a prohibition of *iṭ*.

The root *daridrā* means "to be poor" or "to suffer in a miserable state. It is conjugated as follows: In the present tense (*laṭ*), the form is *daridrāti*. Before an affix beginning with a consonant (*hal-ādi*) that is marked with *k* or *ṅ* (denoted as *kṅit*), there is a substitution of the vowel *i* for the final vowel of *daridrā* according to Pāṇini 6.4.114: *idaridrasya*. Thus, we have *daridritaḥ*. By Pāṇini 6.4.112: *śnābhyastayorātaḥ*, the long *ā* is elided, resulting in *daridrati*. In the imperfect (*laṅ*): *adaridrāt*, *adaridrātām*, *adaridruḥ*. In the imperative (*loṭ*): *daridrātu*, *daridritāt*, *daridritām*, *daridratu*. In the potential (*liṅ*): *daridriyāt*, *daridriyātām*, *daridriyuḥ*.

In the case of *daridrā* used in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), its substitution by *usi* occurs; furthermore, the elision of the penultimate vowel (*ā*) before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix is established by the rule stating that "the elision of *ā* [after *daridrā*] is established even when the suffix is yet to be prescribed. Thus: *daridryāti*, *daridryāstām*. In the *liṭ* (perfect tense), the elision of the *ikāra* (the vowel *i*) is required by the statement: "it should be stated that [the elision applies] after *kāsi* and roots with more than one vowel" (*kāsyanekāca iti vaktavyam*). This is because of the statement regarding the purpose of including *culump* and others. Thus: *daridrāñcakāra*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), according to the rule "in the *adyatanī* (imperfect) there is an option," if the elision of *ā* takes place, we have *adaridrīt*. Otherwise, by the rule *yamarama...* (Pāṇini 7.2.73) and others, the augment *s* and the *iṭ* augment apply, resulting in *adaridrāsīt*.

In the *caṅ* [aorist] after the causative suffix (*ṇic*), there is no elision of the penultimate vowel (*adaridrat*). Because the root is *aglopi* (having an elided penultimate vowel), there is no *sanvadbhāva*. In the *lṛt* and *luṭ* [future and periphrastic future], there is elision of the initial *ā* (*āllopa*). Even though the root ends in a vowel, because it has more than one syllable (*anekāctvāt*), there is an absence of the absence of *iṭ* (*aniṭtvābhāvaḥ*). Thus: *daridriṣyati*, *adaridriṣyat*, *daridritā*. Regarding the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini 7.2.49), which states "for *tan*, *pat*, and *daridrā*, there is an option for *iṭ*," we have: *didaridrāsati* or *didaridriṣati*. It is not said *daridrāyate*. Furthermore, the elision of the penultimate vowel (*lopa*) is not desired in the case of *daridrāṇe*. Some say *didaridrāsati* or *didaridriṣati*.

The root *cakās* means "to shine. In the present tense (*laṭ*): *cakāsti*, *cakāstaḥ*, *cakāsati*. In the imperfect (*laṅ*), with the suffix *tip*: by Pāṇini 8.2.72 (*vasusraṃsudhvaṃsvanaḍuhāṃ daḥ*), the *s* of *asti* (and here, *cakāsti*) becomes *d*; and by the rule *sipi dhātorurvā* (Pāṇini 8.2.74), the *t* is optionally changed to *d*. Thus: *acakāt*, *acakāstām*, *acakāsuḥ*. In the imperative (*loṭ*): *cakāstu*, *cakāstāt*, *cakāstām*, *cakāsatu*. In the potential (*liṅ*): *cakāsyāt*, *cakāsyātām*, *cakāsyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *cakāsyāt*, *cakāsyāstām*, *cakāsyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), as before: *cakāsāñcakāra*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist], [the form] is *acakāsīt*. In the *ṇic* [causative] with the *caṅ* [reduplication], by the rule *ṇau caṅi nāglopi-* (Pāṇini 7.4.1), there is a prohibition of the shortening of the penultimate vowel; thus, [the form] is *acīcakāsat*. [The future forms] are *cakāsiṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *śās* means "to instruct. The suffix *śap* is elided (*luk*). In the case of a *kṅit* suffix beginning with a consonant, by the rule *śāsa id aṅhaloḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.34), the penultimate vowel is changed to *i*. Then, by the rules *iṇkoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.57) and *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* (Pāṇini 8.3.60), there is the substitution of *ṣ* and subsequently *ṣṭu*-hood (*ṣṭutva*), resulting in *śiṣṭaḥ*. [In the present tense: *śāsati*, *śāssi*, *pradiśaḥ*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), with the suffix *tip*, as before, there is the substitution of *h*, yielding *aśāt*, *aśiṣṭām*, *aśāsuḥ*. With the suffix *sip*, as before, there is the substitution of *h* and *r*, yielding *aśāt*, *aśāstam*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *śāstu*, *śiṣṭāt*, *śiṣṭām*, *śāsatu*.

By the rule *śāser̥ śāhau* (Pāṇini 6.4.35), there is the substitution of *śā* for the root *śās*. Because that [substitution] is treated as non-existent (*asiddha*) by the rule *asiddhavadatrābhāt* (Pāṇini 6.4.22), the substitution of *dhi* for *hi* occurs by the rule *hu-jhal-bhyo herdhiḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.101). Thus, *śādhi*. In the optative (*liṅ*), with the substitution of *it* and *ṣatva*, we have *śiṣyāt*; *śiṣyātām*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), [we have] *śiṣyāt*; *śiṣyāstām*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), due to the *kit* designation, we have *śaśāsa*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *sarti-śāsty-artibhyaś-ca* (Pāṇini 3.1.56), there is *aṅ* in place of *cl*; with the previous substitutions of *it* and *ṣatva*, we have *aśiṣat*; *aśiṣatām*.

In the case of the *caṅ* (the aorist marker), there is a prohibition against shortening the penultimate vowel [in the case of the root *śās*]: *aśaśāsat*, *śāsiṣyati*, and so forth. The roots *vid*, *rud*, and those with substitutes beginning with *t* (such as *tan*), as well as those beginning with *śvas*, are *seṭ* (taking the *iṭ* augment).
Excluding those marked with *ū* (*ūdit*), the others are *aniṭ* (not taking the *iṭ* augment) and are *parasmaipada* (active voice).

The root *dīdhīṅ* is used in the senses of shining and playing. In the present indicative (*laṭ*): *ādidhite*. By the rule *eranekācaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.82), *yaṇ* substitution occurs: *ādidhyāte*, *ādīdhyate*. In the imperfect (*laṅ*): *ādidhīta*, *ādīdhyatām*, *ādidhyata*. In the imperative (*loṭ*): *adidhītām*, *ādīdhyatām*. In the potential (*liṅ*), by the rule *yīvarṇayordīdhīvevyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.53), the *īkāra* is replaced; with the elision of the *sīyuṭ* suffix and its *sakāra*, we have *adidhīta*. As before, there is the elision of the *īkāra*: *ādīdhīyātām*, *ādīdhīran*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is the addition of *iṭ*; as before, there is the elision of the final vowel: *ādīdhiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *ādidīdhye*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist]: *ādīdhiṣṭa*; *ādīdhiṣātām*. In the *caṅ* [reduplicated aorist] after the causative suffix (*ṇau*): *ādidīdhat*. [The conditional: *ādīdhiṣyat*. [The periphrastic future: *ādīdhitā*. [The middle desiderative: *ādīdhiṣate*. The root *vevīṅ* is equivalent to *veti*; it is said to be identical [to it]. It belongs to the *seṭ* class and is conjugated in the *ātmanepada*.

The root *vaś* means "to desire. By the rule *vraścādi*, there is the substitution of *ṣ*. Thus, *vaṣṭi* ("he desires"). By the rule *grahijyādi*, there is vocalization (*samprasāraṇa*), followed by the substitution of *ṣ* and *ṭ*; thus, *uṣṭaḥ* ("they two desire"). *Uśanti* ("they desire"). In the *laṅ* (imperfect), after the substitution of *ṣ*, *jaś*, and *car*, we have *avaṭ* ("he desired"). With the augment *āṭ* and *vṛddhi*, *auṣṭām* ("they two desired"). *Auśan* ("they desired"). In the *loṭ* (imperative): *vaṣṭu* ("let him desire"), *uṣṭāt* ("may he two desire"), *uṣṭām* ("may they two desire"), *uśantu* ("may they desire"). *Uḍḍhi* ("desire thou"). In the *liṅ* (potential): *uśyāt* ("he may desire"), *uśyātām* ("they two may desire"), *uśyuḥ* ("they may desire"). In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *uśyāt* ("may he desire"), *uśyāstām* ("may they two desire"), *uśyāsuḥ* ("may they desire"). In the *liṭ* (perfect), there is vocalization of the reduplication; thus, *uvāśa* ("he desired"). By the *grahijyādi* rule, there is vocalization; thus, *ūśatuḥ* ("they two desired"), *ūśuḥ* ("they desired").

In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, [the forms are] *avaśīt*, *avāśīt*, and so forth. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, there is an absence of *saṃprasāraṇa* due to the prohibition [stated in] Pāṇini’s Sūtra 6.1.20, *na vaśaḥ*; thus, [the form is] *vāvaśyate*. [The root] *śās* is used in the sense of commanding;
*sas* is used in the sense of sleeping. Examples [for these] are to be inferred.
The roots ending in *seṭ* are spoken in the *parasmaipada*.

And the *carkarīta* [formation] is to be regarded as having a *parasmaipada* ending and being like roots of the *adādi* class. *Carkarīta* is a technical term (*saṃjñā*) for the elision of *yaṅ* (*yaṅ-luk*) used by former teachers.
The root *hnuṅ* means "to remove. Because it is marked with *ṅ*, there is an absence of *guṇa*. Thus, *nihnute*. As an exception to the *i-ko yaṇ aci* rule, *uvaṅ* is applied: *nihnuvāte*.

The substitution of *jh* for *ha* occurs: *nihnuvate*, *nyahnuta*, *nihnutām*, *nihnuvīta*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), [the forms are] *nihnoṣiṣṭa*; in the *dhvam* ending, *nihnoṣiṣīḍhvam*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *nijuhnuve*. In the *dhvam* ending, there is optionally a cerebral [substitution]: *nijihnuvidhve* or *nijihnuviḍḍhve*. By the rule governing the *kryādigaṇa*, *iṭ* is added in the aorist (*luṅ*): *nyahnoṣṭa*, *nyahnoṣātām*. In the causative with *caṅ* (reduplication), *ajuhnuvat*. [In the future: *nihnoṣyati*. [In the conditional: *nyahnoṣyat*. [In the periphrastic future: *nihnotā*. [In the middle voice: *nijihnuṣate*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), *nijohnuyata*, and so forth.
Thus ends the section on the *adādi* roots with elided conjugational suffixes (*lugvikaraṇa*) in the *Dhātupratyayapañcikā*, composed by the master Hariyogin.

The section on *juhotyādi* [roots]: *hu* in the sense of giving and taking. For the suffixes beginning with *tiP*, there is *Śap* when the agent (*kartṛ*) is expressed. By the rule *juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.75), there is elision of that (*Śap*). By the rule *ślau* (Pāṇini 6.1.10), there is reduplication; the operations of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) apply, and there is *guṇa* for the *sārvadhātuka* suffix: *juhoti*. Because it has the marker *ṅ*, there is an absence of *guṇa*: *juhutaḥ*. By the rule *ubhe abhyastam* (Pāṇini 6.1.5), these two are designated as "reduplicated" (*abhyasta*). By the rule *adabhyastāt* (Pāṇini 7.1.4), *jhi* is replaced by *at*. By the rule *huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke* (Pāṇini 6.4.87), *yaṇ* replaces the vowel, which is an exception to *uvaṅ*: *juhvati*. In the *laṅ* [past tense], it is *ajuhot*.

*ajuhutām*: by *sijabhyastavidibhyaśca* (Pāṇini 3.4.109), the suffix *jhi* becomes *jus*; then, by *jusi ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.83), there is *guṇa*, resulting in *ajahavuḥ*. In the *loṭ* mood: *juhotu*, *juhutāt*, *juhutām*, *juhvatu*. For the substitution of *hi* with *dhi* after *hu* and roots ending in a consonant, by *serhi hujhalbhyo herdhiḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.101), there is the replacement of *hi* with *dhi*, resulting in *juhudhi*. In the *liṅ* mood: *juhuyāt*, *juhuyātām*. By *usyapadāntāt* (Pāṇini 6.1.96), there is the substitution of the subsequent form (*pararūpa*), resulting in *juhuyuḥ*.

By the rule *āśiṣi akṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.25), [the long vowel is applied]: *hūyāt*. By the rule *liṭi bhīhrībhṛhuvāṃ śluvacca* (Pāṇini 3.1.39), there is an option for the *ām* affix: *juhavāñcakāra*. Otherwise: *juhāva*, *juhuvatuḥ*, *juhuvuḥ*, *juhotha*, *juhavitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *sici vṛddhiḥ*, [the form is] *ahauṣīt*. In the *ṇic* with *caṅ* (reduplication), [it is] *ajūhavat*. [Future: *hoṣyati*. [Conditional: *ahoṣyat*. [Periphrastic future: *hotā*. [Desiderative: *juhūṣati*. [Intensive: *johūyate*.

The root *bhī* means "to fear. [In the present tense: there is *guṇa* substitution, resulting in *bibheti*. Before an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant (*hal*) and marked with *k* or *ṅ*, there is optionally the substitution of *i* for the root *bhi* according to Pāṇini 6.4.115 (*id daridrasya bhiyo 'nyatarasyām*), thus *bibhitaḥ* or *bibhītaḥ*. By Pāṇini 6.4.82 (*eranekācaḥ...*), there is *yaṇ* substitution, resulting in *bibhyati*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *saprajāpatir abibhet* (Prajāpati was afraid), *abibhitām*, *abibhītām*; by Pāṇini 7.2.83 (*jusi ca*), there is *guṇa*, resulting in *abibhayuḥ*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *bibhetu*, *bibhītāt*, *bibhītām*, *bibhyatu*. In the *liṅ* (potential/optative): *bibhyāt*, *bibhīyāt*.

[In the present tense: *bibhiyātām*, *bibhiyuḥ*, *bibhīyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśis*): *bhīyāt*, *bhīyāstām*, *bhīyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), as before, there is an optional *ām*: *bibhayāmbabhūva*, *bibhāya*, *bibhyatuḥ*, *bibhyuḥ*, *bibhayitha* (or *bibhetha*). In the aorist (*luṅ*) with the suffix *sic*, there is the *vṛddhi* substitution conditioned by the root ending in a short vowel (*iganta*): *abhaiṣīt*, *abhaiṣṭām*, *abhaiṣuḥ*.

In the case of the causative suffix *ṇic* with the *caṅ* aorist, when the fear is caused by a specific agent (*hetubhaya*), the substitution of *ā* occurs optionally according to Pāṇini 6.1.56, *bibheterhetubhaye*; in that alternative, the augment *yuk* is added. In other instances where the fear is caused by a specific agent, the suffix *ṣuk* is applied. In both cases, the ātmanepada is used according to Pāṇini 1.3.68, *bhīsmyorhetubhaye*. Thus: *muṇḍo bībhayate* ("the shaven-headed one causes fear") and *jaṭilo bibhīṣate* ("the matted-haired one causes fear"). When the fear is not caused by a specific agent, one says *abībhayat* ("he caused fear") and *bheṣyati*, etc.

The root *hrī* is used in the sense of shame (*lajjā*). Present tense: *jihreti*, *jihrītaḥ*. Because it begins with a conjunct consonant (*saṃyogapūrvatvāt*), the rule *eranekācaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.82) does not apply; instead, there is the substitution *iyaṅ*: *jihriyati*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *ajihreta*, *ajihrītām*, *ajihrayuḥ*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *jihretu*, *jihrītāt*, *jihrītām*, *jihriyatu*. In the *liṅ* (potential): *jihrīyāt*, *jihrīyātām*, *jihrīyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *hrīyāt*, *hrīyāstām*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), as before, there is an option for the suffix *ām*: *jihrayāñcakāra*, *jihraya*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *ahraiṣīt*.

By the rule *ṇau caṅy artihrī* (Pāṇini 7.3.36) and others, there is the augment *puK*; the *guṇa* substitution characterized by the suffix having *puK* as its penultimate; and the shortening of the *upadhā* vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsakāya*); thus: *ajihripat*. Similarly: *hreṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *pṝ* is used in the senses of protecting (*pālana*) and filling (*pūraṇa*). By the rules *bhṛñāmit* (Pāṇini 7.4.76) and *artipipartyośca* (Pāṇini 7.4.77), there is *it*-lengthening of the reduplicated syllable and *guṇa* substitution in the *ślau* state, resulting in *piparti*. [The forms are: *pipṛtaḥ*, *piprati*, *piparṣi*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), by the rule *halṅyādi-lopaḥ*, there is elision of *ti* and *sip*, followed by *guṇa*, replacement of *ṛ* by *ra*, and the *visarjanīya*: *apipaḥ*, *apipṛtām*, *apiparuḥ*. Again, [the imperative forms are: *apipaḥ*, *pipartu*, *pipṛtāt*, *pipṛtām*, *pipratu*. In the *liṅ* (optative), [the forms are: *pipṛyāt*, *pipriyātām*, *pipṛyuḥ*.

By the rules *āśiṣi rīṅ ṛtaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.27) and *riṅ śayagliṅkṣu* (Pāṇini 7.4.28), *riṅ* is substituted [for the root vowel] in the sense of benediction (*priyāt*). In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), [the forms are]: *papāra*, *papratuḥ*, *papruḥ*, *papartha*, *paprathuḥ*, *papra*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), [the form is] *apārṣīt*. In the future (*lṛṭ*), *pariṣyati*. The rest should be understood accordingly. In the desiderative (*san*), *pupūrṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the rule *rīṅ ṛtaḥ*, *rīṅ* is substituted: *peprīyate*.
These roots ending in *tāsi* that lack an indicatory *ṅ* are conjugated in the active voice (*parasmaibhāṣā*).

The root *ḍubhṛñ* is used in the senses of "supporting" and "nourishing. For the three roots beginning with *bhṛñ*, the rule *bhṛñām it* applies, whereby the vowel of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) becomes *i* when the suffix *ślau* follows. Thus: *bibharti*, *bibhṛtaḥ*, *bibhrati*, and so forth. As previously mentioned, in the *liṭ* tense there is an option regarding the *ślu* substitution; thus: *bibharāmbabhūva*, *babhāra*, *babhratuḥ*, *babhruḥ*, *babhartha*. In the *luṅ* tense: *abhārṣīt*. By the rule *ṛddhanoḥ sye* (Pāṇini 7.2.70), the augment *iṭ* is added: *bhariṣyati*. In the desiderative (*san*), due to the *kit* designation, the lengthening of the radical vowel, and the subsequent shortening, we have: *bubhūrṣati*.

By *yaṅi ca rīg ṛtvataḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.27), [the substitution] *bebhrīyate* occurs. Likewise: *bibhṛte*, *bibhrāte*, *bibhrate*; *abibhṛta*, *abibhrātām*, *abibhrata*; *bibhṛtām*, *bibhrātām*, *bibhratām*. In the *liṅ* [optative], by *liṅaḥ salopo'nantyasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.79), there is elision of the *s* of *sīyuṭ*; with the *yaṇ* substitute, we have *bibhrīta*, *bibhrīyātām*, *bibhrīran*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), by *uśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), because it is *kit*, there is an absence of *guṇa*: *bhṛṣīṣṭa*. In the *dhvam* [ending], there is a retroflex [substitution]: *bhṛṣīḍhvam*.

In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], [the forms are] *bibhre*, *bibharāñcakre*, and *babharāmbabhūva*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], because of its *kit* status, there is an absence of *guṇa*; by *Pāṇini Sūtra 8.2.26* (*jhalo jhali*) and *Pāṇini Sūtra 8.2.27* (*hrasvādaṅgāt*), there is the elision of the *sic* suffix, resulting in *abhṛta*. This root is *aniṭ* when followed by the *tās* [affix of the periphrastic future] and is used in both voices (*ubhayapada*).

The root *māṅ* means "to measure. In the present indicative (*laṭ*), after the augment *śap*, by Pāṇini 6.4.112 (*śluḥ śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) and 6.4.113 (*ī halyaghoḥ*), there is the substitution of *ī* for the long *ā* before a *kṅit* sārvadhātuka suffix beginning with a consonant; thus, *mimīte*. By Pāṇini 6.4.111 (*āllopaḥ*), the *ā* is elided before non-*kṅit* suffixes: *mimāte*, *mimate*. In the imperfect (*laṅ*), *amimīta*, *amimātām*, *amimata*. In the imperative (*loṭ*), *mimītām*, *mimātām*, *mimatām*. In the potential (*liṅ*), as before, the *ā* is elided: *mimīta*, *mimīyātām*, *mimīran*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), *māsīṣṭa*.

In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, by the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.64), there is elision of the long *ā*; due to its status as a *sthānivadbhāva*, reduplication occurs: *mame*. In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, it is *amāsta*. In the *san* [desiderative], by the rule *sani mīmā* (Pāṇini 7.4.54) and other operations, the *s* is changed to *t*, and following the previous rule for the *san* suffix, it becomes *mitsate*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, when the change to *ī* occurs by the rule *ghumāsthā* (Pāṇini 6.4.66), reduplication follows: *memīyate*.

The root *ohāṅ* means "to go. As before, there is the substitution of *ī* for the vowel; as before, there is the elision of *āl*. [Present Indicative: *jihīte*, *jihāte*, *jihate*. [Imperfect: *ajihata*, *ajihātām*, *ajihata*. [Imperative: *jihītām*, *jihātām*. In the *liṅ* (optative), there is the elision of *āl*: *jihīta*, *jihīyātām*, *jihīran*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), [the form is] *jahe*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), *ahāsta*; [the conditional is] *ajīhapat*; [the future is] *hāsyati*, and so forth. In the *yaṅ* (intensive), [the forms are] *jāhāyate* and *jehīyate*. These belong to the *ātmanepada* voice.

The root *ohāk* means "to abandon. The letter *k* [in *ohāk*] is for the purpose of including both [the roots *ohā* and *ohi*] in the rule *kakāro haśca vrīhikālayoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.148). Regarding the reduplication [of the root] by the rule *laṭ tip śapaḥ śluḥ ślau* (Pāṇini 6.1.10), what is this so-called "operation on the reduplicated syllable" (*abhyāsakārya*)? Here, under the governing rule *lopābhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 7.4.58), the rule *hrasvaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.59) applies; by the principle of "the most similar substitute" (*sthānentaratama*), a single-mora vowel (*ekamātra*) replaces the two-mora vowel (*dvimātra*) of the reduplicated syllable. Thus, in place of an *ec* vowel, an *ic* vowel occurs.

By the rule *igghrasvādeśe* (Pāṇini 1.1.48), there is the elision of one consonant from the reduplicated syllable when it consists of multiple consonants. Among the initial consonants, the *ha* and the *ka*-group (*kavarga*) undergo the substitution of *c*-class sounds (*cutva*) by the rule *kuhoścuḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.62). In that case, because of proximity (*āntaryam*), the *ha* becomes *jha*. Then, by the rule *abhyāse carca* (Pāṇini 8.4.54), the *ja*-class substitution (*jaśtva*) applies due to the mention of *ca*, resulting in *ja*. Now, one might ask: why does *jaśtva* not apply in the case of *cakāra*? It is because of the statement: "The original *car*-sounds become original *car*-sounds."

The meaning of this is as follows: those [consonants] that occur in reduplication (*abhyāsa*) remain in their original form (*prakṛticara*). Among the consonants, because of the internal similarity (*āntaratamya*) of the letter *ka*, there is the substitution of *cu* for *ku-ho* according to Pāṇini 8.4.62 (*kuhoścuḥ*), as in *cakāra* and so forth. For the letters *ya-ra-la-va-na-ma* when they are initial, there is no effect of reduplication; thus we have *yayau*, *vavau*, *rarau*, *lalau*, and *nanāma*. Regarding the letters *jha-bha-gha-ḍha-dha*, by the rule Pāṇini 8.4.54 (*jharo jhari savarṇe*), which includes the word *car* from 8.4.53, the letters *ja-ba-ga-ḍa-da* occur in place of the *jaś* sounds (*jha-bha-gha-ḍha-dha*) when following a *kavarga* [in reduplication].

By virtue of internal similarity (*antaratamatva*), the unaspirated (*jaś*) sounds of the original forms become unaspirated; thus, from *jigāya*, *ḍiḍye*, *dadau*, and *bubudhe*, the *phala* and *yaś* sounds become *ca* and *pa* respectively. Furthermore, even though they were not originally present, the *khayaḥ* (sibilants) preceded by *śar* (voiceless consonants) remain; this is to be understood from the rule *śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.4.61), and so forth.

In the presence of an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with *ha*, and before a *kṅit* suffix, the following rules apply: *ī halyaghoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.113), *iddaridrasya* (Pāṇini 6.4.114), *bhiyo’nyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 6.4.115), and *jahāteśca* (Pāṇini 6.4.116). By these, the substitution of *ī* optionally occurs, resulting in *jahitaḥ* or *jahītaḥ*. Before a vowel-initial suffix, as previously mentioned, there is elision of *ā* (*āllopa*). By the rule *adabhyastāt* (Pāṇini 7.1.4), the form is *jahati*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect) tense: *ajahāt*; *ajihitām* or *ajihītām*.

By the rule *sijabhyastavidibhyaśca* (Pāṇini 3.4.109), the suffix *jhi* is replaced by *jus*; then, by *usyapadāntāt* (Pāṇini 6.1.109), [the *u* of *jus* is dropped], resulting in *ajahuḥ*. In the *loṭ* (imperative) mood: *jahātu*, *jahītāt*, *jahitām*, *jahītām*, *jahatu*. For the suffix *si*, there is the substitution of *hi*; thus, *jahihi* and *jahīhi*. Here, because [the *hi*] is not marked with *pit*, it is treated as *ṅit*; and by *ā ca hau* (Pāṇini 6.4.117), there is optionally the substitution of *ā* [for the final vowel], resulting in *jahāhi*. In the *liṅ* (optative) mood, by *lopo yi* (Pāṇini 6.4.118), there is the elision of the *ā* [of the root], which is an exception to the substitution of *ī*: *jahyāt*, *jahyātam*, *jahyātām*.

In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by *pāṇini-sūtra* 6.4.117, there is the substitution of *ī*: *heyāt*, *heyāstām*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *jahau*, *jahatuḥ*, *jahuḥ*. By *pāṇini-sūtra* 6.4.64, there is the elision of the long *ā*: *jahitha* or *jahātha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), as before, with the augment *s* and the suffix *iṭ*, [the forms are] *ahāsīt*, *ahāsiṣṭām*, *ahāsiṣuḥ*. [The future is] *hāsyati*, etc. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by *pāṇini-sūtra* 6.4.66, there is the substitution of *ī* and reduplication: *jehīyate*. These are parasmaipada verbs.

The root *ḍudāñ* means "to give. It forms *dadāti*. As before, there is elision of the *ā* (by *āto lopa iṭi ca*). [In the present tense: *dattaḥ*, *dadati*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), *adadāt*, *adattam*. By the rule *sijabhyastavidibhyaśca* (Pāṇini 3.4.109), the *jhi* suffix becomes *jus*: *aduḥ*. [In the imperative: *dadātu*, *dattāt*, *dattam*, *dadatu*. By the rule *serhiḥ* and *ghvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaśca* (Pāṇini 6.4.119), there is the substitution of *e* for the root vowel and the elision of the reduplication: *dehi*.

In the *liṅ* [optative], there is elision of the vowel *ā* because, by the rule *īhallyaghoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.113), those verbs designated as *ghu* are excluded; thus, even before a consonant beginning with a *hal*, the substitution of *ī* does not occur: *dadyāt*, *dadyātām*, *dadyuḥ*. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), by the rule *erliṅi* (Pāṇini 6.4.67), there is the substitution of *e*: *deyāt*, *deyāstām*, *deyāsuḥ*. In the *liṭ* [perfect], [the forms are]: *dadau*, *dadatuḥ*, *daduḥ*; *daditha* or *dadātha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], by the rule *gātisthā* (Pāṇini 2.4.77), there is the elision of *sic*: *adāt*, *adātām*. By the rule *ātaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.110), *jhi* is replaced by *jus*: *aduḥ*.

In the *caṅ* [aorist] following *ṇau*, the augment *puK* is applied: *adīdapat*. Regarding "he will give" (*dāsyati*) and so forth: in the *san* [desiderative], it is *ditsati*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive], by *ghumāsthā* (Pāṇini 6.4.66), there is the substitution of *ī*; thus, *dedīyate*. When the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, the *ātmanepada* suffix is used because of the *ñit* designation; as before, there is the elision of *ā*: *datte*. [Third person dual: *dadāte*. [Third person plural: *dadate*. [Imperfect: *adatta*, *adadātām*, *adadata*. [Imperative: *dattām*, *dadātām*, *dadatām*. [Optative: *dadīta*, *dadīyātām*, *dadīran*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), it is *dāsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by *āto lopa* (Pāṇini 6.4.64), there is the elision of *ā*: *dade*.

In the root *luṅ* (aorist), by Pāṇini’s rule *sthāghvoricca* (1.2.27), there is the substitution of the vowel *i* for the suffix *sic*; because *sic* is treated as *kit*, there is no *guṇa* strengthening, and the *s* is elided, resulting in *adita*. The forms *adiṣātām* and so forth are to be understood in the same way. Regarding the root *dā* preceded by the prefix *āṅ* (*ā-dā*), when the action is intended for the agent and refers to one's own body, and when it is intransitive—specifically in the sense of opening the mouth—the *ātmanepada* is used according to Pāṇini’s rule *āṅo do’nāsya-viharaṇe* (1.3.20). Thus, one says *vyādatte* (he opens his mouth). However, when it refers to the opening of something other than the mouth, the *parasmaipada* is used; for example: *vyādadāty annam atra mṛtyuḥ* (Death opens its jaws for the food here).

The root *ḍudhāñ* is used in the senses of "holding" and "nourishing. It functions as before, but with this distinction: when followed by a suffix beginning with *t*, *th*, or *s*, the rule *dadhastathoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.38) applies, whereby *t* and *th* are replaced by *dh*, and furthermore, the substitution of *bhaṣ* for *s* occurs.

The root *ṇijir* is used in the senses of cleansing and nourishing. By Pāṇini 6.1.63 (*ṇo naḥ*), the initial *ṇ* becomes *n*. For the three roots beginning with *ṇij*, there is guna substitution for the reduplicated syllable when *ślau* occurs; thus, by the rule "guna for the three *nij*s in *ślau*," we have *nenekti*. *neniktaḥ* (third person dual), *nenijati* (third person plural). In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *anenek* (second person singular), *aneniktām* (third person dual), *anenijuḥ* (third person plural), *anenijam* (first person singular, where *mip* is replaced by *am*). Here, by the rule beginning with Pāṇini 7.3.67 (*nābhyastasya...*), the guna of the light penultimate vowel is prohibited. In the imperative: *nenektu*, *neniktāt*, *neniktām*, *nenijatu*. In the potential (*liṅ*): *nenijyāt*, *nenijyātām*. In the benedictive (*āśis*): *nijyāt*.

Let them two cleanse themselves: *nijyāstām*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), [the forms are] *nineja*, *ninijatuḥ*, *ninijuḥ*, *ninijitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), because it is marked with the *ir*-indicator, there is *aṅ*: *anijat*; or *anaikṣīt*. [The future forms are] *nekṣyati*, etc. Because it is marked with the *svarita* accent, it takes the *ātmanepada* endings: *nenikte*, *nenijāte*, *nenijate*; *anenikta*, *anenijātām*, *anenijata*; *neniktām*, *nenijātām*, *nenijatām*; *nenijīta*, *nenijīyātām*, *nenijīran*. Regarding the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *āśiṣi liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), there is *kit* status [of the suffix], hence *nikṣīṣṭa*. [In the perfect,] *ninije*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist], as before, there is *kitva*, hence [the forms] *anikta*, *anijātām*, and *anijata*.
