There is no *aṅ* [substitute] by virtue of Pāṇini 3.1.57 (*irito vā*), because that rule applies specifically to the *parasmaipada* [voice]. The root *vicir* means "to separate. As before, all roots from *māṅ* up to *vicir* are invariably *aniṭ* (without the *iṭ* augment) in the *ātmanepada*.

The root *viṣlṛ* is used in the sense of pervasion (*vyāpti*). [Present tense: *veveṣṭi*, *veviṣṭaḥ*, *veviṣati*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect), due to the rules for *jaśtva* and *cartva*, [the forms are] *aveṭ*, *aveḍ*; *aveviṣṭām*; *aveviṣuḥ*, and so forth. [Imperative: *veveṣṭu*, *veviṣṭāt*, *veviṣṭām*, *veviṣatu*. [Optative: *veviṣyāt*, *veviṣyātām*, *veviṣyuḥ*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), because it is marked with *ḷ*, the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *aviṣat*, *aviṣatām*. Similarly, [in the middle voice: *veviṣṭe*, *veviṣāte*, and so forth. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), [it is] *veṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *viviṣe*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), *aviṣṭa*.
These are the roots that take the augment *iṭ* and are conjugated in both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣā*).

The root *ghṛ* means "to flow" and "to shine. The root *hṛ* means "to act with force. Examples [of these] should be inferred. The roots *ṛ* and *sṛ* mean "to go. Regarding the rule *artipipartyośca* (Pāṇini 7.4.77), there is *itva* for the reduplication and *guṇa* for the following [root vowel]. By the rule *abhyāsasyāsavarṇe* (Pāṇini 6.4.78), there is *iyaṅ*. Thus: *iyarti*. [He] emits smoke: *dhūmam iyarti*. [Aorist: *iryṛtaḥ*, *iryati*. In the *laṅ* [with the suffixes] *ti* and *sip*, there is elision by *halṅyādi* [Pāṇini 6.1.68], *āṭ*-vṛddhi, and substitution of *ra* [for *ṛ*]: *aiyaḥ*. [Imperfect third person plural: *airyat*. [Third person dual: *aiyṛtām*. By the rule *jasi ca* (Pāṇini 7.3.109), there is *guṇa*: *aiyaruḥ*. [Imperative: *iyartu*, *iyṛtāt*, *iyṛtām*, *iryantu*. In the *liṅ*: *iyṛyāt*, *iyṛyātām*, *iyṛyuḥ*.

By the rule *āśiṣi guṇortisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29), there is guṇa substitution: *aryāt*, *aryāstām*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), [the root becomes] *ār*. By the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), there is guṇa: *āratuḥ*, *āruḥ*, *āritha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *sartiśāstyartibhyaśca* (Pāṇini 3.1.56), the suffix *aṅ* is applied; and by the rule *ṛdṛśo'ṅi guṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.16), there is guṇa: *ārat*, *āratām*, *āran*. By the rule *ṛddhano sya* (Pāṇini 7.2.70), the augment *iṭ* is added: *ariṣyati*, and so forth. The examples for this root *sṛ* should be inferred as being similar to those of the root belonging to the Bhūvādigaṇa.

The root *bhas* is used in the senses of threatening and shining. In the present tense (*laṭ*), with the suffix *tip*: *babhasti*. By the rule *tipyanasteḥ*, there is the substitution of *d* for the *t* of *tip*, resulting in *ababhata* (imperfect), *ababhastām* (third person dual), and *ababhasuḥ* (third person plural). In the imperative (*loṭ*): *babhastu*. In the potential (*liṅ*): *babhasyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *bhasyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *babhāsa*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *abhāsīt* (with the augment *s*) or *abhasīt* (without the augment *s*). In the conditional (*lṛṅ*): *bhasiṣyat* (future), and so forth.
Thus ends the section on the roots beginning with *juhoti* that take the *ślu* affix, in the *Śābdikābharaṇa* composed by Hariyogin Prollanācārya.

The section on the *divādi* group: *divu* [is used] in the senses of playing, desiring victory, trading, shining, praising, rejoicing, intoxication, sleeping, beauty, and motion. By the rule *divādibhyaḥ śyan* (Pāṇini 3.1.69), *śyan* is substituted [for *śap*]; this is an exception (*apavāda*) to *śap*. Because *śyan* is marked with the *ṅit* indicator, there is no *guṇa* substitution; by the rule *hali ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.77), there is lengthening [of the vowel], resulting in *dīvyati*. *dīvyataḥ* | *dīvyanti* | *adīvyat* | *dīvyatu* | *dīvyet* | In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), with *yāsuṭ*, *dīvyāt*; *dīvyāstām*. In the *liṭ* [perfect tense]: *dideva*, *didivatuḥ*, *didivuḥ*, *didevitha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist]: *adevīt*. In the *caṅ* [reduplicated aorist] of the causative (*ṇau*): *adīdivat*. *deviṣyati*.

He will play (*adeviṣyat*). He will play (*devitā*). Regarding the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini 7.2.49), there is an option for the augment *iṭ*: he desires to play (*dideviṣati*). In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *chvoḥ śūḍanunāsike ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.19), *ūṭh* is substituted, followed by reduplication, resulting in *dudyūṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*) suffix, it becomes *dedīyate*. The root *ṣivu* means "to weave" (*tantusantāne*);
*sivu* means "to go" and "to dry up" (*gatiśoṣaṇayoḥ*).
*ṣṭhivu* (to spit) is used in the sense of ejecting; [it is conjugated] as before.
*klasu* means to move crookedly or to shine; *pluṣa* means to burn. Examples include *klasyati*, *pluṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *nṛt* means "to dance" or "to move the limbs. Present: *nṛtyati*. Imperfect: *anṛtyat*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), with the suffix *yāsuṭ*: *nṛtyāt*. Perfect: *nanarta*, *nanṛtatuḥ*, *nanṛtuḥ*, *nanartitha*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *anartīt*. With the causative suffix *ṇic* and the reduplication suffix *caṅ*: *anīnṛtat*. Desiderative: *ananarttata*. In the case of the suffix *sa* (the periphrastic future), there is an optional *iṭ* augment according to Pāṇini 7.2.57 (*se'sici kṛtacṛtacchṛdatṛdanṛtaḥ*): *nartsyati* or *nartiṣyati*. Conditional: *anartsyat* or *anarttiṣyat*. Periphrastic future: *narttitā*. Intensive (*san*): *ninṛtsati* or *ninarttiṣati*. Frequentative (*yaṅ*): *narīnṛtyate*.

The root *tras* means "to tremble" or "to be agitated. By the rule *vā bhrāśa-* (Pāṇini 3.1.70), the suffix *śyan* is optionally applied, resulting in *trasyati*. The imperfect form is *atrasyat*. In the alternative case where *śap* is applied, one has *trasati*, and so forth. In the benedictive (*āśis*), the form is *trasyāt*. In the perfect, by the rule *vā jṝbhramutrasām* (Pāṇini 6.4.124), there is an option regarding the substitution of *e* for *a* and the elision of the reduplication, resulting in *tresasuḥ* or *tatrasuḥ*; likewise, *tresuḥ* or *tatrasuḥ*; and *tresasitha* or *tatrasitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), the forms are *atrasīt* or *atrāsīt*. The future and other forms are *trasiṣyati*, etc.
The root *kuth* means "to become putrid"; *puth* means "to injure."
The root *gup* is used in the sense of "concealing. An example should be inferred [by the student].

The root *kṣip* is used in the sense of "impelling. [Present tense: *kṣipyati*, etc. [Benedictive: *kṣipyāt*. [Perfect: *cikṣepa*, *cikṣipatuḥ*, *cikṣipuḥ*, *cikṣepitha*. [Aorist: *akṣaipsīt*. [Causative with *caṅ*: *acikṣipat*. [Future: *kṣepsyati*, etc. The root *kṛṣ* is used in the sense of "plowing" or "drawing. [Present tense: *kṛṣyati*, etc. [Perfect: *cakarṣa*, *cakṛṣatuḥ*, *cakṛṣuḥ*, *cakarṣitha*. [Aorist: *akārṣīt*. [Future: *kariṣyati*, etc.

The root *puṣp* means "to blossom"; thus one says *puṣpyati*, and so forth. The roots *tim*, *tīm*, *ṣṭim*, and *ṣṭīm* signify becoming moist; thus one says *timyati*, *tīmyati*, *stimyati*, and *stīmyati*. The root *vrīḍ* signifies urging and shame; thus one says *vrīḍyati*.

The root *iṣ* (meaning "to go") is used as follows: *preṣyati* (present), *preṣyet* (optative); in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), *preṣyāt*; in the perfect (*liṭ*), *iyeṣa*, *īṣatuḥ*, *īṣuḥ*, *iyeṣitha*; in the aorist (*luṅ*), *aiṣīt*; and so on for *preṣiṣyati*. In the causative (*ṇic*) of *iṣ* in the perfect, it becomes *īṣayāmāsa*.

The root *jṛṣ* (variant *jṝṣ*), meaning "decay of age," undergoes the change of *ṛ* to *ī* by Pāṇini 7.1.100 (*ṛta iddhātoḥ*), and lengthening by Pāṇini 8.2.77 (*hali ca*), resulting in *jīryati*. [Forms: *ajīryat* (imperfect), *jīryatu* (imperative), *jīryet* (optative). In the sense of a benediction, with the suffix *yāsuṭ*, it is *jīryāt*. In the perfect, it is *jajāra*.

By the rule *kṛtīṛcchatyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), the *guṇa* [substitution] applies. However, by the rule *na śasadadavādiguṇānām* (Pāṇini 6.4.126), which prohibits the application of the rules beginning with *ata ekahala...* (Pāṇini 6.4.120) regarding the vowel *a* produced by *guṇa*, a prohibition would have ensued; yet, by the rule *vā jṝbhramutrasām* (Pāṇini 6.4.124), the substitution of *etva* (the change to *e*) and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsalopa*) take place. Thus: *jajaratuḥ*, *jeratuḥ*, *jajaruḥ*, *jeruḥ*; [and in the perfect second person singular: *jajaritha*, *jeritha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist], by the rule *jṝstambhu0* (Pāṇini 3.1.58), there is optionally *aṅ* for *cli*; and by *ṛdṛśoṅi guṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.16), there is *guṇa* [substitution] before the *aṅ* of *ṅi*: *ajarat*, *ajārīt*. In the *caṅ* [of the *luṅ* with *ṇic*], *ajījarat*. In the *lṛṭ* [future] and *luṭ* [periphrastic future], by *vṝto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), when the augment *īṭ* is present, there is lengthening: *jariṣyati*, *jarīṣyati*; *ajariṣyat*, *ajarīṣyat*; *jaritā*, *jarītā*.

In the case of *san*, although the prohibition of *iṭ* would apply by Pāṇini 7.2.12 (*sani sanigrahaguhośca*), there is an option for *iṭ* by Pāṇini 7.2.49 (*iṭ sanīva*). When *iṭ* is present, there is an option for lengthening: *jijariṣati* or *jijarīṣati*. Otherwise, due to the *kit* status by Pāṇini 1.2.9 (*iko jhal*), the substitution of *it* by Pāṇini 7.1.100 (*ṛdiddhātoḥ*), and the lengthening by Pāṇini 8.2.77 (*hali ca*), we have *jijīrṣati*. In the *yaṅ* suffix, the substitution of *it* by Pāṇini 7.1.100 results in *jeṃjīryate*. [The roots] ending in *kṣip* and *vṛj* are *seṭ* and are *parasmaipadī*.

The root *ṣūñ* is used in the sense of "procreation" (*prāṇiprasava*). Examples include *prasūyate*, *prāsūyata*, and so forth. Regarding the benedictive mood (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *svarati-sūti-sūyati-dhūjūdito vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.44), there is an option for the augment *iṭ*; thus we have *prasoṣīṣṭa* or *prasaviṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), it is *suṣuve*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *prāsoṣṭa* or *prāsaviṣṭa*. In the future (*lṛṭ*), it is *prāsoṣyate* or *prasaviṣyate*, and so on. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), under the governing rule *śryukaḥ kiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.11), the prohibition of *iṭ* is applied by the rule *sanigrahaguhośca* (Pāṇini 7.2.12).

By the rule *iko jhal* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), there is the status of being *kit*; due to the restriction *stautiṇyoreva* (Pāṇini 8.3.61), there is no *ṣatva* for the letter following the reduplication, as in the previous case. By the rule *sanaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.62), the *ātmanepada* [middle voice] occurs: *prasusūṣate*. The root *dūṅ* means "to suffer pain. Present: *dūyate*. Imperfect: *adūyata*. Benedictive: *daviṣīṣṭa*. Periphrastic perfect: *duduve*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *adaviṣṭa*. Future, etc.: *daviṣyate*, and so forth.

The root *dīṅ* means "to perish. In forms such as *dīyate*, the substitution of *ā* for the vowel of *mī*, *mī*, *dī*, and *dīṅ* before the suffix *lyap* occurs even prior to the arising of the suffix, according to Pāṇini 6.1.50 (*mīnātiminotidīṅāṃ lyapi ca*). Thus, in the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), one has *dāsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by Pāṇini 6.4.63 (*dīṅo yuḍ aci kṅiti*), the augment *yuṭ* is added, resulting in *upadidīye*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), with the same *ā* substitution as before, one has *upādāsta*. In the causative with the suffix *caṅ*, one has *upādīdapat*. The future forms are *upadāsyate* and *upadātā*. In the desiderative, one has *upadidīṣate* and *upadidāsate*. In the passive, one has *upadedīyate*.

The root *mīṅ* is used in the sense of "injury" (*hiṃsā*). [Present tense: *pramīyate*, *prāmīyata*, and so forth. [Benedictive: *prameṣīṣṭa*. [Perfect tense (*liṭ*): By the rule *prakṛti-jaśām*, [the forms are] *pramimye*, *prāmeṣṭa*, *prameṣyate*, *prāmeṣyata*, *prametā*, *pramimīṣate*, *pramemīyate*. The root *ḍīṅ* is used in the sense of "motion through the air" (*vihāyasā gati*). [Present tense: *ḍīyate*. [Benedictive: *ḍayiṣīṣṭa*. By the rule *prakṛti-jaśām prakṛti-jaśaḥ*, [the forms are] *ḍiḍye*, and so forth. The root *dhīṅ* is used in the sense of "disrespect" (*anādara*). The examples for this should be inferred accordingly.

The root *rī* (meaning "to flow") is conjugated as follows: In the present tense: *rīyate*. In the imperfect: *arīyata*. In the imperative: *rīyatām*. In the benedictive: *reṣīṣṭa*; *reṣīḍhvam* (the cerebralization occurs by Pāṇini 8.2.35). In the perfect (*liṭ*): *rerirye*. By the rule *krādiniyamādiṭ vibhāṣeṭaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.79), the augment *iṭ* is optional after a root ending in *iṭ*: *rirayiḍhve*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *areṣṭa*, *areṣātām*. In *dhvam*, the substitution of a cerebral (*mūrdhanya*) occurs: *areḍhvam*. When the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied and the *caṅ* (reduplication) follows, the augment *puK* is added by the rule *artihrī0* (Pāṇini 7.3.36). The rest is as before: *arīripat*.

The root *lī* means "to adhere" (*śleṣaṇe*). Thus, one forms *līyate*, and so forth. Regarding the benedictive (*āśīr*) in the domain of *ej*-affixes, by the rule *vibhāṣā līyateḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.51), there is optionally an *ā*-substitution: *leṣīṣṭa* or *lāsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *lilye*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), as before, there is *ā*-substitution: *alāsta*, *alāsātām*, *aleṣṭa*, *aleṣātām*. When the causative suffix *ṇic* is applied in the sense of deceiving (*pralambhana*) or making someone modest/shy (*śālīnīkaraṇa*), and also when the causative is used in the sense of honoring (*saṃmānana*) or making someone shy (*śālīnīkaraṇa*), the *ātmanepada* is used by the rule *ṇau caṅi pralambhane śālīnīkaraṇayośca* (Pāṇini 1.3.70). Examples: *upālīlapata*, *ālīlapataḥ*.

Alternatively, there is *ātva* (the substitution of *ā*); in the case of *ātva*, in the domain of the nipātana (irregular formation) of *sneha*, the augment *luk* optionally applies to the roots *lī* and *līṅ*. In the absence of *ātva*, the augment *nuk* applies: *alīlapat*, *alīlanat*. Other than in the domain of the nipātana of *sneha*, there is an option between *puk* and *ātva*: *alīlapat*, *alālayiṣati*, *lāsyate*, *leṣyate*, and so forth. In the *san* [desiderative] suffix: *lilīṣate*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix:

*lelīyate*. The root *plīṅ* means "to go": *plīyate*, and so forth. In the benedictive: *pleṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* [perfect], there is *iyaṅ*: *pipliye*. In the *luṅ* [aorist]: *apleṣṭa*. The root *prīṅ* has the meaning "to choose" (*vṛṇoti*): it follows the same pattern as above.
The five roots *dīdhī* (to shine), *dīdhī* (to shine), *plī* (to go), *mlī* (to go), and *rī* (to go) likewise have the vowel *i* as their indicatory letter (*odit*).
Therefore, they take the suffixes *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā* with the augment *iṭ*.
The root *pīṅ* (to drink): it is drunk (*pīyate*), it was drunk (*apīyata*). The rest should be understood accordingly.

The root *prī* (meaning "to please" or "to be pleased"): *prīyate*, *aprīyata*, *prīyatām*, *prīyeta*; in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), *preṣīṣṭa*; in the perfect (*liṭ*), *pipriye*; [in the imperfect], *apiprayat*; [in the passive], *preṣyate*; [in the imperfect], *apreṣyata*; [in the imperative], *pretā*; [in the desiderative], *piprīṣate*; in the intensive (*yaṅ*), *peprīyate*. The root *ī* (meaning "to go"): *īyate*, *aiyata*, *īyatām*, *īyeta*; in the sense of a benediction, *eṣīṣṭa*; [in the perfect], *udīye*; [in the aorist], *udayiṣṭa*; [in the aorist], *udaiṣātām*, *udaiṣata*, and so forth—these forms should be applied accordingly. The roots *iṅ* and *sūyati* are optionally [conjugated] in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*).

The root *śo* means "to thin" or "to sharpen. By the rule *otaḥ śyani* (Pāṇini 7.3.71), there is the elision of the final *o* in roots beginning with *śya*; thus, *śyati*. The forms *aśyat*, *śyatu*, and *śyet* follow. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *ādeca upadeśe'śiti* (Pāṇini 6.1.45), there is the substitution of *ā* for the final vowel, resulting in *śāyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), there is *śaśau*, *śaśatuḥ*, *śaśuḥ*, and *śaśātha*. By the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.64), there is the elision of the *ā* in *śaśitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *vibhāṣā ghrādheṭśācchāsaḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.78), there is optionally the elision of *sic*, resulting in *aśāt*, *aśātām*, and *aśuḥ*. Otherwise, by the rule *yamaramanamātāṃ sak ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.73), the augment *s* and the *iṭ* augment are applied, resulting in *aśāsīt*.

*aśāsiṣṭām*. By the rule *ṇau caṅi śācchā0* (Pāṇini 7.3.37), the suffix *yuk* is an exception to *puṅ*; thus, *aśīśayat*. [The forms] *śāsyati*, *aśāsyat*, *śātā*, *śiśāsati*, and *śāśāyate* follow. The root *cho* means "to cut.
The root *ṣo* means "to finish" (*antakarman*).

The root *ava* is used in the sense of "cutting" (*avakhaṇḍane*). Examples include *avasyati*, *vyavasyati*, and so forth. In the benedictive mood (*āśiṣi*), the rule *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisām hali* (Pāṇini 6.4.66) would require the substitution of *i* for the vowel; however, the subsequent rule *eliṅi* (Pāṇini 6.4.67) prescribes the substitution of *e*. Thus, we have *avaseyāt* and *avadeyāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), by the rule *abhyāse car ca* (Pāṇini 8.4.54), the first sound replaces the second in the reduplication. Since the original sounds are retroflex (*car*), the retroflexes are retained: *avasasau*. Since the original sounds are voiced unaspirated stops (*jaś*), the voiced unaspirated stops are retained: *avadadau*.

By the rule *luṅi vibhāṣā ghrādheḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.78), there is optionally the elision (*luk*) of *sic*; thus, *avācchāt*. In the absence of this elision, with the augment *s* and *iṭ*, we have *avācchāsīt*. With the root *dyati*, by the rule *gāti-sthā-ā-pā-bhū-bhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 2.4.77), there is obligatory elision of *sic*. In the *caṅ* formation with the causative suffix (*ṇic*), by the rule *śāc-chā-sā-hvā-vyā-ve-pāṃ yuk* (Pāṇini 7.3.37), the augment *yuk* is added, and by *che ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.73), the augment *tuk* is added; thus, *acicchayat*. According to the view that "the teaching of augments is not eternal" (*anityam āgama-śāsanam*), the rule *dīrgho laghoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.94) applies, resulting in *acīcayat*.

By the rule *dīrghāt* (Pāṇini 6.1.75), the augment *tuk* is optionally applied, as in *acicchat*. From the root *dyati*, with the *puk* augment, we have *avādīt* and *apāt*. Forms such as *chāsyati* follow the same pattern. As before, from the root *dyati* with the suffix *san*, we have *ditsati*. With the suffix *yaṅ*, we have *dedīyate*. From the root *syati*, we have *sesīyate*. These are the roots that are *aniṭ* (without the *iṭ* augment) and belong to the *parasmaipada* (active voice).

The root *jan* means "to appear" or "to be born. By the rule *śiti jñājanorjā* (Pāṇini 7.3.79), the substitute *jā* is applied, resulting in *jāyate*. The forms are: *ajāyata*, *jāyatām*, and *jāyet*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), the form is *janiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), due to the status of the elision of the penultimate vowel as being *sthānivadbhūta* by the rule *gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅityanaṅi* (Pāṇini 6.4.98), there is reduplication, resulting in *jajñe*.

By the rule *luṅi dīpajana* (Pāṇini 3.1.61), when a suffix expressing the agent (*kartṛ*) such as *ta* follows, there is optionally the substitution of *caṇ* for *cli*. In the case of *caṇ*: *ciṇo luk* (Pāṇini 6.4.104) [the *luk* elision of the *ciṇ* affix]; *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.116) [vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel]; but this vṛddhi does not occur here because of the prohibition in *janivadhyośca* (Pāṇini 7.3.35). Thus, we have *ajani*. In the absence of *caṇ* (i.e., when *sica* follows): *sica iṭ* [the augment *iṭ* is added to *sic*]. Thus, *ajaniṣṭa*. In the causative (*ṇic*): With *caṅ* (reduplication), *ajījanat*. Future: *janiṣyate*. Conditional: *ajaniṣyata*. Periphrastic future: *janitā*. Desiderative: *janiṣyate*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*): By *ye vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini 6.4.43), there is optionally the substitution of *ā* [for the root vowel], resulting in *jājāyate*. In the absence of *ā*, there is the insertion of *nuk* after the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *jañjanyate*.

The root *dīp* is used in the sense of "shining. Present: *dīpyate* Imperfect: *adīpyata* Imperative: *dīpyatām* Optative: *dīpyeta* Benedictive: *dīpiṣīṣṭa* Perfekt: *didīpe* Aorist (*luṅ*): As before, there is an option for the augment *caṅ* after *cli*; thus, *adīpi* or *adīpiṣṭa*. Causative with *caṅ*: By Pāṇini 7.4.13 (*bhrājabhrāsa...* etc.), there is an option for the shortening of the penultimate vowel; thus, *adīdipat*. Future: *dīpiṣyate* Conditional: *adīpiṣyata* Periphrastic Future: *dīpitā* Desiderative: *didīpiṣate* Intensive:

*dedīpyate* The root *pūr* is used in the sense of "filling" or "becoming full. Present: *āpūryate* Imperfect: *āpūryata* Imperative: *pūryatām* Optative: *pūryeta* Benedictive: *pūrṣīṣṭa* Perfekt: *pupūre* As before, there is an option for the augment *ciṇ*; thus, *apūri* or *apūriṣṭa*, and so forth. The root *kūr* is used in the senses of "hastening" and "injury. Present: *kūryate*
*Surī* means to burn;
*pūrī* and *jūrī* mean injury and loss of vitality;
*mārī* and *jūrī* mean injury and motion.

*Śūrī* is used in the sense of injury and paralysis; *mūrī* in the sense of burning. As before, examples are to be cited. *Tapa* means sovereignty. It is conjugated as *tapyate*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), it is *tapsīṣṭa*; in the perfect (*liṭ*), *tepe*. In the aorist (*luṅ*) with a *jhal*-beginning suffix, there is elision of the *s*: *atapta*, *tapsyata*, and so forth.
The root *vṛṅ* means "to choose"; it is conjugated as *vriyate*.
The root *kliś* means "to afflict"; it is conjugated as *kliśyate*.
The root *kāśṛ* means "to shine"; it is conjugated as *kāśyate*.

The root *vāśṛ* means "to sound. It is used in the sense of bellowing in response to the sacrificer (*yajamāna*). Furthermore, with the exception of *tap*, all roots ending in *t* that take the augment *iṭ* are *ātmanebhāṣā* (middle-voice).

The root *mṛṣ* is used in the sense of "endurance. After the prefix *pari*, by the rule *parermṛṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.82), the *parasmaipada* (active voice) ending is obligatory. In other cases—both when the root is used alone and when it is accompanied by a prefix—the *parasmaipada* and *ātmanepada* endings are optional. Examples: *parimṛṣyati*, *mṛṣyati*, *mṛṣyate*; *amṛṣyat*, *amṛṣyata*; *amṛṣata*. In the benedictive (*āśis*): *mṛṣyāt*, *marṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *mamarṣa*, *mamṛṣe*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *amarṣīt*, *amarṣiṣṭa*. In the causative with *caṅ* (the reduplicated aorist): *amīmṛṣata*, *amīmarṣat*. In the future: *marṣiṣyati*, *marṣiṣyate*. In the desiderative (*san*): *mimarṣiṣati*, *mimarṣiṣate*.

The root *śuc* means "to become pure" or "to purify. Between the two suffixes of the *anubandha*, the root is *śuc*. Present: *śucyati*; Aorist: *aśucyat*. Passive: *śucyate*; Aorist: *aśucyata*. In the benedictive (āśīrliṅ): Active—*śucyāt*; Middle—*śociṣīṣṭa*. Perfect: Active—*śuśoca*; Middle—*śuśuce*. Aorist (luṅ): Active—*aśucat*; Root-aorist—*aśocīt*; Middle—*aśociṣṭa*.

The root *ṇah* means "to bind. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.1.65 (*no naḥ*), *naḥ* is substituted for *ṇa*. Present tense: *nahyati* (he binds), *nahyate* (he binds himself). Benedictive mood: *nahyāt* (may he bind). According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 8.2.34 (*naho dhaḥ*), *dha* is substituted for *h*; then by the rule for *carv* substitution, we have *natsīṣṭa* (may he bind). In the perfect tense (*liṭ*): *nanāha*, *nanaddha*, *nehitha*, *nehe*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): By Pāṇini’s sūtra 8.2.34 (*naho dhaḥ*), *dha* is substituted for *h*; then by the rule for *carv* substitution and the vṛddhi of the penultimate vowel before a consonant ending, we have *anātsīt*, *anāddhām*, *anātsuḥ*. In the case where a *jhal*-ending suffix follows, there is elision of *s* (*jhali salopaḥ*). By Pāṇini’s sūtra 8.2.34 (*naho dhaḥ*) and 8.2.40 (*jhaṣastathordho dhaḥ*), we have *anaddha*, *anatsātām*, *anatsata*. The remainder is to be understood in the same manner.

The root *rañj* means "to color" or "to be attached. By the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), there is elision of the nasal (*n*). Thus: *rajyati*, *rajyate*. In the benedictive: *rajyāt*. By the rules *coḥ kuḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.30), *anusvāraparasavarṇau*, and *iṇkoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.57), there is the substitution of *ṣ*; thus: *raṅkṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect: *rarañja*, *rarañje*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is vṛddhi for a root ending in a consonant: *arāṅkṣīt*. When a *jhal* suffix follows, there is elision of *s*: *araṅkta*, *arañjātām*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), there is elision of the nasal: *rārājyate*. The root *śap* means "to curse. Thus: *śapyati*, *śapyate*. *Muṣ* and *śuc* are *seṭ* (taking the *iṭ* augment); the others are *aniṭ* (not taking *iṭ*); they are used in both voices (active and middle).

The root *pad* means "to go. Present tense: *prapadyate*, *prāpadyata*, *prapadyatām*, *prapadyeta*, *prapatsīṣṭa*. Perfect tense: *prapede*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) for the agent (*kartari*), by the rule *padaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.60), *ciṇ* replaces *cl*; thus: *apādi*, *apatsātām*, *apatsata*. Future tense: *patsyate*. Conditional tense: *apatsyata*. With the desiderative suffix (*san*), by the rule *sanimīmā-* (Pāṇini 7.4.54) and others, the appropriate grammatical operations apply; thus: *prapitsate*. With the intensive suffix (*yaṅ*), by the rule *nīgvañcu-* (Pāṇini 7.4.84) and others, the reduplication (*abhyāsa*) takes the augment *nīk*; thus: *panīpadyate*.

The root *vid* is used in the sense of existence (*sattā*). Present: *vidyate*; Perfect: *avidyata*; Imperative: *vidyatām*; Optative: *vidyeta*; Precative: *vitsīṣṭa*. Perfect: *vivide*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), the *sic* suffix is marked with the *kittva* (indicating the absence of *guṇa* and *vṛddhi*): *avitta*, *avitsātām*, *avitsata*. Future: *vetsyate*. The root *khid* is used in the sense of dejection (*dainya*). *Khidyate*; *akhidyata*, etc., are formed as before. The root *budh* is used in the sense of understanding (*avagamana*). Present: *budhyate*; Imperfect: *abudhyata*; Imperative: *budhyatām*; Optative: *budhyeta*. As before, there is *kittva*; then *bhaṣtva* and *cartva* apply: *bhukṣīṣṭa*. Perfect: *bubudhe*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), there is an option between *ciṇ* and the *sic* suffix as before: *abodhi*. As before, there is *kittva*: *abuddha*, etc.

*Yudh* in the sense of combat: *yudhyate*; in the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, *ayudhya*, *ayutsātām*; the remainder is to be understood as before. *Yuj* in the sense of concentration: *yujyate*, etc., as previously explained. *Ana* in the sense of breathing.
*anurudh* (to desire): *anurudhyate*, *anvarudhyata*, *anurudhyatām*, *anurudhyeta*, *anurutsīṣṭa*.
*man* (to know/think): *manyate*, *amanyata*, *manyatām*, *manyeta*, *maṃsīṣṭa*, *mene*, *amaṃsta*, *maṃsyate*.

The root *sṛj* (to create/emit): *visarge* (in the sense of emission): *sṛjyate*, *asṛjyata*, *sṛjyatām*, *sṛjyeta*. In the *āśīrliṅ* (precative), due to its *kit* status, *sṛkṣīṣṭa*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), due to the *kit* status of *sic*, with the application of *ṣatva* and *ṣṭutva*, *asṛṣṭa*. In the *caṅ* (reduplication) of the *ṇic* (causative), *asīsṛjat*; alternatively, *asasarjat*. By the rule "akit-sṛji-dṛśoḥ," there is the augment *am*: *srakṣyate*, *asrakṣyata*, *sraṣṭā*. For the desiderative (*san*), due to its *kit* status, *sisṛkṣate*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), *sarīsṛjyate*. The root *liś* (to become small/diminish): *liśyate*, *aliśyata*, *liśyatām*, *liśyeta*. In the *āśīrliṅ*, due to its *kit* status, *likṣīṣṭa*. In the *luṅ*, by the substitution of *ksa* for *cli*, *alikṣat*, and so forth.
The roots ending in *an* that take the *iṭ* augment are *ātmanepada*.

The roots *rādh* and *sādh* are used in the sense of "accomplishment" (*saṃsiddhi*). From *rādh*, when it is intransitive, it is used only in the sense of "prosperity" (*vṛddhi*): *rādhyati*, *arādhyat*, *rādhyatu*, *rādhyet*. In the benedictive (*āśīḥ*), with the suffix *yāsuṭ*, it is *rādhyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *rarādha*, *rarādhatuḥ*, *rarādhuḥ*. By the rule for roots beginning with *krādi*, the augment *iṭ* is added: *rarādhitha*. However, in the sense of "injury" (*hiṃsā*), by the rule *rādho hiṃsāyām* (Pāṇini 6.4.23), there is elision of the vowel and the reduplication: *redhatuḥ*, *redhuḥ*, *redhitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is the substitution of *ṛ* for *ra*: *arātsīt*. The future is *rātsyati*; the conditional is *arātsyat*. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *rirātsati*. The passive is *rārādhyate*. The same applies to the root *sādh*.

The root *vyadh* means "to pierce. By the rule *grahijyā* (Pāṇini 6.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Present: *vidhyati*. Aorist: *avidhyat*. Imperative: *vidhyatu*. Optative: *vidhyet*. Benedictive: *vidhyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *liṭyabhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 6.1.17), there is vocalization of the reduplication: *vivyādha*. Due to the *kit* suffix, there is vocalization: *vividhatuḥ*, *vividhuḥ*, *vivyaddha*, *vivyadhitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is vṛddhi and the change to *c*: *avyātsīt*. Future: *vyatsyati*. Desiderative: *vevidhyate*.

The root *puṣ* means "to nourish. Present: *puṣyati* Imperfect: *apuṣyat* Imperative: *puṣyatu* Optative: *puṣyet* Precative: *puṣyāt* Perfect: *pupoṣa*, *pupuṣatuḥ*, *pupuṣuḥ*, *pupoṣitha* Aorist (*luṅ*): By the rule *puṣādi-dyutādy-uditaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.55), *cl* is replaced by *aṅ*; thus, *apuṣat*. From here until the end of this section, for those roots beginning with *puṣ*, the substitution of *aṅ* for *cl* is prescribed in the aorist and for *caṅ* after the causative (*ṇic*); thus, *apūpuṣat*. Future: *poṣayiṣyati*, *poṣṭā* Desiderative: *pupūkṣati* Passive: *popuṣyate* *śuṣ* means "to dry up. *tuṣ* means "to be satisfied."

The root *puṣ* is used in the sense of transformation (*vaikṛtye*). It is treated like the preceding [roots]. *Śliṣ* is used in the sense of embracing (*āliṅgane*). Examples: *śliṣyati*, *aśliṣyat*, and so forth. In the benedictive (*āśiṣi*), *āśliṣyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *āśiśleṣa*, *āśiśliṣatuḥ*, *āśiśleṣitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *śliṣa āliṅgane* (Pāṇini 3.1.46), there is *ksa* for the suffix *cli*: *āślikṣat* [he embraced] the girl. When other than embracing, as in *kāṣṭham āśliṣatu* ("let it cling to the wood"), one has *āśliṣyati*, and so forth. *Śak* is optionally used in the sense of endurance (*marṣaṇe*). Regarding *kaś*, some read it as "optionally used" (*vibhāṣita*). Examples: *kaśyati*, and so forth; in the aorist (*luṅ*), *akaśyat*.

The root *kṣvid* (ñikṣvidā) is used in the sense of oozing from the body. [Present: *kṣvidyati*; [Imperfect: *akṣvidyata*; [Aorist: *akṣvidat*; [Future: *kṣvetsyati*; [Conditional: *akṣvetsyat*, and so forth. The root *krudh* is used in the sense of anger. [Present: *krudhyati*; [Aorist: *akrudhat*; [Future: *krotsyati*, and so forth. The root *kṣudh* is used in the sense of hunger.

*Śuc* [is used] in the sense of purification; *ṣidhū* in the sense of propitiation; as before. *Radh* is used in the senses of injury and propitiation. *Randhayati*. *Aradhyat*. In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], by the rule *radhijabhor aci* (Pāṇini 7.1.61), there is the insertion of *num*: *rarandha*, *rarandhatuḥ*, *rarandhitha*. When an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant other than *y* follows, there is an option for the augment *iṭ* by the rule *radhādibhyaś ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.45). In the absence of *iṭ*, there is an absence of *num*: *rarandha*.

By the rule *neṭy aliṭi radheḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.62), there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ* in forms other than the *liṭ* [perfect] when followed by an affix beginning with *iṭ*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], the *aṅ* substitute is applied; by the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), there is elision of the nasal (*n*), and the *cl* suffix is replaced by *aṅ*: *aradhat*. In the causative (*ṇau*) with the *caṅ* reduplication, it is *ararandhat*. As before, there is an option regarding *iṭ*; if *iṭ* is present, there is a prohibition of the *num* augment: *radhiṣyati*. By the rule for *cartva*, it becomes *ratsyati*. The conditional is *aradhiṣyat* or *aratsyat*. The futures are *radhitā* or *raddhā*. The desideratives are *rirandhiṣati* or *riratsati*. The passive is *rāradhyate*.

The root *naś* is used in the sense of "disappearance" (*adarśane*). By Pāṇini 6.1.65, *ṇo naḥ*, the *ṇ* is replaced by *n*. Present tense: *naśyati* (he perishes). Imperfect: *anaśyat*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), the forms are *nanāśa*, *neśatuḥ*, *neśuḥ*, and *neśitha*. In the absence of the augment *iṭ*, by the rule *masjinaśorjhali* (Pāṇini 7.1.60), the augment *num* is added; then, through the rules for *ṣatva*, *ṭutva*, and the substitution of *anusvāra* for the *n*, the form becomes *nanaṃṣṭha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), the form is *anaśat*. Future tense: *naśiṣyati*. In the conditional (*lṛṅ*), the sequence is: first the *num* augment, then the application of *ṣatva*, *katva*, *ṭutva*, and *parasavarṇa* rules, resulting in *naṃkṣyati*. The remainder is to be understood accordingly.

The root *tṛp* means "to satisfy. Present: *tṛpyati* Imperfect: *atṛpyat* Perfect: *tatarpa*, *tatṛpatuḥ*, *tatṛpuḥ*; [second person singular] *tatarpitha* or *tatarptha*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *atṛpat*. By the supplementary rule beginning with *spṛśimṛśī-* etc., there is an optional insertion of the augment *iṭ* for the suffix *sic*, as well as an optional insertion of the augment *am*. Thus: *atarpsīt* or *atrāpsīt*. There is an optionality of *iṭ* by the rule *anudāttasya cardupadhasyānyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 6.1.59), which provides an optionality for the augment *am*; consequently, there are three forms: *trapsyati*, *tarpsyati*, *tarpiṣyati*, and so forth.

By the rule *sani halantācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10), the suffix *san* is marked with the *k* indicator (*kit*), as in *titṛpsati*. In the alternative case where the augment *iṭ* is applied, it becomes *titarpiṣati*. The root *dṛp* means "to rejoice" and "to release. It is treated the same as the preceding [roots]; the purpose of its being *anudātta* (unaccented) is for the sake of the forms *trupya-* and *drupya-*. The root *duh* means "to desire to harm. Present: *druhyati*. Imperfect: *adruhyat*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *adruhat*. In the future (*lṛt*) and conditional (*lṛṭ*), in the alternative case where *iṭ* is applied, it becomes *drohiṣyati*. In the alternative case where there is *ghatva* (the substitution of *gh* for *h*) by the rule *vā druhamuhaṣṇuhaṣṇihām* (Pāṇini 8.2.33), there is *bhaṣbhāva* (the substitution of the voiced unaspirated stop), resulting in *dhrokṣyati*. In the alternative case where there is *ḍhatva* (the substitution of *ḍh* for *h*), there is *katva* (the substitution of *k* for *ṣ*) by the rule *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si* (Pāṇini 8.2.41), and the form is the same; the rest should be understood accordingly.

In the alternative where *iṭ* is present, there is optionally *kit*-treatment according to Pāṇini 1.2.26 (*ralo vyupadhāt...*); in the absence of *iṭ*, the changes of *katva*, *ghatva*, *bhaṣtva*, *cartva*, and *ṣatva* apply, resulting in *dūdhūrṣati*; or alternatively, the changes of *ḍhatva*, *bhaṣtva*, *katva*, and *ṣatva* apply, resulting in *dudhrukṣati*.
[The roots] *muha* in the sense of confusion, and *ṣṇuha* in the sense of vomiting.

*ṣṇiha* is used in the sense of affection (*prīti*). All [the roots] are as previously described, with the exception of the substitution of *bh* for *s*. Regarding the eight roots beginning with *radh* in the rule prescribing the optional *iṭ*: *radh*, *naś*, *tṛp*, *dṛp*, *druh*, *muha*, *ṣṇuh*, and *ṣṇih*—these eight are optionally followed by *iṭ* before an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant (other than *y*).

The root *śam* means "to become tranquil. For the eight roots beginning with *śam* and ending with *mād*, there is lengthening [of the vowel] before the suffix *śyan* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 7.3.74; thus, *śāmyati*. [Imperfect: *aśāmyat*. [Imperative: *śāmyatu*. [Optative: *śāmyet*. In the benedictive: *śamyāt*. [Perfect: *śaśāma*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *aśamat*. [Future: *śamiṣyati*. [Conditional: *aśamiṣyat*. [Periphrastic future: *śamitā*. [Desiderative: *śiśamiṣati*. [Intensive: *śāśamyate*. The root *tam* means "desire. The root *dam* means "to become tranquil."
The root *śram* is used in the senses of ascetic toil and exhaustion;
*bhram* in the sense of instability;
and *kṣamūṣ* in the sense of endurance.
*klamu* means "to be weary";

*madī* means "to rejoice. These are similar to the preceding [roots]. However, for *klam*, even in the alternative where *śap* is applied according to Pāṇini 3.1.170 (*bhrāśa-bhlāśa-bhramu-kla-mu-trasi-truṭi-laṣaḥ*), there is lengthening by Pāṇini 7.3.75 (*ṣṭhivuklamvacamāṃ śiti*), as in *klāmati*.

The root *asu* is used in the sense of "casting" (*kṣepaṇe*). Present: *asyati*. Future: *āsyati*. Benedictive: *asyāt*. Aorist: *āsa*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *aṭ asyatesthuk* (Pāṇini 7.4.17), the augment *thuk* is added, resulting in *āsiṣyat*, and so forth. When preceded by a prefix (*upasarga*), the *ātmanepada* is optionally applied according to the rule *upasargādasyatyūhyoḥ vāvacanam*. Thus, one has *nirasyate* or *nirāsyate*. In the benedictive, one has *nirasīṣṭa* or *nirāse*. By the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyo'ṅ* (Pāṇini 3.1.52), the suffix *aṅ* is applied, and with the *thuk* augment, one has *nirāsthat*, and so forth. The remainder is to be understood accordingly. The root *jasu* is used in the sense of "liberation" (*mokṣaṇe*). The root *tamu* is used in the sense of "wasting away" (*upakṣaye*).
Furthermore: *damu* in the sense of supporting; *vasu* in the sense of a pillar;
*pluṣa* in the sense of division; the examples are to be inferred.
The roots *bhṛśu*, *bhraśu*, and *mraśu* mean "to fall down. *Bhraśyati*; *abhraśyat*. *Muṣa* means "to adorn. *Muṣyati*. *Uca* means "to collect. *Ucyati*.
The root *vṛṣ* (with the prefix *va-raṇe*) means "to choose. It forms *vṛṣyati*.
The root *kṛś* (with the prefix *tanūkaraṇe*) means "to make thin. It forms *kṛśyati*, *akṛśyat*, *kṛśyatu*, *kṛśyet*, *kṛśyāt*, *cakarṣa*, *akṛśat*, *karśiṣyati*, and so forth.
The root *tṛṣ* (marked with *ñit*, meaning *pipāsāyām*) means "thirst. It forms *tṛṣyati*.

The root *hṛṣ* means "to rejoice" or "to be pleased. Present: *hṛṣyati* Imperfect: *ahṛṣyat* Imperative: *hṛṣyatu* Optative: *hṛṣyet* Precative: *hṛṣyāt* Perfect: *jaharṣa*, *jahṛṣatuḥ*, *jahṛṣuḥ*, *jaharṣitha* Aorist (*luṅ*): *ahṛṣat* Future: *harṣiṣyati*, etc. The root *ruṣ* means "to be angry. Present: *ruṣyati* Imperfect: *aruṣat* Future: *roṣiṣyati* Conditional: *aroṣiṣyat* By the rule *tīṣasaha* (Pāṇini 7.2.48), there is an optional *iṭ* augment; thus, the future forms are *roṣṭā* or *roṣitā*. The root *kup* means "to be angry. Present: *kupyati* Aorist (*luṅ*): *akupat* Future: *kopiṣyati*

*Gup* in the sense of agitation: *gupyati*, *gupyāt*. *Lubh* in the sense of greed: *lubhyati*, *alubhyat*; in the *luṅ* [aorist], *alubhat*; *lobhiṣyati*, *alobhiṣyat*. By the rule *tīṣasaha* (Pāṇini 7.2.48), there is an optional *iṭ*: *lobdhā* or *lobhitā*. *Kṣubh* in the sense of trembling/agitation: *kṣubhyati*, *akṣubhyat*; in the *luṅ*, *akṣubhat*; with the causative suffix *ṇic* and the *caṅ* [reduplication], *acukṣubhat*; *kṣobhiṣyati*, etc.

The root *klid* means "to become moist. It forms *klidyati*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), it becomes *aklidat*; in the future, *klediṣyati* or *kletsyati*. The root *ñimidā* means "to become oily/moist. By the rule *miderguṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.82), there is *guṇa* substitution in the domain of *śit* suffixes; thus, *medyati*. The forms *amedyat* and so forth follow. In the *luṅ*, it is *amidat*; in the future, *mediṣyati*, and so on. With the *san* (desiderative) suffix, by the rule *ralo vyupadhāt...* (Pāṇini 1.2.26), there is optionally *kit* status; thus, *mimidiṣati* or *mimediṣati*. The root *ñikṣvidā* means "to become oily" and "to faint. It forms *kṣvidyati*. In the *laṅ*, it is *akṣvidyat*; in the *luṅ*, *akṣvidat*. In the future, *kṣvediṣyati*; in the conditional, *akṣvediṣyat*. The periphrastic future is *kṣveditā*. In the desiderative, *cikṣvediṣati* or *cikṣvidiṣati*. The periphrastic future is *kṣveditā*.

The root *ṛdh* means "to increase. Present tense (*laṭ*): *samṛdhyati* (he increases). Imperfect (*laṅ*): *asamṛdhyat* (he was increasing). Optative (*liṅ*): *samṛdhyatu* (may he increase); *samṛdhyet* (he might increase); *samṛdhyāt* (he should increase). In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), there is guṇa substitution for the light penultimate vowel, reduplication, *uratva* (substitution of *u* for the reduplicated *ṛ*), and lengthening of the reduplicated syllable. Then, by the rule *tasmānnuḍ dvihalaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.71), the augment *nuṭ* is added because the root has two consonants (*dvihala*). Thus: *ānardha*. By the force of the inclusion of the term *dvihala* in the rule prescribing *nuṭ*, *nuṭ* is also applied here: *ānṛdhatuḥ*; *ānṛdhuḥ*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), with the augment *aṭ* and *āṭ*-vṛddhi: *asamārdhat*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the suffix *caṅ*: *ārdidhat*. In the first future (*lṛt*) and conditional (*luṅ*): *samardhiṣyati* (he will increase); *asamardhiṣyat* (he would have increased). Periphrastic future (*lṛṭ*): *samardhitā* (he will increase).

By the rule *sani sanīvantardha0* (Pāṇini 7.2.49), the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied; when it is applied, there is reduplication of the second monosyllabic portion (*ekāc*), resulting in *ardidhiṣati*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *āpjñapyṛdhāmīt* (Pāṇini 7.4.55), *īt* is substituted [for the penultimate vowel], followed by *raparatva* (substitution of *r* for the semivowel), elision of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsalopa*), and *cartva* (substitution of *t* for *d*). Thus, we have *īrdhati* and *airdhat*.

The root *gṛdh* is used in the sense of longing. Present: *gṛdhyati*. Aorist: *agṛdhyat*. Benedictive: *gṛdhyāt*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *jagardha*, *jagṛdhatuḥ*, *jagṛdhuḥ*, *jagardhitha*. Imperfect (*laṅ*): Because it belongs to the *puṣādi* group, the suffix *aṅ* is applied; thus, *agṛdhat*. Causative with *caṅ*: *ajīgṛdhat* or *ajagardhat*. Future: *gardhiṣyati*. Conditional: *agardhiṣyat*. Periphrastic future: *gardhitā*. Desiderative: *jigardhiṣati*. Intensive: *jarīgṛdhyate*.
In this context, the root *kaś* takes the augment *iṭ*; the roots beginning with *radh* (the *ūdit* roots) take the augment *iṭ* optionally;
and the roots beginning with *śam* and ending with *mad* take the augment *iṭ*.

"Ṛdhyati and gṛdhyati [are also included]; the others are aniṭ and parasmaipada. Thus ends the section on the *divādi* class, beginning with the *śyan* conjugational sign, in the *Śābdikābharaṇa*, the work of Ācārya Hariyogin. This concludes the section on the *svādi* class.

The root *suñ* means "to press. As before, the operations of the *laṭ* (present tense) and other suffixes apply. By the rule *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.73), the affix *śnu* is added; this is an exception (*apavāda*) to the affix *śap*. Because it is marked with *ś*, it is treated as a *sārvadhātuka* affix. Due to its *ṅit* nature, there is no *guṇa* strengthening of the root vowel. When the *tip* suffix follows, *guṇa* is applied by the rule *sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ*, resulting in *sunoti*. Regarding the form *abhiṣuṇoti*: because the initial *i* of the prefix (*upasarga*) follows [the *ṣ*], the *ṣatva* (change to *ṣ*) is applied by the rule *upasargāt sārvadhātuke*. Thus, one says *abhiṣuṇoti*.

Because the suffix has the marker *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa* substitution. The rule *iko yaṇ aci* (Pāṇini 6.1.77), which would require *yaṇ*, is set aside, and *uvaṅ* is obtained; however, that is further set aside by the rule *huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke* (Pāṇini 6.4.87), which prescribes *yaṇ* for a stem ending in the suffix *śnu* when it is not preceded by a conjunct consonant and is followed by an affix beginning with a vowel. But in the case of a stem preceded by a conjunct consonant, only *uvaṅ* applies. Thus: *sunvanti*. In the second person singular, *sunoṣi*; in the second person dual, *sunuthaḥ*; and in the second person plural, *sunatha*. In the first person singular, *sunomi*. In the first person dual and plural, the *u* may optionally be elided by the rule *vasmasoḥ lopaścāsya* (Pāṇini 6.4.111). Thus: *sunvaḥ* or *sunuvaḥ*; *sunmaḥ* or *sunumaḥ*.

Even when there is no separation by a vowel (*avyavāya*), the substitution of *ṣ* occurs: *abhyasuṇot*. In the imperative (*loṭ*), [the forms are] *sunotu*, *sunutāt*, *sunutām*, and *sunvantu*. By the rule *serhiḥ utaśca pratyayādasaṃyogapūrvāt* (Pāṇini 6.4.106), there is the elision (*luk*) of *hi*: *sunu somam ulūkhalam*. In the optative (*liṅ*), [the forms are] *sunuyāt* and *sunuyātām*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), [the forms are] *sūyāt* and *sūyāstām*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the form is] *abhiṣuṣāva*. According to the restriction *sthādiṣvatyābhyāsena* (Pāṇini 8.3.64), even though it follows a prefix (*upasarga*), there is an absence of the *ṣ* substitution; instead, there is the substitution of *uvaṅ*: *suṣuvatuḥ*.

*suṣuvuḥ*, *suṣuvitha*, *suṣotha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], by the rule *stusudhūñbhyaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.72), the augment *iṭ* is added; with *sic*, there is *vṛddhi*: *asāvīt*. In the *caṅ* [reduplicated aorist] after the causative suffix (*ṇau*), it is *asūsuvat*. *abhisosyati*. *abhyasosyat*. Here, by the rule *sunoteḥ syasanoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.117), there is a prohibition of the substitution of *ṣ*. In the *luṭ* [future], it is *abhiṣotā*. *abhisusūṣati*.

Here, due to the restrictive rule *atra stautiṇyoreva* (Pāṇini 8.3.61), there is no *ṣatva* (the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*) for the letter following the reduplication; however, for that which follows a prefix, the rule *upasargāt‌ parasya tu sthādiṣveva* applies. One should not say, therefore, that the mention of *san* (the desiderative suffix) is useless, because its purpose is to prohibit *ṣatva* when the suffix *kvip* follows a stem ending in *san*. [The forms are: *sunute*, *asunuta*, *sunutām*. [In the potential mood (*liṅ*),] with the augment *sīyuṭ* and the elision of *s*, the *yaṇ* substitution occurs by the rule *huśnuvoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.87): *sunvīta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *soṣīṣṭa*. [Perfect tense: *suṣuve*. [Aorist: *asoṣṭa*. [Future: *soṣyate*, and so forth.

The root *ṣiñ* is used in the sense of binding (*bandhane*). Present: *sinoti*, *asinot*, *sinotu*, *sinuyāt*, *sinute*, *asinuta*, *sinutām*, *sinvīta*. Aorist: *sīyāt*, *seṣīṣṭa*. Perfekt: *siṣāya*, *siṣiye*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) with the suffix *sic*, there is *vṛddhi*: *asaiṣīt*, *aseṣṭa*.
The root *śiñ* is used in the sense of perceiving (*niśāmane*); it is conjugated like the preceding one.

The root *ḍumiñ* means "to throw. [Present tense: *minoti*, *aminot*, *minute*, *aminuta*, and so forth. In the benedictive (*āśis*), [the form is] *mīyāt*. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 6.1.50, *mīnāti-minotidīṅām lyapi ca*, there is the substitution of *ā* for the vowel in the domain of *ej*-affixes; thus, [the benedictive form is] *māsīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *mamau* and *mimye*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is the substitution of *ā* as before: *nyamāsīt* and *nyamāsta*. [In the periphrastic aorist,] *nyamīmayata*. [Future: *māsyati*, *māsyate*. In the desiderative (*san*), [the forms are] *mitsati* and *mitsate*. [Intensive: *memīyate*.

The root *ci* (meaning "to pile up" or "to collect"): *cinoti*, *cinutaḥ*, *cinvanti*; *cinute*, *cinvāte*, *cinvate*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), *cīyāt* or *ceṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *vibhāṣā ceḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.58), there is optionally *kutva* (the substitution of *k*) for the letter following the reduplication: *cicāya* or *cikāya*; *cicye* or *cikye*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *aceṣīt* or *aceṣṭa*. In the causative (*ṇau*) with the *caṅ* suffix, when the *ātvam* (vowel lengthening) option applies to *cisphurorṇau*, there is the insertion of *puk*: *acīcapat*; otherwise, *acīcayat*. In the future, *ceṣyati* or *ceṣyate*. In the desiderative (*san*), there is optionally *kutva*: *cicīṣati* or *cikīṣati*; *cicīṣate* or *cikīṣate*.

The root *stṝ* means "to cover. Present: *stṛṇoti* (he covers). Imperfect: *astṛṇot* (he covered). Imperative: *stṛṇotu*, *stṛṇutāt*. Optative: *stṛṇuyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is guṇa substitution by Pāṇini 7.4.29 (*guṇortisaṃyogādyoḥ*), resulting in *staryāt*. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), by Pāṇini 7.4.61 (*śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ*), the *khay* consonants following the reduplication remain while the initial *śar* consonants are elided, resulting in *tastāra*. By Pāṇini 7.4.110 (*ṛtaśca saṃyogāderguṇaḥ*), there is guṇa substitution for the root vowel, resulting in *tastaratuḥ* (they two covered) and *tastaruḥ* (they all covered).

The augment *iṭ*, which would have been required by the rule *krādiniyamaprāpta*, is prohibited by the rule *ṛto bhāradvājasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.63) in the case of the suffix *thali*; thus, [the form] is *tastartha*. In the *luṅ* tense, [the form] is *astārṣīt*. By the rule *ṛddhanoḥ sya* (Pāṇini 7.2.70), the augment *iṭ* is applied; thus, [the forms] are *stariṣyati* and *startā*. When the suffix *san* is added, and after the rules for *kit*-status, lengthening, and reduplication have been applied, [the form] is *tistīrṣati*. In the *yaṅ* suffix, by the rule *guṇortisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29), there is *guṇa* substitution due to the inclusion of the term "also in *yaṅ*"; the result of the reduplication process is *tāstaryate*. Because the suffixes are marked with *ṅ*, the *ātmanepada* endings are used: *stṛṇute*, *astṛṇuta*, *stṛṇutām*.

One should spread [the grass] (*stṛṇvīta*). By the rule *āśiṣi uśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), there is *kit*-ness; thus, in the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), one forms *stṛṣīṣṭa*. By the rule *ṛtaśca saṃyogāderguṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.10), the augment *iṭ* is applied; however, because *kit*-ness is absent here, *guṇa* occurs, resulting in *starṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *ṛtaśca saṃyogāderguṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.10), *guṇa* is applied: *tastare*, *tastarāte*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), as before, there is *kit*-ness, and by the rule *hrasvādaṅgāt* (Pāṇini 8.2.27), the *s* is elided: *astṛta*.

Under the governing rule *iṭ sani vā liṅ-sicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11), and with reference to *ṛtaśca saṃyogādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.43), there is an optional *iṭ* augment: *astariṣṭa*, *stariṣyate*, and so forth. The root *kṛñ* is used in the sense of "injury": *kṛṇoti*, *kṛṇutaḥ*, etc.; likewise, *kṛṇute*, etc. The root *vṛñ* is used in the sense of "choosing. Regarding the roots *vṛṅ* and *vṛñ*, they are marked as having the *iṭ* augment (*seṭ*). In the *sic* suffix, there is a *vṛddhi* strengthening: *avārīt*, *avāriṣṭām*, *avāriṣuḥ*. In the *lṛṭ* (future) and *luṭ* (periphrastic future), [the forms are] *variṣyati*, etc. In the *san* (desiderative) suffix, by the rule *iṭ sani vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.41), when *iṭ* is present, there is an option for lengthening: *vivariṣati* or *vivarīṣati*.

In the absence of *iḍ*, there is lengthening before a *jhal* suffix after the desiderative (*san*) marker. For that which exists in the place of both [sounds] receives the designation of either one; thus, since the letter *v* is both dental-labial and labial, the substitution of *u* occurs by the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya* (Pāṇini 7.1.102), and lengthening occurs by the rule *hali ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.77), resulting in *vuvūrṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*) suffix, the substitution of *rīṅ* for the root vowel *ṛ* occurs by the rule *rīṅṛtaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.27), resulting in *vevrīyate*. Likewise: *vṛṇute*, *avṛṇuta*, *vṛṇutām*, *vṛṇvīta*.

Under the governing rule *āśiṣi vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.28), the optional *iṭ* augment is prescribed by *liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11). By *na liṅi* (Pāṇini 7.2.39), the lengthening of this *iṭ* is prohibited, resulting in *variṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], the forms are *vavre*, *vavrāte*, and *vavrire*; the prohibition of *iṭ* is applied here by the rule for *krī*-beginning roots (*krādi-sūtra*) when followed by an affix beginning with a consonant other than a semivowel or nasal (*valādi*). In the *luṅ* [aorist], the forms are *avṛta*, *avariṣṭa*, and *avarīṣṭa*. The remainder should be understood accordingly.

The root *dhuñ* means "to shake. Present: *dhunoti*, *dhunute*. Benedictive: *dhūyāt*, *dhoṣīṣṭa*. Perfect: *dudhāva*, *dudhuvatuḥ*, *dudhuvuḥ*; *dudhotha*, *dudhavitha*; *dudhuve*, *dudhuvāte*. Aorist: *adhauṣīt*, *adhoṣṭa*. Causative with *caṅ*: *adūdhuvat*. Future: *dhoṣyati*, *dhoṣyate*.
[These roots] ending in *vṛ*, excluding those that are *aniṭ*, are used in both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣā*).
*ṭudu* means "to afflict. *Dunoti*, etc., are as explained previously. *Kṣi* means "to perish. *Kṣiṇoti*, *akṣiṇot*, *kṣiṇuyāt*, and so forth.
*Gṛdhu* means "to desire intensely. *Gṛdhnoti*, *agṛdhnot*, and so forth.

The root *hi* means "to go" and "to increase. After a prefix (*upasarga*), the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* occurs in the forms of *hinoti* and *mīnāti*: *prahiṇoti*, *prāhiṇot*, *prahiṇotu*, and *prahiṇuyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśīḥ*), it is *prahīyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *heracaṅi*, there is the substitution of *gh* (the *kutva*) for the letter following the reduplication: *prajighāya*, *prajighyatuḥ*, *prajighyuḥ*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *prāhayiṣīt*. In the causative with the suffix *caṅ*, it is *prājīhayat*. [In the future,] it is *praheṣyati*, and so forth. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *prajihīrṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), it is *prajeghīyate*. The root *ṣṭu* means "to praise": *stunoti*, and so forth.

The root *spṛ* is used in the senses of "to please" and "to protect. *Spṛṇoti*, *aspṛṇot*, and so forth. In the *luṅ* (aorist), it is *aspārṣīt*. [He said: "I have protected this man for a hundred autumns. The root *āplṛ* is used in the sense of "to pervade" (*vyāpti*). *Āpnoti*, *āpnutaḥ*. Because it begins with a conjunct consonant (*saṃyogādi*), the *yaṇ* substitution does not apply by Pāṇini 6.4.87 (*huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke*), and thus there is the *uvaṅ* replacement: *āpnuvanti*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *āpnot*, *āpnotu*, *āpnuyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *āpyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect): *āpa*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), because it is marked with *ḷ* (*lṛdit*), the suffix *aṅ* is applied: *āpat*. [In the future: *āpsyati*, and so forth. In the desiderative (*san*), by Pāṇini 7.4.55 (*āpjñapṛdhāmīt*), there is the substitution of *ī* for the vowel and the elision of the reduplication: *īpsati*.

The root *śak* means "to be able. Present: *śaknoti* Aorist: *aśaknot* Imperative: *śaknotu* Optative: *śaknuyāt* Precative: *śakyāt* Perfect: *śaśāka*, *śekatuḥ*, *śekuḥ*; [2nd person singular] *śekitha* or *śaśaktha* In the *luṅ* (aorist), [the form is] *aṅ* [with *śaka*], as in *aśakṣyat* and so forth. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), operations such as those prescribed by Pāṇini 7.4.54 (*sani mīmā-*) apply. Because of the statement "the root *śikṣ* is used in the sense of desiring to know," the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is taught; thus: *śikṣate*, *śikṣati*. The roots *rādh* and *sādh* mean "to accomplish" or "to succeed. *rādhnoti*, *arādhnot*, *rādhnuyāt*, *rādhyāt*, and so forth. The same applies to *sādh*.

The root *śru* is used in the sense of "hearing. By the rule *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.73), the suffix *śnu* is applied; by the rule *śruvaḥ śṛ ca* (Pāṇini 3.1.74), there is the substitution of *śṛ* for *śru*. Thus: *śṛṇoti*, *aśṛṇot*, *śṛṇuyāt*, *śrūyāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), *śuśrāva*, *śuśruvatuḥ*, *śuśruvuḥ*. By the rule regarding the *krād*-group, the augment *iṭ* is permanently prohibited. Thus: *śuśrotha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *aśrauṣīt*. *Śroṣyati*, etc. In the causative with *caṅ* (the reduplicated aorist), *aśuśravat* or *aśiśravat*. *Śroṣyati*, etc. By the rule *jñā-śru-smṛ-dṛśām ātmanepadam* (Pāṇini 1.3.57), the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used in the desiderative: *śuśrūṣate*.

The middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is applied due to the rule *saṃ-pūrvāt samo gamy-ṛcchi* (Pāṇini 1.3.29), as in *saṃśṛṇute*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), [the forms are] *saṃśroṣīṣṭa*; in the second person plural, *saṃśroṣīḍhvam*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *saṃśuśruve*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *samaśrauṣṭa*. It is *aniṭ* and belongs to the *parasmaipada* class.

The root *aś* is used in the sense of pervasion (*vyāpti*). Present: *aśnute*, *āśnuta*, *aśnutām*, *aśnuvīta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is an option for the augment *iṭ* because of the marker *ū* [in the *dhātu-pāṭha*]: *akṣīṣṭa* or *āśiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), by Pāṇini 7.4.70 (*ata ādeḥ*), the vowel of the reduplication is lengthened; then, by the rule "after the reduplicated syllable of *aśnoti*," the augment *nuṭ* is added: *ānaśe*, *ānaśāte*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), [the forms are] *āṣṭa*, *āśiṣṭa* (by Pāṇini 6.1.36, *sveduhavyaiḥ*). Future: *akṣyate*, *aśiṣyate*. In the desiderative (*san*), by Pāṇini 7.2.74 (*smipūṅrañja...*), the augment *iṭ* is compulsory:

*aśiśiṣate*. Because of the marker *ū*, there is an option for *iṭ* in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*). The root *dhṛṣ* is used in the sense of boldness or audacity (*prāgalbhya*). Present: *dhṛṣṇoti*, *adhṛṣṇot*.

The root *dambh* means "to deceive" or "to obstruct. By the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), there is elision of the nasal (*na-lopa*). Thus: *dabhnoti*, *dabhnutaḥ*, *dabhnuvanti*. In the imperfect (*luṅ*), *adabhnot*. In the imperative (*loṭ*), *dabhnotu*. In the optative (*liṅ*), *dabhnuyāt* or *dabhyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), due to the nasal becoming an *anusvāra*, it is *dadambha*. Regarding the roots *śranth* and *granth*, because they are marked with *k* (indicating the *kit* designation), there is no elision of the nasal. Due to the non-eternality (*anityatva*) of the rule that [the substitution] is as if not accomplished (*asiddha*), the operations such as *ata ekahalmadhye* (Pāṇini 6.4.120) apply; thus: *debhatuḥ*, *debhuḥ*. [In the Vedic form] *detūḥ*, Indra did not deceive the images. [In the perfect], *dadambhitha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist], [the forms are] *adambhīt*, *dambhiṣyat*, and so forth. In the alternative where the augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini 7.2.49), we have *didambhiṣati*. Otherwise, when the substitution of *i* for the root *dambh* is made by the rule *dambha icca* (Pāṇini 7.4.56), there is elision of the reduplication. Because the mention of *hal* in the rule *halantācca* (Pāṇini 1.2.10) refers to the class (*jāti*) of consonants, the suffix is *kit*; consequently, there is elision of the nasal (*nalopa*), the *bhaṣ*-substitution, and the *cartva* change, resulting in *dhitsati*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive], the form is *dādabhyate*. The root *ṛdh* means "to increase" or "to prosper. [Present: *samṛdhnoti*. [Aorist: *samārdhnot*. [Imperative: *samṛdhnotu*. [Optative: *samṛdhnuyāt*. From here onwards, the forms follow those of the root *mṛdh*. However, in the *luṅ* [aorist], the form is *samārdhīt*, and so forth.
The roots ending in *seṭ* (those with the augment *iṭ*) are *parasmaipadī* (active-voice).
Thus ends the section on roots beginning with *svā-* (the first class) characterized by the *śnu* vikaraṇa, in the *Śābdikābharaṇa* composed by Hariyogin Prollaṇācārya.

The section on the *tud*-class roots begins with *tud* in the sense of "to strike" or "to afflict. According to Pāṇini’s rule 3.1.77, *śa* is substituted [for *śap*] after roots beginning with *tud*; this is an exception (*apavāda*) to *śap*. By the rule 1.2.4, "that which is not marked as *apit* is *sārvadhātuka*," this [suffix *śa*] is treated as having the marker *ṅ*. Thus: *tudati*, *atudat*, *tudatu*, *tudet*, *tudyāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*): *tutoda*, *tutudatuḥ*, *tutuduḥ*, *tutoditha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), with the suffix *sic*, there is vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) for a root ending in a consonant: *atautsīt*. Alternatively, by the rule of *aṅ* substitution: *atūtudat*. In the future (*lṛṭ*): *tottsyati*. In the conditional (*lṛṅ*): *atotsyat*. In the periphrastic future (*luṭ*): *tottā*. In the desiderative (*san*): *tutuṣati*. In the passive (*yaṅ*): *totudyate*. The root *nud* is used in the sense of "impelling" or "pushing."
The root *diś* is used in the sense of granting;
*kṣip* in the sense of impelling;
and *kṛṣ* in the sense of scratching. Examples for these should be provided according to the preceding pattern.

The root *bhrasj* means "to cook. Regarding the rule *okāra oditaśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), the specific application should be considered. By the rule *jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi* (Pāṇini 8.4.53), the *s* is changed to *d*; by the rule for *cutva*, that *d* becomes *j*; and by the rule *jhalo jhali* (Pāṇini 8.2.26), the initial consonant of the cluster is dropped at the end of a word. Then, by the rule *grahijyā-vayi-vyadhī-vaṣṭi-vicati-vṛścati-pṛcchatibhṛjjatīnām* (Pāṇini 6.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Thus: *bhṛjjati*. Imperfect: *abhṛjjat*. Imperative: *bhṛjjatu*. Optative: *bhṛjjet*. Precative: *bhṛjyāt*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *babhrajja*.

Regarding the optional rule for *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes, *bhrasjo ropadhayo ram anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 6.4.47), there is optionally the elision of the *repha* (r) and the *upadhā* vowel, and the augment *ram*. Thus, in one alternative, we have *babharja*, *babharjatuḥ*, *babhrajuḥ*, and *babharjuḥ*; [in the other] *babhrajjitha* and *babharjitha*; *babhraṣṭha* and *babharṣṭha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *vadavraja-* (Pāṇini 7.2.3), there is *vṛddhi*; by the rule *vraśca-* etc., there is *ṣatva* (change to ṣ), and the elision of the initial consonant of the conjunct; following the rules for *ṣatva* and *katva*, the rest is easily understood: *abhārṣīt*, *abhārṣṭām*, *abhārṣuḥ*.

By the rule *bhrasjo ropadhayo ram anyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 6.4.47), the augment *ram* is optionally added, resulting in *abhārkṣīt*, *abhārkṣiṣṭām*, and *abhārkṣiṣuḥ*. In the *caṅ* (reduplication) of the causative (*ṇic*), we have *ababhrajjat* or *ababharjat*. The future forms are *bhraṣkṣyati* or *bharkṣyati*, and so forth. The periphrastic future forms are *bhraṣṭā* or *bharṣṭā*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), by the rule *sanīvantardha* (Pāṇini 7.2.49), there is an optionality of the augment *iṭ* and the augment *am*; consequently, there are four possible forms: *bibhrajjayiṣati*, *bibharjayiṣati*, *bibhraṣkṣati*, and *bibharkṣati*.

Regarding the rule *yaṅi rīgṛdupadhasya ca* (Pāṇini 7.4.90), because of the statement that "it should be stated that [the substitute applies] after *ṛ*," the augment *rīk* is added, as in *barībhṛjyate*. The root *mil* (meaning "to meet" or "to join"): - Present: *milati* - Imperfect: *amilat* - Imperative: *milatu* - Potential: *milet* - Benedictive: *milyāt* - Perfect: *mimela* - Aorist: *amelīt* - Future: *meliṣyati*, etc. In the desiderative (*san*), there are two forms: *mimiliṣati* and *mimeliṣati*. Examples for the *tud*-class roots in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) should be inferred accordingly. As for the root *kṣip* ("to throw"), when preceded by *abhi*, *prati*, or *ati*, the rule *abhipratyatibhyaḥ kṣipaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.80) mandates the active voice (*parasmaipada*) exclusively. [Thus, the roots] beginning with *mil*—excluding *mil* itself—are those that do not take the augment *iṭ* (*aniṭ*) and are used in both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣā*).

The root *ṛṣ* means "to go. Present: *ṛṣati* (he goes). Imperfect: *ārṣat* (he went). Optative: *ṛṣyāt* (he may go). Aorist: *ānarṣa* (he went); *ānarṣatuḥ* (they two went); *ānarṣuḥ* (they went). Periphrastic Aorist: *ārṣīt* (he went); *ārṣiṣat* (he had gone). Future: *arṣiṣyati* (he will go). Conditional: *āṣiṣyat* (he would have gone). Periphrastic Future: *arṣitā* (he will go). Desiderative (*san*): *arṣiṣiṣati* (he wishes to go). Intensive (*yaṅ*): [No form is given] because it does not begin with a consonant. The root *juṣ* means "to love" and "to serve. Present: *juṣate* (he loves/serves). Imperfect: *ajuṣata* (he loved/served). Imperative: *juṣatām* (let him love/serve). Optative: *juṣeta* (he may love/serve). Precative: *joṣiṣīṣṭa* (may he love/serve). Perfect: *jujuṣe* (he loved/served). Aorist: *ajoṣiṣṭa* (he loved/served). Conditional: *ajūjuṣat* (he would have loved/served). Future: *joṣiṣyate* (he will love/serve). Conditional: *ajoṣiṣyata* (he would have loved/served). Periphrastic Future: *joṣitā* (he will love/serve). Desiderative: *jujuṣiṣate* (he wishes to love/serve); *jujoṣiṣate*, *jojuṣyate* (intensive forms).

The root *ovijī* is used in the senses of fear and trembling. In the *liṅ* (optative) for the benedictive, by the rule *udavijata āśiṣi vija iṭ* (Pāṇini 1.2.2), the *iṭ* augment is treated as having the marker *ṅ*, resulting in *udvijiṣīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), it is *udvivije*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), it is *udavijiṣṭa*. The future forms are *udvijiṣyate* and the conditional *udavijiṣyata*. The periphrastic future is *udvijitā*. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *udvijiṣate*. The root *olasjī* is used in the sense of shame. Due to the substitution of the voiced stop (*jaśtva*) for the *s* sound, it is conjugated like *bhṛjjati*, as in *lajjate*. The aorist form is *alajjata*, and so forth. These roots are *seṭ* (having the *iṭ* augment) and are *ātmanebhāṣā* (middle-voiced).

The root *vraścū* means "to cut. By the rule *grahijyā* (Pāṇini 6.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Thus: *vṛścati*, *avṛścat*, *vṛścatu*, *vṛścet*, *vṛścyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, there is vocalization of the reduplication, substitution of *u* for *ṛ*, and the rule *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.60). Thus: *vavraśca*, *vavraścatuḥ*, *vavraścuḥ*, *vavraścitha*. Due to the elision of the first consonant of the conjunct (*saṃyogādilopa*), followed by the rules for *ṣatva* and *ṭutva*, we have *vavraṣṭha*. Because the root is marked with *ūdit*, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ* in the *luṅ* (aorist): *avraścīt*. In the absence of *iṭ*, there is elision of the first consonant of the conjunct, followed by *katva* and *ṣatva*, resulting in *avrākṣīt*.
It will tear (*vraściṣyati*), it will tear (*vrakṣyati*), and so forth. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *vivṛściṣati* or *vivṛkṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), it is *varīvṛścyate*.

The root *vyac* is used in the sense of "deception" (*vyājīkaraṇe*). By the rule *grahijyā* (Pāṇini 6.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*); thus: *vicati*. [Imperfect: *avicat*. [Optative: *vicatu*, *vicet*, *vicyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), there is vocalization of the reduplication (*abhyāsa-saṃprasāraṇa*): *vivyāja*. By the rule for vocalization in *grahijyā* etc., [in the dual: *vivicatuḥ*. Because of the statement that *vyac* does not belong to the *kuṭādi* class, when the suffix is marked with *ṅ* (indicating no *guṇa*), there is vocalization as before and no *guṇa*: *vivicitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *avicīt*. In the causative with *caṅ*: *avivyacat*. [Future: *viciṣyati*. [Periphrastic future: *vicitā*. [Desiderative: *viviciṣati*. [Intensive: *vevicyate*.
*uñch* (to glean): *uñchati*, *auñchat*, *uñchatu*, *uñchet*, *uñchyāt*, *uñchāñcakāra*, *auñchīt*, *uñchiṣyati*, *auñchiṣyat*, *uñchitā*, *uñchicchiṣati*. *ubj* (to straighten/arrange);
*ujjh* (to abandon).
The roots *ubha* and *umbha* mean "to fill. As before, [in the present tense] it is *ubhati*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), it is *uvābha*.

The root *ṛcch* is used in the senses of "going," "loss of the senses," and "assuming a form. [Present]: *ṛcchati* [Imperfect]: *ārcchat* [Imperative]: *ṛcchatu* [Optative]: *ṛcchet* [Aorist optative]: *ṛcchyāt* In the *liṭ*, by the rule *tasmānnuḍdvihalaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.71), the augment *nuṭ* is applied; then, by the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), *guṇa* is substituted. Thus, *ānarccha*. Here, because the penultimate vowel is light (*laghu*), the *guṇa* substitution is prescribed by this very rule. [Perfect forms]: *ānarcchatuḥ*, *ānarcchuḥ*, *ānarcchitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), there is *vṛddhi* due to the prefix *āṭ*: *ārcchiṣyat*, etc.

From the root preceded by *sam*, the Ātmanepada suffix is applied according to Pāṇini 1.3.29 (*samo gamyṛcchi*), as in *samṛcchate* and so forth; in the benedictive, *samṛcchiṣīṣṭa*; in the perfect (*liṭ*), *samānarcche*; in the aorist (*luṅ*), *samārcchiṣṭa*; and in the future, *samṛcchiṣyate*, etc. The root *tvac* means "to cover": *tvacati*, *atvacad*, etc. The root *ṛc* means "to praise": *ṛcati*, *ārcat*, etc.; in the perfect, *ānarca*. Regarding the rule *tasmānnuḍ dvihalaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.71), since the vowel *ṛ* is intended to include its constituent *r*, we have *ānṛcatuḥ* and *ānṛcuḥ*; in the second person singular, *ānarcitha*.

The root *lubh* is used in the sense of "to delude. [Present tense: *lubhati*; [Imperfect: *alubhat*; [Imperative: *lubhatu*; [Optative: *lubhet*. The remainder is the same as for the root *lubhyati*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), [the form is] *alobhīt*. The roots *ruṣ* and *ṛṣ* are used in the sense of "injury. [Present tense: *ruṣati*, *ṛṣati*, etc. In the *luṭ* (future), there is an option for the augment *iṭ* according to Pāṇini 7.2.48 (*tīṣasahalubharuṣariṣaḥ*), resulting in *roṣṭā* or *roṣitā*.
The roots *guph* and *gumpha* are used in the sense of "knotting" or "binding. [Present tense: *guphati*, *gumphati*, etc.

The roots *śubh*, *śumbh*, and *śobh* mean "to beautify. Examples include *śubhati*, *śumbhati*, and so forth. The root *dṛbhī* means "to weave" or "to string together. Present: *sandṛbhati* Imperfect: *samadṛmbhat* Imperative: *sandṛbhatu* Optative: *sandṛbhet* Precative: *sandṛbhyāt* Periphrastic Perfect: *sandadarbha* Periphrastic Perfect (3rd du.): *sandadarbhatuḥ* Periphrastic Perfect (2nd sg.): *sandadarbhitha* Aorist: *samadarbhīt* Reduplicated Aorist: *samadadarbhat* Desiderative: *samadīdṛbhat* Future: *sandarbhiṣyati* Desiderative: *sandidarbhiṣati*

The root *cṛt* is used in the sense of "injury. It forms *cṛtati*, *acṛtat*, and so forth. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense: *cacarta*, *cacṛtatuḥ*, *cacṛtuḥ*, *cacartitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense: *acartīt*. Regarding the suffixes *syasanoḥ*, there is an optional *iṭ* augment after *sic* following *kṛ*, *cṛt*, and *tṛd*: thus, *cartsyati* or *cartiṣyati*; *acartsyat* or *acartiṣyat*. In the *luṭ* (future) tense: *cartitā*. In the desiderative: *cicṛtsati* or *cicartiṣati*. The root *vidh* is used in the sense of "arranging" (*vidhāna*). It forms *vidhati*, *avidhat*, and so forth. The root *juḍ* is used in the sense of "going. It forms *juḍati*.
*mṛḍ* means "to please. *mṛḍati*; *amṛḍat*, and so forth. *mṛḍa* is treated in the same way. *prīṇ* means "to please"; *prīṇati*.
*mr̥ṇ* in the sense of injury: *mr̥ṇati*.
*tuṇa* and *tṛṇa* in the sense of crookedness: *tuṇati*, *tṛṇati*. *puṇa* in the sense of auspicious action: *puṇati*.

The root *ghuṇ* is used in the sense of whirling and wandering; it forms *ghuṇati* and *ghūrṇati*. The root *sura* is used in the sense of sovereignty and radiance; it forms *surati*. The root *khura* is used in the sense of cutting and digging; it forms *khurati*.
*Kura* in the sense of sound: *kurati*.
*Mura* in the sense of encircling: *murati*.
*Khura* and *kṣura* in the sense of scratching: *khurati*, *kṣurati*.
*Ghur* occurs in the sense of making a terrible or fearsome sound; *ghurati*.

*Pur* means to go forward; *purati*. Examples for these [roots] should be inferred on the strength of the latent impressions (*saṃskāra*) from the experience of previous grammatical procedures (*prakriyā*).

The root *bṛh* (meaning "to lift up") forms *bṛhati*. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), it is *bṛhyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense: *babarha*, *babṛhatuḥ*, *babṛhuḥ*. Because it is marked with *ū* (*ūdit*), there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*: *babarhitha*. In the absence of *iṭ*, there is the substitution of *ḍ* for *h*, *gh* for *h*, *ṣ* for *t*, and the substitution of the voiced unaspirated stop (*jaś*)—resulting in *babarḍha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense: *abarhīt*. In the absence of *iṭ*, there is *vṛddhi*, followed by the substitutions of *ḍh* for *h*, *bh* for *ṣ*, *k* for *ṣ*, and *ṣ* for *t*—resulting in *abhākṣīt*. [Future: *barhiṣyati*, *bharkṣati*, etc. [Periphrastic future: *barhitā*, *barḍhā*. [Desiderative: *bibarhiṣati*, *bibhṛkṣati*. [Intensive: *barībṛhyate*. The roots *tṛh*, *stṛh*, and *sṛh* (meaning "to injure") follow the same pattern as the preceding one.

The root *iṣ* is used in the sense of "desire. By the rule *iṣugami...* (Pāṇini 7.3.77), there is the substitution of *cha*, and by *che ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.73), the augment *tuk* is added; thus, one forms *icchati* and so forth. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), the form is *iṣyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), with the suffix *tip*: there is *guṇa* substitution; then, because of the status as a *sthānivadbhāva* by the rule *dvirvacane'ci* (Pāṇini 1.1.59), the portion *iṣ* is reduplicated. By *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.60), all but the first consonant is elided, and by *abhyāsasyāsavarṇe* (Pāṇini 6.4.78), the *iyaṅ* substitute is applied, resulting in *iyeṣa*. The forms *īṣatuḥ* and *īṣuḥ* follow. *Iyeṣitha* is formed in the second person singular. In the aorist (*luṅ*), the form is *aiṣīt*. The future is *eṣiṣyati*, and the conditional is *aiṣiṣyat*.

By the rule *luṭi tīṣasaha* (Pāṇini 7.2.48) and others, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*: *eṣitā* or *eṣṭā*. [The desiderative form is] *eṣiṣiṣati*. The root *miṣ* is used in the sense of rivalry: *miṣati*, *amiṣat*, and so forth. The root *kila* is used in the senses of coldness and playing.
*tila* means "to moisten";
*sala* means "to deform"; *vila* means "to move."
*Vila* means covering; *ila* means sleep and casting;
*bila* means splitting.
*Bhila* in the sense of "dense" (*gahane*); *hila* in the sense of "producing devotion" (*bhāvakaraṇe*);
*mila* in the sense of "stone" (*śilā*) and "gleaning" (*uñche*). The examples for these are to be inferred.

*likh* (to write) in the arrangement of letters: *likhati*, *alikhat*, *likhatu*, *likhet*, *likhyāt*; *lilekha*, *lilikhatuḥ*, *lilikhuḥ*, *lilekhitha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], *alekhīt*. In the *san* [desiderative], *lilikhiṣati* or *lilekhiṣati*. *lelikhyate*. From here onwards are the *kuṭādi* [roots], for which there is the rule of treating the subsequent *añ* and *ṇit* suffixes as having the *ṅit* designation.

The root *kuṭ* is used in the sense of "crookedness" (*kauṭilye*). Present: *kuṭati* (he is crooked). Imperfect: *akuṭat* (he was crooked). Imperative: *kuṭatu* (let him be crooked). Optative: *kuṭet* (he may be crooked). Precative: *kuṭyāt* (may he be crooked). Periphrastic perfect: *cukoṭa* (he became crooked). Reduplicated perfect: *cukuṭatuḥ* (the two became crooked), *cukuṭuḥ* (they became crooked). By the rule *gāṅkuṭādibhyo 'ñṇinṅit* (Pāṇini 1.2.1), the suffixes are treated as having the marker *ṅ*; thus, *cukuṭitha* (thou hast become crooked). In the aorist (*luṅ*), *akuṭīt* (he became crooked); due to the *ṅ* marker, there is no *guṇa* strengthening. Future: *kuṭiṣyati* (he will become crooked). Conditional: *akuṭiṣyat* (he would have become crooked). Periphrastic future: *kuṭitā* (he will become crooked). Desiderative:

*cukuṭiṣati* (he wishes to become crooked). Passive: *cokuṭyate* (he is made crooked). *puṭ* is used in the sense of "joining together" (*saṃśleṣaṇe*). *kuc* is used in the sense of "contraction" (*saṃkocane*).
*kuṭ* in the sense of sound;
*guḍ* in the sense of coagulation;
*ḍip* in the sense of throwing.
*vuṇ* in the sense of wetting; *sphuṭa* in the sense of blossoming;
*muṭa* in the senses of throwing and crushing. For this [root], there is optionally the inclusion of the *bhrāśa*-class.
*truṭa* means to quarrel;
*cuṭa* means to cut;
*juḍa* means to bind.
*kuḍa* means intoxication; *guḍa* means measurement;
*luḍa* means clinging.
Kuṭa means to form or construct;
guḍa means density and childhood;
ghuṭa means to strike back or resist.
*Tuḍ* means to break;
*tuṭ* and *sphuṭ* mean to cover;
*huḍ* means to collect or assemble.
*guḍ* in the sense of emission;
*sphura* in the sense of throbbing;
*vruḍ* in the sense of aggregation.

*Juḍa* and *huḍa* mean "to wipe away"; *sphura* and *sphula* mean "to cover"; and *sphula* also means "to collect. These are roots that take the *parasmaipada* (active voice) and are *aniṭ* (not taking the augment *iṭ*); their examples should be inferred as before.

In the sense of "making an effort" (*udyamana*): *āgurute*, *āgurata*, *āguratām*, *āgureta*. Because it belongs to the *kuṭādi* group and is marked with the *ṅit* indicator, there is no *guṇa* strengthening; thus, [the benedictive form is] *aguriṣīṣṭa*. [The imperfect is] *ājugure*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), [the form is] *āguriṣṭa*. [The future is] *āguriṣyate*. [The conditional is] *āguriṣyata*. [The periphrastic future is] *āguritā*. [The desiderative is] *ājuguriṣate*. [The intensive is] *ājogūrjate*. It is a *seṭ* root and is conjugated in the *ātmanepada*.

The root *ṇu* is used in the sense of praising (*stavane*). In the present tense (*laṭ*), the substitution of *uvaṅ* occurs: *nuvati*, *anuvat*, *nuvatu*, *nuvet*, *nūyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *nunāva*, *nunuvatuḥ*, *nunuvuḥ*, *nunuvitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), because the suffix is marked with *ṅ*, there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule *sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu*; thus, with the substitution of *uvaṅ*, we have *anuvīt*. However, according to the statement, "Those who know [the rules] declare these [roots] to be *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*)," one may also say *nuvate*. With the future (*lṛṭ*) augmented by *iṭ*: *nuviṣyati*. In the conditional (*lṛṅ*): *anuviṣyat*. In the periphrastic future (*lṛṭ*): *nuvitā*. In the desiderative (*san*), there is a prohibition of *iṭ* by the rule *sani grahaguhośca* (Pāṇini 7.2.12).
When preceded by the prefix *āṅ*, the *ātmanepada* is applied by the rule *āṅinuchiyorupasaṃkhyānam*. Thus: *ānuvate*, *ānuvete*, *ānuvante*, and so forth, should be applied accordingly.

The root *dhū* is used in the sense of shaking (*vidhūnana*). The substitute *uvaṅ* is applied: *dhuvati*, *adhuvat*, *dhuvatu*, *dhuvet*, *dhūyāt*. [Perfect: *dudhāva*, *dudhuvatuḥ*, *dudhuvuḥ*, *dudhavitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), *adhuvīt*; because it belongs to the *kuṭādi* group and is marked with *ṅit*, there is no *vṛddhi*: *adūdhuvat*. [Future: *dhuviṣyati*, *adhuviṣyat*. [Periphrastic future: *dhavitā*. [Desiderative: *dudhūṣati*. [Intensive: *dodhūyate*. The root *had* is used in the sense of voiding excrement (*purīṣotsarga*).
The root *dhru* is used in the senses of motion and steadiness (*gati-sthairyayoḥ*).
The roots ending in *seṭ* are spoken of as *parasmaipada*.
The root *kuṅ* is used in the sense of sound (*śabde*); it is conjugated as *kuvate*. For roots beginning with *kuṭ*, the rule is complete.

The root *vṛṅ* is used in the sense of exertion (*vyāyāme*). By the rule *riṅ śayagliṅkṣu* (Pāṇini 7.4.28), there is the substitution of *riṅ*; however, by the force of the explicit mention of *yaṅ* [in the subsequent rule], [the substitution does not apply here]. Thus: *vyāpṛyate*, *vyāpṛyata*, *vyāpriyatām*, *vyāpriyeta*. By the rules *liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 1.2.11) and *uśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), there is *kitva* [of the suffix]; thus: *vyāpṛṣīṣṭa*.
