In the case of the suffix *dhvam*, there is a cerebral [substitution]: *vyāpṛṣīḍhvam*. In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], it is *vyāpapre*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], there is *kitva* of the *sic* suffix and the elision of *s*; thus: *vyāpṛta*, *vyāpṛṣātām*. [In the future: *vyāpariṣyate*. [In the conditional: *vyāpariṣyata*. [In the periphrastic future: *vyāpartā*.

In the case of *vuvūrṣate*, there is shortening due to the status of being a *kit* suffix, lengthening, and [the substitution of] *u* for the long vowel. Once the lengthening has been applied, the augment *iṭ* does not occur by the rule *iṭ sani vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.41), which is governed by the heading *vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), because the *ṛ*-vowel here is *lākṣaṇika* (derived). In the case of the *yaṅ* suffix, [the substitution of] *rīṅ* occurs by the rule *rīṅ ṛtaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.27): [the form is] *vyāpṛyate*.

The root *mṛ* is used in the sense of "to give up life. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra *mriyater luṅliṅoś ca* (1.3.61), the ātmanepada voice is applied only in the *luṅ* and *liṅ* tenses; in the *śit* (present-system) tenses, and elsewhere, the parasmaipada voice is used by default for the agent (*kartṛ*). Thus: *mriyate*, *amṛyata*, and so forth, as previously described. In the *liṭ* tense: *mamāra*, *mamratuḥ*, *mamruḥ*, *mamaritha*. In the *luṅ* tense: *amriyata*, and so forth, as previously described. [Note: Roots ending in *tāsi* that lack an *iṭ* augment take the ātmanepada.]

*ruṣ* in the sense of "to go": *ruṣati*. *dhṛ* in the sense of "to hold": with *riṅ* substitution before the intensive suffix (*yaṅ*), it becomes *dhardhyati*. *kṣi* in the senses of "dwelling" and "going": *kṣīyati*.

The root *ṣū* is used in the sense of "impelling. Regarding the change of *s* to *ṣ* after a prefix, the rule *upasargāt sunoti* (Pāṇini 8.3.65) applies, as in *viṣuvati*, *vyuṣuvat*, *viṣuvat*, and *viṣūyāt*. However, by the restrictive rule *sthādiṣvabhyāsena cābhyāsasya* (Pāṇini 8.3.64), there is no change of the reduplication to *ṣ*. Thus: *visuṣāva*, *viśuṣuvatuḥ*, *visuṣuvuḥ*, *visuṣavitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), it is *vyasāvīt*. The future forms are *viṣaviṣyati* and *viṣaviṣyat*. The periphrastic future is *viṣavitā*. In the desiderative (*san*), it is *visusūṣati*. By the restrictive rule *stautiṇyoreva* (Pāṇini 8.3.61), there is no change of the reduplication to *ṣ*.

The root *kṝ* means "to scatter. By the rule *ṛta iddhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.100), the vowel *ṛ* is replaced by *i*, resulting in *kirati*. The forms are: *akirat* (imperfect), *kiratu* (imperative), *kiret* (optative). In the precative (*liṅ*), due to the shortening of the vowel, it becomes *kiryāt*. The perfect forms are: *vicakāra*, *vicakaratuḥ*, *vicakaruḥ*, and *vicakaritha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), the lengthening rule *vṝto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38) does not apply because of the prohibition *na liṅi sici parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.40); thus, we have *akārīt*, *akāriṣṭām*, *akārṣṭa*. The future forms are *kariṣyati*, *karīṣyati*, and so forth.

By the rule *sani grahaguhośca* (Pāṇini 7.2.12), the prohibition of *iṭ* is set aside; and although the option for *iṭ* would have applied by the rule *ihaniṣṭhāyām* (Pāṇini 7.2.45), the compulsory addition of *iṭ* is prescribed by the rule *kṛñca pañcabhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.53) for the five roots ending with *pṛcchati*. Since *iṭ* was not applicable to *pṛcchati*, this [rule] will provide for it. Furthermore, one does not desire the lengthening of this *iṭ* by the rule *vṝto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38). As for the roots *kṛ* and others, the Ātmanepada is employed in the sense of joy and so forth, according to the supplementary rule (*upasaṃkhyāna*) stating: "In the senses of joy, livelihood, and making a nest, [the root] *kṛ* takes the Ātmanepada. In that context, [it applies] when preceded by *ava*.

Under the governing rule *kiratau lavane* (Pāṇini 6.1.140), the rule *apāccatuṣpācchakuniṣvālekhane* (Pāṇini 6.1.142) prescribes that the augment *suṭ* is placed before the root *kṛ* when the sense of scratching quadrupeds or birds is understood; thus, one says *akaskirate*. When violence (*hiṃsā*) is understood, the rule *hisāyāṃ prateśca* (Pāṇini 6.1.141) prescribes *suṭ* after the prefix *prati*; thus, one says *pratiṣkirati*. Regarding the benediction (*āśis*), the *guṇa* substitution and the addition of the suffix *iṭ* occur; although the rule *vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38) would allow for the lengthening of the vowel, there is a prohibition by the rule *na liṅi* (Pāṇini 7.2.39), as in *avasmariṣīṣṭa*.

In the case of the absence of *iṭ* by the rule *liṅsicorātmanepadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.42), because of the *kit* status [of the suffix] by the rule *uśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), we have *avaskarṣīṣṭa*. By the rule *aḍabhyāsavyavāyepi* (Pāṇini 6.1.136), *suṭ* is applied even when there is intervention by *aṭ* or the reduplication, resulting in *avacaskare*. In the *luṅ* tense, with the intervention of *aṭ*, *suṭ* is applied as *avāskarṣiṣṭa*. As before, in the absence of *iṭ* and due to the *kit* status as previously mentioned, we have *avāskarṣṭa*. The forms *avaskariṣyate* and *avaskarīṣyate*, etc., follow accordingly.

The root *gṝ* is used in the sense of "swallowing. Forms such as *nigirati* ("he swallows") and so forth are explained in the same manner as those preceded by *sam* and *ava*. By the rules *ava-agraḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.51) and *samaḥ pratijñāne* (Pāṇini 1.3.52), the Ātmanepada suffix is applied: *avagirate*, *saṅgirate*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), one has *avagiriṣīṣṭa*, *saṅgariṣīṣṭa*, and so forth. Like the root *kṛ*, this root takes the intensive suffix *yaṅ* by the rule *lupasadacara...* (Pāṇini 3.1.24), and by the rule *gro yaṅi* (Pāṇini 7.4.84), the substitution of *l* for *r* occurs, resulting in *jegīlyate*.

The root *dṛṅ* is used in the sense of respect (*ādara*). The suffixes *riṅ* and *yaṅ* are applied as before. Present: *ādriyate*, *ādriyete*, *ādriyante*; *ādriyase*, *ādriyethe*, *ādriyadhve*; *ādriye*, *ādriyāvahe*, *ādriyāmahe*. Imperfect: *ādriyata*, *ādriyetām*, *ādriyanta*; *ādriyathāḥ*, *ādriyethām*, *ādriyadhvam*; *ādriye*, *ādriyāvahi*, *ādriyāmahi*. Optative: *ādriyeta*, *ādriyeyātām*, *ādriyeran*; *ādriyethāḥ*, *ādriyeyāthām*, *ādriyedhvam*; *ādriyeya*, *ādriyevahi*, *ādriyemahi*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), the suffix of the optative is treated as having the *kit* designation. Benedictive: *adriṣīṣṭa*, *adriṣīyāstām*, *adriṣīran*; *adriṣīṣṭhāḥ*, *adriṣīyāsthām*, *adriṣīdhvam*; *adriṣīya*, *adriṣīvahi*, *adriṣīmahi*. Periphrastic perfect: *ādadre*, *ādadriṣe*, *ādadrire*; *ādadriṣe*, *ādadridhve*, *ādadriḍhve*; *ādadre*, *ādadriṣvahe*, *ādadrimahe*. Aorist: *ādṛta*, *ādṛṣātām*, *ādṛṣata*; *ādṛthāḥ*, *ādṛṣāthām*, *ādṛḍhvam*; *ādṛṣi*, *ādṛṣvahi*, *ādṛṣmahi*. [The augment *iṭ* is added by Pāṇini 7.2.70: *ṛddhanoḥ sye*]. Future: *ādariṣyate*, *ādariṣyete*, *ādariṣyante*; *ādariṣyase*, *ādariṣyethe*, *ādariṣyadhve*; *ādariṣye*, *ādariṣyāvahe*, *ādariṣyāmahe*. Conditional: *ādariṣyata*, *ādariṣyetām*, *ādariṣyanta*; *ādariṣyathāḥ*, *ādariṣyethām*, *ādariṣyadhvam*; *ādariṣye*, *ādariṣyāvahi*, *ādariṣyāmahi*. Desiderative (*san*):

Excluding roots ending in *ṛ* or *t*, the form is *ādidariṣate*. Intensive (*yaṅ*): *ādadriyate*. The root *dhṛṅ* is used in the sense of non-stability (*anavasthāna*). Forms such as *hriyate* etc. are to be understood as before. These two roots (*dṛṅ* and *dhṛṅ*) are *aniṭ* (without the augment *iṭ*) and belong to the *ātmanepada* voice.

The root *pracch* is used in the sense of desiring to know (*jñīpsā*). It undergoes *saṃprasāraṇa* (vowel substitution) according to the rule beginning with *grahi* (Pāṇini 6.1.16). Present tense: *pṛcchati*, *apṛcchat*, *pṛcchatu*, *pṛcchet*, *pṛcchyāt*. In the *liṭ* (perfect) tense, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) according to Pāṇini 6.1.17, whether it has already occurred or not. Thus: *papraccha*, *papracchatuḥ*, *papracchuḥ*, *papracchitha*. In the absence of the augment *iṭ*, there is the change of *ṣ* and *ṭ* (due to the rule *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ*), resulting in *papraṣṭha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, there is *vṛddhi* by the rule *vadavraja* (Pāṇini 7.2.3), followed by the changes of *ṣ*, *k*, and *s*: *aprākṣīt*, *aprāṣṭām*, *aprākṣuḥ*. Future tense: *prakṣyati*. Conditional: *aprakṣyat*.

The agent is *praṣṭā*. By the rule *sani rudhvid* (Pāṇini 1.2.8), there is the substitution of *ṣ* and *samprasāraṇa*, resulting in *pipṛṣati*. The passive form is *parīpṛcchyate*. With the prefix *āṅ*, the *ātmanepada* ending is applied according to the rule *āṅi nupṛcchayoḥ upasaṃkhyānam*. With the prefix *sam*, the *ātmanepada* ending is applied by the rule *samogamyṛcchi* (Pāṇini 1.3.29), as in *saṃpṛcchate*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), the form is *saṃprakṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *saṃpapṛcche*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), following the previous rules for *ṣatva* and *katva*, it is *samapṛṣṭa*. The remainder is to be inferred accordingly.

The root *sṛj* [meaning] "to emit" or "to create": *sṛjati*, *asṛjat*, *sṛjatu*, *sṛjatām*, *sṛjet*, *sṛjyāt*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), after *sa-sṛj-a-tha*, since the augment *iṭ* is required by the rule *krādiniyama* (Pāṇini 7.2.13), there is an option for *iṭ* by the rule *vibhāṣā sṛjidṛśoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.65): *sasṛjitha*. In the absence of *iṭ*, there is the substitution of *ṣ* and *ṭ* (by *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ*), and the augment *am*: *asṛṣṭa*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is the augment *iṭ*, and by the rule *vadavraja* (Pāṇini 7.2.3), there is *vṛddhi* and the substitution of *ṣ*: *asrākṣīt*, *asrāṣṭām*, *asrākṣuḥ*. The future is *srakṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *liś* means "to become small. Thus, one says *liśati*, and so forth. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), the forms are *lileśa*, *liliśatuḥ*, *liliśuḥ*, and *lileśitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), the forms are *alikṣat*, *alikṣatām*, and so forth.

The root *ṭumasj* is used in the sense of purification. By the rules for *jaś*-ness and *sat*-ness, we have *majjati*. Imperfect: *amajjat* Imperative: *majjatu* Potential: *majjet*, *majjyāt* Perfect: *mamajja*, *mamajjatuḥ*, *mamajjuḥ*, *mamajjitha* In the absence of the augment *iṭ*, by Pāṇini’s rule *masjinaśorjhali* (7.1.60), the nasal augment *num* is added. According to the statement that *num* occurs before the final letter of *masj* for the purpose of eliding the penultimate (*anuṣaṅga*) and the initial of the conjunct (*saṃyoga*), it occurs between the *s* and the *j*. Following this, there is the elision of the *s* and the rest, and then the application of *kutva*, *anusvāra*, and *parasavarṇa*, resulting in *mamaṅktha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist], the *num* augment and so forth are as before: *amāṅkṣīt*, *amāṅktām*. Before a *jhal* [consonant], there is the elision of *s*: *maṅkṣyati*. *amaṅkṣyat*. *maṅktā*. *mimaṃkṣati*. *māmaṅkṣyate*. *Ruj* in the sense of breaking: *rujati*, *arujat*, *rujatu*, *rujet*, *rujyāt*, *ruroja*, *rurujatuḥ*, *rurujuḥ*, *rurojitha*. In the *luṅ*, there is *vṛddhi*: *arokṣīt*. *rokṣyati*, etc. *Cup* in the sense of touching: *cupati*, etc.

The root *bhuja* means "crookedness," as before. The root *spṛś* means "to touch. [Present tense: *spṛśati*; [Imperfect: *aspṛśat*, and so on. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *pasparśa*, *paspṛśatuḥ*, *paspṛśuḥ*. By the rule regarding roots beginning with *krī* (Pāṇini 7.2.13), the augment *iṭ* is added: *pasparśitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *spṛśimṛśikṛṣeḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.44), there is optionally the suffix *sic*: *aspṛkṣat*. Alternatively, by the rule *anudāttasya cardupadhasya* (Pāṇini 6.1.59), there is optionally the augment *am*: *asprākṣīt* or *aspārkṣīt*. [Future: *sprakṣyati* or *sparkṣyati*. [Aorist: *asprakṣat* or *asparkṣyat*, and so on.

The root *vicch* means "to go. By the rule *che ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.73), there is the augment *tuk*. By the rule *gupūdhūpavicchipaṇi* (Pāṇini 3.1.28), this root takes the suffix *āya*, becoming *vicchāyati*. [Examples: *avicchāyat*, *vicchāyatu*, *vicchāyet*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā* (Pāṇini 3.1.31), the suffix *āya* is optional; thus: *vicchyāt* or *vicchāyyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are]: *vicchāyāñcakāra*, *viviccha*, *vivicchatuḥ*, *vivicchuḥ*, *vivicchitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), [the forms are]: *avicchāyat*, *avicchīt*, and so forth.

The root *viś* means "to enter. It is conjugated as follows: present, *viśati*; imperfect, *aviśat*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it forms *viveśa*, *viviśatuḥ*, *viviśuḥ*, and *viveśitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *cleḥ ksaḥ*, the suffix *ksa* is applied, resulting in *avikṣat*. By the rule *nipūrvāt ner viśaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.17), the Ātmanepada voice is used when preceded by the prefix *ni-*, as in: present, *niviśate*; imperfect, *nyaviśat*; imperative, *niviśatām*; optative, *niviśeta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is optionally *kit*-ness for the suffix, resulting in *nivikṣīṣṭa*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it becomes *nyavikṣata*, and so forth; in the future, *nivekṣyate*, etc.

The root *mṛś* (meaning "to touch" or "to consider") forms its conjugations as follows: *vimṛśati*, *vyamṛśat*, *vimṛśatu*, *vimṛśet*, *vimṛśyāt*, *vimamarśa*, *vimamṛśatuḥ*, *vimamṛśuḥ*, *vimamarśitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, the grammatical operations are like those of the root *spṛś*: *amṛkṣat*, *amrākṣīt*, *amārkṣīt*; and in the future, *mrakṣyati*, *markṣyati*, and so forth.
[Excluding *vicchi*, these roots are *aniṭ* (without the *iṭ* augment) and belong to the *parasmaipada* (active voice).]

The root *muc* is used in the sense of "releasing. For the twenty roots beginning with *muc*, the augment *num* is applied according to Pāṇini’s sūtra 7.1.59 (*śe mucādīnām*), resulting in the forms *muñcati* (present), *amuñcat* (imperfect), *muñcatu* (imperative), *muñcet* (optative), and *muñcyāt* (precative). In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), we have *mumoca*, *mumucatuḥ*, *mumucuḥ*, and *mumocitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), because the root is marked with the *ḷ*-sign (*ḷdit*), the suffix *aṅ* is applied, yielding *amucat*. The future form is *mokṣyati*, and so forth. Because the root is marked with the *svarita* accent, it takes the middle voice (*ātmanepada*), as in *muñcate* and *amuñcata*. In the precative (*āśīr-liṅ*) of the middle voice, the suffix is *kit*, resulting in *mukṣīṣṭa*. The perfect middle form is *mumuce*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, by the rule *luṅi jhalo jhali* (Pāṇini 8.2.26), there is the elision of the suffix *sic*; thus: *amukta*, *amukṣātām*, *amukṣata*. In forms such as *mokṣyata*, and so forth. In the *san* [desiderative] when the agent is also the object (*karmakartṛ*) and the verb is intransitive (*akarmaka*), there is optionally the substitution of *guṇa*; thus, with *guṇa* and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsa-lopa*), we have *mumokṣate* or *mumukṣate* "the calf releases itself. The root *luplṛ* means "to cut" or "to break. Present: *lumpati* Aorist: *alumpat* Imperative: *lumpatu* Optative: *lumpet* Precative: *lupyāt* Perfect (*liṭ*): *lulopa* By virtue of being marked with the *ṛdit* designation, the *aṅ* augment is applied; thus: *alupat* Future: *lopsyati*, and so forth. In the middle voice (*ātmanepada*): *lumpate*, *alumpata*, and so forth.

The root *vid* is used in the sense of "to obtain. Present: *vindati* (he obtains). Imperfect: *avindata* (he obtained). Imperative: *vindatu* (let him obtain). Optative: *vindet* (he may obtain). Precative: *vidyāt* (may he obtain). Perfect: *viveda* (he obtained); *vividatuḥ* (the two of them obtained); *vividuḥ* (they all obtained); *viveditha* (you obtained). Aorist (*luṅ*): *avidat* (he obtained). Future: *vetsyati*, etc. Middle voice (*ātmanepada*): *vindate* (he obtains for himself); *avindata*, etc.

The root *lip* (to smear). Present: *limpati*, *alimpat*, *limpatu*, *limpet*, *lipyāt*. Perfect: *lilepa*, *lilipatuḥ*, *lilipuḥ*, *lilepitha*. Aorist (*luṅ*): By the rule *lipi sici hvaśca* (Pāṇini 3.1.53), *cl-* is replaced by *aṅ*; thus, *alipat*. Future: *lepsyati*, etc. Middle voice (*ātmanepada*): *limpate*, *alimpata*, etc. In the aorist (*luṅ*), by the rule *ātmanepadeṣvanyatarasyām* (Pāṇini 3.1.54), there is an option for *cl-* to be replaced by *aṅ*; thus, *alipta* or *alipata*.

The root *ṣic* means "to sprinkle. Present: *siñcati* (he sprinkles). Imperfect: *asiñcat* (he sprinkled). Imperative: *siñcatu* (let him sprinkle). Optative: *siñcet* (he may sprinkle). Aorist: *sicyāt* (may he be sprinkled). By the rule *upasargāt* (Pāṇini 8.3.65), there is the substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*]: *abhiṣicyāt* (may he be sprinkled over). Perfect: *abhiṣiṣeca* (he sprinkled over). By the rule *aḍabhyāsavyavāye’pi* (Pāṇini 8.3.64), there is the substitution of *ṣ* even when separated by the augment *aṭ* or the reduplication: *abhyaṣicat* (he sprinkled over). Future: *abhiṣekṣyati* (he will sprinkle over). Conditional: *abhyaṣekṣyat* (he would have sprinkled over). Periphrastic future: *abhiṣektā* (he will sprinkle over). By the restrictive rule *stautiṇyoreva* (Pāṇini 8.3.61), there is no substitution of *ṣ* for the letter following the reduplication: *sisikṣati* (he desires to sprinkle). In the intensive (*yaṅ*), by the rule *sico yaṅi* (Pāṇini 8.3.112), there is a prohibition of the substitution of *ṣ*:
*sesicyate* (it is sprinkled repeatedly). Middle voice: *siñcate*. Imperfect: *asiñcata*, etc. Everything is like the case of the root *lip*.
The roots that are taught as being both [vowel-initial and consonant-initial] are aniṭ.

The root *kṛt* (meaning "to cut") is conjugated as follows: Present: *kṛntati* Imperfect: *akṛntat* Imperative: *kṛntatu* Optative: *kṛntet* Precative: *kṛtyāt* Periphrastic Perfect: *cakarta*, *cakṛtatuḥ*, *cakṛtuḥ*, *cakartitha* Aorist (*luṅ*): *akartīt* (the optional absence of *iṭ* is according to Pāṇini 7.2.57, *syasijikṛta*), resulting in forms such as *kartsyati* or *kartiṣyati*.

The root *khid* (meaning "to strike" or "to afflict") is conjugated as follows: Present: *khidati* Imperfect: *akhidat* Imperative: *khidatu* Optative: *khidet* Precative: *khidyāt* Perfect: *cikheda*, *cikhidatuḥ*, *cikhiduḥ*, *cikheditha* Aorist (*luṅ*): *akhaitsīt*, *akhaittām*, *akhaitsuḥ* (vṛddhi by the rule for *sic* after a consonant-final root, and *cartva*). Future: *khetsyati*, etc.

The root *piś* means "to form" or "to shape. Present: *piśati*. Aorist: *apiśat*. Imperative: *tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piśatu* ("May Tvaṣṭṛ fashion forms"). Optative: *piśet*. Benedictive: *piśyāt*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *pipeśa*, *pipiśatuḥ*, *pipiśuḥ*; *pipeśitha*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *apeśīt*, *apeśiṣṭām*, *apeśiṣuḥ*. Future: *peśiṣyati*. Conditional: *apeśiṣyat*. Periphrastic future: *peśitā*. Regarding the reduplication, there is an option for the *kit* suffix by Pāṇini 1.2.26 (*ralovyupadhāt*), resulting in *pipiśiṣati* or *pipeśiṣati*. Middle voice: *pepiśyate*. Regarding the rule for the insertion of the nasal augment (*nuṃ*) in the *śam* class and others, it is said: "Roots *muc*, *lup*, *lip*, *pī* in the sense of 'attainment', *vid* with *sic*, *kṛtī*, and *vidhi*;
*khid*, *śiṣ*, and *ṛṣ*—these are to be known as the *śam* group for the application of the *nuṃ* augment."
Thus ends the section on the *śavikaraṇa* roots beginning with *tud* in the *Śābdikābharaṇa*, composed by the yogi Hari, the teacher Prolla.

Now begins the section on the *rudh*-class roots. The root *rudh* means "to obstruct. According to Pāṇini’s sūtra 3.1.78, *śnam* is added after roots of the *rudh*-class; this is an exception (*apavāda*) to *śap*. When a *sārvadhātuka* suffix follows, the letter *ś* [in *śnam*] is for the purpose of specification by the rule 6.4.111 (*śnasorallopaḥ*). By 8.4.1 (*raṣābhyām*), there is the substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*]. By 8.2.40 (*jhaṣastathordho'dhaḥ*), there is the substitution of *dh* [for *th*]. By 8.4.47 (*anaci ca*), there is doubling [of the consonant]. By 8.4.53 (*jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi*), there is the substitution of *jaś* [sounds]. By 8.4.65 (*jharo jhari savarṇe*), [the first *dh* is optionally elided].

Thus, by the rule *halo'nantarāḥ saṃyogaḥ*, there is the elision (*lopa*) of the letter *d* following the consonant *l*. By the rule *sārvadhātuke kṅiti śnasorallopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.111), there is the elision of the vowel *a*. Following this, the *anusvāra* and its subsequent *parasavarṇa* [become *ṃ*]. The remainder is as before: *rundhaḥ*, *rundhanti*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect) tense: after the elision of *ti* and *sip* by the rule *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal* (Pāṇini 6.1.68), and after the substitution of the *jaś* sound [to *d*], the rule *vā'vasāne* (Pāṇini 8.4.56) applies the *car* substitution [of *t* to *ṭ*]: *aruṇat*. In the case of *sip*: after the *jaś* substitution, the rules *sipi dhātorurvā* (Pāṇini 8.2.74) and *daśca* (Pāṇini 8.2.75) apply the substitution of *ru* [for *s*]: *aruṇaḥ*.

*aruṇat*. *aruṇam*. In the *loṭ* [imperative]: *ruṇaddhu*, *rundhāt*, *rundhām*, *rundhantu*. In the *liṅ* [optative]: *rundhyāt*, *rundhyātām*, *rundhyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *rudhyāt*, *rudhyāstām*. In the *liṭ* [perfect]: *rurodha*, *rurudhatuḥ*, *rurudhuḥ*, *rurodhitha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], by the rule *irito vā* (Pāṇini 3.1.57), there is optionally *aṅ* for the *cl* suffix: *arudhat*; otherwise, *arautsīt*. Future: *arotsyat*. Periphrastic future: *roddhā*. Desiderative: *rurutsati*. Intensive: *rorudhyate*. In the present middle voice, the substitution of *e* for *at* and the elision of the *a* of the suffix, etc., yield: *rundhe*, *rundhāte*, *rundhate*. Imperfect middle: *arundha*.

*arundhātām*, *arundhata*; *rundhām*, *rundhātām*, *rundhatām*. In the *liṅ* (optative), with the augment *sīyuṭ* and the elision of *s*, [we have] *rutsīta*, *rutsīyātām*, *rutsīran*. In the *āśis* (benedictive) *liṅ*, due to *kit* status and the change of *t* to *ṣ*, [we have] *rutsīṣṭa*, *rutsīyāstām*, *rutsīran*. In the *liṭ* (perfect), [we have] *rurudhe*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), due to the *kit* status of *sic* and by Pāṇini 8.2.26 (*jhalo jhali*), there is the elision of *sic*: *arundha*, *arundhātām*, *arundhata*, and so forth.

The root *bhid* is used in the sense of "cleaving. Present tense: *bhinatti*, *bhintaḥ*, *bhindanti*. Aorist: *abhinat*, *abhintām*, *abhindan*; with the suffix *sip*, by Pāṇini 8.2.75 (*sipi daśca*), there is *ru*-substitution: *abhinaḥ*. Imperative: *bhinattu*, *bhindāt*, *bhintām*, *bhindantu*. Optative: *bhindyāt*, *bhindyātām*, *bhindyuḥ*. Benedictive: *bhidyāt*, *bhidyāstām*, *bhidyāsuḥ*. Perfect: *bibheda*, *bibhidatuḥ*, *bibhiduḥ*, *bibhetha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by Pāṇini 3.1.57 (*irito vā*), there is the suffix *aṅ*: *abhinat*; alternatively, *abhaitsīt*.

*bhetsyati* and so forth: *bhinte*, *bhindāte*, *abhinta*, *abhindātām*, *abhindata*; *bhintām*, *bhindātām*, *bhindatām*; *bhindīta*, *bhindīyātām*, *bhindīran*; in the precative (*āśiṣi*), *bhitsīṣṭa*; *bibhide*; *abhitt*; *bhetsyate*; *abhetsyata*, and so forth. The root *chid* (to split) follows the same pattern as before.

The root *ric* is used in the sense of "purging" (*virecana*). It purges itself; it purges the sacrificer (*yajamāna*). [In the present indicative: *riṇakti*, *riṅktaḥ* (with elision of the nasal, anusvāra, and *parasavarṇa*), *riñcanti*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *ariṇak*, *ariṇag*, *ariṅktām*, *ariñcan*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *riṇaktu*, *riṅktād* or *riṅktām*, *riñcantu*. In the *liṅ* (optative): *riñcyāt*, *riñcyātām*, *riñcyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśis*): *ricyāt*, *ricyāstām*, *ricyāsuḥ*. [Perfect: *rireca*, *riricatuḥ*, *riricuḥ*; *recitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *aricat*, *arekṣīt*; *rekṣyati*, etc. [In the middle voice: *riṅkte*, *riñcāte*, *riñcate*. *Ariṅkta*; the remainder is to be inferred. The root *vic* is used in the sense of "separation" (*pṛthagbhāva*).

The root *kṣudir* means "to crush" (*saṃpeṣaṇe*). Present tense: *kṣuṇatti*, *akṣuṇat*, *kṣuṇattu*, *kṣuntām*, *kṣudyāt*. Periphrastic perfect: *cukṣoda*, *cukṣudatuḥ*, *cukṣuduḥ*, *cukṣoditha*. In the periphrastic future (*luṭ*), there is optionally *ah*: *akṣudat* or *akṣotsīt*. Future: *kṣautsyati*. Conditional: *akṣotsyat*. Periphrastic future: *kṣottā*. Desiderative: *cukṣutsati*. Passive: *cokṣudyate*. [By the rule *allopaḥ ṭeḥ*, the elision of the final vowel of the suffix is applied. Present (ātmanepada): *kṣunte*, *akṣunta*, *kṣuntām*, *kṣundīta*, *kṣuntsīṣṭa*. Perfect (ātmanepada): *cukṣude*. Aorist (ātmanepada): *akṣunta*, *kṣotsyate*, *akṣotsyata*, and so forth.

Regarding the root *yuj* in the sense of "joining" (*yoge*): according to Pāṇini’s rule *propābhyāṃ yujeḥ* (1.3.64) and others, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used for the root *yuj*—provided it does not refer to sacrificial vessels (*yajñapātra*)—when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent (*akartrabhiprāya*). However, when the fruit does accrue to the agent (*kartrabhiprāya*), the general rule applies the *taṅ* suffixes (middle endings). In this case, because [the subject] is considered "remaining" (*śeṣatvāt*), the active voice (*parasmaipada*) is used; in both instances, it is the same as the previous case.

The root *utṛdir* is used in the senses of injury and disregard. The verbal root (*dhātu*) is placed between the two suffixes (*anubandha*). The *laṭ* and other suffixes are as before. [In the sense of] "he injures thoroughly," it is thus: *abhitṛṇatti*. [Aorist: *abhyaivena atṛṇat*. [Present optative: *tṛṇattu*, *tṛdyāt*. [Perfect: *tatarda*, *tatṛdatuḥ*, *tatarditha*. [Aorist (*luṅ*): *atṛdat*. [Precative (*liṅ*): *atardīta*. By the rule *sesici* (Pāṇini 7.2.57), the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied: [Future: *tartsyati*, *tardiṣyati*. [Conditional: *atartsyat*, *atardiṣyat*. [Periphrastic future: *tarditā*. [Desiderative: *titṛtsati*. [Passive: *tarītṛdyate*. The formation of forms in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) follows the same pattern as the preceding [root] due to the nasal (*anusvāra*). The root *ucchṛdir* is used in the senses of shining and playing. Everything is as before.
With the exception of *tṛd* and *dṛd*, those that do not take the augment *iṭ* are of both voices (*ubhayatobhāṣā*).

The root *kṛt* (meaning "to cut") is conjugated as follows: Present: *kṛṇatti*, *kṛntaḥ*, *kṛntanti*. Imperfect: *akṛṇat*. Imperative: *kṛṇattu*. Optative: *kṛtyāt*. Perfect: *cakarta*, *cakṛtatuḥ*, *cakṛtuḥ*; *cakartitha*. Aorist: *akartīt*. In the Causative (*ṇic*), with the suffix *caṅ*, it becomes *acīkṛtat* or *acakartat*. In the Future, after a suffix beginning with *s* other than *sic*, there is an optional *iṭ* augment as before: *kartsyati*. Conditional: *akartsyat* or *akartiṣyat*. Periphrastic Future: *kartitā*. Desiderative: *cikṛtsati* or *cikartiṣati*. These roots are *seṭ* (having an indicatory *iṭ*) and are Parasmaipada (active voice).

The root *indh* means "to shine" or "to kindle. By Pāṇini’s rule 6.4.111 (*śnānnalopaḥ śnasorallopaśca*), there is elision of the *n* of the suffix *śnā*, and elision of the *a* of the suffixes *śna* and *śnu*. The final *ṭi* (the *i*) undergoes *etva* (change to *e*), the *t* becomes *dh*, and the *dh* becomes *j* (by the rule of *jastvam*). Thus, we have *indhe*. In the third person plural, *samindhate* ("the young women kindle"). In the imperfect (*laṅ*), we have *aindhata*, *aindhatām*, and *aindhan*. In the imperative (*loṭ*), *indhātām* and *indhatām*. In the potential (*liṅ*), *indhīta*, *indhīyātām*, and *indhīran*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), *indhiṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it becomes *indhibhavati*.

Due to the *kit* designation, there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika*). In the phrase "may he kindle, O best slayer of enemies," the form *samīdhet* occurs not only in the Vedic language (*chandas*) but also in the common language (*bhāṣā*). [Objection: But in the common language, since the root belongs to the *indādi* group, why does the augment *ām* not occur? [Response: Because the rule prescribing the *kit* designation applies specifically to the root *indh*.

If this usage were restricted solely to the Vedic language (*chandas*), the prescription of *kit* status for the *liṭ* affix following the root *indh* would be fruitless; for, by the rule "the *liṭ* is optionally [treated as] both" (*liṭ chandasyubhayathā*), the *liṭ* receives the designation of a *sārvadhātuka*, and by the rule "a *sārvadhātuka* ending in *ap* is *ṅit*" (*sārvadhātukam apit*), the desired result would be achieved simply through its *ṅit* status. Indeed, we perceive no difference between *kit* and *ṅit* status regarding the operations of the vowel *iṭ*. Therefore, the usage *samīdhata* is also appropriate in the spoken language (*bhāṣā*). In the *luṅ* tense: *aidhiṣṭa*; in the *caṅ* (reduplication) of the causative (*ṇic*): *aididhata*; and so forth, such as *aindhiṣyata*.

*Khid* [means] distress or dejection. *Khinte*. *Akhintet*, etc. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), the *liṭ* [affixes] have the *kit* designation; thus, *khitsīṣṭa*. In the *liṭ* [perfect], *cikhide*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], the *sic* [augment] has the *kit* designation, and there is elision of the *s* when followed by a *jhal* [consonant]; thus, *akhitta*. *Khetsyati*, etc. *Vid* [means] deliberation; it is treated as before. [All roots] except *indh* are *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment) and are *ātmanebhāṣā* (middle-voice).

The root *śiṣlṛ* means "to distinguish. It undergoes *ṣṭutva* [becoming *śiṣṭ*]. It is distinguished by the elision of the *al* [the *ś*] and the *anusvāra*. They distinguish (*viśiṃṣanti*). With *katva* and *ṣatva*, it becomes *viśinakṣi*. In the *laṅ* [past tense], *vyaśinaṭ*, *vyaśiṃṣṭām*, *vyaśiṃṣat*. Again, *vyaśinaṭ*. In the *loṭ* [imperative], *viśinaṣṭu* or *viśiṃṣṭāt*, *viśiṃṣṭām*, *viśiṃṣantu*.

By *serhiḥ*, there is elision of *a* (*allopaḥ*). By *herdhibhāvaḥ*, *dh* replaces *hi*. By *ṣṭutvaṃ*, *ṣ* is substituted for *s*. By *jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi* (Pāṇini 8.4.53), there is the substitution of a *jaś* sound; thus, *ḍ* replaces *t*. By *jharo jhari savarṇe* (Pāṇini 8.4.65), there is optionally the elision of that [ḍ]. Since the elision of *a* (*allopasya*) is prohibited by the rule *padāntetyādinā* due to its status as *sthānivadbhāva*, the *anusvāra* and *parasavarṇa* substitutions apply to the *n*. Thus: *viśiṃṣyāt* in the sense of benediction (*āśiṣi*), and *viśiṣyāt* otherwise. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *viśiśeṣa*, *viśiśiṣatuḥ*, *viśiśiṣuḥ*, *viśiśeṣitha*. In the conditional (*lṛṅ*), because it is marked with *lṛṅ*, *aṅ* is applied:
*vyaśiśiṣat*. [The future form is] *viśekṣyati*, and so forth. The root *piṣlṛ* means "to crush. It is treated as before.

The root *bhañj* is used in the sense of "breaking" (*āmardane*). By *śnānna-lopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.23), there is the elision of the nasal (*n*) after the affix *śnā*. By *śnasor allopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.111), there is the elision of the vowel *a* of the root before the affixes *śna* and *śnu*. Thus: *bhakti*, *bhaṅktaḥ*, *bhañjanti*. In the imperfect (*laṅ*): *abhanak*. In the imperative (*loṭ*): *bhaṅktād vā*, *bhaṅktām*, *bhañjantu*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), there is the elision of the nasal (*n*): *bhajyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *babhañja*, *babhañjatuḥ*, *babhañjuḥ*, *babhañjitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), there is the substitution of *k* for the final consonant (*kutva*), followed by the homogeneous nasal (*parasavarṇa*), and then the substitution of *ṣ* (*ṣatva*): *abhāṅkṣīt*. When a *jhal*-ending affix follows, there is the elision of *s*: *abhāṅktām*, *abhāṅkṣuḥ*.

*abhāṅkṣīḥ*. With the suffix *ṇau* and the *caṅ* augment, [the form is] *ababhañjat*. *Bhaṅkṣyati*, and so forth. In the *yaṅ* [intensive], by the rule *japajabha-* (Pāṇini 7.4.86), there is the insertion of *nuk* after the reduplication, resulting in *baṃbhakṣyate*.

The root *bhuj* is used in the senses of "protecting" (*pālana*) and "eating" (*abhyavahāra*). According to the rule *bhujo'navane* (Pāṇini 1.3.66), the *parasmaipada* (active voice) ending is used for "protecting"; thus, *bhunakti*. In examples such as *bhuvaṃ nṛpaḥ* ("the king protects the earth"), the forms are as previously described. In the *liṭ* (perfect tense): *bubhoja*, *bubhujatuḥ*, *bubhujuḥ*, *bubhojitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist): *abhokṣīt*. In the future: *bhokṣyati*, etc. In the *yaṅ* (intensive): *bobhujyate*. In senses other than protecting, by the rule *bhujo'navane* (Pāṇini 1.3.66), the *ātmanepada* (middle voice) ending is used. Following the elision of the penultimate vowel (*allopā*), the substitution of *anusvāra*, and the subsequent *parasavarṇa* change, we have: *bhuṅkte*, *bhuñjāte*, *bhuñjate*.

[The forms] *bhuṅkṣe* [are derived through] elision (*allop*), anusvāra, *parasavarṇa*, and *ṣatva*. In the *laṅ* [mood], *abhuṅkta*; in the *loṭ*, *bhuṅktām*; in the optative (*liṅ*), *bhuñjīta*; in the benedictive (*āśis*), *bhukṣīṣṭa*; in the perfect (*liṭ*), *bubhuje*; in the aorist (*luṅ*), due to the *kit* status of *sic* and the elision of *s*, *abhukta*; and in the conditional (*lṛṅ*), *abhokṣyat*, and so forth.

The roots *tṛh* and *hiṃs* mean "to injure. For the root *tṛh*, when followed by a *pit* sārvadhātuka suffix beginning with a consonant (*hal*), the augment *im* is added to the stem by the rule *tṛhaṇahaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.92). Then, by the rule *ādguṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.87), *guṇa* substitution occurs. By the rule *ho ḍhaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.31), *ha* becomes *ḍha*; then *ḍha* becomes *dha*, *ṭha* becomes *ṭa*, and finally *ḍha* is elided (*ḍhalopa*)—these operations apply in sequence to form *tṛṇeḍhi*. In the present tense (*laṭ*): *tṛṇḍhaḥ* (third person dual); *tṛṃhanti* (third person plural). In the case of the third person singular ending *ti* and the second person singular ending *si*, there is elision of the suffix by the rule *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal* (Pāṇini 6.1.68). Due to the presence of the suffix as a formal cause (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*), the augment *im* is applied. Then, by *ho ḍhaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.31), *ha* becomes *ḍha*; by *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ* (Pāṇini 8.4.41), *ḍha* becomes *ṭha*; and by *ṭhūlope pūrvasya dīrgho'ṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.3.111), the preceding vowel is lengthened, resulting in *atṛṇeṭ* (third person singular imperfect). For the dual and plural: *atṛṇḍhām* (third person dual); *atṛhan* (third person plural).

In the imperative (*loṭ*), [the forms are] *tṛṇedu*, *tṛṇḍhāt*, *tṛṇḍhām*, and *tṛṇhantu*. In the second person singular (*madhyamaikavacana*), *si* is replaced by *hi*; because that is considered as if non-existent (*apit*), there is the augment *ṭuk*. As before, due to the elision of *a* (*allopaḥ*) and the substitution of *ḍha*, etc., [the form is] *tṛṇeḍhi*. In the potential (*liṅ*), due to the elision of *a*, it is *tṛhyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *tatarha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *atarhīt*. [The conditional is] *atarhiṣyat*, and so forth.

The root *hiṃs* is used in the sense of injury. Because it is marked with the *it*-indicator *i*, the augment *nuṃ* is applied; by the rule *śnānnalopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.23), there is the elision of the *n* of the suffix *śna*. Thus, *hinasti*. By the rule *śnasorallopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.111), there is the elision of the vowel *a* of the suffixes *śna* and *as*. Thus, *hiṃstaḥ*; *hiṃsanti*. In the *liṅ* (optative) mood, by the rule *tipsiporhalṅyādilopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.68), there is the elision of the suffixes *tip* and *sip*. In the case of *tip*, by the rule *tipyanasteḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.73), there is the substitution of *d* for *t*, followed by *cartva* (the substitution of *c* for *t*). Thus, *ahinat*. [In the plural], *ahiṃstām*; *ahiṃsan*. In the case of *mip* and *sip*, by the rule *dhātorveti* (Pāṇini 8.2.75), there is the substitution of *d* for *t*, and subsequently *utva* (the substitution of *u* for *t*), resulting in *ahinatvam* for *ahiṃsanasya*. In the *loṭ* (imperative) mood: *hinastu* or *hiṃstāt*; *hiṃstām*; *hiṃsantu*.

In the second person singular, there is the substitution of *dhi* for *hi*; then by *allopaḥ* and *jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi* (Pāṇini 8.4.53), the *jaś*-ness of the *s* results in *d*. The remainder is as before. In the *liṅ* [optative]: *hiṃsyāt*, *hiṃsyātām*. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*): *hiṃsyāt*, *hiṃsyāstām*. In the *liṭ* [perfect]: *jihiṃsa*. In the *luṅ* [aorist]: *ahiṃsīt*, *ahiṃsiṣṭām*, and so forth.

The root *und* means "to moisten. By the rule *śnānnalopaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.23), there is elision of the *n*; by the rule of *cutva*, it becomes *unakti*. In the sense of "the earth moistens with the rain of Yavana," it is *bhūmiḥ yavanavṛṣṭibhūḥ unakti*. By the rule *allopo 'naḥ*, [the *a* of the suffix] is elided: *undanti*. In the present tense (*laṭ*), [the forms are] *samudraḥ kacit oṣunat*, *autām*, *undan*. In the *sic* [augment], there is *utva*: *unattu*, *untād vā*, *untām*, *undantu*. [In the optative: *udyāt*, *udyātām*, *udyuḥ*; *udyāt*, *udyāstām*, *udyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *udāñcakāra*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *audīt*, *audiṣṭām*, *audiṣuḥ*. In the causative with the *caṅ* [reduplication], *audidat*. [In the future, etc.: *undiṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *añj* is used in the senses of manifesting, distinguishing, and going. Present tense (*laṭ*): - Singular: *anakti*, *anaktaḥ*, *añjanti* - Plural: [Included above] Imperfect (*laṅ*): - Singular: *ānak* - Dual: *āṅktām* - Plural: *āñjan* Imperative (*loṭ*): - Singular: *anaktu* or *aṅktād* - Dual: *aṅktām* - Plural: *añjantu* Optative (*liṅ*): - Singular: *añjyāt* - Dual: *añjyātām* - Plural: *añjyuḥ* Benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): Due to the elision of the nasal (*nalopaḥ*), it becomes: *ajyāt*, *ajyāstām*, *ajyāsuḥ*. Perfect (*liṭ*): By the rule *tasmānnuḍdvihalaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.71), the augment *nuṭ* is added: *ānañja*, *ānañjatuḥ*, *ānañjuḥ*. Because the root is marked with *u* (*udit*), the augment *iṭ* is optional: *ānañjitha*, *ānañjathuḥ*.

Likewise, for the roots *vas* and *mās*, in the *luṅ* tense, the augment *iṭ* is obligatory by the rule *añjeḥ sici* (Pāṇini 7.2.71); thus: *āñjīt*, *āñjiṣṭām*, *āñjiṣuḥ*; *āñjiṣyati*, *āṅkṣyati*, and so forth. By the rule *smipūṅrañjaśāṃ sani* (Pāṇini 7.2.74), the augment *iṭ* is also obligatory in the *san* suffix; thus: *añjijiṣati*. The root *tañjū* means "to contract";
*ovijī* means "fear" and "trembling."
The root *vṛj* means "to avoid"; *pṛc* means "to join together. [Examples: *tanaṅkti*, *vinaṅkti*, *vṛṇakti*.
All roots beginning with *śiṣ* and ending with *bhuj*—that is, up to and including *bhuj*—are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*) and are all *parasmaipada* (active voice).
Thus ends the section on the *rudh*-class roots with the *śnam* affix in the *Śābdikābharaṇa*, composed by the master Hariyogin. Now begins the section on the *tan*-class roots.

The root *tan* means "to expand. By the rule *tanādikṛñbhya uḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.79), the suffix *u* is applied; this supersedes the *śap* suffix. In a *sārvadhātuka* affix, there is *guṇa* substitution: *tanoti*. Because the suffix is marked with *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa*: *tanutaḥ*. By the rule *iko yaṇaci* (Pāṇini 6.1.77), there is the *yaṇ* substitute: *tanvanti*. Imperfect (*laṅ*): *atanot*. Imperative (*loṭ*): *tanotu*. Optative (*liṅ*): *tanuyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *tanyāt*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *tatāna*. In the perfect, when a kit suffix follows, by the rule *ata ekahalmadhye* (Pāṇini 6.4.120) and others, the following forms arise: *tenatuḥ*, *tenuḥ*, *tenitha*, and *tatantha*.

In the *nigama* (Vedic), from the root *tan* (to stretch): *atanīt*, *atānīt*; *taniṣyati*; *ataniṣyat*; *tanitā*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), there is an option for the augment *iṭ* by the rule *sani paṭi-daridrāṇām* (Pāṇini 7.2.49). Thus, with *iṭ*: *titaniṣati*. In the absence of *iṭ*, under the heading of *aj-jhan-gamāṃ sani* (Pāṇini 6.4.16), there is an option for lengthening by the rule *tanoter vibhāṣā* (Pāṇini 6.4.17): *titāṃsati* or *titaṃsati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), there is the augment *nuṭ* by the rule *nug ato 'nunāsikāntasya* (Pāṇini 7.4.85): *taṃtanyate*. By the rule *ṭer etvam* (Pāṇini 3.4.79), the final vowel becomes *e*: *tanute*. [Imperfect forms: *atanuta*; *atanutam*.

By the rule *liṅaḥ salopo’nantyasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.79), there is the elision of the *sakāra* of the *sīyuṭ* suffix; then the *yaṇ* substitution [of *i* for *y*] occurs: *tanvīta*, *tanvīyātām*. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), [the form is] *taniṣīṣṭa*. [In the perfect tense: *tene*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), *ataniṣṭa*. By the rule *tanādibhyastathāsoḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.79), there is the elision of *sic*; optionally, by the rule *anudāttopadeśa* (Pāṇini 6.4.37), there is the elision of the nasal: *atata*, *ataniṣātām*, *ataniṣata*, *atathāḥ*, *ataniṣṭhāḥ*.

From here until the end of the section on *agaṇa*, one should apply the rule for the elision of *siC* after [roots] beginning with *tam* and *tathā* when followed by *tathāso*; furthermore, the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika*) should be understood there as appropriate, and so forth, as previously explained.

The root *ṣaṇ* means "to give. The change to *ṣa* is the removal of the *ṇ*. In forms such as *sanoti*, it is as explained previously. By the rule *sanimīmā-* (Pāṇini 7.4.54), there is an option for the augment *iṭ*: thus *sisaniṣati*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.42), there is the substitution of *ā* [for the penultimate vowel]; and because the restriction of the rule *stautiṇyoreva* (Pāṇini 8.3.61) does not apply here, the rule *iṇkoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.57) effects the change to *ṣ*, resulting in *siṣāsati*. By the rule *somādyāṭiyaṅbhāṣā* (Pāṇini 7.4.55), there is the substitution of *ā*, resulting in *sāsāyate*. In the absence of this *ā*-substitution, there is the insertion of *nuk* after the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *saṃsanyate*.

Likewise, *sanute*; *asanuta* and so forth. In the *luṅ* [aorist], by the rule *tanādibhyastathāsoḥ* (Pāṇini 2.4.79), there is optionally the elision (*luk*) of *sic*. By the rule *janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.42), there is the obligatory substitution of *ā* [for the root vowel]. In the absence of the elision of *sic*, [the forms are] *asāniṣṭa*, *asaniṣātām*, *asaniṣata*, *asāthāḥ*, *asaniṣṭhāḥ*.

The root *kṣi* is used in the sense of "to destroy" (*hiṃsā*). **Parasmaipada (Active Voice):** Present: *kṣiṇoti* Imperfect: *akṣiṇot* Imperative: *kṣiṇotu* Potential: *kṣiṇuyāt* Precative: *kṣiṇyāt* Periphrastic Perfect (*liṭ*): *cikṣeṇa*, *cikṣiṇatuḥ*, *cikṣiṇuḥ*, *cikṣeṇitha*, etc. **Ātmanepada (Middle Voice):** Present: *kṣiṇute* Imperfect: *akṣiṇuta* Imperative: *kṣiṇutām* Potential: *kṣiṇvīta*, etc. Aorist (*luṅ*): Due to the elision of the nasal (*anunāsikalopa*) after the suffix *sic*, [the forms are] *akṣiṇita*, *akṣeṇiṣṭa*, *akṣithāḥ*, *akṣeṇiṣṭhāḥ*. Periphrastic Perfect (*liṭ*): *cakṣaṇa*, *cakṣaṇatuḥ*, *cakṣaṇuḥ*, *cakṣaṇitha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist] tense, there is a prohibition of *vṛddhi* by the rule *luṭi hmyantakṣaṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.5), as in *kṣaṇiṣyati*, and so forth. [Present tense: *kṣaṇute*; [Imperfect: *akṣaṇuta*; [Imperative: *kṣaṇutām*; [Optative: *kṣaṇvīta*; [Benedictive: *kṣaṇiṣīṣṭa*. [In the sense of "one who discerns" (*vicakṣaṇe*): In the *luṅ* [aorist], [the forms are] *akṣaṇiṣṭa*, *akṣaṇiṣātām*, *akṣaṇiṣata*, *akṣathāḥ*, *akṣaṇiṣṭhāḥ*, and so forth.

The root *ṛ* means "to go. Present: *ṛṇoti*, *ṛṇutaḥ*, *ṛṇvanti*; *ṛṇoṣi*, *ṛṇuthaḥ*, *ṛṇutha*; *ṛṇomi*, *ṛṇuvaḥ*, *ṛṇumaḥ*. Imperfect: *ānarṇot*, *ānarṇutām*, *ānarṇuḥ*; *ānarṇoḥ*, *ānarṇutam*, *ānarṇuta*; *ānarṇavam*, *ānarṇuva*, *ānarṇuma*. Optative: *ṛṇuyāt*, *ṛṇuyātām*, *ṛṇuyuḥ*; *ṛṇuyāḥ*, *ṛṇuyātam*, *ṛṇuyāta*; *ṛṇuyām*, *ṛṇuyāva*, *ṛṇuyāma*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *ata ādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.70), there is lengthening of the initial vowel; then, by the rule *tasmānnuḍ dvihalaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.71), the augment *nuṭ* is added: *ārṇyāt*, *ārṇyāstām*, etc. Aorist (*luṅ*): *ānarṇīt*, *ānṛṇiṣṭām*, *ānṛṇiṣuḥ*; *ānarṇīḥ*, *ānṛṇiṣṭam*, *ānṛṇiṣṭa*; *ānarṇiṣam*, *ānṛṇiṣva*, *ānṛṇiṣma*. [Note: In the third person singular, the guṇa of the light penultimate vowel does not apply due to the prohibition *mā bhavānārṇīt* and similar forms. Middle voice (*ātmanepada*): Present—*arṇute*, *arṇvāte*, *arṇvate*; *arṇuṣe*, *arṇvāthe*, *arṇudhve*; *arṇve*, *arṇuvahe*, *arṇumahe*. Imperfect—*ārṇuta*, *ārṇetām*, *ārṇanta*; *ārṇuthāḥ*, *ārṇethām*, *ārṇudhvam*; *ārṇe*, *ārṇuvahi*, *ārṇumahi*. Optative—*arṇvīta*, *arṇvīyātām*, *arṇvīran*; *arṇvīthāḥ*, *arṇvīyāthām*, *arṇvīdhvam*; *arṇvīya*, *arṇvīvahi*, *arṇvīmahi*. Benedictive—*ārṇiṣīṣṭa*, *ārṇiṣīyāstām*, *ārṇiṣīran*; *ārṇiṣīṣṭhāḥ*, *ārṇiṣīyāsthām*, *ārṇiṣīdhvam*; *ārṇiṣīya*, *ārṇiṣīvahi*, *ārṇiṣīmahi*. Perfect—*ānṛṇe*, *ānṛṇāte*, *ānṛṇire*; *ānṛṇiṣe*, *ānṛṇāthe*, *ānṛṇidhve*; *ānṛṇe*, *ānṛṇivahe*, *ānṛṇimahe*. Aorist—*ārṇiṣṭa*, *ārṇiṣātām*, *ārṇiṣata*; *ārṇiṣṭhāḥ*, *ārṇiṣāthām*, *ārṇiḍhvam*; *ārṇiṣi*, *ārṇiṣvahi*, *ārṇiṣmahi*. [Note: In the third person plural, the form is *ārṇiṣata* as per the rules for *sa* and *jha* endings. [End of section]
In the *caṅ* (aorist) with the suffix *ṇau*: *ārṇiṇat*, *ārṇiṣyate*, *ārṇiṣyata*, *ārṇitāse*, *ārṇiṇiṣate*.
For *tṛṇu* (in the sense of eating) and *ghṛṇu* (in the sense of shining), the examples should be inferred as including the grammatical operations belonging to the *tan*-class.

The root *van* (to desire) is of both types (*ubhayatobhāṣā*). **Present:** *vanute*, *avanuta*, *vanutām*, *vanvīta*, *vaniṣīṣṭa*. **Periphrastic Perfect:** In the *liṭ* [perfect], *vavane*, *vavanāte*. **Aorist:** In the *luṅ*, *avaniṣṭa*, *avathāḥ* (or *avaniṣṭhāḥ*). **Future:** *vaniṣyate*. **Periphrastic Future:** *vanitā*. **Desiderative:** *vivaniṣate*. The root *man* (to think/understand). **Present:** *manute*. **Imperfect:** *amanuta*. **Imperative:** *manutām*. **Optative:** *manvīta*. **Precative:** *maniṣīṣṭa*. **Perfect:** *mene*, *menāte*. **Aorist:** In the *luṅ*, *amata*, *amaniṣṭa*, *amaniṣātām*, *amaniṣatām*, *amathāḥ* (or *amaniṣṭhāḥ*). **Future:** *maniṣyate*. **Conditional:** *amaniṣyata*. **Periphrastic Future:** *manitāse*. **Desiderative:** *mimaniṣate*. **Intensive:** *maṃmanyate*.
The roots *śī* and *ṭīv* are conjugated in the Ātmanepada.

The root *ḍukṛñ* is used in the sense of "doing. In both cases, by the rule *sārvadhātukayor guṇaḥ*, there is *guṇa* substitution [resulting in *karoti*]. Regarding the augment *suṭ*: while the rule *aḍabhyāsavyavāye 'pi* continues in effect, the rule *samparibhyāṃ karotau bhūṣaṇe samavāye ca* and *upāt pratiyatnavaikṛtavākyādhyāhāreṣu ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.139) prescribes the introduction of the augment *suṭ*. Thus, in the form *saṃskṛti*, the *k* replaces the *s* of *sam* due to the rule for *kutva*; this becomes a *visarjanīya*. Then, by the rule *vā śari* (Pāṇini 8.3.36), that *visarjanīya* remains as such. This applies everywhere where it is applicable, as in the case of the group beginning with *saṃ*.

Regarding the word *satva*: the suffix *satva* always optionally transforms the preceding vowel into an *anusvāra* or an *anunāsika*. Because the *sārvadhātuka* suffix is treated as having the marker *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa* substitution; instead, it undergoes the *utva* change prescribed by Pāṇini’s rule *ata utsārvadhātuke* (6.4.110). The *yaṇ* substitution would apply [in other cases]. In the forms *saṃskurvaḥ* and *saṃskurmaḥ*, the *u* of *vas* and *mas* is dropped because it is stated that [the suffix] always effects the *karoti* [operation]. In the *laṅ* tense, the augment *suṭ* is applied according to the rule *aḍvyavāye’pi*, resulting in *namaskarot*. In the *loṭ* tense, it is *saṃskarotu*.

In the second person singular, *si* is replaced by *hi*. By the rules *ato heḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.105) and *utaśca pratyayādasaṃyogapūrvāt* (Pāṇini 6.4.106), there is elision (*luk*) of *hi*. Thus, [one says] *saṃskuru*. Similarly, in all cases among the *tan*-class verbs, when the optative (*liṅ*) suffixes are applied, there is elision of the vowel *u* according to *ye ca* (Pāṇini 6.4.109). When a long vowel would have been required by *hali ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.77), it is prohibited by *na bhakurchurām* (Pāṇini 8.2.79); thus, [one says] *saṃskuryāt*.

By the rule *āśiṣi riṅ śayagliṅkṣu* (Pāṇini 7.4.28), the substitution *riṅ* occurs. Now, one might ask: why does the rule *guṇo 'rtisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29) not apply to cause *guṇa* when *suṭ* is present? [The answer is: because *suṭ*, being characterized as "external" (*bahiraṅga*), is considered unestablished (*asiddha*) or because it is a subordinate element (*bhakta*) in the formation; thus, due to the refinement [of the root], *suṭ* is applied in the Perfect tense (*liṭ*) even when there is an intervention by the reduplication (*abhyāsa*), as in *saṃcaskāra*.

Regarding the rule *ṛtaśca saṃyogāderguṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.10), which prescribes guṇa for roots beginning with a conjunct consonant, the inclusion of the phrase "beginning with a conjunct" (*saṃyogādi*) is intended for the sake of *kṛ*, just as the mention of "having a penultimate vowel" (*upadha*) is for the sake of *val*. Thus, we have *saṃcaskaratuḥ* and *saṃcaskaruḥ*. According to the rule *thali ṛto bhāradvājasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.63), the prohibition of *iṭ* applies only to *kṛ* when followed by the suffix *suṭ*; hence, *saṃcaskaritha*. For forms not preceded by *suṭ*, we have *cakratuḥ*, *cakruḥ*, and *cakartha*. In the luṅ (aorist), we have *asamaskārṣīt*.

In the case of the suffix *ṇic* followed by *caṅ*, when the fruit of the action does not benefit the agent (*akartrabhiprāya*) and the verb *kṛ* is preceded by the word *mithyā*, the *ātmanepada* endings are used according to the rule *mithyopapadāt kṛño 'bhyāsaḥ*. Thus: *mithyā acīkarat*. When the fruit benefits the agent (*kartrabhiprāya*), the *ātmanepada* is used everywhere by the rule *ṇicaśca* (Pāṇini 1.3.74): *acīkarata*. In other cases, because they fall under the remainder (*śeṣa*), the *parasmaipada* is used: *acīkarat*. [Examples of the future and desiderative forms: *saṃskariṣyati* / *samaskariṣyat* *saṃskartā* *saṃciskīrṣati* *saṃceṣyate*

By the rules *guṇo 'rtisaṃyogādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.29) and *yaṅi ca* (Pāṇini 7.4.30), the *guṇa* substitution does not occur for this reason already mentioned. In the case of *pariṣkaroti*, the change to *ṣ* is applied by the rule *parinivibhyaḥ sevasitasayasivusahasuṭsusvañjām* (Pāṇini 8.3.70). Furthermore, while the Ātmanepada is prescribed for the root *kṛ* when the fruit of the action does not benefit the agent and when it has meanings such as "hinting" (*gandhana*) and so forth, here, because the prefix *parā* precedes it, the Parasmaipada is applied by the rule *anuparābhyāṃ kṛñaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.79).

However, when the action is intended for the agent (*kartrabhiprāya*), the *ātmanepada* affixes are applied by the rule *svaritañitaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.72): *saṃskurute*, *samaskuruta*, *saṃskurvīta*. In this view—that in the benedictive (*āśis*) the root is first joined with its object (*sādhana*) and subsequently with the prefix—the augment *suṭ* is not applied because it is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) due to being a "non-internal" (*bahiraṅga*) feature; thus, the rule *ṛtaśca saṃyogādeḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.10) does not apply. Furthermore, because the suffix is marked with *k* (*kit*) by the rule *uśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), there is an absence of *guṇa* substitution, resulting in *saṃskṛṣīṣṭa*. In the absence of *suṭ*, it would be *kṛṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), as before, there is *guṇa*: *saṃcaskare*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *samaskṛta*, *samakṛthāḥ*, and so forth.

Thus ends the section on the *snā* suffix and others; now begins the section on the *krī* group. The root *√krīñ* (with the marker *ñ*) means "to exchange goods. It receives the designation of a verbal root (*dhātu*). The marker *ñ* serves the purpose of the middle voice (*ātmanepada*), according to the rule *ñitaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.72), which applies when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. In place of the *la* suffix, the *tiṅ* endings (*ti*, etc. are substituted because they are *antaraṅga* (internal). Subsequently, the *guṇa* substitution is reached. As for the *vikaraṇa* (conjugational suffix), because it applies whether [the subsequent operation] has been performed or not, it is considered *nitya* (obligatory); thus, the *śnā* suffix is applied as an exception (*apavāda*) to the *śap* suffix. By the rule *raṣābhyām* (Pāṇini 8.4.1), the *ṇatva* (nasalization of the *n*) occurs, resulting in *krīṇāti*.

By the rule *sārvadhātukamapit* (Pāṇini 1.2.4), the suffix [śnu] is treated as having the marker *ṅ*. By the rules *śnābhyastayorātaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.112) and *ī halyaghoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.113), the form *krīṇītaḥ* is obtained. When an affix beginning with a vowel follows, there is elision of the *ā* of the roots *śnā* and *abhyasta*; likewise in subsequent forms, they become *krīṇanti*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *akrīṇīt*, *akrīṇītām*, *akrīṇan*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *krīṇātu* or *krīṇītāt*, *krīṇītām*, *krīṇantu*, *krīṇīhi*. In the *liṅ* (potential): *krīṇīyāt*, *krīṇīyātām*, *krīṇīyuḥ*. In the *āśis* (precative): *krīyāt*, *krīyāstām*, *krīyāsuḥ*.

By the rule *aco ñṇiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.115), there is vṛddhi: *cikrāya*, *cikriyatuḥ*, *cikriyuḥ*. Here, because it is preceded by a conjunct consonant (*saṃyogapūrvatvāt*), the *yaṇ* substitution applies according to *eranekācaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.82): *cikretha*, *cikrayitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), there is vṛddhi for the *sic* suffix: *akrāiṣīt*, *akrāiṣṭām*, *akrāiṣuḥ*. In the causative (*ṇau*) with the *caṅ* (reduplication), the root *krī* takes the form *krīṇī*—whereby the *ā* is substituted, the *puṅ* augment is added, and the penultimate vowel is shortened—resulting in *acikrayat*. [In the future: *kreṣyati*; [in the conditional: *akreṣyata*; [in the periphrastic future: *kretā*. In the desiderative (*sani*): *cikrīṣati*. In the intensive (*cekrīyate*), the *ātmanepada* occurs because of the *ñit* designation; thus, [in the present: *krīṇīte*.

*krīṇāte*, *krīṇate*; *akrīṇīta*, *akrīṇātām*, *akrīṇata*; *krīṇītām*, *krīṇātām*, *krīṇatām*. Regarding the optative (*liṅ*), by the rule *liṅḥ salopo'nantyasya* (Pāṇini 7.2.79), there is the elision of the *s* of *sīyuṭ*: *krīṇīta*, *krīṇīyātām*, *krīṇīran*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), *kreṣīṣṭa*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *cikriye*, *cikriyāte*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), *akreṣṭa*, *akreṣātām*, *akreṣata*. *Kreṣyata*, and so forth.
When the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, the middle voice (*ātmanepada*) is used after the prefixes *pari*, *vi*, *ava*, and *pra* with the root *kri* (Pāṇini 1.3.18).

The root *prī* means "to satisfy" and "to please," as before. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the *caṅ* suffix, it becomes *apiprīṇāt*. For the root *dhṛ*, the elision (*luk*) should be stated; thus, there is elision. The root *śrī* means "to cook": *śrīṇāti*. Forms such as *aśrīṇāt* and so forth should be applied accordingly.

The root *mī* is used in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*). As before, according to the appropriate application, there is the substitution of *it* and the elision of *āl*. Regarding the rule *upasargātparasya hinumīnāḥ* (Pāṇini 8.4.15), when preceded by the prefix *tiṣi* (the augment *iṭ*), the rule *pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.80) applies, resulting in the shortening of the vowel for the root *mī* in the sense of injury. Thus, one injures a king or a friend: *pramināti*. However, in the common language (*bhāṣā*), it is *pramīṇāti*, *pramīṇītaḥ*, *pramīṇanti*, and so forth. In the benedictive mood (*āśis*), it is *pramīyāt*, *pramīyāstām*.

In the context of the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, the substitution of *ā* for the root vowel according to Pāṇini 6.1.50 (*mīnātimīnotidīṅām*) occurs, as in *pramamau*. According to Pāṇini 7.1.34 (*āta au ṇalaḥ*), the substitution of *au* occurs before the suffix *ṇal*. In the *liṭ* tense with a *kit* suffix, there is no substitution of *ā*, as in *pramimatuḥ* and *pramimyuḥ*. In the case of the *thal* suffix, according to the school of Bhāradvāja, there is the augment *iṭ*, and the elision of *ā* (*āllopaḥ*) occurs: *pramamitha* or *pramamātha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist) tense, when *iṭ* is not present, we have *prāmāsīt* and *prāmāsiṣṭām*. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the *caṅ* (reduplication) suffix, we have *pramimye*, *pramimyāte*, *prāmāsta*, *prāmāsātām*, *prāmāsata*, *pramāsyate*, and so forth.

The root *ṣiñ* means "to bind. Present: *sināti* Aorist (luṅ): *asināt* Imperative: *sinātu* Optative: *sinīyāt*; in the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), *sīyāt*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *siṣāya*. Aorist with *sic*: there is *vṛddhi* [of the root vowel]; *asaiṣīt*. Future: *seṣyati*, and so forth. Likewise, the middle voice forms are: *sinīte*, *asinīta*, *sinītām*, *sinīta*; in the benedictive, *seṣīṣṭa*; in the aorist with *sic*, there is elision (*luk*) [of the *i*]; *aseṣṭa*; *aseṣyata*, and so forth. The root *ṣuñ* means "to float" or "to swim. The root *muñ* means "to bind."
The roots *kuñ* (in the sense of sound) and *duñ* (in the sense of motion)—examples for these should be inferred—[are included]. Regarding *pūñ* (in the sense of purification):

for roots beginning with *pū* and ending with *plī* (in the sense of motion), there is shortening in the domain of *śit* [affixes] according to Pāṇini 7.3.80: "There is shortening for roots beginning with *pvā*. Thus: *punāti*. In the presence of an affix marked with *ṅ*, as before, there is optionally *īt* and elision (*alopa*) according to the requirements: *punītaḥ*; *punanti*, and so on. In the benedictive (*āśis*): *pūyāt*, *pūyāstām*, *pūyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *pupāva*, *pupuvatuḥ*, *pupuvuḥ*; *pupaviṣṭa*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), with the suffix *sic*, there is vṛddhi; the rest is to be understood accordingly: *apāvīt*, *apāviṣṭām*. In the causative with *caṅ*: *apīpavat*. Future: *paviṣyati*. Conditional: *apaviṣyat*. Periphrastic future: *pavitā*.

By the rule *sani śryukaḥ kiti sanigrahaguhośca* (Pāṇini 7.2.12), there is a prohibition of *iṭ*; by *iko jhal* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), the suffix is *kit*, resulting in *pupūṣati*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix, it becomes *popūyate*. Likewise: *punīte*, *apunīta*, *punīyātām*, *punīta*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), *paviṣīṣṭa*, *paviṣīyāstām*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), *pupuve*, *pupuvāte*, *apaviṣṭa*, *apīpavata*, *paviṣyata*, and so forth. The root *lūñ* (meaning "to cut") follows the same pattern as the preceding one.

The root *stṛñ* means "to cover. Present tense: *stṛṇāti*, *stṛṇītaḥ*, *stṛṇanti*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *astṛṇāt*, *astṛṇītām*, *astṛṇan*. Imperative: *stṛṇātu* or *stṛṇītāt*, *stṛṇītām*, *stṛṇantu*. Optative (*liṅ*): *stṛṇīyāt*, *stṛṇīyātām*, *stṛṇīyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), by the rule *ṛta iddhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.100), there is *kit*-treatment; by *hali ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.77), there is lengthening, and the doubling of the *yakāra* results in: *stīryāt*, *stīryāstām*, *stīryāsuḥ*.

In the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, there is *vṛddhi* for a root ending in a vowel. In the case of *kit* suffixes in the *liṭ*, there is *guṇa* by the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11). Thus: *tastāra*, *tastaratuḥ*, *tastaruḥ*, *tastaritha*. In the *luṅ* [aorist] with the *sic* suffix, the augment *iṭ* is added; however, the lengthening of this *iṭ* which would otherwise apply by the rule *stṛvā* is prohibited by the rule *liṭi sici ca parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.40). There is *vṛddhi* in the *sic* [aorist]: *astārīt*, *astāriṣṭām*, *astāriṣuḥ*. In the *caṅ* [reduplicated aorist] of the causative (*ṇic*), we have *atastarat*.

By the rule *lṛluṭoḥ vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied; when it is present, there is lengthening: *starīṣyati* or *stariṣyati*; likewise, *astarīṣyat* or *astariṣyat*; and *starītā* or *staritā*. By the rule *iṭ sani vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.41), the augment *iṭ* is optional in the desiderative (*san*); when *iṭ* is present, there is lengthening: *tistarīṣati* or *tistariṣati*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *iko jhal* (Pāṇini 1.2.9), the suffix is marked with the *kit* designation. Similarly: *stṛṇīte*, *stṛṇāte*, *stṛṇate*; *astṛṇīta*, etc.

By the rule *āśiṣi vṝto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), the long vowel of the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied; however, this is prohibited by the rule *laṭi* [in the context of the *luṅ*]. Thus we have *astariṣīṣṭa* or *astāriṣīṣṭa*. By the rule *asaṃyogālliṭ kit* (Pāṇini 1.2.5), the *liṭ* affixes are *kit*; consequently, by the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), there is *guṇa* substitution, resulting in *ātastare*, *ātastarāte*, *ātastarire*. By the rule *vṝto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), the long vowel of the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied in the *luṅ* tense, yielding *astariṣṭa* or *astīrṣṭa*, *astariṣātām* or *astīrṣātām*, *astariṣyata*, and so forth; the remainder should be understood accordingly. The root *kṛñ* is used in the sense of injury (*hiṃsā*).

The root *vṛñ* means "to choose. It forms *kṛṇāti*, *vṛṇāti*, and so forth, as previously described. The root *dhūñ* means "to shake. [Present: *dhunāti*; [Imperfect: *adhunāt*; [Optative: *dhunīyāt*. In the benedictive: *dhūyāt*, *dhūyāstām*. In the perfect (*liṭ*): *dudhāva*, *dudhuvatuḥ*. By the rule *svarati* (Pāṇini 1.2.72), there is an optional *iṭ*: *dudhotha* or *dudhavitha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), although an optional *iṭ* would otherwise apply, by the rule *añjeḥ stusudhūñbhyaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.72), *iṭ* is compulsory: *adhāvīt*, *adhāviṣṭām*. In the causative with *caṅ* (reduplication): *adūdhuvat*.

The suffix *bhuk* should be stated for the roots *dhū* and *vī*. There is elision (*luk*) [of the suffix]. Regarding the optional application of the augment *iṭ* in the *lṛt* and *luṭ* tenses, by the rule *svarati-sūti-sūyati-dhūñ-ūdito vā* (Pāṇini 1.2.72), we have: *dhoṣyati* or *adhaviṣyat*. In the *luṅ* tense: *adhoṣyat* or *adhaviṣyat*. In the *lṛṭ* tense: *dhotā* or *dhavitā*. In the *san* (desiderative) suffix, by the rule *śryukaḥ kiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.11) and *sanigrahaguhośca* (Pāṇini 7.2.12), there is a prohibition of *iṭ*: *dudhūṣati*. In the *yaṅ* (intensive) suffix, because it is marked with *ñ*, the *ātmanepada* voice applies: *dodhūyate*. In the *parasmaipada*: *dhunīte*. Imperfect: *adhunīta*. Imperative: *dhunītām*. *dhunīta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), as before, there is an option: *dhoṣīṣṭa* or *dhaviṣīṣṭa*; *dhoṣīyāstām* or *dhaviṣīyāstām*.

The root *dṝ* is used in the sense of "tearing apart" (*vidāraṇe*). By the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), and by the rule *śṝdṝprāṃ hrasvo vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.12), a *guṇa* substitution occurs; there is optionally a short vowel, and in the case of the short vowel, a *yaṇ* replacement takes place. Thus, [the forms] are *vidadratuḥ*, *vidadruḥ*, and *vidadaratuḥ*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), the forms are *adārīt* and *adāriṣṭām*. Here, by the rule *sici ca parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.40), there is a prohibition of the long vowel for the augment *iṭ*. There is the substitution of *a* for the reduplicated syllable, resulting in *adadarat*. By the rule *vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), there is optionally a long vowel for the augment *iṭ*; thus, [the future forms are] *dariṣyati* and *darīṣyati*.

*adarīṣyat*, *adarīṣyat*. The future forms are *daritā* and *darītā*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), by the rule "ighrati vā" (Pāṇini 7.2.38), there is optionally the augment *iṭ* and a long vowel; thus, there are three forms: *didariṣati*, *didarīṣati*, and in the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule "iko jhal" (Pāṇini 1.2.9), the suffix is marked with *k* (kit), resulting in *didīrṣati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*), it becomes *dedīryate*. The root *ṝ* means "to injure"; *pṝ* means "to protect" and "to fill," following the same pattern as before.

The root *vṛ* means "to choose. In the case of the desiderative suffix *saN*, when the *caṅ* (the reduplication of the causative) follows, with the exception of the substitution of *at*, there is the specific rule that if *iṭ* is absent, the substitution of *ut* for the vowel preceding *ud* applies optionally according to the rule *udeḥ pūrvasya*. Thus, one forms *vuvūrṣati*.
The root *mṛ* means "to die," and *bhṛ* means "to fry."
The roots *jhṝ* (to fear), *nṝ* (to lead), and *śṝ* (to cook)— the examples for these roots should be inferred according to the preceding pattern.

The root *jyā* is used in the sense of "wasting away" (*vayohāni*). By the rule *grahijyā* (Pāṇini 6.1.16), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*), and by the rule *halaḥ* (6.4.2), there is lengthening; subsequently, by the rule regarding roots beginning with *pvā*, there is shortening. Thus: *jināti*, *jinītaḥ*, *jinanti*, and so forth. In the benedictive (*āśis*), there is vocalization by the *grahijyā* rule, and lengthening by *halaḥ*; thus: *dīryāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the form is] *jijyau*. In the presence of a *kit* suffix, there is vocalization and reduplication; by the rule *eranekācaḥ* (6.4.82), [the forms are] *jijyatuḥ*, *jijyuḥ*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), as before, there are the augment *s* and the *iṭ* augment; thus: *ajyāsīt*, *ajyāsiṣṭām*.

In the *caṅ* [aorist] with the causative suffix (*ṇic*), *ajijyapat*. In the future: *jyāsyati*; in the conditional: *ajyāsyat*. In the desiderative (*san*): *jijyāsati*. In the intensive (*yaṅ*): *jeṅjīyate*. The root *gṝ* means "to sound. Present: *gṛṇāti*. Imperfect: *agṛṇāt*. Imperative: *gṛṇātu*. Optative: *gṛṇīyāt*. In the benedictive, by the rule *ṛta iddhātoḥ* (Pāṇini 7.1.100), there is *it*-substitution, followed by *rapara*-substitution, and then lengthening: *gīryāt*, *gīryāstām*, *gīryāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*) with the *ṇal* suffix, there is *vṛddhi*: *jagāra*, *jagaratuḥ*. By the rule *ṛcchatyṝtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11), there is *guṇa*: *jagaruḥ*. [Second person singular: *jagaritha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *agārīt*, *agāriṣṭām*, *agāriṣuḥ*. In the *caṅ* [aorist] with the causative suffix (*ṇic*): *ajīgarat*.

By the rule *vṝto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), there is optionally a lengthening of the *iṭ* augment; thus, one says *gariṣyati* or *garīṣyati*. In the *san* (desiderative) suffix, as before, there is a threefold form: *jigariṣati*, *jigarīṣati*, and *jigīrṣati*. Regarding the *yaṅ* (intensive) suffix, some say that because the rule *ṛta it* [applies] and because the subsequent rule *yo yaṅi* [applies], there is *latva* (the substitution of *l* for *ṛ*), resulting in *jegilyate*. Others, however, maintain that the *yaṅ* suffix does not occur here due to non-usage (*anabhidhāna*). The root *jṝ* (in the sense of "decay of age") follows the previous pattern. The root *vṝ* (in the sense of "choosing"): *vṛṇāti* and so forth. In the causative (*ṇic*) with the *caṅ* (reduplication) suffix, by the rule *arti-hrī-vlī-...* (Pāṇini 7.3.36) and others, there is *puṅ* (the addition of *puk*), the *guṇa* substitution conditioned by *puganta*, and the shortening of the *upadhā* vowel; thus, *avivriyat*.

The root *rī* is used in the senses of "going" and "seeking. **Present:** *riṇāti*, *riṇītaḥ*, *riṇanti*. **Imperfect (*laṅ*):** *ariṇāt*, *ariṇītām*, *ariṇan*. **Imperative:** *riṇātu*, *riṇītām*, *riṇantu*. **Optative:** *riṇīyāt*, *riṇīyātām*, *riṇīyuḥ*. **Benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*):** *riṇīyāt*, *riṇīyāstām*, *riṇīyāsuḥ*. **Perfect (*liṭ*):** In the perfect, by the rule *eranekācaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.82), *yaṇ* substitution occurs, followed by reduplication: *rirāya*, *ririyatuḥ*, *ririyuḥ*; *riretha*, *rirayitha*. **Aorist (*luṅ*):** *araiṣīt*, *araiṣṭām*, *araiṣuḥ*. **Causative with *caṅ* (Reduplicated Aorist):** In the causative with *caṅ*, as before, *puṅ* etc. are applied: *arīripat*. **Future (*lṛṭ*):** *reṣyati*, and so forth.

The root *lī* is used in the sense of "adhering" (*śleṣaṇe*). Present: *lināti*. Aorist: *alināt*. Imperative: *linātu*. Optative: *linīyāt*. In the benedictive: *līyāt*. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), by the rule *iṭ paramedviṣaye vibhāṣā līyateḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.51), there is optionally an *ā*-vowel substitution before the suffix *ṇal*: *lalau*; otherwise, *lilāya*. Perfect: *lilyatuḥ*, *lilyuḥ*. Second person singular: *liletha* or *lilātha* / *lilayitha*. Aorist: *alāsīt*. Future: *leṣyati*, etc. The root *plī* is used in the sense of "going" (*gatau*); *plīnāti*, etc. For roots beginning with *pvā*, the aforementioned grammatical operation applies. The root *vlī* is used in the sense of "covering" (*varaṇe*). Present: *vlīnāti*. Aorist: *avlīnāt*. Imperative: *vlīnāt*. Optative: *vlīnīyāt*, etc.—these forms are to be inferred accordingly.

The root *bhrī* means "to fear. [Conjugations: *bhrīṇāti*, *abhṛṇāt*, *bhṛṇāti*, *bhṛṇīyāt*. From this point onward, it is similar to the root *jṝ* in the sense of "loss of vitality. The root *kṣiṣ* means "injury"; the letter *ṣ* is for the sake of forming the feminine (*ṅīp*). Forms such as *kṣiṇāti* and so forth are to be understood by analogy with the remainder.

The root *jñā* is used in the sense of "to know. In the context of the *śit* affixes, the substitution of *jā* for *jñā* and *jan* is applied according to Pāṇini 7.3.79 (*jñā-janor-jā*). Thus: *jānāti*. As before, depending on the requirements, there is the substitution of *ī* and elision [of the penultimate vowel]. *jānītaḥ*; *jānanti*. In the *laṅ* (imperfect): *ajānāt*, *ajānītām*, *ajānanta*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *jānātu*, *jānītāt*, *jānītām*, *jānantu*. In the *liṅ* (potential): *jānīyāt*, *jānīyātām*, *jānīyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśīr-liṅ*), by Pāṇini 6.4.67 (*erliṅi*) and 6.4.68 (*vānyasya saṃyogādeḥ*), there is optionally the substitution of *e*: *jñeyāt* or *jñāyāt*. [In the perfect: *jajñau*, *jajñātha*.

In the *luṅ* [aorist], as before, there is the addition of *sag* and *iṭ* due to the characteristic of roots ending in long *ā*: *ajñāsīt*, *ajñāsiṣṭām*, *ajñāsiṣuḥ*. Because it belongs to the *ghaṭādi* class, there is shortening of the vowel for the meanings beginning with "knowledge" according to Pāṇini 6.4.92 (*mitāṃ hrasvaḥ*). Otherwise, in the *caṅ* [reduplicated aorist] after the causative suffix *ṇi*, there is shortening of the penultimate vowel: *ajijñapat*. The future is *jñāsyati*; the conditional is *ajñāsyat*. The periphrastic future is *jñātā*. Regarding the desiderative (*san*), Pāṇini 1.3.57 (*jñāśrusmṛdṛśāṃ sanaḥ*) prescribes the middle voice (*ātmanepada*). As for the present *jānāti*, the middle voice is prescribed by Pāṇini 1.3.44 (*anupasargājjñaḥ*) when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent and there is no prefix (*anupasarga*).

In general, the Ātmanepada is established there by the following rules: *apahnave jñaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.44), *kevalādādikarmaṇi kṛtaḥ kartari ca* (Pāṇini 1.3.45), and *saṃpratibhyāmanādhyāne* (Pāṇini 1.3.46). Furthermore, for the root preceded by *anu* and followed by the desiderative suffix (*san*), the rule *nāno jñaḥ* (Pāṇini 1.3.58) excludes that [Ātmanepada]. There are two summary verses: "When the fruit of the action resides in the agent, when there is a connection with a prefix in the sense of concealment (*apahnava*), and when the root *jñā* follows *sam* and *prati* in the sense of non-study (*anādhyāna*)—these are the cases. [The verse continues: "When the root *jñā* follows *anu*, when it is in the desiderative form (*sananta*), and when it is preceded by *nañ*—in these cases, the Ātmanepada is excluded. Summary Verses: When the fruit of the action resides in the agent, when there is a prefix in the sense of concealment, and when the root follows *sam* and *prati* in its intransitive state; When it is preceded by *anu*, when it is in the desiderative, and when preceded by the negative particle *nañ*—the Ātmanepada is excluded.
One should know that the *ātmanepada* occurs after the root *jñā* even when followed by the suffix *saN*;
however, it does not occur after *jñā* preceded by *anu*, nor after it preceded by *prati* or *ā*.

The root *bandh* means "to bind. Because the suffix *snā* is marked with the indicatory letter *ṅ*, there is elision of the nasal *n* according to Pāṇini Sūtra 6.4.24 (*aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti*). The remainder is as before. Present tense (*laṭ*): *badhnāti*, *badhnītaḥ*, *badhnanti*. Aorist (*laṅ*): *abadhnāt*, *abadhnītām*, *abadhnan*. Imperative (*loṭ*): *badhnātu*, *badhnītāt*, *badhnītām*, *badhnantu*. According to Pāṇini Sūtra 3.1.83 (*halaḥ śnaḥ śānajjhau*), the substitute *śnā* becomes *śānac* when followed by *jhi* (the first-person plural ending). Optative (*liṅ*): *badhyāt*, *badhnīyāt*, *badhnīyātām*, *badhnīyuḥ*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is elision of the nasal *n* as before: *badhyāt*.

*badhyāstām* (optative); *badhyāsuḥ*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), [the forms are] *babandha*, *babandhatuḥ*, *babandhuḥ*, *babandhitha*; and by the substitution of the unaspirated (*jaś*) for the aspirate (*dhatva*), *babandha*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), after the suffix *cli* is replaced by *sic*, there is the substitution of *bhaṣ* and the change of *c* to *k*, and the vṛddhi prescribed for stems ending in a consonant: *abhāntsīt*. When a *jhal* follows, there is the elision of *s*: *abāddhām*, *abhāntsuḥ*. *bhatsyati*, etc.
These roots ending in *ṛ* are *seṭ* (taking the *iṭ* augment) and are *aniṭ* (not taking the *iṭ* augment) in the *parasmaipada*.

The root *vṛṅ* is used in the sense of "to choose" (*sambhaktau*). Present tense (*laṭ*): *vṛṇīte*, *vṛṇāte*, *vṛṇīṣe*. Aorist (*laṅ*): *avṛṇīta*, *avṛṇātām*, *avṛṇata*. Imperative (*loṭ*): *vṛṇītām*, *vṛṇātām*, *vṛṇatām*; *vṛṇīta*. Optative (*liṅ*): *vṛṇīyātām*, *vṛṇīran*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), there is optionally the augment *iṭ* and the lengthening of the vowel; however, this is prohibited by the rule *liṅi* (Pāṇini 1.2.11). Thus: *variṣīṣṭa*, *variṣīyāstām*, *variṣīran*.

By the rule *uśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12), the *liṭ* affix does not become *kit* because it begins with a vowel (*aj*) followed by a non-consonant (*ahal*). Regarding the optional *iṭ* augment for the *liṅ* and *sic* in the *ātmanepada*, when the *iṭ* is absent, *uśca* (Pāṇini 1.2.12) applies the *kit* designation, resulting in: *vṛṣīṣṭa*, *vṛṣīyāstām*, *vṛṣīran*. In the perfect tense: *vavre*, *vavrāte*, *vavrire*. By the rule concerning roots beginning with *kṛ* (the *krādi-sūtra*), there is a prohibition [of the *ṇatva* substitute], so we have *vavṛṣe*. In the second person plural (*dhvam*), the retroflex (*ūrdhanya*) is obligatory: *vavṛḍhve*. And: *vavṛvahi*.

In the *liṅ* (optative), there is an optional *iṭ* augment according to Pāṇini 7.2.42 (*liṅi iṭ sani vā liṅsicorātmanepadeṣu*). In the case where *iṭ* is present, there is optionally a long vowel: *avariṣṭa*, *avarīṣṭa*. In the absence of *iṭ*, there is *kit*-treatment by Pāṇini 1.2.12 (*uśca*), and the elision of *s* by Pāṇini 8.2.27 (*hrasvādaṅgāt*): *avṛta*, *avṛṣātām*, *avṛṣata*. [The futures are] *variṣyate*, *varīṣyate*; [the conditionals are] *avariṣyata*, *avarīṣyata*; [the periphrastic futures are] *varitā*, *varītā*.

Before the suffix *san*, there is optionally the augment *iṭ*. In the alternative where *iṭ* is present, by the rule *vṛto vā* (Pāṇini 7.2.38), there is optionally a lengthening of the vowel; thus, there are three forms: *vivariṣate* and *vivarīṣate*. In the absence of *iṭ*, due to the *kit* designation, there is no lengthening and the *ṛ* becomes *u*: *vuvūrṣate*. In the *yaṅ* suffix, by the rule *rīṅ ṛtaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.27), *rī* is substituted: *vevrīyate*. The root *manth* (meaning "to churn") undergoes the elision of its nasal by the rule *aniditām* (Pāṇini 6.4.24): *mathnāti*. Aorist: *amathnāt*. Imperative: *mathnātu*. Optative: *mathnīyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), there is elision of the nasal: *mathyāt*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *mamantha*, *mamanthatuḥ*, *mamanthuḥ*, *mamanthitha*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *amathnīt*, *amanthiṣṭām*, *amanthiṣuḥ*. Future: *mathiṣyati*, etc.

The roots *śranth* and *muc* are used in the sense of "releasing"; *śranth* and *granth* in the sense of "binding" or "composition"; and *kuth* in the sense of "afflicting. Examples [of these] are to be inferred. Regarding these, because of the rule *ādau śranthigranthidanbhiṣvañjīnāṃ ca* (Pāṇini 7.2.59), there is the *kit* suffix, which causes the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika*). Under the governing rule *ata ekahalmadhya* (Pāṇini 6.4.120), the rule *tṛphalabhajatrapaśca* (Pāṇini 6.4.122) contains the particle *ca*, which serves to include what has not been explicitly mentioned; therefore, even for a root situated between multiple consonants, there is the substitution of *e* for *a* and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsa-lopa*). Thus: *śrethatuḥ*, *śrethuḥ*, *śrethitha*. In other forms, the shape is identical to that of *manth*.

The root *mṛd* (meaning "to crush") is as follows: present indicative—*mṛdnāti*; imperfect—*amṛdnāt*; imperative—*mṛdnātu*; optative—*mṛdnīyāt*; in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*)—*mṛdyāt*; perfect (*liṭ*)—*mamarda*, *mamṛdatuḥ*, *mamṛduḥ*; aorist (*luṅ*)—*amardīt*; conditional—*amardiṣyat*, and so forth.
The root *mṛḍ* means "to delight"; the root *gud* means "to be angry."

*ksubh* means "to shake" (*sañcalane*). *nabha* and *tubha* mean "to injure" (*hiṃsāyām*). Examples for these are to be inferred. *kuṣa* means "to extract" (*niṣkarṣe*). Present: *kuṣṇāti*. Imperfect: *akuṣṇāt*. Imperative: *kuṣṇātu*. Optative: *kuṣṇīyāt*. Benedictive: *kuṣyāt*. Perfect: *cukoṣa*, *cukuṣatuḥ*, *cukuṣuḥ*; *cukoṣitha*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), after the substitution of *sic* for *cli*, by Pāṇini 7.2.46 (*niraḥ kuṣaḥ*), there is an optional *iṭ* augment for the *ārddhadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant. Thus: *nirakoṣīt*. In the absence of *iṭ*, *cli* is replaced by *ksa*; after the changes of *k* to *ṭ* and *ṣ* to *ṣṭ*, we have *nirakuṣat*. Dual: *nirakuṣatām*. In the *lṛṭ* (future), *luṭ* (periphrastic future), and the *san* (desiderative), we have *niṣkoṣiṣati*. First future: *niṣkoṣyati*. Conditional: *nirakoṣiṣyat*. Second conditional: *nirakokṣyat*.

*niṣkoṣitā*, *niṣkoṣṭā*; *niṣkuṣiṣati*, *niṣkoṣiṣati*; *cukukṣati*, *cokuṣyate*. The root *kliś* (meaning "to afflict"): *kliśnāti*. Aorist: *akliśnāt*. Imperative: *kliśnātu*, *kliśnītāt*; *kliśnītām*; *kliśnantu*. Aorist (injunctive): *akliśnāt*. Optative: *kliśnīyāt*. Benedictive: *kliśyāt*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *cikleśa*, *cikliśatuḥ*, *cikliśuḥ*. Because it is marked with *ū*, there is an option regarding the augment *iṭ*: *cikleśitha*, *cikleśa*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *akleśīt*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule *igupadhādi cleḥ ksaḥ*, the suffix *ksa* is applied; after the application of the rules for *ṣatva*, *katva*, and *cartva*, we have *aklikṣat*. Future: *kleśiṣyati*, *klekṣyati*, etc., should be formed accordingly.

The root *aś* is used in the sense of eating. Present tense (*laṭ*): *aśnāti*, *aśnītaḥ*, *aśnanti*; *aśnāsi*, *aśnīthaḥ*, *aśnītha*; *aśnāmi*, *aśnīvaḥ*, *aśnīmaḥ*. Imperative (*loṭ*): *aśnātu*, *aśnītāt*, *aśnītām*, *aśnantu*; *aśāna*, *aśnītam*, *aśnīta*; *aśnāni*, *aśnāva*, *aśnāma*. Optative (*liṅ*): *aśnīyāt*, *aśnīyātām*, *aśnīyuḥ*; *aśnīyāḥ*, *aśnīyātam*, *aśnīyāta*; *aśnīyām*, *aśnīyāva*, *aśnīyāma*. Benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *aśyāt*, *aśyāstām*, *aśyāsuḥ*; *aśyāḥ*, *aśyāstam*, *aśyāsta*; *aśyāsam*, *aśyāsva*, *aśyāsma*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *āśa*, *āśatuḥ*, *āśuḥ*; *āśitha*, *āśathuḥ*, *āśa*; *āśiva*, *āśima*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *āśīt*, *āśiṣṭām*, *āśiṣuḥ*; *āśīḥ*, *āśiṣṭam*, *āśiṣṭa*; *āśiṣam*, *āśiṣva*, *āśiṣma*. Causative with *caṅ* (reduplication): *āśiśat*. Future (*lṛṭ*): *āśiṣyati*. Conditional (*lṛṅ*): *āśiṣyat*. Periphrastic future (*lṛṭ*): *āśitā*. Desiderative (*san*): *āśiśiṣati*. By the rule "An addition for *sūci*, *sūtri*, *mūtri*, *yasū*, and *ṇoti*," there is *yaṅ*:
