*aśāśyate*. The root *iṣ* is used in the sense of repetition (*ābhīkṣṇya*): *iṣṇāti*. The root *viṣ* is used in the sense of separation (*viprayoga*): *viṣṇāti*.
The roots *puṣ* and *pluṣ* mean "to moisten" and "to fill. They form *puṣṇāti* and *pluṣṇāti*.
The root *kaṣ* means "the appearance of putrefaction"; the example *kaṣṇāti* is to be inferred.

The root *muṣ* means "to steal. Present tense (*laṭ*): *muṣṇāti*, *muṣṇītaḥ*, *muṣṇanti*. Aorist (*laṅ*): *amuṣṇāt*, *amuṣṇītām*, *amuṣṇan*. Imperative (*loṭ*): *muṣṇātu*, *muṣṇītāt*, *muṣṇītām*, *muṣṇantu*; [Vocative: *muṣāṇa*. Potential (*liṅ*): *muṣṇīyāt*, *muṣṇīyātām*, *muṣṇīyuḥ*. Benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*): *muṣṇyāt*, *muṣṇyāstām*, *muṣṇyāsuḥ*. Perfect (*liṭ*): *mumoṣa*, *mumuṣatuḥ*, *mumuṣuḥ*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *amoṣīt*, *amoṣiṣṭām*, *amoṣiṣuḥ*. Causative with *caṅ* (reduplication): *amūmuṣat*. Future (*lṛṭ*) and conditional (*lṛṅ*): *moṣiṣyati*, *amoṣiṣyat*. Periphrastic future (*luṭ*): *moṣitā*.

When the suffix *san* follows, the optionality of the *kit* designation for the penultimate short vowel (*upadhā*) applies; however, by Pāṇini 1.2.8 (*rudavidamuṣagrahi...*), the *kit* designation for *san* is compulsory. Thus: *mumuṣiṣati*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix: *momuṣyate*.

For the root *puṣ* (to nourish): *puṣṇāti*, etc., as before. When *san* follows, by Pāṇini 1.2.26 (*ralo vyupadhāl lopaḥ...*), the *kit* designation is optional: *pupuṣiṣati* or *pupoṣiṣati*. These roots ending in *seṭ* (with an indicatory *i*) are *parasmaipada* (active voice).

The root *grah* means "to seize" or "to take. For roots beginning with *grah*, *jyā*, and others, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). Present tense (*laṭ*): *gṛhṇāti* (he seizes), *gṛhṇītaḥ* (they two seize), *gṛhṇanti* (they seize); *gṛhṇāsi* (you seize), *gṛhṇīthaḥ* (you two seize), *gṛhṇītha* (you all seize); *gṛhṇāmi* (I seize), *gṛhṇīvaḥ* (we two seize), *gṛhṇīmaḥ* (we seize). Aorist (*laṅ*): *agṛhṇāt* (he seized), *agṛhṇītām* (they two seized), *agṛhṇan* (they seized); *agṛhṇāḥ* (you seized), *agṛhṇītam* (you two seized), *agṛhṇīta* (you all seized); *agṛhṇām* (I seized), *agṛhṇīva* (we two seized), *agṛhṇīma* (we seized). Benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*)—with vocalization: *gṛhyāt* (may he seize), *gṛhyāstām* (may they two seize), *gṛhyāsuḥ* (may they seize); *gṛhyāḥ* (may you seize), *gṛhyāstam* (may you two seize), *gṛhyāsta* (may you all seize); *gṛhyāsam* (may I seize), *gṛhyāsva* (may we two seize), *gṛhyāsma* (may we seize). Perfect (*liṭ*): *jagrāha* (he seized), *jagṛhatuḥ* (they two seized).

They took (*jagṛhuḥ*). You took (*jagrahitha*). You two took (*jagṛhathuḥ*). You all took (*jagṛha*). He took (*jagrāha*). We two took (*jagṛhiva*). We all took (*jagṛhima*). Regarding *jagṛha* in the Vedic usage, there is lengthening of the *iṭ* augment according to Pāṇini 7.2.37: "In the *luṅ* [aorist], for the root *grah*, there is lengthening of the *iṭ* except in the *liṭ*. Thus: he took (*agrahīt*). They two took (*agrahiṣṭām*). They all took (*agrahiṣuḥ*). You took (*agrahīḥ*). You two took (*agrahiṣṭam*). You all took (*agrahiṣṭa*). I took (*agrahiṣam*). We two took (*agrahiṣva*). We all took (*agrahiṣma*). In the causative with *caṅ* (the reduplicated aorist): he caused to take (*ajigrahat*). They two caused to take (*ajigrahatām*). They all caused to take (*ajigrahan*). You caused to take (*ajigrahaḥ*). You two caused to take (*ajigrahatam*). You all caused to take (*ajigrahata*). I caused to take (*ajigraham*). We two caused to take (*ajigrāva*).

We seized. In the *lṛṭ* (future): he will seize, they two will seize, they will seize; you will seize, you two will seize, you all will seize; I will seize, we two will seize, we all will seize. He will have seized, they two will have seized, they will have seized; you will have seized, you two will have seized, you all will have seized; I will have seized, we two will have seized, we all will have seized. He is about to seize, they two are about to seize, they are about to seize; you are about to seize, you two are about to seize, you all are about to seize; I am about to seize, we two are about to seize, we all are about to seize. He will be a seizer, they two will be seizers, they will be seizers; you will be a seizer, you two will be seizers, you all will be seizers; I will be a seizer, we two will be seizers.

We have grasped [the rule]. By the rule *sani rudavidamuṣagrahi* (Pāṇini 1.2.8), the suffix *san* is *kit*; by the rule *sanigrahaguhośca* (Pāṇini 7.2.12), there is a prohibition of the augment *iṭ*. Thus: *jighṛkṣati*. [Aorist: *ajighṛkṣata*. [Imperative: *jighṛkṣatu*. [Optative: *jighṛkṣet*. [Precative: *jighṛkṣyāt*. [Periphrastic perfect: *jighṛkṣāñcakāra*. [Aorist: *ajighṛkṣīt*. [Conditional: *ajighṛkṣet*. [Future: *jighṛkṣiṣyati*. [Conditional future: *ajighṛkṣiṣyat*. [Periphrastic future: *jighṛkṣitā*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix: *jarīgṛhyate*, etc. Because the root is marked with the *svarita* accent, the *ātmanepada* endings are used: *gṛhṇīte*, *gṛhṇāte*, *gṛhṇate*.

gṛhṇīṣe | gṛhṇāthe | gṛhṇīdhve | gṛhṇe | gṛhṇīvahai | gṛhṇīmahai | agṛhṇīta | agṛhṇātām | agṛhṇata | agṛhṇīthāḥ | agṛhṇīthām | agṛhṇīdhvam | agṛhi | agṛhṇīvahi | agṛhṇīmahi | In the *loṭ* [mood]: gṛhṇītām | gṛhṇātām | gṛhṇatām | gṛhṇīṣva | gṛhṇīthām | gṛhṇīdhvam | gṛhṇai | gṛhṇāvahai | gṛhṇāmahai | In the *liṅ* [mood]: gṛhṇīta | gṛhṇīyātām | gṛhṇīran | gṛhṇīthāḥ | gṛhṇīyāthām | gṛhṇīdhvam |

Let us take: *gṛhṇīya*, *gṛhṇīvahi*, *gṛhṇīmahi*. In the sense of benediction (*āśis*), there is lengthening of the vowel of the root *grah* in the periphrastic future (*liṭ*): *grahīṣīṣṭa*, *grahīṣīyāstām*, *grahīṣīran*; *grahīṣīṣṭhāḥ*, *grahīṣīyāsthām*, *grahīṣīdhvam*; *grahīṣīya*, *grahīṣīvahi*, *grahīṣīmahi*. The perfect forms are: *jagṛhe*, *jagṛhāte*, *jagṛhire*; *jagṛhiṣe*, *jagṛhāthe*, *jagṛhidhve*; *jagṛhe*, *jagṛhivahe*, *jagṛhimahe*. The vowel of the augment *iṭ* does not undergo lengthening because of the prohibition "not in the case of *aliṭ*" (Pāṇini 7.2.35). Thus: *agrahīṣṭa*, *agrahiṣātām*, *agrahīṣata*.

*agrahīṣṭhāḥ*; *agrahiṣāthām*. By the rule *dhi ca* (Pāṇini 8.2.25), there is the elision of *s*: *agrahīdhvam*; *agrahīḍhvam*. *agrahīṣi*; *agrahīvahi*; *agrahīmahi*. In the *lṛṭ* (future): *grahīṣyati*; *grahīṣyate*; *grahīṣyete*; *grahīṣyante*; *grahīṣyase*; *grahīṣyethe*; *grahīṣyadhve*; *grahīṣye*; *grahīṣyāvahe*; *grahīṣyāmahe*. In the *lṛṅ* (conditional): *agrahīṣyat*; *agrahīṣyetām*; *agrahīṣyanta*; *agrahīṣyathāḥ*; *agrahīṣyethām*.

[Second person plural: *agrahīṣyadhvam* | [First person singular: *agrahīṣye* | [First person dual: *agrahīṣyāvahi* | [First person plural: *agrahīṣyāmahi*. In the *luṭ* (periphrastic future), [the forms are]: *grahītā*, *grahītārau*, *grahītāraḥ*; *grahītāse*, *grahītāsāthe*, *grahītādhve*; *grahītāhe*, *grahītāsvahe*, *grahītāsmahe*. Likewise, the *l*-suffixes in the passive voice are: *gṛhyate*, *agṛhyata*, *agṛhyetām*, *gṛhyeta*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), there is an option for the *ciṇvadiṭ* augment: *grāhiṣīṣṭa*. In the absence of the *ciṇvadiṭ* augment, there is lengthening by the rule for *liṅ* after a suffix beginning with *val*: thus, in other cases as well, *grahīṣīṣṭa*.

In the *liṭ* [perfect tense], there is *jagṛhe*. In the *luṅ* [aorist], when the word *ta* follows, by the rule *ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.66), there is *ciṇ*; then by *ciṇo luk* (Pāṇini 6.4.104), there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *śap*, resulting in *agrāhi*. In other cases, there is optionally the *ciṇvad-iṭ* augment for *sic*: *agrāhiṣātām* or *agrāhiṣatām*. In the *lṛṭ* [future], *grāhiṣyate* or *grahiṣyate*. In the *lṛṅ* [conditional], *agrāhiṣyata* or *agrahiṣyata*. In the *luṭ* [periphrastic future], *grāhitā* or *grahītā*.
Thus end the verbs of the *kryādi* class with the *śnā* conjugational marker (*vikaraṇa*). This concludes the section on the *curādi* [denominative] class.

The suffix *ṇic* is added in the sense of the root itself by the rule *satyāpapāśa-* (Pāṇini 3.1.25). By the rule *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.1.32), the designation "root" (*dhātu*) is applied; as before, the *laṭ* and other tenses follow. By the rule *kartari śap* (Pāṇini 3.1.68), the *śap* affix is added, resulting in the substitution of *guṇa* and *āy*. Thus: *corayati* (he steals). In the *laṅ*: *acorayat*. In the *loṭ*: *corayatu*. In the *liṅ*: *corayet*. In the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), by the rule *ṇeraniṭi* (Pāṇini 6.4.51), there is elision of the *ṇic* affix: *coryāt*.

By the rule *kāspratyayādām amantre liṭi* (Pāṇini 3.1.35), the suffix *ām* is introduced; when the *ṇi*-suffix is elided, the substitution of *ay* for *ṇi* occurs by the rule *ayāmantālvāyyetviṣṇuṣu* (Pāṇini 6.4.55). Thus: *corayāñcakāra*. In the *luṅ* (aorist), by the rule *ṇiśridruṣubhyaḥ car̥ṅ* (Pāṇini 3.1.48), *aṅ* replaces *cl*, and the *ṇi*-suffix is elided. The penultimate vowel is shortened (*upadhāhrasva*), reduplication (*dvirvacana*) occurs, and by the rule *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.60), all but the first consonant of the reduplicated syllable are dropped. Since the condition for *bha*-status does not apply here, the lengthening of a light vowel (*dīrgho laghoḥ*) by the rule *aco ñṇiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.115) does not take effect. Thus: *acūcurat*. In the *lṛṭ* (future): *corayiṣyati*. In the conditional (*lṛṅ*): *acorayiṣyat*. In the periphrastic future (*lṛṭ*): *corayitā*.

*sani* [in the sense of desire]: *cucorayiṣati*. Because the *yaṅ* affix is not included among the roots listed in the *atyalloka* group, the *ātmanepada* ending is applied when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, according to Pāṇini 1.3.74 (*ṇicaśca*). Thus: *corayate*, *acorayata*, *corayatām*, *corayeta*. In the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), there is the addition of *iṭ*: *corayiṣīṣṭa*. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*): *corayāñcakre*. In the aorist (*luṅ*): *acūcurat*. In the conditional (*lṛṅ*): *corayiṣyat*, and so forth. This should be understood to apply to all subsequent [roots] up until the end of the section, as far as the *gaṇa* permits. This concludes the section on the *kaṇḍvādi* group.

The root *kaṇḍū* is used in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*). There is elision of the suffix *ya* [after the root]. In the optative (*liṅ*), active: *kaṇḍūyāt*; middle: *kaṇḍūyiṣīṣṭa*. In the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), active: *kaṇḍūyāñcakāra*; middle: *kaṇḍūyāñcakre*. In the aorist (*luṅ*), active: *akaṇḍūyīt*; middle: *akaṇḍūyiṣṭa*. Regarding the causative (*ṇic*) with the reduplication (*caṅ*), according to the rule stating that "for roots beginning with *kaṇḍū*, there should be a statement that the third singular *ekāc* (monosyllabic) element undergoes reduplication," the syllable *ya* is reduplicated, resulting in *akaṇḍūyiyat*. In the future (*lṛṭ*), active: *kaṇḍūyiṣyati*; middle: *kaṇḍūyiṣyate*. In the conditional (*lṛṅ*), active: *akaṇḍūyiṣyat*; middle: *akaṇḍūyiṣyata*. In the periphrastic future (*lṛṭ*), active: *kaṇḍūyitā*; active with *si*: *kaṇḍūyitāsi*; middle: *kaṇḍūyitāse*. In the desiderative (*san*), active: *kaṇḍūyiyiṣati*; middle: *kaṇḍūyiyiṣate*.
There is no intensive (*yaṅ*) formation because the root has more than one syllable (*anekāctvāt*). The root *vrīṇī* is conjugated as follows: *vrīṇīyate*.
mahīṅ mahīpate;
tiras tirasyeti;
duḥkha ato lopaḥ duḥkhyati.
*sukha* forms *sukhyati*;
*bhiṣaj* forms *bhiṣajyati*.
Thus end the *kaṇḍv-ādi* roots.

According to the Sautra roots *stambhu*, *stumbhu*, *skambhu*, *skumbhu*, and *skuñ* (Pāṇini 3.1.82), the suffixes *śnu* and *śnā* are applied. Because these are marked with the indicatory letter *ṅ*, there is the elision of the nasal (*anunāsika-lopa*). By the rule *upasargādiṇa uttarasya stanbheḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.67), there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*. Thus: *viṣṭabhnoti* or *viṣṭabhnāti*. Even when separated by the augment *aṭ*, we have *vyaṣṭabhnot* or *vyaṣṭabhnāt*. In the imperative: *viṣṭabhnotu* or *viṣṭabhnātu*; in the potential: *viṣṭabhnuyāt* or *viṣṭabhnīyāt*. In the benedictive (*āśis*), there is the elision of *na*: *viṣṭabhyāt*. In the perfect (*liṭ*), it is *vitastambha*; in the aorist (*luṅ*), it is *vyaṣṭambhīt*.

In *vyaṣṭambhiṣuḥ*, there is a prohibition of the substitution of *ṣ* by Pāṇini’s rule *stambhusivusahāṃ caṅi* (Pāṇ. 8.3.116). In the *luṭ* [future] tense: *viṣṭambhiṣyati* (active), *viṣṭambhiṣyate* (middle); *vyaṣṭambhiṣyati* (active), *vyaṣṭambhiṣyata* (middle). In the *san* [desiderative] suffix: *vitastambhiṣati*. In the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix: *vitāṣṭabhyate*. For the root preceded by *ut*, the substitution of the homogeneous vowel of the preceding syllable applies by Pāṇini’s rule *udaḥ sthāstambhoḥ pūrvasya* (Pāṇ. 8.4.61), as in *uttabhnāti*, and so forth; this should be applied accordingly. In the same manner, examples for the other roots should also be cited.

By the rule *skabhnāteḥ parasya veḥ skabhnāternityam* (Pāṇini 8.3.77), there is the substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*] after the root *skabh* when followed by *vi*; thus, one says *viṣkabhnāti*. For other [prefixes], it does not occur; thus one says *pariskabhnāti*, *viskabhnoti*, *skubhnoti*, *śkubhnoti*, and so forth—this should be inferred accordingly. Thus ends the section on roots from the Sūtras in the *Śābdikābharaṇa*, a work by Hariyogin Proḷanācārya, concerning the fivefold system of verbal roots and suffixes. The purpose for which the formation of *ūrṇu* is treated like *ṇu* is the establishment of the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix.
And because of the inclusion [of the term] "ekācaḥ" (monosyllabic) for the purpose of prohibition, it is *āma*.

This is its meaning: the sense is that the root *ūrṇuñ* (in the sense of "covering") must be stated as being equivalent to *ṇu* (in the sense of "praising"). What is the purpose? The purpose is the establishment of the *yaṅ* suffix. According to the rule *dhāto-rekāco hal-ādeḥ kriyā-samabhihāre yaṅ*, the *yaṅ* suffix is applied to a one-vowel root beginning with a consonant when there is an intensification of the action (*kriyā-samabhihāra*). Now, *nauti* (from *ṇu*) is indeed a one-vowel root beginning with a consonant; therefore, the *yaṅ* suffix would [otherwise] apply to it.

Therefore, for the sake of establishing the *yaṅ* [intensive suffix] even for the root *ūrṇu*, the status of being like *ṇu* (*ṇuvadbhāva*) must be stated. Furthermore, there is another purpose: by the rule "ijādeśca gurumato 'nṛcchaḥ," the suffix *ām* is prescribed after a root beginning with *ij* that has a heavy vowel (*gurumat*), when the *liṭ* [perfect tense] follows; and since *ūrṇoti* both begins with *ij* and has a heavy vowel, the suffix *ām* would consequently apply to it. Therefore, to prevent that, the status of being like *ṇu* must be stated for the root.

There is yet another purpose: "if [the root] has a single vowel (*ekāc*) due to the mention of *iṭ*. The ablative case in *iḍupagrahāt* is used with the elision of a suffix ending in *-lyap*, as in the expression "he looks from the palace" (*prāsādāt prekṣate*). According to the rule stating that the ablative is to be prescribed when there is the elision of a suffix ending in *-lyap*, this refers to the mention of *iṭ*; that is, the prohibition of *iṭ*. The meaning is that having considered the prohibition of *iṭ*, the substitution of *ṇu* (the *ṇuvadbhāva*) must be stated. Now, one might object: both *nau* and *ūrṇo* are indeed *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*), for they are both listed among the roots ending in long *ū* in the *Anit-kārikā*: "Now, *ūrṇoti* and *kṣṇuvi* [are mentioned]."

How then is the *aniṭ* (non-iṭ) status of the root *ūrṇu* established by its similarity to *yu*, whereby that which is already established (*siddha*) is sought to be proven by means of what is not yet established (*asiddha*)? This is not a fault. This substitution of *ṇu* for the purpose of prohibiting *iṭ* does not have a general scope; rather, it has a specific scope.

By the rule *śryukḥ kiti*, because of the governing context of *ekācaḥ* (one-syllable roots), the prohibition of *iṭ* is applied to one-syllable roots ending in *i* or *u* when followed by *kit* suffixes—just as it occurs in *yuyotavān*—so that it may also occur in *ūrṇutavān*. Thus, the meaning is that even in this case, the substitution of *ṇu* must be stated.
Thus ends the *Śābdikābharaṇa* composed by Hariyogin.

Regarding the verbal suffixes (*tiṅ-pratyaya*), there are ten distinct types of *śap*: *śabluk*, *ślu*, *śyan*, *śnu*, *śa*, *śnam*, *u*, *śnā*, as well as the suffixes used in their own sense (*svārtha*) and the causative (*ṇic*).
A specific reading must be stated; the application of the *ūrṇu* rule as if it were *ṇu*, the establishment of *yaṅ*,
and the prohibition of *ām* due to the inclusion of "monosyllabic roots" (*ekācaḥ*) are the purposes.

This is its meaning: the sense is that the root *ūrṇuñ* (in the sense of "covering") should be stated as being equivalent to *ṇu* (in the sense of "praising"). What is the purpose? The purpose is the establishment of the *yaṅ* suffix. By the rule "the *yaṅ* suffix is applied after a one-vowel root beginning with a consonant to denote frequent or intense action," *yaṅ* is applied to roots that have one vowel and begin with a consonant when there is frequent or intense action; however, *nauti* (from *ṇu*) is such a root—it has one vowel and begins with a consonant—and therefore *yaṅ* would result.

Therefore, for the sake of establishing the *yaṅ* [intensive] suffix even for the root *ūrṇu*, the status of being like *ṇu* (*ṇuvadbhāva*) must be stated. Furthermore, there is another purpose: by the rule "ijādeśca gurumato 'nṛcchaḥ," the *ām* suffix is prescribed after roots beginning with *ij* that have a heavy vowel (*gurumat*) when the *liṭ* suffix follows; since the root *ūrṇoti* is both heavy and begins with *ij*, the *ām* suffix would consequently apply to it. Therefore, the status of being like *ṇu* must be stated for the root in order to prevent that.

There is yet another purpose [for this rule]: "if [the root] has a single vowel (*ekāc*) and there is the inclusion of *iṭ* (*iḍupagrahāt*). In the expression *iḍupagrahāt*, the ablative case is used with the elision of the suffix *-lyap* (as in *prāsādāt prekṣate*—"he looks from the palace"), meaning that the ablative in the sense of the object (*karman*) should be stated when there is the elision of *-lyap*. Thus, the meaning is: having observed the inclusion of *iṭ*, the prohibition of *iṭ* (*iṭ-pratiṣedha*), one must state the treatment as *ṇu* (*ṇuvadbhāva*). Now, an objection might be raised: both *nau* and *ūrṇu* are indeed *seṭ* (taking *iṭ*); for it is stated in the *Anit-kārikā* regarding roots ending in *ū*: "two are listed among those ending in *ū*: *ūrṇoti* and also *kṣṇuvi*."

How then is the absence of the augment *iṭ* for the root *ūrṇu* established through its similarity to *yu*, such that what is already established (*siddha*) is being proven by what is not yet established (*asiddhena*)? This is not a fault. This substitution of *ṇu* (ṇuvadbhāva) for the purpose of prohibiting *iṭ* does not have a general scope; rather, it has a specific scope.

By the rule "śryukṅti" (Pāṇini 1.2.29), because of the governing context of "ekācaḥ" (one-syllable roots), the prohibition of *iṭ* is applied to one-syllable roots ending in *iṭ* when followed by *kit* affixes, as in the case of *yu*—for example, *nunūtavān*. The meaning is that this same *ṇu*-substitution must be stated so that the form *ūrṇutavān* may also be obtained.
Thus ends the *Śābdikābharaṇa* composed by Hariyogin.

Regarding the verbal suffixes (*tiṅ*), there are ten distinct types of affixes: *śabluk*, *ślu*, *śyan*, *śnu*, *śa*, *śnam*, *u*, *śnā*, the *ṇic* added in its own sense (*svārtha*), and likewise *śap*.
